suggestion.title: PAM Module Replacement & Backdoor Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'replaced legitimate pam_unix.so modules with backdoored versions' discovering 'nine distinct variants of the malicious PAM module, each compiled in a separate build environment.' This is the primary persistence and credential-harvesting vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file integrity of pam_unix.so and related PAM modules in /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/security/ and /lib64/ for hash mismatches against baseline packages. Detect pam_unix.so in unexpected paths and alert on process execution loading non-standard PAM modules. File timestamps misaligned with package metadata are strong indicators of compromise.

suggestion.title: SSH Binary Trojans (ssh, sshd, scp Replacement)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers 'replaced OpenSSH components such as ssh, sshd, and scp with trojanized versions that captured credentials, logged commands entered during SSH sessions, and stored the collected data locally for future retrieval.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hash OpenSSH binaries (ssh, sshd, scp) against known-good vendor baselines and flag mismatches. Monitor sshd for anomalous child processes, credential file access, or unusual environment variables. Detect SSH processes with command-line arguments inconsistent with normal authentication or session management.

suggestion.title: Systemd Service Persistence Implantation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers achieved 'persistence either via a malicious systemd service or through startup script modification.' Systemd services persist across reboots and provide hands-off C2 execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/systemd/system/ and /usr/lib/systemd/system/ for newly created or modified .service files outside change-control windows. Alert on systemd units spawning reverse shells, connecting to external IP addresses, or executing binaries from non-standard directories. Correlate with systemctl enable/start activity.

suggestion.title: SOCKS5 Proxy Masquerading as Samba Daemon
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'custom SOCKS5 proxy... ran as a daemon masquerading as smbd -D, using different filenames and ports on each host' to tunnel traffic into the isolated network.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes with command-line 'smbd -D' originating from paths other than /usr/sbin/smbd. Alert on multiple distinct processes claiming smbd identity on different high-numbered ports. Correlate with SOCKS5 handshake signatures in network traffic; genuine Samba processes should match package baselines.

suggestion.title: Nginx/FastCGI Remote Execution Bridge into Isolated Network
suggestion.rationale: Article details how attackers 'modified the configuration of a compromised internet-facing Nginx server to proxy specially crafted requests to a compromised backend server' running 'fcgiwrap' as an 'execution bridge' launching 'a custom binary named uptime' to establish SSH tunnels into the isolated network.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor nginx.conf for proxy_pass rules forwarding to localhost on unusual ports, particularly fcgiwrap sockets or high-numbered ports. Alert on fcgiwrap spawning shell interpreters or system execution binaries. Detect nginx access logs with POST requests containing binary/hex payloads, unusual Content-Type headers, or User-Agent patterns consistent with automated RCE frameworks.

suggestion.title: GS-Netcat Reverse Shell via Hardcoded Relay Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Velvet Ant deployed a modified GS-Netcat reverse shell disguised as a legitimate system component that connected to a hardcoded relay domain, providing encrypted remote shell access.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GS-Netcat process signatures via string scanning, capability analysis, or behavior profiling. Monitor for uncommon processes establishing encrypted outbound connections on non-standard ports to external domains. Alert on sustained encrypted sessions with unusual C2-like patterns (beaconing, command injection via network packets). Cross-reference DNS queries to suspected relay domains.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Unauthenticated Code Execution Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Attackers Run Code Without Authentication'—defines the exact attack. Zero detection rules generated for web-based RCE attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Splunk web interface (ports 8000, 8089) from unauthenticated sessions containing template-injection syntax, serialized Python/Java objects, or shell metacharacters in URL parameters or POST bodies. Correlate with failed prior authentication attempts.

suggestion.title: Splunk Process Spawn and Command Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated RCE implies arbitrary code execution. Must detect child processes spawned by splunkd or Splunk web service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash spawned as children of splunkd.exe or Splunk web service process. Establish whitelist of legitimate child processes; flag any deviation, especially with network outbound activity.

suggestion.title: Splunk Web Service Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: RCE executed under service account; attackers typically escalate privileges post-exploitation. No privilege-escalation detection rules generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect UAC bypasses, token elevation, or service-account privilege additions within Splunk process context. Monitor for modification of Splunk scheduler/saved-search ACLs or sudoers rules on Linux deployments.

suggestion.title: Splunk Port Scanning and Service Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Initial-access phase: attackers enumerate Splunk deployments before exploitation. 'Attackers' implies active reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect TCP SYN scans targeting Splunk default ports (8089 admin, 8000 web, 9998 KV store) from external IPs. Correlate rapid port probing with subsequent HTTP GET requests to /en-US/ or /api/ endpoints as exploitation indicator.

suggestion.title: Splunk Reverse Shell or C2 Callback
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE, attackers establish C2 or persistence. No outbound-communication or post-exploitation detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound HTTPS or DNS from Splunk process to external IPs/domains not in whitelist. Correlate with process-execution logs showing concurrent child-shell spawning; flag reverse-shell patterns (bash -i, nc callbacks).

suggestion.title: Splunk Configuration or Secret Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: RCE context provides access to credentials stored in Splunk configs. No data-exfiltration detection for secrets, API keys, or database creds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file reads from Splunk configuration directories ($SPLUNK_HOME/etc/) and secret-storage paths (passwd.conf, authentication.conf) by non-admin users or from unexpected processes. Detect exfiltration of .conf files or credential objects via HTTP/HTTPS.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Email Sender Reputation + URL Reputation Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: AI-generated phishing (from title) often exploits nascent infrastructure; mismatch between sender reputation and URL reputation is signature of low-infrastructure attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails from low-reputation or newly-registered sender domains that hyperlink to high-reputation domains (domain spoofing). Cross-check SPF/DKIM alignment; misalignment indicates sender-spoofing attempt.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Externally Reachable Network Reconnaissance

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Ivanti Sentry fleet for appliances not enrolled in EPMM or Neurons for MDM, lacking mTLS enforcement, or with unrestricted HTTPS access enabled. Flag as high-risk if externally reachable.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Root-Level RCE Execution Hunting
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as outcome. Pipeline must detect privilege-escalation patterns and root spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance process logs for unexpected root-spawned processes, especially shell invocations, network tools (curl, wget, nc), or reverse shells. Correlate with prior unauthenticated HTTP request anomalies.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Externally Reachable Instance Inventory

Cross-reference against internal asset database to flag unmanaged appliances. Alert on public DNS A/CNAME records pointing to Sentry instances.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated API Access Attempts

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Patterns in Sentry Requests

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect URL parameters, POST bodies, and headers sent to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for command substitution syntax. Flag requests containing patterns: $(cmd), `cmd`, cmd|cmd, cmd;cmd, cmd&&cmd. Correlate with process creation events to confirm injection success.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Child Process Spawning from Sentry Service

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell.exe) spawned by Ivanti Sentry service process with UID=0 (root) or SYSTEM privilege. Flag unexpected interpreter execution, reverse shells, or data exfiltration tools launched from Sentry parent.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry instances that are both internet-routable (external IP on 443/8443) and NOT enrolled in mTLS with EPMM or behind Neurons for MDM. Cross-correlate asset inventory with enrollment status and flag unmanaged, exposed instances as exploitable.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection in Ivanti Sentry Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the attack vector. Detection must target injection metacharacters in HTTP payloads to Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for command shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&&`, backtick, `$()`, pipe chains) in URL parameters, POST bodies, or headers. Baseline legitimate requests; alert on unauthenticated payloads with injection signatures matching common OS command injection patterns (e.g., `; whoami`, `| id`).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Root Privilege Escalation Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability achieves 'root-level remote code execution.' Post-compromise detection must hunt for unexpected root-level process spawning on Sentry hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance process execution logs (auditd, /var/log/auth.log) for child processes spawned with UID 0 (root). Baseline legitimate service processes; alert on anomalous privilege elevation, especially processes spawned by Sentry service daemon user (typically non-root) that escalate to root.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance and Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with explicit federal patch due date (2026-06-14). Standard vulnerability management detection to flag unpatched or missing-from-inventory Ivanti Sentry instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner (Nessus, Qualys, etc.) and software inventory for Ivanti Sentry presence and version. Flag instances running versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-10520 (pre-patch release). Correlate with patch date; escalate any systems overdue for remediation past federal due date.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry mTLS and EPMM Enrollment Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies mTLS with EPMM and restricted HTTPS through Neurons for MDM as the key mitigations that 'make interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Compliance hunt must verify these controls are active.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Ivanti Sentry configuration/audit logs to confirm all instances have mTLS enforcement enabled AND are enrolled in EPMM, OR are behind Neurons for MDM with restricted HTTPS access. Flag any externally-exposed Sentry instance without both controls as non-compliant and exploitable.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access Spike to Ivanti Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability exploitable by 'remote unauthenticated user.' Spike in unauthenticated requests to Sentry endpoints may signal probing or exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate unauthenticated requests to Ivanti Sentry (e.g., enrollment checks, MDM health queries). Alert on statistical anomalies: sudden increase in volume, requests from new geolocations, or requests containing command injection/path traversal patterns. Correlate with unpatched or exposed instances.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — identifying externally exposed instances is the foundational prerequisite for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances accessible from untrusted networks via inventory or port scanning. Prioritize instances without mTLS enforcement or restricted HTTPS access that fall within the federal 2026-06-14 remediation window.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated OS Command Injection Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability allows 'remote unauthenticated user' to 'achieve root-level remote code execution' via 'OS command injection' — monitor for command metacharacter payloads in HTTP requests to vulnerable endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints containing shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&`, `$()`, backticks) or common command injection patterns. Alert on unauthenticated access attempts reaching application logic that processes external input.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Root-Level Process Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability grants 'root-level remote code execution' — detect behavioral anomaly of unexpected root-privilege process spawning from Ivanti Sentry service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate root operations from Ivanti Sentry processes. Flag unexpected process creation, command execution, or privilege escalation initiated by Ivanti Sentry java/daemon processes with UID 0.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scan and Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article cites federal patch due date '2026-06-14' and warns 'patch lag is the silent killer' — proactive vulnerability scanning is critical given CISA KEV active exploitation status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Ivanti Sentry instances with CVE-2026-10520 in vulnerable state. Correlate with asset management system; flag any instances still unpatched beyond 2026-06-14 federal deadline or with publicly routable management interfaces.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Post-Compromise Network Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Root-level RCE enables attacker control of appliance; article does not specify post-exploitation behavior, but standard pattern includes lateral movement or data exfiltration to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish network baseline for legitimate Ivanti Sentry outbound connections. Monitor for new outbound connections to unknown or suspicious IP ranges, high-entropy domains, or geographies inconsistent with organization footprint.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Phishing Email Content Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly addresses 'AI Phishing' in title; detection pipeline should flag emails with signatures of LLM-generated content (unusual grammar patterns, generic closings, repetitive phrasing) that differ from organizational baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify inbound emails with high cosine similarity to known LLM token distributions, unusual word-frequency profiles, or entropy spikes in sender domain/subject combinations suggesting generated content. Filter on recipient list size (bulk phishing) and temporal clustering (batch sends).

suggestion.title: Phishing Volume Spike Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title emphasizes 'crushing SOCs with alert volume'—suggests campaigns at scale. Pipeline should detect anomalous phishing email rate from new/spoofed senders, clustered by domain similarity or sender reputation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when phishing email count from unique senders or lookalike domains exceeds 3-sigma baseline in 1h window. Include domain registration age, DMARC/SPF alignment failures, and sender-to-recipient domain mismatches (external→internal high-value users).

suggestion.title: High Credential-Submission Rate Post-Phishing
suggestion.rationale: If 'AI Phishing' is being used for credential harvesting, pipeline should correlate phishing email receipt with subsequent login attempts from non-standard geolocations or impossible-travel scenarios within minutes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 5min of phishing email receipt, detect login attempts to same org domain from email-inferred high-risk countries, unusual user-agents, or IPs associated with known phishing infrastructure. Correlate by recipient email domain.

suggestion.title: BEC/CEO Fraud with AI-Synthesized Communication Style
suggestion.rationale: Article title mentions phishing without specifying commodity vs. targeted; if AI is enabling impersonation at scale, need detection for requests from spoofed executive accounts with anomalous outbound volume or timing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound emails from high-value accounts (C-suite, finance, HR) with receiver outside normal contact list, urgent language patterns (redacted PII, time pressure), wire-transfer requests, or mismatch vs. sender's historical behavior profile.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and recommends asset-exposure hunt templates. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite direct guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner results showing Ivanti Sentry (formerly MobileIron Sentry) with CVE-2026-10520 present. Filter for unpatched versions prior to vendor remediation date (2026-06-14). Cross-reference against network exposure data to prioritize externally-reachable instances.

suggestion.title: Externally Exposed Ivanti Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is exploitable 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Requires network exposure detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances (product name match, known ports/signatures) with inbound connectivity from untrusted networks (non-RFC1918, non-corporate). Prioritize instances without mTLS or HTTPS restriction as described in the article.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Requires execution-layer detection for injection payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry service/process for anomalous child process spawning or command-line execution (particularly shell interpreters: /bin/bash, /bin/sh, cmd.exe). Flag processes executed with root/SYSTEM privilege from Sentry service context. Correlate with vulnerability scanner results showing CVE-2026-10520.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Sentry Appliance Enrollment Status Check
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unmanaged state' as the risk condition and notes mTLS/restricted HTTPS mitigates the risk. Requires detection of misconfigured enrollment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Ivanti Sentry appliances (via inventory) that report enrollment status=unmanaged or lack valid mTLS certificates for EPMM/Neurons integration. Cross-reference against network accessibility to find unmanaged+exposed combinations.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Sentry Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'root-level remote code execution' as the exploitation outcome. Requires privilege escalation detection if initial compromise succeeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation events where the parent process is Ivanti Sentry service and spawned processes run with UID=0 (root) or SYSTEM privilege. Investigate unauthorized privilege elevation patterns from known-vulnerable CVE-2026-10520 appliances.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Vulnerability Scanning Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'it's worth one quick check across your fleet' and references asset-exposure hunts using vulnerability scanning for CVE-2026-10520.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vulnerability scanner outputs and CMDB for Ivanti Sentry instances with CVE-2026-10520 detections. Prioritize systems flagged as unmanaged or externally reachable. Validate patch status against federal due date (2026-06-14).

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Endpoint Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploitable when 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' mTLS and restricted HTTPS are identified mitigations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances with external network accessibility via firewall rules, port scans, or DNS records. Validate that mTLS and restricted HTTPS policies are enforced; flag instances lacking these mitigations as high-risk.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Against Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level RCE.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Sentry endpoints for unauthenticated requests containing shell metacharacters (;, |, &, $(), backticks, newlines). Correlate with HTTP 200/500 responses indicating command execution. Alert on patterns consistent with command injection payloads.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Root Process Spawning from Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes successful exploitation 'achieve root-level RCE,' requiring detection of privilege escalation and persistence signals post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by Sentry service with UID 0 (root). Flag unexpected executables (sh, bash, curl, wget) launched from Sentry context. Correlate timing with external HTTP requests containing injection payloads.

suggestion.title: Sentry Service Reconnaissance and Version Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Threat actors must identify and enumerate vulnerable Sentry instances before exploitation; article notes only 'unmanaged state with externally reachable endpoints' are vulnerable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect reconnaissance probes: repeated HTTP GET requests to Sentry default paths, requests with non-standard/scanner User-Agent strings, or deliberate HTTP error triggering. Flag systematic probing patterns consistent with vulnerability enumeration.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scan: CVE-2026-10520
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' This is the primary detection vector for an in-the-wild exploited vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Ivanti Sentry instances with CVE-2026-10520. Identify all affected asset owners and triage for immediate patch deployment before federal due date (2026-06-14).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Asset exposure is the precondition for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate internet-facing Ivanti Sentry instances via port/service scanning, DNS queries, and SSL certificate logs. Cross-reference with management platform connectivity to identify 'unmanaged' appliances (no heartbeat/control-plane check-in).

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article root cause: 'OS command injection vulnerability.' Exploitation requires shell metacharacters in HTTP payloads—this is the execution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry application logs and network sensors for OS command metacharacters (|, ;, &, $(), backticks, >>, InputStream injection patterns) in HTTP request parameters. Alert on payloads targeting known vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Sentry Management
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Unauthenticated connection attempts are exploitation precursors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry management interfaces that complete without authentication challenge (401/403 bypass, or direct access to protected endpoints). Correlate source IPs with threat intel for malicious context.

suggestion.title: Root-Privilege Process Spawning on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Attack outcome: 'root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation, unexpected UID=0 processes spawned via HTTP handlers or Sentry service account are strong indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution with root/UID=0 context on Ivanti Sentry appliances, especially spawned by HTTP request handlers, Sentry daemons, or unprivileged service accounts. Baseline normal Sentry process behavior to reduce FP.

suggestion.title: mTLS/Restricted Access Control Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes mitigation: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible.' Bypass attempts indicate attacker adaptation to controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP→HTTPS protocol downgrade attempts, mTLS certificate mismatches, or port-hopping to reach Sentry on non-standard ports. Flag proxying/tunneling behavior that circumvents mTLS certificate pinning.

suggestion.title: Linux PAM Module Unauthorized Replacement or Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly details attackers replacing pam_unix.so with nine distinct backdoored variants: 'replaced legitimate pam_unix.so modules with backdoored versions that accept hardcoded passwords and harvest user credentials.' This is a critical persistence and credential-harvesting mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/pam.d/ directory and /lib/security/ for unauthorized file modifications and hash changes to pam_unix.so. Alert on PAM module replacement, unsigned variants, or config changes permitting hardcoded password acceptance. Correlate with logon and credential-harvest telemetry.

suggestion.title: Trojanized OpenSSH Binary Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article describes replacement of ssh, sshd, scp with trojanized versions: 'replaced OpenSSH components such as ssh, sshd, and scp with trojanized versions that captured credentials, logged commands entered during SSH sessions, and stored the collected data locally for future retrieval.' Dual-purpose malware enabling persistence and credential exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SSH binary integrity via hash and signature verification. Alert on ssh/sshd/scp launched from unexpected paths, with unexpected parent processes, or with compilation timestamps inconsistent with OS baseline. Track SSH authentication anomalies and side-channel credential exfiltration.

suggestion.title: System Service Masquerading for Proxy/Tunneling
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The proxy ran as a daemon masquerading as 'smbd -D', using different filenames and ports on each host.' SOCKS5 proxy used for internal lateral movement while evading process-inspection controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for processes claiming to be smbd or other service daemons with unexpected parent, binary path, or listening on non-standard ports. Alert on legitimate service names making outbound connections to internal networks or spawning child processes atypical for that service.

suggestion.title: Nginx Configuration Modification for Command Execution Relay
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'modified the configuration of a compromised internet-facing Nginx server to proxy specially crafted requests to a compromised backend server...forward requests to a FastCGI process (fcgiwrap) listening on a separate port. The FastCGI wrapper acted as an execution bridge, processing requests and launching a custom binary.' Converts web server into remote-execution bridge.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Nginx configuration files for unexpected proxy_pass directives pointing to internal FastCGI, localhost, or unusual ports. Alert on fcgiwrap process spawning or unexpected child execution. Track HTTP POST requests with SSH-like parameters. Correlate web server process spawning shell/SSH children.

suggestion.title: Systemd Service Creation for Reverse Shell Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'achieved persistence either via a malicious systemd service or through startup script modification.' Modified GS-Netcat reverse shell connected to hardcoded relay domain, maintaining persistence across password changes and session termination.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/systemd/system/ and /usr/lib/systemd/system/ for new or modified units. Alert on services spawning shell interpreters, reverse shells, or connecting to hardcoded external domains. Verify service legitimacy against package manifests and track enable/disable operations.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST Parameter-Driven SSH Tunnel to Isolated Network
suggestion.rationale: Article describes novel C2 mechanism: 'established SSH connections to systems within the isolated critical infrastructure network using parameters supplied in HTTP POST requests. By chaining these modifications, Velvet Ant established a remote-execution path into the segregated environment via simple HTTP requests.' Critical lateral movement into air-gapped networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP POST request bodies for SSH connection parameters (host, port, key, user). Alert on web server processes spawning SSH or establishing SSH outbound connections in response to HTTP requests. Track fcgiwrap or other FastCGI processes executing SSH or custom binaries. Correlate web server logs with network-egress SSH sessions.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Splunk Endpoint Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Attackers Run Code Without Authentication'—core attack vector is bypassing auth to reach Splunk APIs. Pipeline missed the initial access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk instances for HTTP requests to authenticated endpoints (e.g., /services/*, /api/*) from sources that do not have an active authenticated session. Track 401/403 followed by 200 responses in the same session, or direct 200s without prior auth handshake.

suggestion.title: Splunk Remote Code Execution via Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'Run Code Without Authentication'—execution phase is the attack impact. No detection for this critical outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by splunkd.exe or splunk processes (e.g., cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) without corresponding user login or scheduled task trigger. Monitor for process execution with parent=splunkd and grandparent not in expected whitelist.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Outbound Connections from Splunk Enterprise
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE typically leads to C2 or data exfiltration. Pipeline missed post-exploitation behavior detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate outbound connections from splunkd and related processes. Flag connections to non-whitelisted external IPs, especially to known malicious infrastructure, or connections to unusual ports (reverse shells on 4444, 5555, 8888).

suggestion.title: Splunk Configuration or Knowledge Object Tampering
suggestion.rationale: RCE in Splunk could enable persistence through malicious configuration or searches. Article describes a flaw in 'Splunk Enterprise'—no detection for post-breach persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk audit logs for unexpected modifications to saved searches, dashboards, app configurations, or alert actions. Alert on creation of searches containing suspicious keywords (curl, wget, powershell, bash -i) or new scripted inputs from unauthenticated sources.

suggestion.title: CVE-Based Splunk Vulnerability Scanning Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article is about a critical Splunk flaw—no detection for reconnaissance or exploitation tools probing for the vulnerability. Attackers must discover Splunk instances first.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create signature-based detection for CVE-specific exploit payloads in HTTP requests to Splunk ports (8000, 8089). Monitor for characteristic URL patterns, malformed requests, or known PoC beacon traffic targeting Splunk endpoints.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation via kernel flaw – root shell spawn
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Enables Local Root Access' — privilege escalation from local unprivileged process to root is the core attack. No detection UC addresses privilege boundary crossing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unprivileged processes spawning child processes with euid=0 or elevated capabilities (CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYSADMIN). Detect UID/GID transitions without sudo/su/doas invocation. Alert on process parent is non-root but child runs as root.

suggestion.title: Suspicious kernel module operations post-exploit
suggestion.rationale: Kernel exploits commonly load malicious modules. Article does not detail post-exploitation behavior, but kernel-level persistence via module loading is high-signal indicator for this class of flaw.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor insmod/modprobe/rmmod execution from user-space processes, particularly if spawned by non-system accounts. Detect kernel module insertions that lack corresponding source in /lib/modules or are executed from /tmp, /var/tmp, or other attacker-writable locations.

suggestion.title: Abnormal syscall sequences indicating memory corruption
suggestion.rationale: One-character kernel vulnerabilities often rely on memory corruption. Article emphasizes 'one-character flaw' but pipeline did not generate detection for syscall anomalies that precede exploit success.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for syscall sequences involving mmap/mprotect/mremap followed by rapid ioctl or prctl calls with unusual arguments. Detect processes that cross memory boundaries or attempt to write to kernel address space (mmap with MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE failures, bad return codes).

suggestion.title: Public exploit invocation – known-bad binary/payload patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Exploits Now Public' — pipeline should flag execution of known public PoC tools or malicious scripts associated with this CVE once identifiers are confirmed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Once CVE identifier is confirmed and exploit code is available, maintain hash/path indicators of public PoC binaries. Alert on execution of any matching binary or shell invocations that download/execute exploit payloads from known staging domains.

suggestion.title: Capability escalation – CAP_SYS_ADMIN or kernel-level capabilities
suggestion.rationale: Privilege escalation to root typically requires kernel capabilities. No detection rule addresses capability escalation, which is a natural side-effect of kernel exploits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes gaining CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYSLOG, or CAP_SYS_PTRACE without explicit setcap or privilege inheritance chain. Detect capability bounding set modifications (prctl PR_CAPBSET_DROP) that indicate post-exploit hardening evasion.

suggestion.title: Pre-exploitation enumeration – kernel version/config discovery
suggestion.rationale: Exploit success depends on target kernel version. Pipeline should flag processes enumerating /proc/version, uname -a, or kernel config files — common reconnaissance preceding kernel exploit execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unprivileged processes executing uname -r, cat /proc/version, or reading /boot/config-* and /proc/config.gz in rapid succession. Correlate with subsequent attempts to execute suspicious binaries or shell scripts — indicator of pre-exploit reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly establishes exposure condition: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Foundational detection is asset inventory mapped to exposure risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Ivanti Sentry appliances in production. Cross-reference against firewall rules and proxy logs to confirm management interfaces (HTTPS, typically 443) are NOT accessible from untrusted networks. Flag appliances with public-facing DNS records or listening on external IP interfaces.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article prescribes 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner' as the detection mechanism. CISA KEV entries require active vulnerability scanning as primary detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-10520 findings. Prioritize unpatched and unknown-patch-status Ivanti Sentry instances. Correlate findings with asset exposure hunt to identify externally-reachable vulnerable appliances requiring emergency patching.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Access to Sentry Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated user' can exploit, meaning the vulnerability does not require valid credentials. Detection should surface authentication-bypass or early-stage unauthenticated access to management endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP/HTTPS requests to Sentry management interfaces that lack valid session tokens, authentication headers, or pre-auth credentials. Flag requests to /admin, /sentry, /mdm, or /manage paths without authenticated context. Baseline expected authenticated request patterns first.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload in Sentry HTTP Parameters
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause explicitly stated: 'OS command injection vulnerability.' Attackers inject shell metacharacters into application parameters. Detection should flag command-injection patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Sentry ingress and application logs for shell metacharacters in HTTP request parameters: backticks, $(...), pipe, semicolon, &&, ||, newline-escape sequences. Prioritize requests from untrusted networks hitting Sentry before authentication boundary.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root-Level Process Execution on Sentry Appliance Post-Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies outcome as 'root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation detection should surface unexpected process spawning as root on the Sentry host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry process execution logs for unexpected child processes spawned from Sentry management services (e.g., Java application container, nginx, tomcat) running as root. Flag any deviation from baseline expected processes. Correlate process spawn with unauthenticated HTTP access from same source within 1-10 second window.

suggestion.title: Network Segmentation Validation: Sentry Management Interface mTLS and MDM Integration
suggestion.rationale: Article states protective controls: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Inverse: absence of mTLS or MDM integration indicates severe risk. Detection should validate protection is active.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify each Ivanti Sentry appliance enforces mTLS client-certificate validation and is integrated with EPMM or Neurons for MDM. Alert on Sentry instances with: mTLS disabled, TLS certificate pinning absent, MDM/EPMM integration unconfigured, or HTTPS ingress accessible without client-certificate requirement.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - Asset Exposure Scope
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — this is the foundational precondition enabling exploitation. Pipeline must establish scope before hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry / MobileIron Sentry appliances running vulnerable versions (pre-patch) that are internet-routable (WAN-facing, non-RFC1918). Cross-reference with MDM status to surface unmanaged instances lacking mTLS/EPMM proxy protection.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the attack vector. Pipeline must detect injection payloads in HTTP requests to vulnerable endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests (GET/POST/PUT) to Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters and command separators (;, |, &, backticks, $() syntax) in query parameters or POST bodies. Alert on command-injection payloads (id, whoami, cat, chmod, curl) especially from unauthenticated sources. Baseline: expect no such patterns against these endpoints.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - Root-Level RCE Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes impact as 'root-level remote code execution' — post-injection, attackers execute commands with root privilege. Must detect RCE execution signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Sentry appliances, detect shell interpreter spawning (bash, sh, python, perl) from web service processes or Sentry application processes with root UID. Flag unusual child processes, commands from /tmp, and post-compromise discovery patterns (whoami, ifconfig, netstat, ps aux).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - Suspicious Outbound Traffic from Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Full appliance RCE implies C2 establishment or data exfiltration. Article's 'root-level' access enables unrestricted network access from the compromised host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound traffic from Sentry appliance IPs for anomalies: unexpected connections to external IPs, non-standard ports, suspicious DNS queries, beaconing patterns. Establish baseline of expected Sentry egress (vendor updates, MDM heartbeats) and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - Weak mTLS / Unencrypted Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes mitigation: 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible' — detection should flag absence of these controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Sentry instances without mTLS enforcement: plaintext HTTP on Sentry ports, TLS missing client-certificate validation, HTTP served on standard ports, external (non-proxy) direct connections from untrusted networks. Flag appliances not routed through Neurons/EPMM intermediary.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - Persistence and Lateral Movement Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Root-level RCE enables persistence mechanisms (cron, SSH keys, user creation) and lateral movement into trusted networks. Article's uncontained compromise implies network-wide risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor compromised Sentry appliance for persistence: cron job creation, SSH authorized_keys modification, new user account creation, sudoers edits. Detect lateral movement: SSH connection attempts to internal hosts, SMB reconnaissance, password dumping from Sentry, network scanning from appliance IP range.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Network Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'endpoints externally reachable' is the prerequisite for exploitation. Pipeline missed the foundational asset-exposure hunt identifying Internet-facing Sentry appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances with external network reachability via asset inventory, public IP scans, or exposure scanning. Cross-reference against internal asset database to flag unexpected externally-reachable management interfaces.
