suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by Sentry service with root privileges. Flag shell execution, reverse shells, or utility processes (curl, wget, nc) spawned from the Sentry appliance—anomalous for a network monitoring tool.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated HTTP Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated' exploitation possible. OS command injection in web-facing applications manifests as malformed HTTP requests with command metacharacters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to exposed Sentry instances for payloads containing shell metacharacters, backticks, $(command), or command separators in URL parameters or POST bodies targeting admin/API/config endpoints.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry mTLS Enforcement Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible.' Missing these controls indicates unmitigated exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify Sentry instances enforce mTLS (client certificate validation) or sit behind Neurons for MDM gateway. Flag instances with direct external HTTPS access to management interfaces without intermediate authentication layer.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scan Hits
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner'; pipeline must surface vulnerable appliances. Criterion for remediation tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any Ivanti Sentry asset with CVE-2026-10520 unpatched status. Correlate with asset inventory to confirm due-date compliance (federal due 2026-06-14). Segment by deployment model: unmanaged + externally-reachable = critical risk.

suggestion.title: Externally-Reachable Ivanti Sentry Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Asset exposure is the prerequisite for this entire attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for inbound Internet-to-Sentry traffic on typical management ports (443, 8443, others). Correlate with asset ownership and mTLS/HTTPS mitigation status. Flag unmanaged or isolated Sentry appliances accepting external connections.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Ivanti Sentry Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated user' can exploit; pipeline must detect unauthenticated session establishment. This is the gateway condition for RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliance auth logs (if available) and WAF/perimeter logs for repeated unauthenticated requests to Sentry endpoints. Spike in 401/403 responses or session initiation without credentials is a leading indicator.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Execution
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is OS command injection (T1059); article does not detail attack vector but RCE implies shell metacharacters or system calls. Pipeline must detect command execution phase, not just access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliance process spawning for unexpected child processes (sh, bash, curl, wget, nc) or system calls with shell metacharacters. Look for processes spawned by Sentry service account with administrative intent (e.g., package installation, user creation, network config).

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Sentry Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'root-level remote code execution'; pipeline must detect privilege escalation from Sentry service context to root. This is the impact confirmation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes running as root that have parent or ancestry in the Sentry service tree (or spawned from Sentry-controlled file/socket). Correlate with process creation timestamps and command-line arguments suggesting post-exploitation activity (persistence, lateral movement, exfiltration).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Deployment Configuration Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article notes mTLS/HTTPS restrictions and EPMM/Neurons integration mitigate exposure. Pipeline should detect security-relevant config drift (unmanaged state, disabled mTLS) that increases attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Sentry deployment configs across fleet for: (1) unmanaged state flag, (2) mTLS disabled on external interfaces, (3) HTTPS access controls bypassed, (4) absence of EPMM/Neurons enrollment. Any deviation from hardened baseline = increased CVE-2026-10520 exploitability.

suggestion.title: External Ivanti Sentry Management Interface Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'endpoints externally reachable' and 'unmanaged state' — critical indicator. Exposed management ports are the attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound connections to Ivanti Sentry management ports (443, 8443, 9000) from external/untrusted IP space. Flag clusters of connection attempts from single source or impossible-travel patterns preceding successful authentication.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Command Injection Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability' — payload patterns will contain shell metacharacters (pipes, semicolons, command substitution).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints for command-injection indicators: $(command), backticks, pipe|, semicolon;, &&, ||. Correlate with 5xx errors or subsequent root-privilege process spawning.

suggestion.title: Sentry Service Root UID Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'root-level remote code execution' — post-exploitation behavior is child processes under root privilege from Sentry daemon.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell interpreters (bash, sh, perl, python) or suspicious binaries spawned as children of Ivanti Sentry processes with UID=0. Baseline legitimate children first.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated Access Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated user' — exploit works without credentials. Look for successful API/management access with no corresponding auth events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful HTTP responses (200, 302) to authenticated endpoints without prior login session or auth header. Repeat requests across discovery endpoints suggest automated exploitation.

suggestion.title: Sentry Reverse Shell or Bind Shell Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'root-level remote code execution' — attackers will establish interactive shells. Look for sh -i, nc reverse shells, nohup background persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect /bin/bash -i, /bin/sh -c 'bash -i', nc/socat spawned by Sentry with outbound network connections to attacker IPs. Flag parent=sentry service, unexpected child interpreters.

suggestion.title: Phishing email detection: AI brand impersonation lures
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states 'threat actors are using the AI hype in social engineering.' Pipeline failed to surface email-based detections for spoofed AI company branding, which is the primary attack vector described.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails claiming to be from OpenAI, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or other major AI services, especially those containing urgency keywords (verify account, confirm identity, unusual activity) or requesting credential submission. Cross-reference against legitimate sender domains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious redirect chain from AI-branded phishing links
suggestion.rationale: AiTM attacks require initial phishing link delivery. Article keywords include AiTM but pipeline missed detection for link-based credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect URL clicks on AI-branded phishing domains that redirect through intermediary proxy or redirect chain. Flag when user later authenticates to legitimate service from different IP than initial click or within minutes of suspicious link interaction.

suggestion.title: AiTM attack pattern: Credential submission followed by immediate re-authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article metadata explicitly keywords 'Adversary-in-the-middle' but pipeline produced no AiTM-specific detections. AiTM harvests credentials then proxies re-auth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate credential submission events (web form submission, API auth) from phishing proxy infrastructure with subsequent legitimate authentication from different source IP within 5–60 seconds. Flag when re-auth includes MFA bypass or unusual challenge response.

suggestion.title: Domain registration: AI company name typosquatting and homograph variants
suggestion.rationale: Social engineering campaigns leveraging AI brand hype require spoofed domains. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs despite this being primary observables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor new domain registrations using AI company names with typos (e.g. openai-verify.com, claude-confirm.us), homograph variants, or lookalike TLDs. Cross-reference WHOIS for suspicious registrant patterns, privacy masking, or bulk registrations.

suggestion.title: Forced authentication attack via spoofed OAuth/SSO redirect
suggestion.rationale: AiTM and social engineering tactics described in article likely include forced re-authentication through malicious OAuth flows. Pipeline missed forced-auth detection patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag OAuth/SSO redirect flows originating from untrusted domains or redirecting to non-standard ports. Correlate with suspicious certificate issuance for domains impersonating AI services or legitimate auth providers.

suggestion.title: Session token exfiltration: AiTM proxy capturing bearer tokens
suggestion.rationale: AiTM attacks capture session tokens, not just passwords. Pipeline produced no detection logic for token-based credential theft despite AiTM being explicitly mentioned in article metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for proof-of-concept AiTM proxy tools (mitmproxy, Evilginx2, etc.) running on user endpoints. Flag suspicious process executions spawning proxy listeners on loopback + outbound tunneling to attacker infrastructure. Correlate with simultaneous credential input events.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-10520 as the exploited vulnerability ('CVE-2026-10520 — Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection'). This is the primary indicator for vulnerability scanners and threat intel correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner detecting CVE-2026-10520 in Ivanti Sentry products. Flag unpatched instances for immediate action given CISA KEV status and observed wild exploitation (federal remediation due 2026-06-14).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Network Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Network exposure is the prerequisite for attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify externally-accessible Ivanti Sentry instances via port scans, passive DNS, and certificate transparency. Flag any management interfaces reachable from untrusted networks without mTLS or restricted HTTPS as deployed (article notes mTLS with EPMM or Neurons for MDM provides protection).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated OS Command Injection Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote unauthenticated user' achieving RCE through 'OS command injection vulnerability.' This is credential-free network exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry network-facing interfaces for unauthenticated requests followed by OS command execution. Detect shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, $(), backticks) in URLs, POST data, or headers sent to unprotected endpoints without prior authentication.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Network Source
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability achieves 'root-level remote code execution.' Process spawning at root privilege from network-initiated requests is the execution outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when root-level child processes are spawned by Ivanti Sentry daemon processes or when Sentry services spawn interactive shells at elevated privilege. Look for unexpected process lineage (Sentry service → /bin/bash → commands).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged Appliance State Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability only exploitable when appliance is in 'unmanaged state' (not enrolled in EPMM or Neurons for MDM). Configuration state directly correlates to exploitability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory to identify Ivanti Sentry appliances not enrolled in EPMM or Neurons for MDM. Cross-reference unmanaged instances with network exposure data to identify overlapping at-risk assets.

suggestion.title: Absent mTLS/Restricted HTTPS on Sentry Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article notes mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access 'makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Absence of these mitigations is a risk indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Ivanti Sentry interfaces configured without enforced mutual TLS or that accept cleartext HTTP. Monitor for certificate pinning bypass or absence of client-certificate validation on management endpoints.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'CVE-2026-10520' with 'Ivanti Sentry' affected. CISA KEV designation mandates detection of exploited-in-the-wild vulnerability in fleet inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner data for Ivanti Sentry appliances matching CVE-2026-10520. Cross-reference against CISA KEV remediation timeline (federal due date 2026-06-14). Escalate any unfixed instances immediately.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' This is the prerequisite for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry appliances with management interfaces (typically ports 443/8443) accessible from untrusted networks (WAN, internet-facing). Verify firewall rules are restricting access to known admin networks only.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' This is the core exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance logs for suspicious OS command execution, shell spawning, or unexpected process trees spawned from network-accessible services. Look for shell metacharacters or command chaining in request parameters.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Sentry Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' The vulnerability requires no authentication, making any request to management endpoints a potential attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry management endpoints (e.g., /sentry, /api/admin) without valid session tokens or authentication headers. Correlate with command injection payloads or unusual parameter encoding.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability achieves 'root-level remote code execution.' Any exploitation will spawn processes with root privileges—an abnormal state for application services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process execution with root/system privileges originating from Ivanti Sentry service accounts or network-reachable services. Cross-reference against known legitimate administrative tasks.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry external exposure hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Detection opportunity: identify any Sentry instance reachable from internet without mTLS/EPMM/restricted HTTPS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan external IP space for open Ivanti Sentry management ports; correlate against asset inventory. Look for instances missing mTLS/EPMM certificates or running in default-unmanaged mode. Flag any reachable appliance as exploitation risk.

suggestion.title: OS command injection payload detection (Ivanti Sentry)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability.' Search for malicious shell metacharacters, command substitution syntax, or encoded payloads in HTTP requests targeting Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for requests to Ivanti Sentry containing shell metacharacters (| ; ` $() && ||), command separators, or base64-encoded strings targeting known vulnerable endpoints. Baseline normal traffic first to avoid false positives on legitimate management calls.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry root-level process execution anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' is achievable. Detection opportunity: monitor for unexpected child processes spawned from Sentry service running as root/SYSTEM.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any process spawned by Sentry services (e.g., java, tomcat, node if applicable) running with elevated privileges (uid=0 or SYSTEM), especially shell interpreters (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell) or network utilities (curl, wget, nc). Establish baseline of expected child processes per version.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry state detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states risk is 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS mitigates. Look for Sentry instances without expected security controls configured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Sentry appliances for missing/disabled mTLS certificate validation, absence of EPMM enrollment, or HTTP (not HTTPS) management interface enabled. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-10520 exposure.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Externally Accessible
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes exploitation precondition: 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Asset exposure is the gate control for this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Ivanti Sentry or MobileIron Sentry appliances (product identifiers, banners, certificate CN) reachable on internet-facing IPs. Correlate asset inventory against firewall/cloud egress rules to identify exposed instances. High-priority given Federal due-date 2026-06-14.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly described as 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level RCE.' Attackers exploit via malformed input to application endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints (common paths: /api/*, /admin/*, /system/*) containing shell metacharacters (semicolon, pipe, ampersand, backticks, dollar-paren) or encoded command separators. Unauthenticated requests to these paths are suspicious baseline.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Privilege Escalation / Root Process on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation grants 'root-level remote code execution.' Post-compromise, detect unexpected processes running with root/system privileges on the appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation events on Ivanti Sentry appliances for new/anomalous processes spawned with UID 0 (root). Flag any process execution initiated from web service accounts with privilege escalation patterns. Cross-reference against golden baseline of expected root processes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Detection — Unpatched Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV mandates rapid patching; article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-14.' Vulnerability scanners are the first-line detection for asset risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any Ivanti Sentry appliance (identified by product name, version banner, authenticated scan fingerprint) with CVE-2026-10520 in unpatched state. Prioritize by criticality and external reachability. Due-date alert for 2026-06-14.

suggestion.title: Network Scanning / Service Enumeration Targeting Ivanti Sentry Ports
suggestion.rationale: Before exploitation, attacker must discover exposed Sentry instances. Article implies external reachability; network reconnaissance is the prerequisite step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound port scans or repeated connection attempts to ports commonly used by Ivanti Sentry (443/HTTPS for admin console typical; 8080 for APIs). Multiple failed connections from external IPs followed by successful connection warrant escalation.

suggestion.title: Detect phishing emails with AI-generated persona and linguistic anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'AI Phishing'—suggests LLM-crafted phishing with evasive language patterns. No UC generated despite this being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with uncommon n-gram patterns, high cosine similarity to known phishing templates, suspicious sender domain lookalikes (typosquatting, homograph variants), and urgent language markers. AI-generated phishing often exhibits statistical anomalies in syntax and semantic consistency compared to human-written campaigns.

suggestion.title: Detect alert storm amplification from phishing campaigns
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'crushing SOCs with alert volume'—implies attackers deliberately generate false-positive noise to mask real compromise activity. No defense-evasion UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate alert volume spikes (phishing batch sends, credential-stuffing attempts, or reconnaissance scans) with simultaneous real-threat activity (failed logins followed by successful privilege escalation, or web-shell uploads). Cluster alerts by source/campaign and flag when phishing alert ratio exceeds historical baseline.

suggestion.title: Detect suspicious browser password-manager events post-phishing delivery
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns often target credential capture. Article emphasizes 'crushing SOCs' implies post-compromise activity is missed. No credential-access UC despite implicit credential-theft vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious access to browser credential stores or password managers immediately following email phishing delivery (URL click, attachment open, or credential entry forms). Flag unusual calls to Chrome/Firefox password APIs, clipboard access for passwords, or automated form-fill events within 10 minutes of phishing detection.

suggestion.title: Detect forwarding rule creation post-phishing click
suggestion.rationale: Phishing commonly leads to account compromise and exfiltration via email forwarding. Article implies end-user compromise; no persistence/exfiltration UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbox rules or email forwarding additions within 2 hours of confirmed phishing click/credential entry. Correlate with new device sign-in, atypical login geography, or failed auth attempts. Alert on rules forwarding to external domains or hidden folders.

suggestion.title: Detect credential re-use across phishing and internal systems
suggestion.rationale: Article implies AI phishing targets SOC staff directly (or users with critical access). No lateral-movement or privilege-escalation UC for post-phishing pivot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful phishing (confirmed click + credential submission) with failed/successful logins to high-value systems (AD, cloud admin portals, SIEM) using the same account within 60 minutes. Alert on logins from new IPs immediately post-phishing delivery.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states Ivanti Sentry vulnerability and provides CVE identifier. Standard asset-exposure hunt required for CISA KEV entries: 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for hosts running Ivanti Sentry with CVE-2026-10520 signature. Prioritize appliances with external endpoint reachability and unmanaged state indicators. Federal remediation deadline 2026-06-14 creates urgency for patch-lag detection.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Endpoint Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is exploitable 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — core precondition for attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry management interfaces (standard ports) with inbound internet traffic. Flag unmanaged appliances (no mTLS certificate, HTTPS restrictions absent). Correlate with asset inventory to find misconfigured deployments.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attempt Against Sentry Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user' — specific exploitation method. Look for command injection payloads in HTTP request bodies/parameters targeting Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters, command substitution syntax ($(), backticks, pipes, semicolons), or encoded command payloads in query parameters and POST bodies. Flag unauthenticated requests (no valid session/certificate).

suggestion.title: Sentry Process Spawning Unexpected System Commands
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies RCE grants 'root-level remote code execution' — post-exploitation process execution should be detected. Sentry service account should not spawn shells or system utilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Sentry appliance processes (Java/backend processes) spawning /bin/bash, /bin/sh, cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or other shell interpreters. Flag command execution utilities (curl, wget, nc) spawned as children of Sentry. Baseline normal process trees first to eliminate false positives from legitimate admin tasks.

suggestion.title: mTLS Certificate Bypass or Restricted HTTPS Access Circumvention
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors' — implication is that absence of these controls enables exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Sentry management interface access without valid mTLS client certificate (missing certificate subject validation, untrusted CA, no mutual auth). Detect HTTP fallback attempts on management ports. Alert on direct IP access bypassing hostname-based restrictions.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exists only when 'appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' This is the prerequisite condition for exploitation and the primary hunt vector for at-risk assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry appliances (product identifier in banners, HTTP headers, SSL certificates) responding on standard ports (443, 8080) from external IP space. Cross-reference against asset inventory; flag instances not listed as intentionally internet-facing or protected by mTLS/EPMM.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attempts Against Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability.' This is the exploitation mechanism. Attackers inject shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `$(...)`, backticks) into request parameters to trigger unintended command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to identified Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters and command substitution syntax in query strings, POST bodies, and headers. Flag requests containing patterns like `; id;`, `| whoami`, `$(cat /etc/passwd)`, or backtick substitution.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution Successful
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Successful exploitation bypasses authentication entirely, so detection must rely on post-compromise behavioral signals rather than auth logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag execution of arbitrary commands originating from the Ivanti Sentry service process (or child processes spawned by it) without corresponding legitimate administrative activity. Focus on shell spawns, network connections, and privilege-escalation attempts.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Sentry Context
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies impact is 'root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation, attackers will execute commands with root privileges. This is an impact-phase signal distinct from initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation events where the parent is the Ivanti Sentry service or a child spawned from it, and the new process runs as root or SYSTEM. Baseline legitimate Sentry administrative activity; alert on anomalous commands (reverse shells, persistence tools, lateral-movement utilities).

suggestion.title: Sentry Appliance in Unmanaged State Configuration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly calls out vulnerability condition: 'when the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Unmanaged state is a configuration red flag distinguishing vulnerable from protected deployments (protected via mTLS or restricted HTTPS).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Sentry appliance configuration and enrollment status. Flag instances that are NOT enrolled in EPMM, NOT using mTLS, or NOT behind restricted HTTPS access controls. Cross-reference against approved unmanaged-state use cases; escalate all others.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Ivanti Sentry Command Injection Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline generated zero use cases for exploit detection despite this being a CISA KEV (actively exploited in the wild).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests targeting Ivanti Sentry endpoints with OS command injection payloads (backticks, $(), semicolons, pipes in query parameters or POST bodies). Baseline against known Sentry endpoints; flag unauthenticated access attempts.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Appliance External Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' No network-based asset exposure detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances externally reachable (public IP/domain) lacking mTLS enforcement or restricted HTTPS controls. Cross-reference with CVE-2026-10520 scanner data; flag unpatched + exposed appliances.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Root-Level Process Execution from Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation yields 'root-level remote code execution.' No detection for post-exploitation activity following command injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by Ivanti Sentry service accounts running with elevated/root privileges. Correlate process execution timeline with HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints from previous UC.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanning & Patch Status
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CISA KEV status ('currently being exploited') and federal patch due-date (2026-06-14). Standard vulnerability management detection missing entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for CVE-2026-10520 detections; prioritize unpatched Ivanti Sentry instances. Cross-check patch dates against 2026-06-14 deadline; escalate any systems past due-date or with pending patches.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Security Control Bypass (mTLS/Restricted HTTPS Absence)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes vulnerability mitigatable by 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM.' Absence of these controls indicates exploitability; no detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Ivanti Sentry appliances without mTLS enforcement or Neurons MDM integration. Identify instances accepting plain HTTP or unencrypted HTTPS without client certificate validation; correlate with external reachability.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PAM Module Replacement or Loading
suggestion.rationale: Core technique of Operation Highland. Article: 'replaced legitimate pam_unix.so modules with backdoored versions…Sygnia identified nine distinct variants.' This is the signature 10-year persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /lib/security and /lib64/security for unauthorized modifications to pam_unix.so or other PAM modules via file integrity monitoring, hash anomalies, or timestamp deviations. Alert on unexpected PAM module loading from non-standard paths or by non-root processes. Correlate auditd/SELinux logs for anomalous PAM library access outside business hours.

suggestion.title: Trojanized SSH Binary Execution with Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Secondary persistence layer. Article: 'replaced OpenSSH components such as ssh, sshd, and scp with trojanized versions that captured credentials, logged commands entered during SSH sessions.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for ssh/sshd/scp execution with anomalous command-line parameters, unexpected parent processes, or mismatched file hashes. Alert on SSH binaries executing from non-standard paths or spawning unexpected child processes. Correlate process hash changes with system modification timelines.

suggestion.title: Custom SOCKS5 Proxy Masquerading as SMB Daemon
suggestion.rationale: Internal pivot mechanism. Article: 'custom SOCKS5 proxy…ran as a daemon masquerading as smbd -D, using different filenames and ports on each host.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for processes with commandline 'smbd -D' from non-standard directories, mismatched process hashes, or unexpected listening ports. Monitor for SOCKS5 protocol traffic on internal networks. Cross-reference Samba process metadata against baseline SMB process signatures.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST to FastCGI Chain for Remote Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Bridge into air-gapped network. Article: 'modified Nginx server to proxy specially crafted requests to a compromised backend server…forwarded requests to a FastCGI process (fcgiwrap) listening on a separate port. The FastCGI wrapper acted as an execution bridge…launching a custom binary named uptime.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Nginx access logs for HTTP POST requests with ssh-like parameters or SSH connection parameters in request body. suggestion.title: GS-Netcat Reverse Shell Persistence via Systemd or Startup Script
suggestion.rationale: Initial foothold and persistence. Article: 'deployed a modified GS-Netcat reverse shell disguised as a legitimate system component that connected to a hardcoded relay domain…achieved persistence either via a malicious systemd service or through startup script modification.'

Alert on startup script modifications in /etc/rc.d or shell rc files (bashrc, profile, zshrc) containing reverse shell patterns. suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credential Backdoors in PAM Module Variants
suggestion.rationale: Persistence-independent access. Article: 'replaced legitimate pam_unix.so modules…that accept hardcoded passwords and harvest user credentials…nine distinct variants of the malicious PAM module, each compiled in a separate build environment.'

Alert on SSH or su authentication attempts with unusual password patterns. Correlate successful logins from unexpected source IPs with PAM module modification timelines.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Splunk Web Access to Admin Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Attackers Run Code Without Authentication'—this implies successful access to privileged endpoints (likely /en-US/app/ or /api/ paths) without valid session tokens. suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk web access logs for HTTP requests with POST/PUT/PATCH methods to sensitive paths (/en-US/app/, /api/auth/, /api/admin/) that originate from external IPs, lack valid session cookies (jsessionid=null or missing), and return HTTP 200 or 201. Correlate with rapid successive requests to multiple endpoints—hallmark of exploitation scanning.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code Execution via Splunk Custom Command/Alert Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Run Code Without Authentication'—post-exploit behavior likely involves injecting code into Splunk custom commands, saved searches, or alerts. suggestion.title: Exploitation Payloads in Splunk HTTP Request Logs

suggestion.title: Splunk Process Spawning Unexpected Child Processes

Flag if parent command line contains unusual arguments (inline encoding, obfuscated strings). Prioritize if parent process has low privilege context (NETWORK SERVICE) or unexpected user context.

suggestion.title: Detect One-Character File/Parameter Injection to Kernel Files

Flag any write operations of exactly 1-2 bytes or writes that modify privilege-related kernel parameters (capability bits, ns_user configs, etc.). suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for clicks/downloads of URLs impersonating WhatsApp login, recovery, or notification flows. Flag unconventional referrers (phishing emails/messages) to WhatsApp domains or lookalike domains. Correlate with failed login attempts within 5 minutes post-click.

suggestion.title: NSO Group Infrastructure Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies NSO Group as attacker; no command-and-control detection UCs generated despite NSO's known infrastructure patterns and previous attribution data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference outbound traffic against NSO-attributed IP ranges and C2 domains from threat feeds (Pegasus campaign infrastructure). Alert on traffic to regions/ASNs historically hosting NSO callback servers.

suggestion.title: Spearphishing Message with WhatsApp Theme
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is described as phishing; pipeline did not generate email/message-based detection UCs for WhatsApp impersonation templates despite being the attack entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with WhatsApp-impersonating subject lines (e.g., 'verify account', 'unusual login', 'confirm identity') and attachments or links pointing to phishing infrastructure. Flag sender-domain spoofing or lookalike domains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious WhatsApp Web / Desktop Login Spike
suggestion.rationale: Phishing goal is credential harvest; article implies victims may attempt WhatsApp login post-phishing. No credential-access detection UCs for unusual auth patterns on WhatsApp endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WhatsApp Web and Desktop login endpoints for rapid failed authentication attempts from compromised credentials. Alert on successful login from unusual geoip/device + failed login 5 minutes prior (indicates credential testing).

suggestion.title: NSO Pegasus-Related Exploit Traffic
suggestion.rationale: NSO's tool-set historically includes zero-day exploits; article omits technical details but pipeline should flag known Pegasus/NSO payload signatures and exploitation patterns as secondary detection layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Signature-based detection of known NSO Pegasus payload patterns (shellcode markers, exploit deliverables). Monitor for suspicious process spawns or memory injection post-WhatsApp interaction.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthorized External Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation requires 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — this is the critical prerequisite that should trigger immediate asset exposure hunting across firewall and network telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances (port 8443, characteristic cert fingerprints, Sentry banners in HTTP responses) accessible from untrusted external networks. Flag instances lacking mTLS termination or Neurons for MDM access control restrictions. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner data against network exposure logs.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection on Ivanti Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the exploitation mechanism — direct attack vector requiring signature-based or heuristic detection on HTTP request payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints (e.g., /api/*, /mobilecontrol/*, /services/*) containing shell metacharacters (semicolon, pipe, ampersand, backtick, command substitution) or base64/URL-encoded command patterns. Prioritize unauthenticated endpoints and POST requests.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root-Level Process Execution on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' — post-exploitation detection of privileged shell spawning on compromised appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution on Ivanti Sentry appliances with UID=0 (root) spawned from unexpected parent processes, particularly web server processes (httpd, tomcat, java) or from non-standard execution contexts. Correlate unexpected shell invocations (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, sh, cmd) with user=root.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry mTLS Protection Absence
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible' — absence of this compensating control is a critical configuration audit finding.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry HTTPS connections (port 8443 default) where ClientCertificate validation is absent or unenforced. Monitor for successful TLS handshakes to Sentry endpoints from external sources where mutual authentication was not required; indicates unprotected external surface.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Asset Exposure Hunt (CVE-2026-10520)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references asset-exposure hunt templates but pipeline generated zero use cases. Core hunt: identify Ivanti Sentry appliances, confirm patch status, validate external reachability against federal due date 2026-06-14.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry appliances and match against CVE-2026-10520 patch status. Correlate with network exposure scanning to identify externally reachable instances. Alert on unpatched systems exposed to internet.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Detection (CVE-2026-10520)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability exploitable only 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' This precondition-based detection was completely missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances where management agent is inactive or absent (unmanaged state) and simultaneously have externally routable addresses. This combination indicates immediate exploitation risk.

suggestion.title: Mitigation Control Gap - Missing mTLS/Restricted HTTPS (CVE-2026-10520)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Pipeline missed detecting appliances NOT protected by these controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Ivanti Sentry appliances for TLS mutual authentication and mTLS configuration. Verify firewall rules restrict HTTPS endpoints to authorized EPMM/MDM controllers only. Flag appliances missing both controls as requiring emergency hardening.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection - Ivanti Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' as attack vector but pipeline generated zero execution-phase detections. Need behavioral/signature detection for injection attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry unauthenticated endpoints for OS command injection metacharacters (;, |, &, `, $(), etc.). Alert on process spawning from Sentry service with unexpected privileges or shell invocations. Establish baseline of legitimate operations and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Root-level Process Execution from Ivanti Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'root-level remote code execution' as outcome but pipeline missed privilege escalation phase. Successful exploitation produces elevated process creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any process spawned by Ivanti Sentry service or child processes executing with root/SYSTEM privileges, especially shells, reverse shells, installers, or package managers. Establish baseline of normal Sentry operations and flag deviations as likely exploitation.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Attempts Against Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote unauthenticated user' can exploit. Pipeline missed detection for requests attempting to bypass authentication or access protected endpoints without credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor and alert on HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry management interfaces that lack authentication headers or bypass authentication checks. Track failed authentication attempts from external IP ranges to Sentry console/API endpoints. Establish baseline of legitimate admin traffic.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scan Hit — Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-10520 is the sole threat indicator in a CISA KEV entry flagged as actively exploited in the wild. Vulnerability scanner hits are the baseline hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner detection of CVE-2026-10520 against Ivanti Sentry/MobileIron Sentry instances. Cross-reference with patch status and appliance inventory to identify unpatched instances exposed externally. Federal due date 2026-06-14 is a strong temporal signal for post-deadline breach risk.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Appliance Network Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states exploitation occurs 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Scanning for this configuration is a direct hunt trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Sentry services (default ports, SSL certificate fingerprints) visible from the internet via network scanning, threat-intel feeds, or passive DNS. Correlate with asset inventory to flag unmanaged instances. Restrict external access via mTLS or firewall rules to reduce attack surface.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload — Sentry HTTP Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'OS command injection' allowing 'remote unauthenticated user' RCE. Payloads exploit HTTP/HTTPS request parameters on exposed interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, $, backticks, $()), command-substitution syntax, or OS-specific command injection patterns in HTTP POST/GET parameters sent to Sentry endpoints. Flag any successful responses (200 OK) paired with injection attempts. Look for encoded variants (URL encoding, double-encoding, Unicode escapes).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Root-Level Code Execution — Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation yields 'root-level remote code execution.' Detection of arbitrary commands executing as root on Sentry instances is the impact signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliance process logs, system audit logs, or endpoint detection for unexpected child process spawning under root context. Flag anomalous binaries (sh, bash, curl, nc, whoami, id) executed as uid=0 outside normal administrative activities. Correlate timing with external HTTP requests to Sentry services.

suggestion.title: mTLS Bypass or Restricted HTTPS Circumvention Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article notes mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access mitigates exposure. Detection of attempts to bypass these protections is a defensive posture hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on TLS handshake failures with certificate validation errors, invalid mTLS client certs, or SSL/TLS downgrade attempts targeting Sentry endpoints. Flag proxied or tunneled traffic that bypasses mTLS enforcement. Monitor for HTTP→HTTPS downgrade or unencrypted Sentry API calls.

suggestion.title: Sentry Appliance State Configuration — Managed vs. Unmanaged Drift
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation risk is contingent on 'unmanaged state.' Continuous configuration monitoring to ensure appliances remain in secure (managed) state is a preventive hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any configuration change that transitions a Sentry appliance from managed to unmanaged state, or any removal of MDM/EPMM enrollment without authorization. Cross-reference with network-exposure signals to identify appliances at high risk. Enforce baseline configuration as code and flag drift.

suggestion.title: Asset-Exposure Hunt: Ivanti Sentry External Reachability
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Must inventory exposed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances reachable from untrusted networks on standard administrative HTTPS ports. Cross-reference against MDM enrollment (Neurons for MDM, EPMM) and mTLS certificate stores. Flag unmanaged instances as high-risk for this CVE.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Execution-phase detection for injection attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry API endpoints for command-injection metacharacters in parameters (backticks, `$()`, pipe, semicolon, `&&`, `||`). Match against known CVE-2026-10520 exploit signatures.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation: Unexpected Root Process Spawning from Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' Must detect child processes spawned as root from Sentry daemon after successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal Sentry process activity; alert on spawning of shells, interpreters, or system utilities (bash, sh, perl, python) as children of Sentry with EUID=0. Exclude patched/upgrade maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Patch Verification: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerable Sentry Versions Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and sets federal patch deadline 2026-06-14. Critical to verify patched vs. vulnerable inventory post-deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management system for Ivanti Sentry appliances. Extract version numbers and cross-reference against CVE-2026-10520 affected versions. Flag any non-compliant (unpatched) instance found after 2026-06-14 for escalation.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Sentry Appliance Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article distinguishes vulnerable condition 'in an unmanaged state' from protected state 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM.' Must identify Sentry instances not enrolled in enterprise protections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Ivanti Sentry asset inventory against MDM enrollment records and mTLS certificate repository. Flag any Sentry appliance lacking active enrollment, mTLS authentication, or network-level access controls as unmanaged and at-risk.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Hunting: System Persistence Indicators from Sentry RCE
suggestion.rationale: Upon achieving root RCE ('root-level remote code execution'), attacker can establish persistence. Hunt for suspicious system-level changes within 24–48 hours of exploitation window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for file writes to /etc, /root, cron directories, or sudoers originating from Sentry process context. Look for creation of system services, cron jobs, or user accounts in temporal proximity to exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline produced zero use cases despite this direct instruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match patch status and asset inventory against CVE-2026-10520. Flag any Ivanti Sentry appliance instances (via SHODAN, passive DNS, or asset DB) lacking patches dated ≥2026-06-14. Cross-reference with network exposure scans.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Accessibility Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation requires 'endpoints externally reachable' and conditions under which 'interfaces are inaccessible' (mTLS, restricted HTTPS). Detection gap: asset-exposure hunt for Sentry appliances visible from untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Sentry appliances on public-facing ports (default HTTPS, management ports) without mTLS or IP-restriction controls. Correlate external accessibility with patch status per CVE-2026-10520 timeline.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline missed behavioral detection for injection payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry application logs and HTTP access logs for command-injection syntax (backticks, $(), semicolons, pipes) in request parameters. Flag unauthenticated requests with shell metacharacters to known-vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Execution from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation yields 'root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline omitted post-exploitation behavioral detection despite clear impact statement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation events with parent = Sentry service (e.g., sentry-daemon) spawning unexpected shells, scripting interpreters, or reconnaissance tools. Baseline should exclude legitimate Sentry plugin/update processes.

suggestion.title: Sentry Unmanaged-State Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article restricts exploitability to 'cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Detection gap: identify and flag appliances not enrolled in EPMM/Neurons management plane.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Sentry fleet inventory for appliances with management_status != 'enrolled' or epmm_registration == null. Cross-correlate with external accessibility and patch status.

suggestion.title: Sentry Exploitation Attempt Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article documents active exploitation in wild (CISA KEV status). Pipeline missed behavioral pattern for attack probes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences: (unauthenticated request) → (injection payload) → (HTTP 200 or 500 with banner/error data revealing version). Multiple attempts across fleet suggest reconnaissance or exploitation sweep.

suggestion.title: Exposed Ivanti Sentry Management Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — external exposure is the attack prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for externally accessible Ivanti Sentry management interfaces via certificate analysis, network scanning, or Shodan. Alert on appliances responding to HTTPS on typical Sentry ports (8443, 9443) from untrusted networks without mTLS/EPMM protection.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payloads to Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly 'OS command injection' enabling 'root-level remote code execution' — exploitation requires injected shell metacharacters in request parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry API/web logs for payloads containing shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), pipe, semicolon, ampersand) in request parameters. Correlate with unauthenticated access attempts. Flag common injection patterns: `/bin/sh`, backtick substitution, command chaining.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Sentry Appliance Configuration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability only exploitable on 'unmanaged state' instances; 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM' are protective. Configuration state is attack enabler.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry appliances against MDM enrollment and EPMM/Neurons enrollment records. Alert on appliances marked unmanaged or lacking mTLS certificate pinning and restricted access controls.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Sentry Administrative Functions
suggestion.rationale: Attack is explicitly 'remote unauthenticated' — authentication bypass or pre-auth RCE is the attack vector. Article emphasizes no credentials required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry administrative endpoints for successful HTTP responses (200/302) from external IPs without prior authentication. Flag anomalies in access patterns to protected endpoints from unauthenticated callers.

suggestion.title: Root-Privilege Process Execution from Sentry RCE
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation yields 'root-level remote code execution' — post-exploitation behavior includes privileged command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Sentry appliances, monitor for root/system-privilege process spawning from web service contexts (Tomcat, Java, nginx). Flag unexpected root shells or system utilities (bash, sh, curl, wget) executed by application processes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Presence in Vulnerability Scans
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal remediation deadline 2026-06-14 — baseline vulnerability scan detection is canonical check.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management for CVE-2026-10520 detections on all Ivanti Sentry appliances. Cross-reference patch version against Ivanti security advisories. Escalate any unpatched instances as active-exploitation risk.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Public Asset Exposure Detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry appliances (HTTPS, port 443, identifiable via certificate or HTTP banner) reachable from untrusted networks without mTLS or IP-layer access controls. Cross-reference against MDM enrollment logs to identify unmanaged instances.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Command Injection Exploit Attempt

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Post-Exploitation Root Process Activity

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on anomalous process spawning from Ivanti Sentry web service worker processes running as root, or unexpected child processes of Sentry system services. Flag outbound network connections (C2, data exfil) initiated from root-owned Sentry processes.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated Admin Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated user'—the vulnerability requires zero credentials; any successful admin/API access without prior authentication is exploitation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry web interface for successful administrative or API endpoint access without preceding authentication events. Flag requests missing authorization headers or with forged session tokens accessing normally-protected endpoints.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Match

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trigger on vulnerability scanner detections of CVE-2026-10520 matched against Ivanti Sentry product instances. Correlate with patch-compliance timelines and prioritize remediation for externally-reachable appliances in unmanaged states.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Appliance Exposed to External Access

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect internet-facing Ivanti Sentry instances on default ports (8443/TCP) via SSL certificate parsing, port enumeration, and vulnerability scanner asset tagging. Flag appliances with unmanaged status, default configurations, or missing security zone enforcement.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Requests to Ivanti Sentry Management Endpoints

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Patterns in Ivanti Sentry Request Payloads

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution Following Ivanti Sentry Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline omitted privilege escalation phase and post-exploitation process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliances for root-level shell spawning (bash, sh, zsh) or privileged system commands (useradd, setuid, iptables) initiated from management daemon/servlet processes. Correlate with successful command-injection web logs (same source IP, millisecond-level timestamps).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Detection Coverage
suggestion.rationale: Article references scanner checks for CVE and federal patch due-date (2026-06-14) as mandatory compliance check. Pipeline ignored vulnerability management use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output for Ivanti Sentry instances flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2026-10520. Cross-check patch application dates against 2026-06-14 federal deadline. Alert on unknown versions, unscanned appliances, or scanner detection failures.

suggestion.title: mTLS/HTTPS Security Configuration Weakening on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Use of mTLS...makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Pipeline should detect configuration changes that disable this protection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests (non-HTTPS) to Ivanti Sentry endpoints, configuration drift events disabling mTLS requirements, SSL/TLS downgrade attempts, or certificate pinning bypasses. Flag Sentry instances where mTLS enforcement was previously enabled then disabled.

suggestion.title: Phishing email impersonating AI service brand

Flag emails with urgency language ('verify account', 'confirm identity') and links to non-official login pages. Correlate with subsequent credential submission events.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sign-ins from IPs geographically impossible relative to prior activity, followed by legitimate service access. Flag cases where MFA token is obtained but user reports no login attempt. Detect proxy HTTPS interception indicators (certificate issuer mismatch, self-signed certs on encrypted endpoints).

suggestion.title: Suspicious OAuth/MFA token exchange during AI service registration
suggestion.rationale: Social engineering targeting 'AI hype' likely includes fake AI service signup flows that request OAuth permissions or MFA registration—attackers harvest session cookies and refresh tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect OAuth token requests from newly-registered AI impersonator domains. Flag cases where tokens are issued but access is not used immediately (token theft for later replay). Monitor for consent grants to suspicious OAuth apps with AI brand names.

suggestion.title: Account takeover via credential re-use after AI phishing

Flag bulk email forwarding rules, inbox rules, or permission grants set immediately post-compromise. Cross-reference compromised credential indicators with downstream account access.

suggestion.title: AI brand domain reputation monitoring and typosquatting
