suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ensure all Sentry instances appear in vulnerability scanner results. Alert on instances still reporting CVE-2026-10520 as unpatched post-deadline. Cross-reference with CMDB for orphaned/legacy systems.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Product Inventory Sweep
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries require baseline asset visibility. Detect the vulnerable product across the fleet independent of exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan network and query asset management systems for any Ivanti Sentry instances (legacy MobileIron Sentry rebranding included). Map to network zones and external connectivity status.

suggestion.title: Known Vulnerable Sentry Appliance Detected (CVE-2026-10520)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE: CVE-2026-10520' as recommended hunt. CISA KEV only includes actively exploited vulnerabilities. Vulnerability scanner must detect and alert on this CVE as highest priority.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any scan result or inventory entry showing Ivanti Sentry with CVE-2026-10520 or version prior to patch date 2026-06-14. Prioritize assets with external reachability flag (article specifies exploitation requires externally reachable endpoint).

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload in Sentry HTTP Request
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Command injection payloads (shell metacharacters: `;`, `|`, `$()`, backticks) are detectable in HTTP request logs to Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints for command injection metacharacters. Baseline legitimate requests should not contain shell syntax. Alert on POST/GET parameters containing backticks, semicolons, pipes, or `$()` substitution targeting Sentry API or management interface.

suggestion.title: Sentry Appliance Without mTLS or Neurons MDM Protection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable. The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible.' Unprotected exposed instances are the sole target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Sentry appliances and classify by protection level: (1) mTLS + EPMM enforcement present = low risk; (2) Neurons for MDM restriction active = low risk; (3) neither = high risk. Alert on any appliance in category 3 with public/external IP routing.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root-Level Process Execution from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'root-level remote code execution' is the outcome of successful exploitation. Suspicious child processes spawned from Sentry service context with root privileges indicate successful RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Sentry appliances, baseline the normal process tree from Sentry parent process (e.g., Java daemon). Alert on: (1) unexpected shell spawning from Sentry context, (2) network utilities (curl, wget, nc) launched as children, (3) file writes to system directories (/etc, /bin, /usr/bin), (4) network connections initiated from Sentry process context.

suggestion.title: External Connection Attempts to Sentry Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is exploitable only 'where the Sentry appliance is...externally reachable.' Baseline legitimate access and alert on external sources probing or accessing admin interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound TCP connections to Sentry management ports (typically 443 for HTTPS, verify product docs) from external/non-corporate IP ranges. Establish baseline of legitimate access sources (corporate VPN, MDM servers, internal networks). Alert on: international IPs, VPS/hosting providers, mass scanning patterns (multiple connection attempts in short window).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Email Volume Spike from Single Sender or Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'AI Phishing Is Crushing SOCs with Alert Volume'—bulk phishing campaigns are the stated threat driver. Pipeline missed high-volume phishing delivery detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails from single sender/domain domain exceeding org baseline in 1-hour window. Correlate with user-reported phishing complaints and failed security training validation. Flag if recipient count > 50 and sender external.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with Malicious URL or Credential-Harvesting Landing Page
suggestion.rationale: Phishing is explicitly the attack vector; articles discussing phishing at scale must include URL-based credential theft (T1598.003, T1598.004).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails with shortened URLs, lookalike domains (homoglyph, typosquatting), or known credential-harvesting landing pages. Correlate with user clicks and failed logins from harvested credentials.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Phishing Email Characteristics (Linguistic Anomalies)
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifically names 'AI Phishing'—implies LLM-crafted emails. Pipeline should flag linguistic markers: unusual punctuation, formal register inconsistent with sender, absence of personal info despite claim of urgency, or template patterns common to ChatGPT/Claude output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest email body text; apply NLP model trained on ChatGPT-generated phishing samples to detect LLM linguistic patterns (e.g., overly formal closing, salutation inconsistency, lack of typos in long-form body). Alert if confidence > 0.75 and recipient is non-technical user.

suggestion.title: Email Impersonation via Domain Lookalike or Subdomain Spoofing
suggestion.rationale: Standard phishing enabler. Article context (SOC alert volume) implies widespread email-borne threats; subdomain spoofing (mail.example.cn vs. mail.example.com) is a common AI-phishing technique to evade basic DMARC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor emails from domains with Levenshtein distance < 2 from known internal or trusted-partner domains. Alert if DMARC/SPF/DKIM validation fails yet email bypasses gateway. Escalate if multiple recipients from same sender domain variant.

suggestion.title: Credential Re-use Post-Phishing (Impossible Travel + Failed Auth Spike)
suggestion.rationale: If phishing succeeds, compromised credentials will be used. Article context (SOC overload) implies need for downstream validation: detect stolen creds before breach deepens. Pipeline missed post-phishing lateral move/auth indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track failed authentication attempts immediately after phishing email send. Correlate impossible-travel scenarios (email opened in US, login attempt 2 minutes later from China). Alert if cred re-use from new device/location within 30min of phishing click.

suggestion.title: User Reported Phishing and Macro/Attachment Detonation Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article frames Tier 1 analyst burden; many phishing emails carry malicious attachments. Pipeline missed detection of attachment-based delivery (T1598.004) and should tie manual reporting to sandbox/YARA signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: When user reports phishing via security button, auto-detonate attachment in isolated sandbox. Alert if macro execution detected, suspicious child processes spawned, or file hash matches known-malware DB. Auto-block sender domain org-wide if detonation confirms malware.

suggestion.title: Exploit CVE-2026-10520: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline produced zero use cases despite T1190 being explicitly applicable (KEV implies active exploitation).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/GET requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints (typically /services or /api paths) containing shell metacharacters or command injection payloads (;, |, &, `, $(), backticks) from untrusted sources. Flag patterns like `; whoami`, `/bin/sh`, or `cmd.exe` in URI query parameters or request bodies targeting unpatched Sentry instances.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Appliance Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Pipeline missed asset-discovery detection logic for unprotected Sentry instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Ivanti Sentry appliances (identify by service banner on TCP 443/8443 or HTTP headers containing 'Sentry') that lack evidence of mTLS/EPMM enforcement or are reachable from untrusted network segments. Cross-reference with asset database to identify management state.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Code Execution Post-CVE-2026-10520
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline missed execution-phase detection for post-compromise command execution on Sentry appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry appliances, detect process execution events spawned by web service user (root/admin context) with unexpected shell invocations (/bin/sh, /bin/bash, cmd.exe) or suspicious network connections immediately following HTTP request ingestion from external IPs.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Vulnerability Scanner Signature
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends vulnerability scanning for CVE-2026-10520 as canonical detection. Pipeline listed CVE but produced no scanner-based UC (contradicts its own template reference).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Ivanti Sentry appliances running vulnerable versions (pre-patch versions after 2026-06-14 cutoff). Match against known fingerprints (service banners, X-Powered-By headers, default credential endpoints).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated Interface Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated user' can exploit this. Pipeline missed detection for authentication bypass or unauthenticated endpoint access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry logs for HTTP requests that bypass authentication (HTTP 200/302 responses without valid session tokens to admin endpoints like /console, /api/v1/config) or successful responses to endpoints that should require authentication.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — external reachability is the exploitation prerequisite
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vulnerability scanning and network telemetry for Ivanti Sentry management interfaces accessible from untrusted networks. Alert on exposed Sentry endpoints and positive CVE-2026-10520 scanner detections with external routing.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Command Execution from Ivanti Sentry Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow...root-level remote code execution' — post-exploitation execution indicator
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected shell commands, script execution, or process spawning from Ivanti Sentry service accounts, particularly those executing with elevated/root privileges. Flag anomalous process trees originating from Sentry components.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Patch Compliance Before Federal Due Date
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-14' and CISA KEV indicates active wild exploitation — patch lag is the primary risk vector
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management and vulnerability scanning systems for Ivanti Sentry instances. Flag any system with CVE-2026-10520 unpatched or external network exposure detected before federal remediation deadline.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state' — configuration control gap
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference asset inventory against EPMM/MDM enrollment records to identify Ivanti Sentry appliances not enrolled in proper management frameworks. Alert on unmanaged instances with external network routing.

suggestion.title: Absent or Misconfigured Sentry mTLS/HTTPS Restrictions
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access...makes interfaces inaccessible' — absence is vulnerability condition
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry admin interface access for non-mTLS, non-HTTPS, or unrestricted access patterns. Alert on plaintext or improperly authenticated connections to Sentry management endpoints.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — this is the primary precondition for exploitation. Pipeline missed the asset-exposure hunt entirely despite article referencing standard templates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for inbound traffic to known Sentry ports (typically 8443, 8080) from external IP ranges. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify Sentry instances lacking mTLS or EPMM integration. Flag Sentry appliances with internet-routable IPs or missing restrictive network ACLs.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection in Sentry HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' exploited via 'remote unauthenticated' access — pipeline should detect command injection patterns in HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Sentry for command injection indicators: backticks, $(), command substitution, semicolons followed by system commands, pipe chains, or shell metacharacters in parameter values. Correlate with Sentry version to confirm CVE-2026-10520 applicability.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Spawning from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'could allow root-level remote code execution' — pipeline missed detection of elevated privilege execution spawned from compromised Sentry process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by Sentry (sentry.exe, java if JVM-based) with SYSTEM/root privileges. Baseline normal Sentry behavior; flag deviations like command shells, PowerShell, bash, or unexpected binary execution from Sentry service context.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Sentry Appliance Identification via Configuration Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state' — configuration-based detection pipeline completely omitted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Sentry admin console or configuration files for management state. Flag instances without mTLS enforcement, without EPMM integration, or with default/missing authentication. Cross-check CMDB to identify which unmanaged instances are internet-exposed.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Network Activity from Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: After achieving root RCE via CVE-2026-10520, attackers typically establish C2 or move laterally — pipeline should generate UC for post-compromise behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from Sentry appliance IP to unusual destinations (non-vendor IPs, known C2, high-risk ASNs). Alert on unexpected protocols/ports, especially SSH/RDP from Sentry to internal hosts (lateral movement). Correlate with exploitation timeline.

suggestion.title: PAM Module Replacement Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'attackers replaced legitimate pam_unix.so modules with backdoored versions' with 'nine distinct variants of the malicious PAM module' compiled separately. Zero detection for authentication stack modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized modifications to /lib*/pam_unix.so and /usr/lib*/pam_unix.so. Alert on file timestamp anomalies, unexpected compilation dates, or hash mismatches against known good versions. Correlate PAM library writes with sshd/sudo process restarts or unexpected auth behavior patterns.

suggestion.title: OpenSSH Binary Trojanization
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'replaced OpenSSH components such as ssh, sshd, and scp with trojanized versions that captured credentials, logged commands entered during SSH sessions.' No detection rule generated for OpenSSH binary replacement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect writes to /usr/bin/ssh, /usr/sbin/sshd, /usr/bin/scp outside normal package managers. Monitor compile timestamps of SSH binaries for anomalies versus OS patching schedules. Alert on sshd processes that exhibit unusual child process spawning or file write patterns (credential logging).

suggestion.title: Nginx Proxy Chain to Remote Execution Bridge
suggestion.rationale: Article describes critical technique: 'modified the configuration of a compromised internet-facing Nginx server to proxy specially crafted requests to a compromised backend server' whose Nginx then 'forward requests to a FastCGI process (fcgiwrap)' which 'launched a custom binary named uptime' to establish SSH into isolated network. This multi-stage proxy-to-execution chain for air-gap penetration completely absent from detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor nginx.conf and included configs for unexpected proxy_pass directives, especially chains targeting FastCGI backends on non-standard ports. Alert on fcgiwrap process spawning with custom binary execution (non-standard .so loading). Correlate HTTP POST traffic containing SSH parameters with subsequent SSH connection initiations from web server UIDs.

suggestion.title: SOCKS5 Proxy Masquerading as SMB Daemon
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'custom SOCKS5 proxy for network traffic tunneling' that 'ran as a daemon masquerading as smbd -D, using different filenames and ports on each host, turning compromised servers into internal pivot points.' No detection for this lateral-movement infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on smbd processes with command lines containing only '-D' flag or unusual arguments. Monitor smbd listening on high-numbered ports (>10000) inconsistent with SMB/CIFS. Detect smbd spawning network connections to non-Samba-standard destinations. Flag file system activity from smbd that doesn't match share definitions.

suggestion.title: GS-Netcat Reverse Shell with Systemd Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article states initial compromise deployed 'modified GS-Netcat reverse shell disguised as a legitimate system component' with 'persistence either via a malicious systemd service or through startup script modification.' No detection for modified reverse shells or their persistence mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GS-Netcat process creation using signature-based matching on known reverse shell indicators. Monitor /etc/systemd/system/ and /usr/lib/systemd/system/ for new service files created outside package manager. Alert on systemd services with ExecStart lines containing network tools (nc, ncat, bash -i, /dev/tcp). Monitor /etc/rc.local and /etc/init.d/ for injected network connection commands.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credential Acceptance and Auth Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'replaced legitimate pam_unix.so modules with backdoored versions that accept hardcoded passwords' enabling auth bypass where 'administrative activity became fully observable: every login; every command executed.' No detection for authentication flow manipulation or hardcoded credential acceptance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor authentication logs for successful logins immediately following multiple failed attempts on same account (hardcoded password acceptance after failures). Detect rapid-fire auth events with mixed success/failure patterns inconsistent with user behavior. Alert on command execution from accounts without corresponding interactive login events in auth logs. Flag sessions where user commands appear in logs but login/logout events are missing.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Splunk REST API Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'code execution without authentication' — core attack vector is bypassing auth. Detection must flag REST API calls (e.g., /services/*, /api/*) lacking valid auth headers or using malformed credentials to Splunk listener ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Splunk service endpoints with missing Authorization header or HTTP 401 response, followed within 60 seconds by successful HTTP 200 request from same source IP to a privileged endpoint (e.g., /api/server/info, /api/apps/local).

suggestion.title: Child Process Execution Under Splunkd
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerability allows arbitrary code execution — must detect anomalous child processes spawned by splunkd.exe or Splunk Python/search processes outside normal search operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spawning of shell interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh) or system utilities (whoami, ipconfig, curl) as children of splunkd.exe, python.exe (under Splunk), or splunk.exe. Exclude known scheduled searches and admin operations via whitelist.

suggestion.title: Unusual External Inbound Connection to Splunk Service Ports
suggestion.rationale: Critical RCE vulnerability will be actively exploited from external sources — detect external traffic to Splunk listener ports (8089, 8000, 9997) from non-baseline IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound connections from external IPs to ports 8089 (Splunk indexer), 8000 (web UI), or 9997 (indexer peer) that are not in approved vendor/partner ranges. Correlate with HTTP GET/POST requests containing encoded payloads or shell syntax.

suggestion.title: Splunk Search Query Injection with OS Command Syntax
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation path likely involves injecting OS commands into search fields or API parameters — detect payloads containing shell metacharacters or command substitution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify search queries or REST API body payloads containing backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons, or common OS commands (cat, ls, whoami, curl, wget) passed to Splunk search endpoints. Alert especially on unauthenticated requests.

suggestion.title: Rapid Succession of Failed Auth + Successful Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Exploit workflow is: probe unauthenticated endpoint (fail), trigger RCE payload (succeed) — detection correlates auth failure/bypass with subsequent process or network anomaly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP 401 responses to Splunk endpoints from a single source within 10 seconds of that source triggering DeviceProcessEvents (child process spawn) or DeviceNetworkEvents (outbound connection). Short time delta suggests automated exploit delivery.

suggestion.title: Linux Kernel Exploit Execution Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'One-Character Linux Kernel Flaw Enables Local Root Access' and 'Exploits Now Public'—pipeline must detect syscall patterns, kernel error messages, or process exits indicative of kernel exploit triggering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal syscalls (prctl, ioctl, mmap, userfaultfd) from low-privileged processes, kernel warnings/panics, or Oops messages. Correlate with process privilege escalation (uid 0 acquisition). High fidelity for public kernel exploits targeting known flaws.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root Process Spawning from User Context
suggestion.rationale: 'Enables Local Root Access' is the attack outcome; detection should alert on processes gaining root UID without sudo/su authorization or credential use.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes where getuid() != 0 initially but child processes run with uid 0, or where EUID changes from non-zero to zero without setuid binary execution or PAM/sudo audit trails. Watch for kernel-stack-based privilege escalation patterns.

suggestion.title: Kernel Module Anomalies Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Kernel-level exploits may load unsigned modules or manipulate kernel memory; article confirms kernel as attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for insmod/modprobe calls, unsigned module loads, or anomalous entries in /sys/modules. Cross-reference with failed kernel signature verification events. High confidence indicator of post-exploitation persistence.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Kernel Memory Corruption Indicators
suggestion.rationale: 'One-character' flaw suggests memory safety issue (off-by-one, buffer overflow, logic error) typical of CVEs like userfaultfd, DirtyCOW variants, or stack corruption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect segmentation faults, stack canary violations, heap corruption warnings, or CPU exceptions (SIGSEGV, SIGABRT) immediately preceding privilege escalation. Kernel logs should show address-space layout violations. Time-window correlation: crash → root spawn within <5s.

suggestion.title: Known Kernel Exploit Payload/IOC Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Exploits Now Public'; detection must include file hashes, process command-line signatures, or network IOCs of public PoC tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of known kernel exploit PoCs (CVE-XXXX-XXXXX tools, e.g., public GitHub PoC repos); detect file writes to /tmp or /dev/shm followed by chmod +x and immediate execution. Hash-based detection of published exploit binaries.

suggestion.title: Typo-Squatted Go Package Download Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies the attack vector: 'The malicious Go Module Mirror's was named github.com/botdb-go/bolt, similar to the original one i.e. github.com/boltdb/bolt' — similarity-based package detection is the primary control for this threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor go get, go mod, and go.mod parsing for package names at small edit distance from known legitimate packages (e.g., boltdb→botdb-go). Alert on first-time resolution of lookalike variants, especially from non-canonical mirrors or with unsigned checksums.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Command & Control Communication from Go Application
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'This backdoor allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands' — outbound C2 callbacks from the backdoored module are observable kill-chain evidence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected HTTP/HTTPS callbacks from Go binaries to external non-organizational domains, particularly POST requests with command-like payloads, or keepalive patterns consistent with remote code injection awaiting instructions.

suggestion.title: Malicious Module Persistence via Package Cache Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article details the persistence mechanism: 'Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in, and that cached the backdored module' — the cache served the malicious version for 3+ years after the original was reverted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go module cache directories ($GOPATH/pkg/mod) for versions cached before a known removal date but accessed long after discovery. Flag timestamp inconsistencies where module metadata differs between local cache and canonical Go Proxy.

suggestion.title: Dependency Version Update to Unvetted or Suspicious Package
suggestion.rationale: Article observes: 'we now wish to update our systems to the latest dependencies, which led developers to update the version that stayed in the system for 3 years' — routine dependency bumps re-activated dormant malicious code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag go mod tidy or go get upgrade operations that pull versions not present in your baseline supply-chain graph, lack cryptographic signatures from known maintainers, or introduce packages with newly-created GitHub accounts/repos.

suggestion.title: Lookalike Package Mirror or Alternative Resolver Detection
suggestion.rationale: The typo-squatted name github.com/botdb-go/bolt vs github.com/boltdb/bolt demonstrates supply-chain misdirection. Article explains the mechanism: 'They hope people will mistakenly download and install these dangerous versions instead of the legitimate software'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go build/module operations for resolver mismatches: go get commands where the canonical package (e.g., boltdb/bolt) is overshadowed by a near-homograph alternative (botdb-go/bolt), or where GOPROXY environment variable points to non-standard registries.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Unpatched Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Standard asset-exposure hunt against vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-10520.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Ivanti Sentry instances flagged with CVE-2026-10520, cross-reference patch status. Flag unpatched and externally reachable assets as critical. Compare against EPMM/MDM console to identify unmanaged instances.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the exploitation method. Application logs and HTTP access logs should be monitored for command injection patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry HTTP endpoints for shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&&`, backticks, `$()`, `%(...)s`) in request parameters. Correlation with HTTP 200 responses to error responses indicates successful vs. failed injection attempts.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability exploitable when appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Unmanaged state removes protective mTLS and firewall restrictions. Detection should identify Sentry appliances not reporting to EPMM/Neurons console.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query EPMM/Neurons management console for Sentry appliances with stale heartbeats or marked unmanaged. Identify network interfaces lacking mTLS enforcement. Flag as exploitable without remediation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Root-Level Process Spawning from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation grants 'root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation detection should identify unexpected shell or command execution process spawning under Sentry service principal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry service process (typically privileged user/group) for unexpected child processes: /bin/bash, /bin/sh, cmd.exe, powershell.exe spawned as root or SYSTEM. High-fidelity post-compromise indicator.

suggestion.title: Sentry Interface Accessible Without mTLS Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access...makes interfaces inaccessible.' Absence of mTLS or firewall restrictions on management interfaces is a precondition for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Ivanti Sentry management ports (443, 8443) for absence of mutual TLS. Cross-reference certificate inventory for Sentry instances without enforced mTLS on EPMM/Neurons connections. Identify appliances reachable from external networks without firewall restriction.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Internet Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' This is the canonical first-line detection—identify all Sentry instances exposed to untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry/MobileIron instances accessible from internet (port 8443, HTTP User-Agent, known URI paths). Correlate with asset inventory to flag unmanaged or unpatched instances. Alert if mTLS/restricted HTTPS fronting is not in place (per article: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access...makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors').

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection in HTTP Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly 'OS command injection'—payload delivery via HTTP requests containing shell metacharacters. Article does not provide exact parameter names but standard injection markers (;, |, &&, ||, backtick, $()) will be present in exploit attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints with shell metacharacters in query parameters or POST body: semicolons, pipes, logical operators (&&, ||), backticks, command substitution ($(...)), or newline injection attempts. Baseline Sentry's legitimate traffic (MDM enrollment, device sync) to filter benign requests.

suggestion.title: Root-Privilege Process Spawning from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'root-level remote code execution'—successful exploitation will spawn arbitrary processes running as root/SYSTEM from Sentry service context. This is the privilege-escalation hallmark of the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation where parent is Sentry/MobileIron service (sentry.jar, mobileironcore, or known Sentry daemon) spawning child processes with uid=0 (Linux) or LocalSystem (Windows), especially if child is shell, cmd.exe, bash, curl, wget, nc, or other utilities not expected in normal Sentry operation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance Check
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV signals active exploitation. Article provides federal patch due date 2026-06-14 (overdue relative to article date 2026-06-11). Patch inventory is now a blocking detection requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and patch systems for Ivanti Sentry instances with CVE-2026-10520 unpatched. Flag any match as critical, especially if correlated with internet-accessible instances from exposure hunt. Track remediation SLA violation (due 2026-06-14); alert if unpatched instances remain.

suggestion.title: Sentry Service Crash and Abnormal Restart Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation activity via RCE (arbitrary root-level command execution) will likely cause service instability, crashes, or unexpected restarts—an operational detection signal of compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Sentry/MobileIron service crashes, unexpected restarts, or high-frequency restart patterns (e.g., >3 restarts in 1 hour). Correlate with OS command-injection attempts and root-privilege process spawning to confirm exploitation in progress.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Hunt — Ivanti Sentry Externally Reachable
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—this is the primary attack surface for CVE-2026-10520 exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and vulnerability scanners for Ivanti Sentry (including legacy 'MobileIron Sentry' naming) with external reachability to HTTP(S) management interfaces. suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Ivanti Sentry management interfaces for OS command injection indicators: backticks, `$()`, pipes, semicolons, command operators (|&, &&, ||) in URI query parameters and POST data. Unauthenticated requests are high-confidence signals given the flaw's unauthenticated nature.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Without mTLS or Restricted HTTPS
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies protective controls: 'The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors'. Detect absence of both controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Ivanti Sentry appliance TLS configurations for lack of client-certificate authentication (mTLS) and network access policies permitting unrestricted HTTPS. Appliances without both protections are exploitable from the internet.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Root RCE Activity from Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation achieves 'root-level remote code execution'. Detect process spawning, privilege escalation, or shell activity originating from Sentry service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process creation, privilege escalation, or interactive shells executing under Ivanti Sentry service identity (typically running as root pre-exploitation or as privileged service account post-exploitation). Include file-system modifications, new user creation, or lateral-movement connections from the appliance.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Remote Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote unauthenticated user' exploiting 'externally reachable' Sentry appliances. Pipeline generated zero use cases for initial compromise despite explicit external access vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to externally exposed Ivanti Sentry management interfaces. Alert on requests from untrusted networks exhibiting exploitation patterns: suspicious parameter injection, URI path traversal indicators, or request patterns consistent with known Sentry exploits.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attack in Ivanti Sentry HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'OS command injection vulnerability'—the execution mechanism. Pipeline omitted execution-phase detections and failed to surface T1059.001 command injection patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP request payloads to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters (;, |, &, backticks, $(), newlines) and command substitution syntax. Flag encoded or obfuscated payloads attempting command injection through HTTP parameters.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution on Ivanti Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as the attack outcome. Pipeline generated no detections for post-exploitation process execution or privilege escalation indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected processes spawned with UID 0 (root context) on Ivanti Sentry appliances following exploitation attempts or HTTP anomalies. Correlate with command injection detection and baseline normal root activities.

suggestion.title: Externally Exposed Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploitable only when 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Asset discovery is prerequisite; template referenced in recommendations but no use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate externally accessible Ivanti Sentry appliances via port scanning, SSL certificate analysis, or HTTP banner grabbing. Cross-reference against internal asset management to identify unmanaged instances or those without mTLS/restricted HTTPS protections mentioned as mitigations.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Mandatory asset-exposure hunt for T1190 execution path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Ivanti Sentry instances (product names matching 'Sentry' + 'Ivanti'/'MobileIron') listening on external interfaces. Correlate against patch baseline for CVE-2026-10520. Flag any unpatched instance reachable from non-RFC1918 sources on default ports 8080/8443.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection – Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Direct detection requirement for exploit attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters (pipes, semicolons, command substitution $(), &&, ||) in query params, POST bodies, headers. Correlate with process spawning (bash, sh, nc) from Sentry service account.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RCE – Root Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated user' achieving 'root-level remote code execution.' Privilege escalation from unprivileged service account to root requires process-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Ivanti Sentry service processes spawning shell interpreters (bash/sh/zsh) or system commands with elevated privileges (UID 0/SYSTEM). Correlation: trigger only when immediately preceded by external HTTP request (unauthenticated exploit attempt).

suggestion.title: mTLS Bypass / Restricted Interface Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible.' Detection required to identify evasion of these mitigations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry endpoints for: (1) HTTP requests to interfaces that should enforce HTTPS-only, (2) mTLS handshake failures followed by successful unauthenticated access, (3) certificate anomalies (missing, self-signed, CN mismatch).

suggestion.title: CISA KEV Patch Compliance – CVE-2026-10520
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'anything in CISA KEV is currently being exploited…Even if your scanners say "not vulnerable" because of patches, it's worth one quick check.' Federal due date 2026-06-14 requires compliance tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated compliance check: flag all Ivanti Sentry instances that are (1) installed, (2) externally reachable, (3) unpatched as of 2026-06-14. Include instances where scanner reports 'not vulnerable' but version history indicates unpatched code—scanner lag is a known risk.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Asset Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Externally-reachable instances are the prerequisite attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry or MobileIron Sentry appliances with internet-routable IPs and HTTPS access from untrusted IP ranges. Flag appliances in unmanaged state without mTLS, EPMM enrollment, or Neurons for MDM integration that restricts external access.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to exposed Sentry endpoints for command injection payloads (shell metacharacters: semicolons, backticks, $(), pipes) in URL parameters or POST bodies. Alert on unauthenticated requests containing execution patterns.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: Privileged Process Spawning from Sentry Daemon
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' Captures the privilege escalation/impact outcome of successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation where parent process is Ivanti Sentry service spawning child processes with root privileges (UID 0). Flag shell invocations (sh, bash, command, system) originating from Sentry context; correlate with external HTTP requests.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance and Vulnerability Tracking
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal due date 2026-06-14; compliance detection and residual-risk tracking are essential for federal and regulated environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Ivanti Sentry appliances in production. Track CVE-2026-10520 vulnerability scanner findings. Alert on unpatched instances, especially those externally reachable. Monitor patch deployment against federal due date and flag post-deadline non-compliance.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged Appliance with External Reachability
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—this is the primary exposure condition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances in unmanaged state with management interfaces accessible from untrusted networks. Monitor asset inventory for missing mTLS configuration or HTTPS restrictions. Prioritize appliances without VPN/IP whitelisting on management ports.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution'—the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry API and web endpoints for command-injection payloads (backticks, $(...), semicolons, pipe characters) in HTTP requests from unauthenticated sources. Correlate with HTTP 5xx errors or application exceptions to flag exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Root-Level Process Execution from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation directly grants 'root-level remote code execution'; any child process spawned by Sentry service running as root indicates successful compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned by Sentry/sentry-api service running as root or SYSTEM. Baseline normal service behavior; flag unexpected system tools (sh, bash, curl, wget, python) invoked from Sentry context or working directories.

suggestion.title: Disabled or Downgraded mTLS/HTTPS Protection on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible'—disabling these re-exposes the appliance to exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliance configuration changes for disabled mTLS enforcement, downgrade to plaintext HTTP, removal of IP restrictions, or modification of EPMM/Neurons integration settings that weaken access controls.

suggestion.title: Credential/API Key Extraction from Compromised Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Root-level RCE enables pivoting; Sentry appliances typically store credentials and API keys for downstream endpoint management—high-value targets for lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for extraction or enumeration of Sentry configuration files, credential stores, database files, or environment variables containing API tokens. Alert on authentication attempts using Sentry service account credentials on unrelated systems.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Ivanti Sentry Version Not Patched by Due Date
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due-date 2026-06-14 and CISA KEV designation implies active wild exploitation—version inventory is the first detection layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and vulnerability scans for Ivanti Sentry instances running versions prior to the published patch date or known-vulnerable versions. Cross-reference with network exposure data; flag externally-reachable vulnerable appliances for immediate escalation.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry internet-facing asset inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Detection of exposed Ivanti Sentry instances without mTLS or HTTPS restrictions is the prerequisite hunt for this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for internet-routable Ivanti Sentry appliances (port 8443 or known Sentry service ports) with inbound connections from untrusted/external ASNs. Correlate with vulnerability scanner data to identify unpatched instances as of 2026-06-14.

suggestion.title: OS command injection attempts against Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user.' Detect HTTP POST/GET requests containing shell metacharacters or command-injection payloads targeting known Ivanti Sentry endpoint paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints containing shell command operators (;, |, &&, `, $, backticks) or known command-injection payloads. Baseline against legitimate administrative traffic and filter by destination port/path specific to Sentry.

suggestion.title: Process spawning from Ivanti Sentry service context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'root-level remote code execution.' After command injection, the attacker executes OS commands in the context of the Ivanti Sentry process, which should not normally spawn child processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected parent processes matching Ivanti Sentry service names (ivanti-sentry, mobileIron-sentry, etc.) spawning cmd.exe, bash, sh, or PowerShell child processes. Establish baseline of legitimate administrative child processes; flag deviations as exploitation.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation from Ivanti Sentry network service context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'root-level remote code execution.' Detect privilege escalation techniques originating from the Ivanti Sentry service process, which typically runs as a service account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on privilege escalation events (sudo, UAC elevation, setuid, etc.) initiated by Ivanti Sentry service processes or their child processes. Cross-reference with failed authentication logs to identify exploitation attempts vs. legitimate administrative activity.

suggestion.title: Reverse shell or data exfiltration from Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'root-level remote code execution' implies post-exploitation impact. Detect C2 beacons or data exfiltration initiated from the compromised appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network connections originating from Ivanti Sentry appliance IPs to suspicious external destinations (high-entropy domains, known C2 infrastructure, Tor exit nodes). Baseline against legitimate administrative outbound traffic.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry configuration tampering post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes appliance behavior in 'unmanaged state.' Post-exploitation, attacker may disable mTLS enforcement, weaken HTTPS restrictions, or modify enrollment policies to maintain access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on changes to Ivanti Sentry security settings (mTLS certificates, HTTPS policies, enrollment profiles, API access controls) without corresponding change-control ticket. Correlate with process-execution detections to identify attacker-initiated changes vs. legitimate administration.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Asset exposure is the primary detection vector for initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry appliances (via banner grab, asset inventory tags, or certificate fingerprinting) reachable from untrusted networks. Correlate externally reachable instances with management state (unmanaged = critical risk). Prioritize appliances without mTLS enforcement or Neurons for MDM HTTPS restriction.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Match Alert
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and warns 'patch lag is the silent killer' despite scanner false-negatives. Requires alert on any scanner detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate scanner detections for CVE-2026-10520 against Ivanti Sentry. Alert regardless of patch status (scanners lag). Cross-correlate with network accessibility findings. Flag all hits with federal remediation deadline (2026-06-14) for escalation.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability.' Behavioral detection of command injection syntax and patterns in HTTP requests to Sentry interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for OS command injection signatures: backtick execution (`` `cmd` ``), command substitution ($(...)), pipe chains, shell metacharacters in parameter values. Alert on payload attempts whether blocked or passed through. Correlate with CVE-2026-10520 context.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Configuration Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitability requires appliance 'in an unmanaged state' and notes mTLS+EPMM or Neurons-restricted HTTPS blocks external access. Configuration compliance detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Ivanti Sentry appliances for enrollment status in EPMM/Neurons for MDM and mTLS enablement. Identify unmanaged instances. Cross-reference with network reachability data. Flag unmanaged + externally reachable instances as critical.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution and Privilege Escalation on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'root-level remote code execution' outcome of successful exploitation. Post-exploitation detection for privileged process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process execution on Ivanti Sentry appliances for unexpected commands spawned by web server or Sentry daemon processes. Focus on high-privilege execution (root context) and indicators of post-compromise activity: reverse shells, credential access, persistence (cron jobs, systemd units).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'vulnerability...exploitable in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' External exposure is the precondition for all downstream attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry/MobileIron Sentry instances accessible from the internet (ports 443, 8443, or non-standard admin ports). Correlate firewall/WAF logs showing inbound traffic to Sentry endpoints with CMDB to flag unmanaged appliances lacking mTLS or network ACL restrictions. Alert if appliances show externally routable addresses without required compensating controls.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the attack vector. Detection must identify malicious input attempting to break out of command context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints (API, admin interfaces) for OS command injection metacharacters in unauthenticated requests: backticks, $(), command substitution, pipes, semicolons, && chains. Pair with WAF rules to block injection payloads before they reach the appliance.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Root-Level Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow...root-level remote code execution.' Successful exploitation manifests as unexpected elevated process spawning from web service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Sentry appliance processes (httpd, tomcat, java, python) spawning child processes with root/uid 0, particularly reverse shells, curl/wget downloads, SSH key installs, sudoers modifications, or user account creation. Correlate with HTTP access logs to identify triggering requests.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Patch Compliance Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-14.' Patch inventory is the primary remediation control for CISA KEV entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all Ivanti Sentry appliances for product version and build number. Flag any instance below Ivanti's published patch build for CVE-2026-10520. Cross-reference CMDB to ensure complete coverage; missing appliances from inventory indicate discovery gap.

suggestion.title: Mitigation Control Validation (mTLS / Network Restriction)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access...makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Verify compensating controls prevent exploitation even if patching lags.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Validate all externally reachable Ivanti Sentry appliances enforce at least one control: (a) mTLS with mandatory client certificate validation, (b) network ACL limiting access to internal subnets only, or (c) reverse proxy with authentication gating. Alert if any exposed instance lacks all three.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Ivanti Sentry Externally Reachable
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'exploitable in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—this prerequisite must drive hunting for exposed assets across the fleet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry appliances (fingerprinted via HTTP headers, SSL certificates, or scanner signatures) accessible from untrusted networks. Cross-reference asset inventory for unmanaged instances or those without enforced mTLS/HTTPS-only access.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'OS command injection vulnerability'—exploitation manifests as payloads containing shell metacharacters, command separators, or variable expansion in HTTP requests to vulnerable endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Ivanti Sentry appliances for command-injection signatures: backticks, $(), semicolons, pipes, &&, ||, or newlines embedded in request parameters or POST bodies. Alert on anomalous frequency or source IPs outside administrative ranges.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution on Ivanti Sentry Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as the exploitation outcome—successful compromise manifests as unexpected root-privileged processes, file/system modifications, or network activity initiated from the appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance for unexpected root-privilege process creation (especially shell interpreters, network utilities, or package managers), new user/group additions at root level, SSH key injections, or filesystem modifications outside expected maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article cites federal remediation due-date 2026-06-14 and warns 'patch lag is the silent killer'—compliance verification must identify unpatched instances and track remediation status to deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset database for Ivanti Sentry appliances with vulnerable-version signatures for CVE-2026-10520. Flag any appliances past federal due-date (2026-06-14) without documented patch or approved remediation exception.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Management Interface Access Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article notes mTLS and Neurons MDM HTTPS restrictions mitigate external access—unauthenticated or anomalous access from untrusted sources indicates either misconfiguration or active exploitation bypassing these controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Ivanti Sentry management ports (443, 8443, or custom mgmt ports) originating from external/untrusted IP ranges. Flag unauthenticated session attempts, SSL/TLS failures, or connections not routing through configured MDM channels.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Ivanti Sentry Externally Reachable
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Core precondition for exploitation; mandatory asset hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry appliances reachable from untrusted networks. Correlate external IP accessibility, management-state configuration (unmanaged = high risk), and absence of mTLS/restricted HTTPS controls. Flag all externally accessible instances for immediate isolation or network segmentation review.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance Scan

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all Ivanti Sentry instances against CVE-2026-10520. Flag unpatched systems and cross-reference with external exposure status. Escalate instances still vulnerable past due date with compliance-timeline enforcement.

suggestion.title: Command Injection Attempt Detection on Ivanti Sentry

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry HTTP requests (unauthenticated paths) for shell metacharacters (backtick, pipe, semicolon, $(), &&, ||) and command-substitution patterns. Alert on payloads resembling command injection (base64-encoded shells, reverse-shell signatures, whoami/id enumeration).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Root Privilege Acquisition on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation achieves 'root-level remote code execution.' Post-compromise, attacker inherits or escalates to root; monitor for unexpected privilege acquisition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on root account authentication from external IP ranges, unexpected sudo/privilege-escalation events, and sudden elevation of previously-unauthenticated sessions to administrative roles. Baseline normal admin access patterns and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Sentry Network Segmentation Control Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors'—this is the hardening control; weak segmentation is an exploitability precondition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify Sentry management interfaces enforce mutual TLS and reject unrestricted HTTPS connections from external ranges. Identify appliances not protected by mTLS gateways, with certificate pinning absent, or accepting connections from non-whitelisted IPs. Test external-vantage reachability to confirm boundary enforcement.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Asset Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploitable when 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Asset-exposure hunt explicitly recommended via template reference; this is the gating condition for exploitation.

Cross-reference internal network inventory to identify exposed appliances; flag any publicly reachable or incorrectly segmented instances. Correlation with mTLS/EPMM configuration audit identifies unmitigated exposure.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends substituting CVE-2026-10520 into template asset-exposure hunt; this is the canonical indicator for this vulnerability. Scanner or nessus-type logs should flag positive matches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scan result positive for CVE-2026-10520 on Ivanti Sentry instances. Given CISA KEV status (actively exploited), prioritize immediate remediation timeline awareness; correlate with patch-due date 2026-06-14.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Exploitation Attempt to Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability is 'remote unauthenticated'—attackers do not need valid credentials. Detection should focus on unauthenticated HTTP requests containing OS command injection payloads or suspicious patterns targeting Sentry admin/API endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST/GET requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints (e.g., /admin, /api/*) originating from unauthenticated sessions containing shell metacharacters (backtick, $(), |, ;, &&, ||) or known command-injection patterns. Cross-reference with vulnerability-scanner baseline to identify exploit attempts vs. noise.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Command Execution from Ivanti Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow...root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation detection must capture child processes spawned with UID 0 or unusual privilege context from the Sentry service account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any process creation events where the parent is an Ivanti Sentry service (e.g., sentry, mobileironserver) and the child process runs with UID 0 / SYSTEM privilege, or on unusual command-line arguments (shell invocations, reverse shells, file exfil) spawned by the Sentry service.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry mTLS/EPMM Security Configuration Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Absence of these mitigations is a risk signal that should be inventoried.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit all Ivanti Sentry instances to verify mTLS with EPMM is enabled OR restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM is in place. Flag any instances without these mitigations as high-risk; correlate with asset-exposure findings to prioritize remediation.

suggestion.title: HTTP request to PHP endpoint with URI-scheme wrapper patterns in file parameters
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation via file parameter containing wrapper scheme: 'When the input has the form phar:///path/file.phar/inner'. Pipeline should hunt application-level file-load attempts with wrapper patterns, not just HTTP network detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to PHP endpoints that accept file-path parameters (e.g., /upload, /import, /load). Flag any parameter value containing URI schemes (phar:, php:, data:, expect:, zip:, file:) followed by ://. Correlate with subsequent child-process creation or file writes by web-server process within 30 seconds.

suggestion.title: URI scheme with 3+ forward-slashes—wrapper bypass detection
suggestion.rationale: Core exploit is the bypass condition: 'with three or more slashes after the scheme'. Simple phar:// detection is insufficient; this is specifically about the bypass vector phar:/// or phar///.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Signature-level hunt: HTTP requests with URI patterns matching (php|phar|data|expect|zip):///{1,}(forward slashes only, not URL-encoded). This is lower-volume and higher-fidelity than generic wrapper detection.

suggestion.title: PHPSpreadsheet library file-load on path containing stream wrapper

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search application logs for PHPSpreadsheet load attempts (IOFactory::load, fromFile, from methods) where the file argument contains phar://, php://, or data:// schemes. Requires verbose PHP logging enabled.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Exploitation Attempt Detection

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Configuration Check

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Ivanti Sentry Service

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for root-level process spawning from Ivanti Sentry service accounts (sentry, mobileiron user contexts). Flag unexpected child processes (bash, sh, python) launched with elevated privileges.

suggestion.title: External Reachability Scan: Ivanti Sentry Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article notes exploitation requires 'endpoints externally reachable' and 'Sentry appliance in unmanaged state'—asset inventory / exposure detection is fundamental remediation lens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run vulnerability scanners (Qualys, Tenable Nessus) for CVE-2026-10520 against all Ivanti Sentry instances. Independently confirm external accessibility via port scans (443, 8443) to internet-facing appliances; prioritize patching unmanaged instances.

suggestion.title: mTLS/HTTPS Restriction Bypass Attempt
