suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploitable only when 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—mandatory asset-exposure hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for inbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Ivanti Sentry (default port 443) from external sources. Cross-reference with asset inventory; flag appliances confirmed externally reachable and lacking mTLS/EPMM enrollment.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' exploitable by 'remote unauthenticated user'—command-injection payload detection required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for command-injection payloads (backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons, newlines in URL parameters and POST bodies). Alert on requests from unauthenticated session context.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Root Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes outcome is 'root-level remote code execution'—post-compromise process-execution detection required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry appliances, alert on process creation with UID=0 from unexpected parent processes (web daemons, network services). Correlate with recent failed or unauthenticated HTTP access logs.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged Deployment State Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'unmanaged state' as exploitation precondition—configuration-drift hunt required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query MDM/EPMM enrollment logs for Ivanti Sentry appliances not enrolled or dis-enrolled. Cross-reference with vulnerability scans and external-reachability assessments; flag unmanaged instances reachable from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: mTLS/Restricted Access Control Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access...makes interfaces inaccessible'—defense-evasion detection required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on TLS certificate validation failures, HTTP 401/403 responses, or repeated connection attempts to Ivanti Sentry management interfaces. Cluster by source IP; correlate with known exploit-scanner signatures.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance / Patch-Lag Risk Assessment
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal patch due-date 2026-06-14; article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer'—inventory-based hunt required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for Ivanti Sentry instances flagged for CVE-2026-10520 and unpatched. Cross-reference with patch-deployment logs; surface appliances past federal due-date 2026-06-14 without remediation plan.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—asset exposure is the prerequisite for exploitation. No use case addresses detection of internet-facing Sentry instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for Ivanti Sentry appliances (ports 80, 443, custom listening ports) accessible from WAN/untrusted networks. Correlate public IP enumeration results with internal asset registry; flag unmanaged instances not behind mTLS or restricted HTTPS proxies per article mitigations.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated OS Command Injection Attempts on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes 'remote unauthenticated user' can exploit. No detection for unauthenticated HTTP/HTTPS requests containing command injection payloads (shell metacharacters, command separators) targeting Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry application logs and WAF telemetry for HTTP requests lacking valid authentication tokens/cookies containing shell metacharacters (backticks, pipes, semicolons, command substitution syntax) in URL parameters, POST bodies, or headers. Baseline legitimate query patterns and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Command Execution from Sentry Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'root-level remote code execution'—post-exploitation telemetry should detect shell spawning under Sentry service account/process with uid=0. No use case captures this privilege escalation or execution indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned from Ivanti Sentry daemon/service with effective UID 0 (root). Flag shell spawns (sh, bash, zsh) or system utilities (curl, wget, nc) initiated by Sentry, especially if followed by unexpected network connections or file modifications.

suggestion.title: Sentry API Access Without Valid Session/mTLS
suggestion.rationale: Article mitigations cite 'restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM' and 'mTLS'—implies normal operation requires authentication. Successful bypass is an indicator; no use case detects unauthenticated API access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry API logs for requests lacking valid JWT/session tokens or mTLS client certificates that succeed (HTTP 200-299 responses). Baseline normal API paths and detect requests to administrative endpoints without proper authentication.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and references canonical asset-exposure hunt templates. No use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Vulnerability scanner reports indicating Ivanti Sentry product versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-10520 (pre-2026-06-14 patches). Filter for appliances with external reachability flags or public-facing network exposure.

suggestion.title: Exposed Ivanti Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' No asset exposure use case was generated despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances (product signatures, SSL cert analysis, HTTP response headers) responding to external/untrusted networks on standard ports. Flag as unmanaged if lacking mTLS EPMM or Neurons for MDM indicators.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Against Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' No execution-phase detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Ivanti Sentry appliances for URL-encoded or shell metacharacter payloads (|, ;, &&, $(), backticks) in query parameters or POST bodies, particularly against known vulnerable endpoint paths.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Root-Level Process Spawning from Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 'root-level remote code execution' as the impact. No impact-phase or privilege escalation detection was generated to catch successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify root or system-privilege processes spawned by Ivanti Sentry service accounts (parent process: sentry/MobileIron processes), particularly unusual command interpreters (sh, bash, python) or network utilities (curl, nc, wget) without corresponding legitimate administrative activity.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Patch Compliance Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies Federal patch due date 2026-06-14 and warns 'patch lag is the silent killer.' No compliance or patch-state detection use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management and vulnerability systems for Ivanti Sentry instances post-due-date without applied security updates for CVE-2026-10520. Cross-reference with Federal audit timelines and organizational SLAs.

suggestion.title: Plugin Script Modification & Obfuscated Code Injection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'WordPress Plugin Scripts Tampered' — requires detection for file modifications in plugin directories, particularly PHP injections, base64-encoded payloads, eval() calls, or obfuscated function definitions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /wp-content/plugins/* for unexpected .php file modifications (hash changes, timestamp anomalies). Alert on additions of obfuscated code, eval/assert/create_function calls, or base64-encoded payloads. Cross-reference against WordPress.org repository hashes for baseline validation.

suggestion.title: Backdoor Execution from Plugin Context
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Hidden Backdoors' planted via plugins — detection needed for command execution spawned from PHP/Apache processes with suspicious parent-child relationships or credential abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe/powershell.exe/bash spawned from php-cgi.exe, apache2.exe, or nginx processes. Flag obfuscated command lines using variable expansion or encoding. Correlate with process creation from web-accessible plugin directories.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin Account Creation via Backdoor
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain backdoors commonly create hidden admin accounts for post-exploitation persistence — detection should flag unexpected wp_users table inserts with administrator role.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress user creation (wp_users.INSERT) for accounts with admin role created outside normal admin interface. Alert on rapid user creation or creation from non-WordPress admin IP contexts. Cross-reference timestamp against plugin modification window.

suggestion.title: Malicious Web Shell or Hidden Admin Interface Detection
suggestion.rationale: Hidden backdoors in WordPress plugins typically manifest as web shells or rogue admin endpoints — detection needed for suspicious HTTP POST requests to plugin files with command/execute parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to /wp-content/plugins/* with suspicious query/POST parameters (cmd, shell, execute, action, function). Alert on non-standard User-Agents or requests originating from foreign IP ranges. Correlate with 200 responses followed by outbound C2 connections.

suggestion.title: Plugin-Origin Outbound C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Tampered plugins commonly establish C2 channels — detection should identify unexpected outbound connections from PHP/web server processes to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound TCP/UDP from PHP processes to ports outside 80/443 or to non-CDN 443 destinations. Alert on DNS queries from web server context for newly registered or malicious domains. Correlate with plugin file modification timestamps within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: Plugin Version/Hash Integrity Baseline Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Tampered plugins will have altered checksums or unexpected version downgrades — detection requires comparison of installed plugins against official WordPress.org repository metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Periodically pull plugin manifests from WordPress.org. Alert on installed plugins with mismatched hashes, version downgrades, or file timestamps inconsistent with release dates. Flag plugins with recent modifications but no corresponding WordPress update events in logs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Inventory and Patch Compliance Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and is CISA KEV actively exploited. Federal patch deadline 2026-06-14 is overdue as of review date.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Ivanti Sentry appliances in environment; flag those with CVE-2026-10520 vulnerability status. Cross-reference against vendor patch release dates and federal remediation deadline. Escalate unpatched instances immediately.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged + Externally-Reachable Ivanti Sentry Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Exact attack precondition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset hunt: cross-reference Ivanti Sentry instances flagged as unmanaged in MDM/EPMM systems with those resolvable from external DNS or on internet-routable interfaces. Exclude instances protected by mTLS with EPMM or Neurons for MDM. Flag exposed unmanaged instances as critical.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payloads to Ivanti Sentry HTTP Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Core attack vector requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Ivanti Sentry for command-injection signatures: backticks, $() substitution, pipe/semicolon/&&/|| chains, shell keywords (bash, sh, wget, curl) in URL parameters and POST bodies. Alert on unauthenticated requests with injection patterns.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Shell Process Spawned by Ivanti Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Successful OS command injection RCE will spawn shell or arbitrary processes under the Sentry service account context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected child processes from Ivanti Sentry service (sentry, ivanti user). Alert on shell spawning (bash, sh, dash), reverse-shell signatures (/dev/tcp, nc -e, bash -i), and suspicious commands (wget, chmod, useradd, sed).

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation to Root from Ivanti Sentry Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'root-level remote code execution' indicates privilege escalation to UID 0 as part of the attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for privilege escalation events where Ivanti Sentry service processes (or child processes) transition to UID 0 (root). Alert on sudo invocations, setuid/setgid abuse, or direct privilege escalation in Sentry process trees.

suggestion.title: Go Module Dependency on Typo-Squatted Package
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies malicious package 'github.com/botdb-go/bolt' (typo of legitimate 'github.com/boltdb/bolt'). Pipeline extracted zero IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor go.mod files and module imports for package names matching known typo-squatted variants of legitimate modules. Alert on any import of 'github.com/botdb-go/bolt' or dependencies pulled from Go Module Proxy that resolve to suspicious package paths deviating from canonical upstream locations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Go Module Version Pinning or Outdated Version Adoption
suggestion.rationale: Malicious version 1.3.1 was released November 2021, cached for 3+ years, then imported when developers updated dependencies in 2024. Pipeline missed version-specific detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on imports of BoltDB module versions significantly older than the latest release (3+ year gap). Correlate bulk version update operations with resolution to outdated or cached versions, indicating potential exploitation of persistent caching vulnerability.

suggestion.title: Go Module Proxy Persistent Cache Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes Go Module Mirror's 'indefinite caching' allowed backdoored module to persist 3 years undetected: 'Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in, and that cached the backdored module.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go Module Proxy access logs for requests to modules with known CVEs or malicious indicators. Cross-reference module caching timestamps against removal/revocation dates from upstream repositories. Alert if a module is served from proxy cache after documented removal from source.

suggestion.title: Backdoored Package Remote Command and Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'This backdoor allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands i.e. via a command and control server.' Pipeline missed C2 detection use case entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify network communication patterns from systems that imported github.com/botdb-go/bolt v1.3.1. Look for outbound connections to hardcoded C2 infrastructure, unusual DNS queries, or HTTPS traffic with certificate anomalies originating from processes linked to Go module initialization or runtime.

suggestion.title: Malicious Supply Chain Package Inventory Alerting
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates impact on 'thousands of organizations for over three years.' Detection should include proactive inventory scanning against known-malicious package database (Snyk advisory SNYK-GOLANG-GITHUBCOMBOLTDBGOBOLT-868841, GO-2025-3451).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Periodically scan all go.mod files and vendored dependencies across the organization against curated lists of known-malicious Go packages (integrate Snyk, socket.dev, and OpenSSF vulnerability feeds). Alert on any historical imports of github.com/botdb-go/bolt or derived artifacts with compromise timestamps between Nov 2021 and Jan 2025.

suggestion.title: Module Proxy Behavioral Anomaly on Cached Malicious Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack surface as 'how Go manages and caches its modules, allowing it to go unnoticed for several years.' Pipeline missed infrastructure-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go Module Proxy service logs for anomalous cache hit patterns: high request rates to specific module versions days/weeks after documented removal, requests to modules from clients in same network segment, and cache coherency violations (serving stale module metadata after upstream revocation notification).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Reachability Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Network exposure is the precondition for exploitation—requires immediate hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances (by product fingerprinting, certificate inspection, or port 8443 service banners) reachable from external networks. Correlate against asset inventory and internal-only placement policy. Flag any instance not protected by mTLS/Neurons for MDM as per article mitigation guidance.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Hit Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates CISA KEV patch due 2026-06-14 and explicitly recommends 'match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline must establish baseline scanner coverage and alert on any Ivanti Sentry instance without patch status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Continuous scan for CVE-2026-10520 across Ivanti Sentry instances. Alert on any unpatched appliance with external reachability. Track patch lag against federal due date to predict remediation compliance risk.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Root-Level Process Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' capability via OS command injection. RCE spawning unexpected child processes from Ivanti Sentry root context is the execution indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process spawning from Ivanti Sentry service accounts with root/SYSTEM privilege, especially shell commands (sh, bash, cmd.exe) or reverse-shell indicators. Baseline legitimate Sentry processes first to minimize FP.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Unmanaged appliances bypass mTLS protections and are high-risk targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Ivanti Sentry appliances and validate enrollment status in EPMM/Neurons for MDM. Flag any appliance not reporting active management heartbeat or showing disabled mTLS. Cross-reference against network exposure findings.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry HTTP Request Injection Pattern
suggestion.rationale: OS command injection vulnerabilities typically manifest as malformed requests with shell metacharacters (backticks, pipes, semicolons, $() substitution). Article specifies command injection, so HTTP request inspection is appropriate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters, command-substitution syntax, or encoded variants. Pivot to application logs if WAF detects potential injection attempts.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and defines Federal patch due 2026-06-14. This is the primary detection mechanism cited.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output and patch management systems for Ivanti Sentry instances. Alert on any system matching product name 'Ivanti Sentry' with version ≤ highest vulnerable version for CVE-2026-10520. Prioritize systems with external network exposure.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' as the exploitation precondition. This is the critical exposure hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances on standard ports (443, 8443, 8080) with inbound connectivity from untrusted networks. Cross-reference asset inventory to confirm lack of mTLS/EPMM or Neurons for MDM protection.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Command Injection Attempts Against Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'remote unauthenticated user' RCE via 'OS command injection.' This is the attack mechanism that should trigger behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for unauthenticated requests containing shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), pipes, &&, semicolons) in request parameters. Alert on 4xx responses followed by suspicious process creation.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution on Ivanti Sentry Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability achieves 'root-level remote code execution.' Active exploitation (CISA KEV status) should trigger process-level hunting on vulnerable appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry appliances with external reachability, hunt for unexpected processes spawned with root privileges: network utilities (curl, wget, nc), script interpreters, or reverse-shell signatures. Establish baseline of normal root-level operations to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Root RCE on a public-facing appliance typically precedes lateral movement into internal infrastructure. CISA KEV implies active exploitation chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for egress file transfers and outbound connections from Ivanti Sentry appliances to internal hosts not normally contacted. Flag downloads of attacker tools or suspicious internal reconnaissance traffic post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Persistence Mechanisms
suggestion.rationale: Known-exploited vulnerabilities in public-facing apps are targeted for persistent access. Should hunt for backdoors or scheduled task creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Ivanti Sentry appliance logs for creation or modification of cron jobs, systemd units, or init scripts with suspicious command payloads. Monitor /etc/cron.d, /etc/systemd/system, and similar persistence locations.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states appliance is vulnerable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — external network accessibility is the necessary precondition enabling exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances responding to external network requests on standard Sentry ports. Alert on connectivity from non-corporate IP ranges or unusual geographic origins. Correlate with vulnerability scanner results confirming Sentry product presence.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability as 'OS command injection vulnerability' enabling 'remote unauthenticated user' exploitation — malformed payloads containing shell metacharacters are the exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons, &, ||, &&) in URL parameters and POST bodies. Alert on URL-encoded or Unicode-escaped variants of command separators targeting Sentry API endpoints.

suggestion.title: Root-Privilege Process Spawning from Ivanti Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies successful exploitation achieves 'root-level remote code execution' — successful abuse manifests as arbitrary process creation with elevated privileges spawned from the Sentry service account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation events where parent process is Ivanti Sentry service (sentry, mobileIron daemon, or appliance management process) and child process executes with UID 0 (root) or SYSTEM equivalent. Flag novel command lines outside baseline administrative operations.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Appliance Identification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly specifies vulnerability applies only when 'the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state' — configuration assessment directly correlates to exploitability and indicates non-compliant deployments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Ivanti Sentry inventory against management platform enrollment status (Neurons for MDM, EPMM connectivity). Flag appliances not reporting to management console, missing recent health check-ins, or explicitly marked as unmanaged in device telemetry.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerable Asset Inventory Query
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'CVE-2026-10520' with federal patch due-date 2026-06-14 — vulnerability scanner results should be queried immediately to identify at-risk assets before active exploitation begins.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scan results and CMDB for Ivanti Sentry (and legacy MobileIron Sentry) instances with CVE-2026-10520 flagged as unpatched. Confirm product/version via HTTPS service-banner grabbing. Prioritize remediation timeline against federal deadline.

suggestion.title: mTLS/Restricted HTTPS Access Control Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors' — detection should flag attempts to circumvent these protective controls indicating attacker reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for TLS handshake failures on Sentry endpoints (failed certificate validation retried repeatedly), HTTP-to-HTTPS downgrade attempts, or proxy/tunnel traffic routing around restricted HTTPS policies. Alert on access patterns diverging from legitimate MDM management communication profiles.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Appliance Internet Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is exploitable only 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Asset discovery and exposure mapping is the first line of defense.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry instances (product signatures, certificate analysis, known service ports) accessible from untrusted networks. Correlate with vulnerability scanner data. Ivanti Sentry instances should only receive traffic from trusted MDM management networks; external inbound is suspicious.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated Remote Request Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows 'remote unauthenticated user' exploitation via OS command injection. Detection should flag unauthenticated requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints that carry command-injection-like payloads (shell metacharacters, backticks, command separators).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry HTTP/HTTPS traffic for unauthenticated requests containing shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, `, $(), backticks) in parameters. Baseline legitimate traffic; flag deviations. Look for 400/401 responses followed by error-verbose responses suggesting parameter enumeration.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Root-Level Process Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability results in 'root-level remote code execution.' Post-compromise detection should monitor for unexpected root-privilege processes spawned from the Ivanti Sentry service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes spawned by Ivanti Sentry service account (e.g., ivanti, sentry, or appliance-specific user) with SYSTEM/root privilege level, especially shell interpreters (sh, bash, cmd, powershell) or utilities (curl, wget, nc). Correlate with HTTP request logs to establish causality.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Outbound Anomaly Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE, compromised Ivanti Sentry appliances become C2 beachheads. Article context (federal agencies, high-value targets) suggests command-and-control or data exfiltration as likely post-exploitation goals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ivanti Sentry appliances should have tightly scoped outbound communication (cloud management, MDM sync, NTP). Flag unexpected outbound connections to non-allowlisted IPs, especially those on high ports (8080+, 443 outside known management) or to geographies inconsistent with legitimate Ivanti infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry MobileIron Migration/Rebranding Detection Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Ivanti Sentry (formerly known as MobileIron Sentry).' Legacy systems may still run MobileIron product names. Scans targeting only 'Ivanti Sentry' will miss unpatched MobileIron instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Expand asset discovery to include both 'Ivanti Sentry' AND 'MobileIron Sentry' product signatures. Cross-reference asset inventory against certificate CN/SAN, HTTP Server headers, and service banners to identify instances running legacy product names, then prioritize for patching.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' and explicitly recommends asset-exposure hunt from _TEMPLATES.md. This is the primary detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound connections to Ivanti Sentry appliances (typically ports 8443, 443) from external IPs. Correlate with asset inventory to identify unmanaged instances. Flag geographically anomalous connections or connection patterns inconsistent with internal management traffic.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Alerts
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry means active wild exploitation. Vulnerability scanner correlation for CVE-2026-10520 on Ivanti Sentry instances is a foundational detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scan result flagging CVE-2026-10520 on Ivanti Sentry. Prioritize unpatched instances exposed to external networks. Cross-reference patch due date (2026-06-14) against remediation timestamps.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' leading to 'root-level remote code execution.' Detection must capture injection attempts and post-exploitation command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry application logs and process execution on the Sentry appliance for shell metacharacters, command substitution, or unusual process spawning (bash, sh, cmd.exe). Look for POST/GET request payloads containing pipe, semicolon, backtick, or $(…) patterns targeting known RCE endpoints.

suggestion.title: Sentry Unmanaged Configuration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' This is a necessary prerequisite for exploitation; detect state change or misconfiguration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Ivanti Sentry appliance changes from managed to unmanaged state, or when EPMM/Neurons MDM connection is lost. Simultaneously check network position—if the unmanaged appliance becomes network-accessible from external subnets, escalate to critical.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution on Sentry Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states RCE achieves 'root-level' access. This is the privilege-escalation and impact phase; detect unexpected root-owned processes spawned by remote input.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry appliances, monitor for any process spawned with UID 0 (root) initiated by a non-root parent process or by network-facing service accounts. Correlate with time-window of external HTTP/HTTPS requests to the appliance.

suggestion.title: mTLS / HTTPS Restriction Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible.' Detect attempts to circumvent these controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed mTLS handshakes or certificate validation errors targeting Ivanti Sentry from external IPs. Also detect plain HTTP requests to endpoints that should enforce HTTPS, or HTTP/2 ALPN downgrades on restricted paths.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Ivanti Sentry Externally Reachable Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' and explicitly recommends the asset-exposure hunt template. Pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Ivanti Sentry instances from asset inventory. Verify external reachability to known MobileIron/Sentry ports (typically 8443). Alert on unpatched Sentry with CVE-2026-10520 that is accessible from untrusted networks or internet-facing. Cross-check mTLS/EPMM configuration to confirm restricted access controls are in place.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt: OS Command Injection Against Sentry Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' No exploitation detection generated despite clear attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry ingress for suspicious HTTP/HTTPS payloads containing shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), semicolons, pipes) in request parameters. Alert on unauthenticated requests followed by unexpected process spawning or file writes on Sentry appliance. Correlate failed authentication attempts with command injection patterns.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payloads to Ivanti Sentry Endpoints

suggestion.title: Root-Level Child Processes from Ivanti Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article: vulnerability 'allow[s] a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation indicator: unexpected processes executed with root privileges under Sentry service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes spawned by Ivanti Sentry service with root/system privilege. Baseline normal child processes; shell interpreters (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, cmd.exe, powershell.exe) spawned directly from Sentry parent are high-confidence RCE confirmations.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Root-level compromise of network infrastructure enables pivot. Article describes appliance-layer breach—subsequent internal reconnaissance and lateral movement should be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sustained outbound connections from compromised Sentry appliance to internal subnets on uncommon ports (SSH 22, RDP 3389, WinRM 5985, database ports). Cross-reference with CVE-2026-10520 exploitation detection window.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged Configuration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Proactive configuration inventory can identify high-risk deployments before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Periodic audit of all Ivanti Sentry appliances for management status (managed vs. unmanaged). Flag unmanaged instances, especially if externally routable. Confirm status via vendor APIs or SSH enumeration.

suggestion.title: Low-Privilege User Escalation via LiteLLM Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Low-Privilege Users Take Over AI Gateway Servers' — core privilege escalation attack; pipeline failed to emit any detection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation or token impersonation events originating from low-privilege context (non-admin user, service account) that spawn children with elevated privileges. Track API calls to LiteLLM gateway endpoints that result in permission token escalation or elevation of privilege responses.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Authentication Bypass or Session Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability chain attack implies auth/session weaknesses; 'chain' suggests multi-step exploitation; pipeline did not surface initial access or credential mechanisms
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repeated failed API authentication attempts to LiteLLM gateway, successful logins from unusual geographies/user-agents, or API token creation/modification by non-admin accounts. Monitor for session cookie theft or JWT manipulation.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised AI Gateway Server
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Take Over AI Gateway Servers' — compromised gateway becomes pivot point; pipeline omitted lateral movement detection despite it being implicit in the takeover scenario
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After compromise of gateway process, monitor for outbound connections from the gateway server to internal network segments, service-to-service authentication (Kerberos tickets, API calls) issued by the compromised gateway, and lateral movement tools (psexec, wmi) spawned from gateway host.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Process Execution with Elevated Privileges
suggestion.rationale: Gateway takeover implies attacker gains ability to execute code in LiteLLM process context; pipeline failed to suggest process-level detection despite 'take over servers' language
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PowerShell, cmd.exe, or bash execution spawned from LiteLLM parent process; detect inline script execution or encoded command invocation; flag network-bound commands issued from the gateway process.

suggestion.title: Persistence via LiteLLM Configuration or Cron/Scheduler Modification
suggestion.rationale: Full gateway takeover implies persistence mechanism; article title suggests sustained compromise not one-shot attack; pipeline omitted persistence detections entirely
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modification of LiteLLM config files (litellm_config.yaml, .env, requirements.txt), creation of cron/systemd timer jobs by non-admin, addition of startup scripts, or injection into LiteLLM application startup chain.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Request to LiteLLM Inference Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Unauthenticated RCE'—the vulnerability requires no authentication, meaning malicious requests bypass credential checks entirely. This is the attack surface and initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to LiteLLM endpoints (/v1/completions, /models, /proxy) without Authorization header or with Authorization: Bearer null/empty. Flag requests originating from external IPs followed by 200-299 responses. Establish baseline request volume per endpoint and alert on >3σ spike.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Process Spawns Child Process via RCE Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation 'chains to unauthenticated RCE', meaning arbitrary code execution on the host. Successful exploits result in process spawning (shell, command interpreter, or reverse shell) from the LiteLLM service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe, /bin/bash, /bin/sh, or powershell.exe spawned as children of LiteLLM application processes (python.exe, node.exe, java.exe depending on LiteLLM deployment). Alert on process creation with suspicious parent/child relationship, especially when command line contains encoded payloads (base64, URL-encoded strings).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Payload in LiteLLM Request Parameters
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerabilities in LLM services typically exploit parameter injection or unsafe deserialization. Malicious payloads would be embedded in the HTTP request body or URL parameters (model name, API key field, or custom parameter injection).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to LiteLLM endpoints containing shell metacharacters (backticks, $(…), |, ;, &, >, <) in parameter values (model, key, messages, prompt fields). Monitor for requests with unusual encoding (double URL-encoding, unicode escapes, hex escapes). Correlate with 5xx responses (indicative of payload interpretation attempt).

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Connection from Compromised LiteLLM Service
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation C2 or data exfiltration. A compromised LiteLLM instance may initiate unexpected outbound connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure for shell callbacks, malware staging, or stolen data transmission.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections initiated by LiteLLM process to non-cloud, non-API-provider IPs. Flag connections to reserved/private IP ranges that should not be reached from application (e.g., 0.0.0.0/8, 127.0.0.0/8 unless localhost). Alert on connections to ports 4444, 5555, 6666, 8888 or HTTPS to unknown CAs.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Application Log Anomalies or Gaps Following Exploit Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Attackers may clear logs post-exploitation. Successful RCE may also cause unhandled exceptions or service restarts that appear in logs. Absence of expected application telemetry is itself suspicious.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sudden absence of LiteLLM application logs after a suspicious HTTP request. Detect unhandled exception signatures (stack traces, segfaults) in application logs. Alert on LiteLLM service restart without corresponding admin-initiated shutdown event. Track log write failures or permission-denied errors that indicate defensive log wiping.
