suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Post-Exploitation System Modification Detection
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation leads to 'root-level remote code execution'—detect post-exploitation indicators such as account creation, persistence mechanisms, or data exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for signs of attacker persistence: new user accounts created on appliance, SSH authorized_keys modified, cron jobs or at jobs added, unexpected systemd services installed, or suspicious network connections from Sentry to external C2 addresses or internal targets.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Internet-Facing Ivanti Sentry Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is exploitable when 'endpoints externally reachable.' Discovery of Sentry instances visible from the internet is the canonical initial-access hunt for any public-facing RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan internet-facing assets for Ivanti Sentry service signatures (banner fingerprints, SSL certificates, HTTP headers). Cross-correlate with vulnerability scanners to identify unpatched instances. Flag any Sentry appliance reachable from untrusted networks without mTLS/EPMM protection as immediate patch target.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly 'OS command injection' enabling RCE. Exploitation attempts manifest as shell metacharacter injection in HTTP requests to vulnerable endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry administrative or API interfaces for command injection payloads: shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&`, `$()`, backticks), path traversal sequences, and command chaining patterns. Alert on payloads destined for known vulnerable parameters or endpoints.

suggestion.title: Elevated Process Execution from Sentry Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution.' Successful exploitation manifests as unexpected process spawning with root/SYSTEM privileges from the Sentry service account context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Ivanti Sentry service process events with privilege escalation indicators: child processes running as root/SYSTEM spawned from lower-privileged Sentry service parent, or unexpected shell/command interpreter spawned from network-accessible Sentry interfaces.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Sentry Configuration Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes vulnerability is exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Unmanaged instances (lacking mTLS/EPMM or restricted HTTPS) represent maximum-risk surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Ivanti Sentry asset inventory with configuration management data to identify instances NOT protected by mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access controls. Flag unmanaged instances as critical patch priority, especially if external reachability is confirmed.

suggestion.title: Remote Unauthenticated Access to Sentry Admin Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows 'remote unauthenticated' exploitation. Successful bypass of authentication controls or processing of unauthenticated requests to Sentry endpoints indicates attack surface exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry access and application logs for unauthenticated requests to known vulnerable endpoints (admin panels, API paths, management interfaces) originating from external IP ranges. Alert on requests lacking authentication headers that receive non-403 responses, or that trigger successful API responses.

suggestion.title: External Sentry Appliance Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'endpoints externally reachable' as the critical exploitation condition and explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt'; identifying unprotected Sentry instances on external-facing networks is the baseline detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances accessible from untrusted networks via service fingerprinting, SSL certificates, or port scanning. Flag instances lacking mTLS/EPMM gateway protection as exploitation-ready; correlate against CMDB to identify unmanaged state systems.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Command Injection to Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'OS command injection...remote unauthenticated user'; detection of injection syntax in pre-auth requests to Sentry endpoints is the kill-chain execution indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints arriving before authentication containing shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), semicolons, pipes, command substitution) in parameters, headers, or request body. Injection payloads precede valid auth tokens.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as the impact; post-exploitation, unexpected privileged process spawning from Sentry daemons is detectable via process telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for legitimate Sentry service process trees. Alert on unexpected child processes spawned as root/UID 0, especially shells, curl, wget, nc, or reverse-shell patterns; correlate with recent unauthenticated connection attempts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scan Match
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry indicates active in-the-wild exploitation; vulnerability scanner must identify unpatched Ivanti Sentry instances. Federal patch due-date 2026-06-14 requires mandatory compliance tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Vulnerability scanner flags Ivanti Sentry appliances below patched version for CVE-2026-10520. Triage by external reachability and management state; 'unmanaged' instances with external-facing endpoints are critical priority.

suggestion.title: Sentry Service Anomaly Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE will disrupt Sentry daemon state, spawn unexpected listeners, or corrupt process trees; auditlog and sysmon will capture post-exploitation artifacts even on unmanaged appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliance listening ports and process trees for baseline deviations. Alert on unexpected port bindings, service restarts following failed authentication, or new child processes from Sentry services indicating command execution.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Externally Exposed Asset Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'externally reachable' endpoints are vulnerable; detection of Sentry appliances exposed to untrusted networks is foundational.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances (typically port 443, MobileIron/Sentry fingerprints in TLS cert or HTTP headers) exposed to the internet or untrusted networks. Compare against authorized asset inventory.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' allowing RCE; should detect payload injection attempts against Sentry API endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry API endpoints for shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&`, `` ` ``, `$()`) in HTTP request parameters, especially on endpoints known to be injectable. CISA/Ivanti will likely publish specific vulnerable parameters post-disclosure.

suggestion.title: Sentry Command Injection / RCE Success Indicator
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'root-level remote code execution' is achievable; post-exploitation activity on compromised Sentry hosts should trigger immediate incident response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process spawning, outbound connections, or privileged command execution originating from Sentry appliance (e.g., curl, wget, bash spawned by Java/Sentry daemons). Baseline normal Sentry behavior and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Sentry State Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes vulnerability is 'successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state'; detect appliances not enrolled in EPMM or lacking mTLS protection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Sentry/EPMM enrollment status and mTLS certificate chain for appliances. Flag any Sentry instances NOT protected by mTLS, EPMM enrollment, or restricted HTTPS access as high-risk for exploitation.

suggestion.title: Sentry Unauthenticated Request Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated user' can exploit; should alert on abnormal volume of unauthenticated requests to Sentry endpoints, especially from external sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for legitimate unauthenticated requests to Sentry (e.g., certificate pinning checks, enrollment flows). Alert on sustained spike in 401/403 responses or unauthenticated API calls from external IP space, especially if repeated payload patterns detected.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerable Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and provides template reference with CVE substitution. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite clear directive. Article states 'works...where the Sentry appliance is...externally reachable'—asset exposure is the primary defense vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry instances flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2026-10520. Correlate with firewall/network exposure data to identify internet-reachable appliances. Flag unmanaged instances per article description.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' and 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' This is execution via command injection (T1059.x), absent from pipeline kill-chain and use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for OS command injection patterns: shell metacharacters (pipe, semicolon, backtick, command substitution), environment variable expansion. Alert on deviation from baseline API traffic.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Web Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states successful exploitation 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline captured no privilege escalation or impact phase detections for post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance process logs for unexpected root-level process spawning from HTTP daemon, particularly shell invocations or binary execution outside normal maintenance windows. Baseline known legitimate root processes and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Network Reconnaissance of Exposed Ivanti Sentry Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability success depends on external reachability: 'cases where the Sentry appliance is...externally reachable.' Threat actors must first discover exposed instances. Pipeline missed discovery-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect external scanning of Ivanti Sentry: banner grabbing on typical ports (8080, 8081, 443), version detection probes against known Sentry endpoints, or service enumeration attempts. Correlate source IPs with known scanner ASNs.

suggestion.title: Bypass of mTLS / Restricted HTTPS Controls
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access...makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Successful attacks must bypass these controls. Pipeline did not surface defense-evasion use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry connections for invalid/missing mTLS certificates, HTTP-to-HTTPS downgrade attempts, or anomalous Neurons-for-MDM traffic patterns. Flag connections attempting to bypass certificate pinning.

suggestion.title: Identification of Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Configuration state is a key risk indicator. Pipeline generated zero configuration-based detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Sentry appliances for management enrollment state: flag instances not connected to EPMM, not receiving policy updates, or not reporting to Ivanti management console. Cross-reference with external network exposure.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated Command Injection Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'remote unauthenticated user' exploiting 'OS command injection' — primary attack vector with zero use-case coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST/GET requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints with shell metacharacters, backtick command substitution, or wildcard expansion in query parameters. Correlate with unexpected child processes or outbound connections from Sentry appliance.

suggestion.title: OS Command Execution from Ivanti Sentry Process
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection' vulnerability execution path — missing execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Sentry hosts: monitor for unexpected child process spawning from Sentry service parent, shell command-line flags (bash -c, sh -i, cmd /c), or process parent mismatches. Flag processes spawned from network-facing Sentry components.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Code Execution from Ivanti Sentry Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article states impact is 'root-level remote code execution' — privilege-escalation outcome undetected. No privilege-elevation use case in output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned as UID 0/SYSTEM from Sentry service context, sudoedit/sudo invocations from Sentry process, or unexpected elevation of unprivileged service accounts.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation succeeds when 'appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Article explicitly references template-based asset-exposure hunt. Foundational detection completely absent from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline hunt: enumerate all Ivanti Sentry instances with externally routable addresses, ports 443/8443 responding to internet-sourced traffic, mTLS disabled, and EPMM/Neurons integration absent. Cross-reference against CVE-2026-10520 patch status.

suggestion.title: Bypass of mTLS / Restricted HTTPS Protections
suggestion.rationale: Article describes mitigations: 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible.' No detection for adversarial bypassing of these controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry access logs for successful unauthenticated connections, TLS certificate validation failures followed by successful plaintext/weak-cipher fallback, or HTTP requests to HTTPS-only endpoints.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance + Exploitation Signal Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer' and directs asset-exposure hunt. Pipeline missed correlation between scanner 'not vulnerable' verdicts and behavioral RCE indicators—the core federated audit concern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vulnerability scanner reports Sentry as patched/unaffected but subsequent behavioral telemetry shows command-injection patterns, root process spawning, or network anomalies consistent with exploitation.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution' — must detect injection payloads in HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints before successful RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic to known Ivanti Sentry endpoints for command injection metacharacters (;, |, &, backticks, $(), `$(...)`) in URL parameters and POST bodies. Focus on publicly-exposed instances where mTLS/restricted HTTPS are not enforced.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Successful Command Injection Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' — detect successful exploitation via process execution artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected child processes spawned from Ivanti Sentry service context running as root, particularly shells (bash, sh) or system utilities (curl, wget, nc) not associated with baseline Sentry operations.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Internet-Accessible Endpoint Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — prerequisite for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset-exposure tools for externally-reachable Ivanti Sentry instances (port 443, service banners). Cross-reference against remediation due date 2026-06-14 to identify unpatched assets.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry HTTP Error Spike Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Command injection attempts frequently trigger HTTP 400/500 errors and timeouts — article attack path involves malformed parameter injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spike in 4xx/5xx responses from Sentry endpoints, especially paired with unusual parameter patterns (shell metacharacters, base64 payloads, SQL keywords). Alert on persistent scanning patterns.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Network Lateral Movement Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Once root RCE achieved ('root-level remote code execution'), attacker gains full system access for lateral movement — monitor for post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry hosts for unexpected outbound connections after anomalous process execution, particularly to internal networks. Flag SMB, SSH, or RDP connections originating from compromised appliances.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Accessibility Check
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Requires immediate network segmentation audit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Ivanti Sentry instances reachable from untrusted networks (external IPs, third-party subnets) without mTLS or restricted HTTPS enforcement. Cross-reference asset inventory tags for 'unmanaged' appliances and flag immediately.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Missing Patch Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV mandates federal patch due 2026-06-14. Article describes patched and unpatched version differentiation via configuration hardening (mTLS, restricted access). Asset vulnerability scanners must flag unpatched Sentry instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query scanners for 'CVE-2026-10520' or Ivanti Sentry version detection below patched baseline. Correlate positives with network exposure logs to rank risk. Alert on any unpatched + externally reachable combination.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Command Execution from Ivanti Sentry Context
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' permitting 'root-level remote code execution.' Successful exploitation spawns system commands under the vulnerable application context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation events where parent process matches Ivanti Sentry binaries (e.g., sentry, mobileIron) and child process is unexpected shell (/bin/sh, /bin/bash, powershell) or system command (curl, wget, nc). Baseline normal operations first to reduce FP.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Spawning from Web Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability yields 'root-level remote code execution' with no prior privilege escalation. Indicates command injection directly executing with service privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any Ivanti Sentry process (typically running as non-root service account) spawning children with root/SYSTEM-level privileges. Baseline legitimate administrative operations; anomalies warrant immediate investigation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Ivanti Sentry Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated user' as the threat actor. Exploitation requires reaching vulnerable endpoints without credentials—detectable via HTTP/HTTPS access logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor reverse proxy/WAF logs or Ivanti application logs for requests to management endpoints (e.g., /admin, /api/admin paths—exact paths vendor-dependent) from external source IPs with missing or invalid authentication headers. Correlate with vulnerability scanner hits on same IPs.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-10520 and states 'CISA KEV entry' with 'observed exploited in the wild.' No use case to detect the vulnerable product version via vulnerability scanner or asset inventory queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any Ivanti Sentry appliance (formerly MobileIron Sentry) with version vulnerable to CVE-2026-10520. Cross-reference with network exposure tools to confirm external reachability and unmanaged state (no mTLS with EPMM, no restricted HTTPS via Neurons for MDM).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - Remote Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'OS command injection vulnerability' allowing 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' No detection for malicious payloads or unusual HTTP/HTTPS request patterns targeting vulnerable endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP(S) requests to Ivanti Sentry appliances for patterns consistent with OS command injection (shell metacharacters, backticks, $(), semicolons, pipes in query parameters or POST bodies). Focus on unauthenticated access paths.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - Root-Level Command Execution Post-Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'root-level remote code execution' as the attack outcome. No use case to detect suspicious process execution spawned from the Sentry appliance with elevated privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance system logs for unexpected child processes spawned with root privileges, particularly shells (sh, bash) or command execution utilities (curl, wget, nc) launched by the Sentry service or web process.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - Unmanaged State Appliance Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability exploitable only 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Absence of use case to detect and flag at-risk configurations (no mTLS, no HTTPS restriction via Neurons).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Ivanti Sentry appliances and flag those not enrolled in or disconnected from EPMM management, lacking mTLS configuration, or not using Neurons for MDM with restricted HTTPS. Cross-reference with external port scanning or shodan data to confirm internet exposure.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 - Patch Compliance Audit
suggestion.rationale: Federal patch due-date is 2026-06-14 (article states this explicitly). No use case to audit patch status and flag non-compliant or lagging systems post-deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-remediation compliance check: verify all Ivanti Sentry appliances in fleet are patched above the CVE-2026-10520 vulnerability threshold. Alert on any unpatched instances still present after federal deadline (2026-06-14) or organizational remediation SLA.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Privilege Escalation Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'vulnerability chain lets low-privilege users take over'—direct privilege escalation vector requiring detection for exploitation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect low-privilege user or service account successfully executing privileged operations against LiteLLM gateway without prior privilege escalation event in auth logs. Monitor for unusual token elevation, access control mechanism bypass, or impersonation tokens issued to low-privileged principals.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Gateway Admin Function Access from Low-Privilege Context
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'low-privilege users' accessing gateway server functions they shouldn't—API or direct command access control bypass
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when low-privileged accounts (UIDs < threshold or service-account-like principals) invoke LiteLLM gateway admin endpoints (config, user-management, security-control APIs) that are normally restricted to admin roles. Baseline expected admin accounts first.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Configuration or Persistence Modification Post-Exploit
suggestion.rationale: 'Take over' implies establishing control—likely via configuration changes, security control disabling, or persistence mechanism installation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized modifications to LiteLLM config files (auth policies, user stores, API key lists), registry entries managing service startup, or logging/audit settings. Flag deletions of audit logs or security-relevant configs immediately post-exploit window.

suggestion.title: Execution from LiteLLM Process or Gateway Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Takeover scenario implies command execution within the compromised gateway—either lateral code execution or privilege-inherited command spawn
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal LiteLLM process tree (legitimate child processes only). Alert on unexpected child processes spawned from LiteLLM gateway service, especially command shells, PowerShell, or process-hollowing patterns. Restrict execution context to expected users/accounts.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement or Credential Access Following LiteLLM Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Gateway server takeover often precedes lateral moves to upstream services (model providers, auth backends, data stores) or credential harvesting from process memory
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual outbound connections from compromised gateway to upstream model APIs, credential managers, or data backends with unexpected authentication strings or frequency. Detect process memory scraping or API key extraction patterns in gateway logs.

suggestion.title: Denial of Service or Disruptive Actions Against Gateway After Takeover
suggestion.rationale: Post-compromise impact: attacker may disable gateway functions, corrupt routing, or cause availability damage ('take over' extends to control, which can include shutdown)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-exploit baseline: normal gateway request patterns, error rates, and available resources. Alert on sudden unavailability of LiteLLM services, mass auth failures, mass API rejections, or configuration rollbacks that disable security controls after privilege escalation event.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-20262 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and recommends asset-exposure hunt. No scanner-based detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20262 findings. Correlate with asset inventory to identify unpatched Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Managers exposed to network. Alert on any finding regardless of patch status (article notes patch lag is 'silent killer').

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'directory or path traversal vulnerability' without specifying detection method. Should monitor for exploitation attempts on exposed management interface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager for path traversal patterns (../, ..%2F, encoding variants, /etc/passwd references). Alert on any matched attempt to public-facing management port.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Creation/Overwrite on Cisco SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow...create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem' but no post-exploitation file monitoring use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager system for unexpected file creation in sensitive directories (/etc/, /var/www/, config paths). Alert on file overwrites of binaries, configs, or certificates outside normal maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Unauthenticated Access or Auth Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'authenticated' but is in CISA KEV (active wild exploitation); suggests auth bypass or exposed credentials. No auth anomaly detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate authentication patterns to Cisco SD-WAN Manager. Alert on failed auth attempts that spike, or successful logins from unexpected geos/IPs. Correlate with file modification events.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Exposure Check
suggestion.rationale: Article implies SD-WAN Manager should not be internet-exposed. Article section recommends asset-exposure hunt template but no network-exposure detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query firewall/NSM for inbound connections to SD-WAN Manager management port from untrusted networks. Cross-reference with asset inventory for expected management access patterns. Alert on any external IP reaching management interface.

suggestion.title: Typo-Squatted Package Import Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack: 'malicious Go Module Mirror's was named github.com/botdb-go/bolt, similar to the original one i.e. github.com/boltdb/bolt'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for imports or go.mod additions of package names with edit distance <3 from known high-value packages (boltdb, requests, numpy, etc.). Correlate with organization's declared dependency whitelist and flag unrecognized variants.

suggestion.title: Go Module Proxy Serving Reverted-Malicious-to-Legitimate Package
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights persistence exploit: 'Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in, and that cached the backdored module' even after source reversion, allowing malicious binary to persist in proxy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Validate Go module resolution against both source repository and cached versions. Alert when a go.mod pull resolves to a version absent from the current repository source, or when checksum mismatches between source and proxy occur.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing from Go Binary with Unknown Destination
suggestion.rationale: Article states backdoor 'allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands' — direct C2 communication from infected binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline outbound network activity from Go binaries to known package registries and mirrors. Flag connections to non-registry endpoints, especially dynamic DNS, rogue IPs, or domains without certificate matching package names.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain: Developer Dependency Update to Cached Malicious Version
suggestion.rationale: Article notes infection vector: 'we now wish to update our systems to the latest dependencies, which led developers to update the version that stayed in the system for 3 years'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor dependency update commands (go get -u, go mod tidy, npm update) and validate fetched versions against package registry API to detect cache-serving of reverted or flagged versions.

suggestion.title: Package Version Removal Event without Corresponding Binary Removal
suggestion.rationale: Article documents the gap: even after module removal from GitHub/registry, 'Go Module Proxy's indefinite caching' meant clients continued to pull infected version for 3+ years.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference package removal announcements (CVE/vulnerability DB) with running processes using those packages. Alert on execution of binaries compiled from versions flagged as removed/reverted, indicating cache-served or locally-retained malicious code.

suggestion.title: Long-Dwell Malicious Package in Registry (3-Year Persistence)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes defense-evasion success: 'went unnoticed for several years' and 'impacted thousands of organizations for over three years' — slow-burn supply chain persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package creation and modification timestamps in registries. Flag packages with long inactive periods in source repos but continued activity in caches/mirrors, or packages with sudden spike in downloads after extended dormancy.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote attacker' can 'create a file or overwrite any file' via path traversal. T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) is explicitly mapped but no detection case generated to catch exploitation patterns in logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager web server and WAF logs for path-traversal payloads (../, ..\, encoded variants, double-encoding) in HTTP requests targeting API/console endpoints. Alert on combinations of unusual directory requests + HTTP success (200/201/204) from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Unexpected File Creation/Modification on SD-WAN Manager Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'can create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem of an affected system.' No post-exploitation detection case was generated despite this being the direct impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of normal file create/modify activity on Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager servers (config directories, log rotation, updates). Alert on unexpected file creation outside maintenance windows, particularly in system directories or with suspicious extensions.

suggestion.title: Authentication Followed by File System Abuse on SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated, remote attacker' but no detection correlates successful login to post-auth suspicious behavior. Enables identification of compromised or default credentials being exploited.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful authentication to SD-WAN Manager with subsequent file system events or API calls outside normal admin/automation patterns. Baseline expected post-auth activity (config reads, status checks) and alert on deviation or activity inconsistent with role.

suggestion.title: Exposed Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' template and federal patch deadline (2026-06-29). No use case generated to identify or prioritize unpatched instances across fleet despite CISA KEV indicating active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances with CVE-2026-20262. Cross-reference patch dates against federal deadline and flag unpatched systems exposed to remote access. Correlate with network telemetry to confirm internet-facing exposure.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Path Traversal Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'directory or path traversal vulnerability' allowing file write — no detection use case generated for the core exploitation technique despite clear URI-based attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager HTTP(S) traffic for path traversal indicators (../, ..\, %2e%2e, double-encoding) in URI paths and parameters. Alert on requests containing filepath escape sequences attempting directory traversal outside application root.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Creation on SD-WAN Manager Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker 'could create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem' — no post-exploitation file activity detection exists despite explicit impact description.

High specificity if initiating-process UID differs (browser→node context switch).

suggestion.title: Compromised Service Account Email Access Post-Rule Creation
suggestion.rationale: GWS admins or service accounts with broad mailbox access may be compromised to establish rule-based forwarding at scale. Article targets 'research and defense'—suggests targeting of multiple high-value mailboxes, likely via service-account abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on service accounts or admin accounts accessing 10+ distinct user mailboxes within a 1-hour window, especially if followed by rule creation in those mailboxes. Correlate with lateral movement indicators (impossible travel, unusual login geo, device changes).

suggestion.title: Hidden Folder Creation for Rule-Based Email Staging
suggestion.rationale: Advanced attackers create hidden or non-standard folders (e.g., named with spaces, Unicode, or system-reserved names) to stage emails collected via rules before forwarding. This obscures the attack from casual review.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of Gmail labels/folders with suspicious naming patterns (spaces-only, Unicode characters, system folders like '[Gmail]' modifications) that co-occur with rule creation or large email moves.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise - Developer Tool Repository Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'developer tools' are being turned into 'malware delivery channels' — requires detection of malicious packages/updates in public/private repos or mirrors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package repositories (npm, PyPI, NuGet, etc.) and local package caches for unexpected checksums, signature validation failures, or suspicious post-install scripts. Flag developer tools receiving updates from non-canonical sources or with altered manifests.

suggestion.title: Trojanized Developer Tool Execution - Process Spawning & Network Callbacks
suggestion.rationale: Weaponized developer tools must execute malware payloads; article implies tools are being delivered and run by developers unaware of compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect developer tools (IDEs, build tools, package managers) spawning unexpected child processes, especially shells (cmd.exe, PowerShell, bash) or creating network connections to non-standard infrastructure. Baseline normal tool behavior and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Developer Credential Harvesting from Tool Memory/Config
suggestion.rationale: Compromised developer tools with access to source repos, CI/CD, cloud credentials — article implies tools are being leveraged to steal credentials from development workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor processes spawned by developer tools accessing credential stores (git config, .aws/, .kube/, token files). Flag unexpected credential reads from tools that should not need them. Alert on dev tool processes reading from registry/filesystem where SSH keys or API tokens are stored.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Build/CI Pipeline
suggestion.rationale: Developer tools often integrate with CI/CD systems; compromise of tools implies potential pipeline abuse to propagate to downstream builds or internal infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual commands or scripts injected into CI/CD workflows, unexpected checkout of private repositories, or credential exfiltration through build logs. Monitor for dev tool processes authenticating to internal infrastructure or cloud platforms using harvested credentials.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion - Unsigned or Tampered Developer Tool Binaries
suggestion.rationale: North Korean attackers distributing tools imply signature stripping or tamper to evade detection by endpoint security; article indicates tools are bypassing security controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on developer tool binaries with missing or invalid digital signatures, unsigned DLLs loaded by dev tools, or tools with mismatched metadata (version, publisher). Monitor for dev tools executing from temporary locations or with renamed/obfuscated filenames.

suggestion.title: Command & Control via Developer Tool Callbacks
suggestion.rationale: Article describes tools as 'malware delivery channels' — implies embedded C2 or callback functionality in weaponized tools for post-exploitation communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline network behavior of legitimate developer tools (package manager registries, update servers). Alert on dev tool processes contacting non-canonical IPs, suspicious domains, or obfuscated C2 infrastructure. Monitor for encrypted or tunnel-based comms from dev tool processes.

suggestion.title: Low-Privilege Process Escalation in LiteLLM Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Low-Privilege Users Take Over AI Gateway Servers'—this is a direct privilege escalation attack that requires detection. Pipeline produced zero UCs to capture this core attack path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unprivileged user processes spawning system-level child processes or accessing restricted gateway configuration. Flag token elevation events where a low-privilege account suddenly gains admin-level permissions in LiteLLM daemon context.

suggestion.title: Exploited Vulnerability Chain in LiteLLM Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'vulnerability chain'—implies sequential CVE exploitation. Pipeline failed to identify execution-phase exploitation patterns or version-specific attack sequences.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor LiteLLM HTTP access logs for exploitation signatures: malformed API requests, path traversal attempts, or parameter injection targeting known vulnerable versions. Alert on successful exploitation indicators (500→200 status transitions, unexpected child process spawning).

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Lateral Movement from Compromised Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article states takeover of 'servers' (plural), suggesting lateral movement post-escalation. Pipeline identified no impact-phase or lateral-movement tactics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor compromised LiteLLM gateway for outbound SSH/RDP connections to internal hosts, unusual proxy or tunnel creation, and authentication patterns attempting to breach other AI services or infrastructure using stolen gateway credentials.

suggestion.title: WinRAR Archive Extraction with Embedded Executable Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'WinRAR Flaw Exploited...to Deploy Stealers.' Pipeline missed the delivery/execution vector—archive extraction abuse with embedded malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WinRAR/unrar process extraction of archives containing executables; alert on WinRAR spawning cmd.exe, PowerShell, or rundll32 as immediate child. Flag suspicious parent processes (Outlook, Teams, web browsers) launching WinRAR with archives from unexpected paths.

suggestion.title: Credential Stealer Behavior — LSASS/Clipboard/Browser Profile Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: stealers deployed post-WinRAR. Pipeline identified zero collection-phase detections for harvesting browser passwords, clipboard, registry SAM, or LSASS memory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned from archive-extraction chains attempting access to LSASS, registry credential stores (SAM/SECURITY), AppData\Local\*\User Data, or clipboard APIs. Flag sequential file opens to browser credential DBs.

suggestion.title: Stealer Exfiltration to C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article targets Ukraine with stealer payloads; no C2 communication detection generated. Exfiltration channels are core to measuring breach scope and attribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate newly spawned executables from archive-extraction chains with large-volume HTTPS/HTTP POST requests to non-standard ports or newly registered domains. Alert on Cyrillic-alphabet domain registrations; DNS queries for bulk domain lists.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Using Harvested Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Ukraine-targeted campaign implies infrastructure compromise; pipeline missed post-stealer lateral-movement detection using exfiltrated credentials for domain pivot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for logon events using credentials matching stealer-harvested usernames from different source IPs or non-business hours. Flag Kerberoasting (T1558.001) or pass-the-hash attempts correlating with stealer execution timeline.

suggestion.title: WinRAR Vulnerability Version Detection with Suspicious Extraction Ancestry
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies WinRAR flaw as attack vector; pipeline absent any CVE-version matching or artifact correlation logic for vulnerable WinRAR execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate WinRAR process version (vulnerable < patch X) with archive extraction of files containing embedded executables. Alert on extraction from temp/downloads folders or initiated by email/web clients.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Persistence via Registry/Startup Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Stealer malware establishes persistence; article describes initial compromise but pipeline missed run-key/scheduled-task injection indicators for sustained access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag registry modifications to HKCU/HKLM Run/RunOnce, Startup folder writes, or WMI event subscription creation by processes spawned from archive-extraction chains. Alert if parent process context deviates from expected auto-start locations.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Internet-Accessible Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'could allow an authenticated, remote attacker'—implying exposed management interface. CISA KEV entries are actively exploited; asset inventory is the immediate control. Detection of externally reachable instances is the baseline hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances accessible over internet on management ports (typically 443/TCP). Correlate with vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20262 patch status. Use port-scan enrichment (Shodan, Censys), DNS reverse-lookup, and internal asset inventory to establish baseline of exposed instances and priority remediation targets.

suggestion.title: Exploitation: Path Traversal Attack Pattern in HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability vector: 'directory or path traversal vulnerability.' Exploitation will manifest as characteristic path-escape patterns in application logs. Phrase: 'directory or path traversal vulnerability'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request logs on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager endpoints for path-traversal indicators: ../ sequences, ..\, encoded variants (%2e%2e%2f), or unicode/null-byte escapes in URI parameters. Spike in 401/403 errors followed by 200 responses, or unusual directory access patterns, may indicate exploit attempts. Baseline expected URIs per deployment to flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Impact: Unauthorized File Creation/Overwrite on SD-WAN Manager Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Explicit impact: 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem of an affected system.' Post-exploitation monitoring for filesystem tampering is critical for damage assessment and persistence detection. Phrase: 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation/modification events on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager systems, prioritizing config directories, executable paths, and authentication stores. Flag unexpected file types (executables, scripts) in data directories, modifications by unexpected user accounts, and bulk file operations. Establish file integrity baselines (checksums) for critical system files and alert on divergence.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: Service Restart and Configuration Corruption Signals
suggestion.rationale: File overwrites via path traversal may corrupt config files or binaries, triggering service instability. Product criticality (SD-WAN Manager) makes uptime anomalies reliable compromise indicators. Phrase: 'overwrite any file on the filesystem' combined with critical infrastructure context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected service restarts, crashes, or high-error rates on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager systems following successful authentication events. Compare configuration snapshots before/after suspicious sessions. Unplanned service interruptions combined with filesystem modifications within the same session indicate likely exploitation.

suggestion.title: Credential Abuse: Authenticated Sessions to SD-WAN Manager with Unusual Characteristics
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires authentication; actively exploited KEV suggests compromised or weak credentials in use. Session anomalies are early signals. Phrase: 'authenticated, remote attacker'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Catalyst SD-WAN Manager authentication logs for: failed login spikes followed by success (credential guessing), logins from unusual geographies/IPs, service-account logins with interactive activity, sustained sessions outside business hours, or rapid successive logins. Baseline normal access patterns per role/admin and alert on deviation. Correlate with file-modification events.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Confidence Gap: CVE-2026-20262 Patch Verification
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV note: 'even if your scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, it's worth one quick check—patch lag is the silent killer.' Scanners may lag or misreport. Direct verification closes gaps. Phrase: 'patch lag is the silent killer'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-check vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20262 against actual running software versions on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances (via software inventory, service fingerprinting, or authenticated patch-level queries). Flag false-negatives: systems scanner marks patched but version check confirms vulnerable. Prioritize instances where scanner and inventory disagree.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerability Scanner Hit
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends substituting CVE into standard vulnerability-scanner template; pipeline generated no detection for systems flagged by scanners.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when any vulnerability scanner (Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7, etc.) detects CVE-2026-20262 on Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. Cross-reference scan timestamps with authentication logs to prioritize assets with recent access.

suggestion.title: Exposed Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability requires 'remote attacker' access; asset exposure hunt is explicitly recommended per template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances exposed on routable internet addresses via certificate transparency logs, port-scan telemetry, DNS records resolving to public IPs, and continuous monitoring of externally-reachable Catalyst endpoints.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'directory or path traversal vulnerability'; should detect exploitation attempts with path-traversal sequences in HTTP requests to the service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager for path traversal payloads (../, ..\ variants, unicode/encoding bypasses, null bytes). Flag requests with unusual URL depth or filesystem-path references (etc/passwd, windows/system32, boot files).

suggestion.title: Unexpected File Creation by SD-WAN Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'; post-exploitation file writes are the observable impact of successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file-creation or file-modification events from Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN processes (or parent web-service processes) writing to sensitive directories (/etc, /boot, Windows\System32) or overwriting system binaries, configuration files, or audit logs.

suggestion.title: Bulk File Overwrites from Web Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal exploitation typically leaves footprints in file-write patterns; article emphasizes 'overwrite any file' capability suggesting enumeration or intentional destruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous file-write volume or rate from Catalyst SD-WAN processes over short time windows. Flag patterns consistent with directory traversal enumeration (sequential file access across tree) or targeted log/config destruction (rapid overwrites of audit/config locations).

suggestion.title: Authentication Spike to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated, remote attacker'; exploitation requires valid credentials or successful auth bypass; baseline deviation indicates potential compromise attempt timing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline login/session-initiation volume to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager by source, time-of-day, and geography. Alert on spikes, failed-to-successful transitions, or activity sourced from ASNs with no historical access. Compare patterns before/after patch due-date (2026-06-29); post-deadline spikes suggest unpatched systems under active reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Typo-Squatted Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The malicious Go Module Mirror's was named github.com/botdb-go/bolt, similar to the original one i.e. github.com/boltdb/bolt.' Typo squatting is the explicit attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor go.mod imports for package names with minimal edit distance (1-3 chars substitution/transposition) from known-good registry packages. Flag when 'botdb-go/bolt', 'boltdb-go/bolt', or similar variants appear in dependency trees alongside or instead of legitimate 'boltdb/bolt'.

suggestion.title: Malicious Module Persistence via Proxy Caching
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in, and that cached the backdored module... developers to update the version that stayed in the system for 3 years.' Caching enabled multi-year undetected compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Go module proxy cache hits for package versions explicitly marked as revoked, removed, or superseded in advisory databases. Flag version rollback or re-activation patterns where a cached variant resurfaces after official removal from repositories.

suggestion.title: Go Module Backdoor C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'This backdoor allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands i.e. via a command and control server.' Explicit C2 capability within module initialization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate outbound network connections from Go runtime processes against imports of github.com/botdb-go/bolt v1.3.1. Flag DNS queries or HTTP(S) to C2 infrastructure triggered during module load/init phases. Monitor for process spawning or privilege escalation following backdoor initialization.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Similarity Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article describes typo-squatting pattern: 'bad actors create and upload harmful software packages to online libraries using names very similar to popular ones. They hope people will mistakenly download and install these dangerous versions instead of the legitimate software they thought.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest active go.mod/go.sum files and compute Levenshtein distance between imported paths and legitimate packages in public Go registry. Alert on imports where distance is 1-3 edits from a known legitimate package, especially for common libraries (database, HTTP, crypto).

suggestion.title: Weak-Maintenance Dependency Supply Chain Risk
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'over 80+ unresolved issues in the original repository since 2015' and compromise persisted 3+ years. Weak maintenance correlates with higher compromise risk and delayed detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag production dependencies with >24 months age, zero commits, >50 open issues, or no published security patches. Cross-reference against CVE/advisory databases. Alert on sudden re-activation of old unmaintained versions after security removals.

suggestion.title: Go Module Proxy Cache Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Module was cached on Go Module Proxy, which continued to serve clients' and 'Malicious packages can still be searchable on Go Module Proxy' after removal — cache continued poisoning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go module proxy requests for package versions explicitly delisted or removed from official registries. Detect timing anomalies where a revoked version reappears or continues being served. Flag requests to non-standard/mirror proxy instances serving known-malicious packages.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerability Scan Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-20262 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt'. Pipeline generated zero hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances returning CVE-2026-20262 as exploitable or unpatched. Correlate with external network exposure via asset management tools. Federal due date 2026-06-29 provides urgency for triage.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Internet Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article implies SD-WAN Manager is 'public-facing' (T1190) and vulnerable to remote authenticated attack. Pipeline missed asset-exposure correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco SD-WAN Manager instances listening on internet-routable IPs (not behind VPN/bastion). Cross-reference with authentication logs for brute-force attempts or credential reuse patterns from breach databases.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Filesystem Write Events
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows attacker to 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'. Pipeline missed post-exploitation impact detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager process for unexpected file writes or overwrites outside normal application paths. Flag modifications to web-accessible directories, config files, or binary paths as high-severity.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Authentication Logs Spike
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is authenticated-access only ('authenticated, remote attacker'). Pipeline missed reconnaissance / credential-testing phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Spike in failed login attempts against SD-WAN Manager UI or API endpoints, especially from external IPs or novel source geographies, preceding successful exploitation. Correlate with known-compromised credential disclosure.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Directory Traversal Request Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability specifically named 'directory or path traversal'. Pipeline missed request-pattern exploitation detection that doesn't require successful filesystem write.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP(S) requests to SD-WAN Manager containing path traversal sequences ('../', '..\\', '%2e%2e', unicode variants) in URI or POST parameters. Filter to authenticated sessions or known attacker IPs for medium confidence; unauthenticated attempts are high confidence.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Emergency Patch Verification
suggestion.rationale: Federal due date 2026-06-29 provided in article. Pipeline missed deadline-driven remediation hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query CMDB/asset management for all Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances and their patch version. Verify CVE-2026-20262 fix is applied (vendor patch details required). Flag instances unpatched within 14 days of due date as regulatory risk.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Account Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'authenticated, remote attacker' — pipeline must hunt for compromised admin accounts. No detection offered for unusual login patterns, failed-auth-then-success sequences, or credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager authentication logs for successful logins from new source IPs, unusual times, or after multiple failed attempts. Correlate with vulnerability scanner alerts for CVE-2026-20262. Flag rapid-fire login attempts or privilege escalation within admin console immediately post-exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal File Creation on SD-WAN Manager Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem' — this is the direct exploitation artifact. Pipeline provides no file-integrity or process-execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager host filesystem for unexpected file creation in system directories (/etc, /opt, /var/spool, /lib), particularly shell scripts or config overwrites. Track process execution spawned from web-server service accounts. Alert on suspicious cron job injection or systemd unit file modifications.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Initiation from Compromised SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article implies persistence/RCE potential via filesystem write. Pipeline missed that successful exploitation grants foothold for pivot. No detection for network connections, credential theft, or scanning initiated from SD-WAN manager.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for outbound connections from SD-WAN Manager host. Alert on new outbound SSH, RDP, or HTTP to internal assets post-CVE-2026-20262 exploitation window. Correlate with host-based execution events (new processes, reverse shells, credential-dumping tools) to confirm lateral-movement chain.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Persistence Mechanism Detection
suggestion.rationale: Filesystem write capability implies attacker plants backdoors or persistence agents. Article does not specify detection for webshells, reverse tunnels, or scheduled tasks — critical for containment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for new cron jobs, systemd timers, or scheduled tasks created on SD-WAN Manager post-compromise. Look for startup scripts added to /etc/init.d or .bashrc injection. Cross-reference with file integrity baselines to detect unauthorized persistence hooks planted via path-traversal write.

suggestion.title: Critical System File Overwrite Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal to 'any file on the filesystem' includes /etc/passwd, /etc/sudoers, SAM registry — core privilege-escalation and access-control vectors. Pipeline offers no FIM-based detection for these sensitive targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for write attempts to authentication/authorization files (/etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/sudoers, Windows SAM, SYSTEM registry). Enforce file-integrity monitoring with immutable attributes or SELinux AppArmor controls. Alert immediately on successful overwrites with severity CRITICAL and escalate to incident response.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Exploitation Pattern Cluster
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline did not correlate authentication anomalies + file creation + outbound connections into a multi-stage exploitation pattern. Composite detection increases confidence and reduces alert fatigue.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create correlation rule: failed-auth attempts → successful login from new IP → file creation in system directories → outbound connection within 1-hour window on SD-WAN Manager. Any 3+ of 4 events = probable exploitation. Assign CRITICAL severity; auto-isolate or require immediate SOC review.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances via port scanning, API discovery, or CMDB. Cross-reference against CISA KEV due-date 2026-06-29 to identify unpatched assets. Alert on any instance still running vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Exploitation Attempt Detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager management interfaces for HTTP requests with path traversal payloads (../, ..\) or directory-access indicators targeting configuration or system files.

suggestion.title: File Creation/Overwrite on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Catalyst SD-WAN Manager logs for unexpected file creation or modification in system/configuration directories, especially writes from web server processes or authenticated sessions. Alert on modifications to startup scripts or binaries.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-20262 Asset Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists under 'Indicators of Compromise': 'CVE-2026-20262 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and directs use of asset-exposure template. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this directive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management system for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances with CVE-2026-20262 flagged exploited-in-wild. suggestion.title: Authenticated Access to SD-WAN Manager Followed by Unauthorized File Write

suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Directory or Path Traversal Vulnerability' as attack vector. Pipeline did not generate detection for traversal payload patterns in HTTP requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Cisco SD-WAN Manager for path traversal indicators: ../ and ..\\ sequences, URL-encoded variants (%2e%2e%2f, %252e%252e%252f), null-byte injection (%00), or symlink creation attempts in URI or POST body. Alert on external-origin requests and restrict by approved geolocation/ASN.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process Spawning from SD-WAN Manager App
suggestion.rationale: File-write capability on control-plane asset enables command execution. Article implies post-compromise impact but pipeline did not infer execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Cisco SD-WAN Manager hosts, flag if web application service account spawns shells (bash, /bin/sh, cmd.exe, powershell), utilities (nc, curl, wget, ssh), or compilers. suggestion.rationale: Article identifies Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager as actively exploited target with federal patch due 2026-06-29; no asset discovery use case generated despite infrastructure criticality. 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date.'

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager - Credential Compromise and Suspicious Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated, remote attacker' but provides no detection for credential compromise, brute force, or valid-account abuse preceding exploitation. Authentication context is essential for baseline and detection.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager - Log and Security Control Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attacker can 'overwrite any file'; if security logs, audit trails, or monitoring configs are targeted, evidence destruction and lateral movement are enabled. No detection for suspicious overwrites of defensive artifacts.

Flag truncated logs, timestamp anomalies, or permission elevation. Correlate overwrites with prior path traversal and auth events.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager - Patch Remediation Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Federal patch deadline is 2026-06-29, 14 days from publication. No remediation tracking use case provided despite time-critical compliance requirement and active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results (Nessus, Qualys, etc.) for CVE-2026-20262 detections by scan date. Verify patch deployment against patch management logs. suggestion.title: Authenticated Remote Access to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Before Exploitation

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Catalyst SD-WAN Manager authentication logs for successful remote logins from unusual geographies, IPs, or at unusual times. suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts Against SD-WAN Manager

suggestion.title: Unexpected File Creation/Overwrite in Catalyst SD-WAN Manager System Directories

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected file creation, modification, or deletion in Catalyst SD-WAN Manager binary directories, configuration paths, and system-critical locations (/bin, /etc, /lib). suggestion.title: High-Frequency JavaScript Timing API Abuse

Baseline normal timing-API usage per domain and alert on orders-of-magnitude increases. Correlate with POST requests exfiltrating timing arrays.

suggestion.title: Timing-Data Exfiltration from Web Pages
suggestion.rationale: Attack outcome stated as 'websites track...what apps you open'—requires attacker to collect and exfiltrate timing profiles correlating file access with application signatures. 'Track' implies data exfiltration of inferred behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for structured POST/WebSocket messages containing arrays of numeric values (timing deltas) from untrusted origins. Detect beacons to atypical C2 ports/protocols. Correlate exfiltration with pages that previously triggered high-frequency timing measurements.

suggestion.title: Application/File Enumeration via SSD Access-Time Inference
suggestion.rationale: Article phrase 'can track what sites and apps you open'—attacker must build correlation model between file-access timing patterns and installed applications. This enumeration/discovery phase should be detectable through file-system or driver-level monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of rapid file-open/close operations (stat calls, directory enumerations) followed by timing measurements, originating from browser process or JavaScript context. Flag patterns consistent with building application-to-timing-signature mappings (e.g., repeated attempts to access known app paths: Program Files, /Applications, ~/.config).

suggestion.title: Initial Access: Attacker-Hosted Malicious Web Page

suggestion.title: Lateral movement detection within initial access window

suggestion.title: AI/automation evasion tactics in rapid-response environment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'AI-driven automation' as modern SOC capability; implies attackers may use obfuscation or timing-based evasion to bypass automated detection within 72-minute window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for living-off-the-land binaries (LOLBins) executed with encoded/obfuscated arguments, DLL injection, or process hollowing. Monitor for rapid tool execution chains designed to evade signature-based detection. Flag cleanup activity (log deletion, temp file removal) within 72-minute post-breach window.

suggestion.title: Vitest Browser Mode API launched bound to non-loopback interface

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor node/npm/yarn/pnpm processes executing Vitest with --browser.api.host=0.0.0.0 or equivalent non-loopback binding. Non-loopback binding exposes the CDP proxy to network attackers.

suggestion.title: Inbound network connections to Vitest Browser Mode listener port (TCP 63315)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exposed API; port 63315 is the default listener. Any non-loopback inbound connection is an attack surface. UC_4_4 marked in article but absent from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on RemoteIPType != Loopback inbound connections to TCP 63315 where source is not 127.0.0.1 or ::1. Vitest Browser Mode should only accept local connections.

suggestion.rationale: Article attack prerequisite: browser process must load @vitest/@playwright modules to execute malicious plugin code. suggestion.title: Download and Execution of Trojanized Developer Tool Distribution

suggestion.title: Suspicious binding.gyp Execution During npm Install

suggestion.title: Authentication Anomaly: Successful Authentication to SD-WAN Manager by Unauthorized Accounts

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scan Match: CVE-2026-20262 Detection in Scanner Output
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'CVE-2026-20262' explicitly and mandates federal patch by 2026-06-29. Simplest detection: direct scanner correlation. Pipeline produced no IOCs or use cases for vulnerability matching despite CISA KEV template recommending this.

suggestion.title: HTTP Error Logging: 400/403/404 Patterns Indicating Directory Enum or Access Denied
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal and directory traversal exploits often generate HTTP error codes (403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found) when attackers probe non-existent paths or trigger access control checks. suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Write to SD-WAN Manager Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'could allow an authenticated, remote attacker to create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'. Pipeline missed file-creation/modification detection entirely.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Authentication to Exposed SD-WAN Manager
