suggestion.title: Authenticated Remote Access Abuse – SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability requires 'authenticated, remote attacker.' CISA KEV exploitation implies either auth-bypass or legitimate-credential abuse. Pipeline skipped credential/privilege detection layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager authentication logs for failed login spikes, password spraying, or rapid sequential login attempts. Establish baseline for admin access pattern (time-of-day, geolocation, device type). Flag authentications outside baseline, especially if followed by HTTP traversal patterns or unusual config-push activity.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Lateral Movement from SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: SD-WAN Manager is a network orchestration control point. Article does not preclude post-compromise lateral movement or device-wide provisioning attacks after file-write. Pipeline missed command-and-control or lateral-movement detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from SD-WAN Manager to non-standard ports or unexpected internal subnets. Flag any configuration-push or device-provisioning events to edge SD-WAN routers that were not preceded by administrative change request. Detect East-West traffic initiated from Manager that deviates from baseline orchestration patterns.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Detection – CVE-2026-20262
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates CVSS match: 'worth one quick check across your fleet.' Pipeline extracted zero IOC for automated scanner correlation despite this being the primary detection vector for KEV entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner detection of CVE-2026-20262 on Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. Treat as critical; corroborate scanner result even if asset appears patched (patch-lag is cited as 'silent killer'). Validate actual running version against scanner output and patch manifest. Assign to response queue with federal deadline 2026-06-29 as escalation trigger.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Patch Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'patch lag is the silent killer' and explicitly recommends asset-exposure hunts with CVE matching. No use case was generated for scanner/inventory detection of this exploited vulnerability despite being the article's core ask.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and CMDB for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances and their patch status relative to CVE-2026-20262 baseline. Flag any host not patched before federal due date 2026-06-29. Correlate with Shodan/Censys for public-facing instances.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Unexpected File Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'could allow...create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem.' Pipeline missed the impact detection; behavioral detection for file modification is critical for post-exploitation forensics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager process (typically running as restricted service account) for file creation/modification outside expected configuration directories (/opt/cisco/csd-wm/, /etc/cisco/, /var/cisco/). Alert on unexpected .jar/.conf/.sh/.xml creation by sd-wan-related processes.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Attempt Against Cisco SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly involves 'directory or path traversal'—pipeline missed the behavioral precursor detection. Traversal patterns (../ sequences, encoded dots) in HTTP requests should trigger before successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Cisco SD-WAN Manager containing traversal patterns: %2e%2e, %252e, \.., ..\, or encoded variants in URI path or parameters. Correlate with successful 200/302 responses and subsequent file-system events.

suggestion.title: Authenticated Session + File Manipulation Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated, remote attacker'—detection should correlate successful login sessions with anomalous file-system or network-config modifications during same session window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful SSH/HTTPS authentication to Cisco SD-WAN Manager with file creation/modification events within 5-minute window. Flag if user/service account is not in approved admin list or modification touches critical files (.conf, routing tables, certificate stores).

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'authenticated, remote attacker' to exploit, implying exposed internet-facing assets. 'CISA KEV entry...only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild' demands immediate asset visibility before federal due date 2026-06-29.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances accessible from untrusted networks via port scans or cloud service discovery. Correlate asset inventory against vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20262 presence. Flag all detected instances as tier-1 remediation priority.

suggestion.title: File Creation/Modification Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker can 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem of an affected system.' File system artifacts are critical for both forensic investigation and real-time detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager system file events for unexpected creation or modification of system binaries, configuration files, or web root paths. Alert on any file writes to sensitive directories post-exploitation window or outside change management windows.

suggestion.title: Authentication Events to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires authentication: 'authenticated, remote attacker.' Establishing baseline and detecting anomalies in auth patterns identifies credential misuse or brute-force activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline and monitor successful and failed authentication events to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager APIs and web interface. Alert on failed attempts followed by success, lateral auth from untrusted source IPs, or authentication outside business hours.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Pattern Detection in HTTP Logs
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability name explicitly calls out 'directory or path traversal.' Classic exploitation pattern detectable via URL-encoded and raw ../ sequences in HTTP requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager for path traversal indicators: ../, ..\, %2e%2e, unicode-encoded variants, and backslash-encoded equivalents in URL paths and parameters. Cross-reference with known vulnerable endpoint paths from vendor advisories.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Web Request Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Exploit delivery manifests as HTTP requests to public-facing application. Anomalous request patterns (unusual HTTP methods, payload sizes, parameters) during active exploitation windows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of normal HTTP methods, user-agents, content-types, and request patterns to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager endpoints. Alert on non-standard HTTP methods (PUT, DELETE, PATCH), oversized payloads, or requests to administrative endpoints from untrusted source IPs.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure - Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager (CVE-2026-20262)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in template. Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>'. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this direct guidance and CRITICAL/KEV status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify exposed Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances by scanning for service presence, version enumeration, and build identifiers. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner logs (Qualys, Nessus, Rapid7) for CVE-2026-20262 detection. Correlate with network-accessible instances on standard ports (8443, 443).

suggestion.title: Path Traversal - File Write/Create (CVE-2026-20262)
suggestion.rationale: Article states the vulnerability 'could allow authenticated, remote attacker to create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'. This describes the core exploitation mechanism—path traversal payload execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager API/web endpoints for HTTP requests containing path traversal sequences (../, ..\, %2e%2e, unicode variants) in URI or POST parameters. Flag requests that attempt filesystem writes outside documented application directories. Correlate with downstream file creation events on the SD-WAN Manager host.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via File Overwrite (CVE-2026-20262)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the vulnerability allows overwriting 'any file on the filesystem', implying potential for configuration, credential, or privilege-escalation file targets. Requires detection of post-exploitation file modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful CVE-2026-20262 exploitation attempts with subsequent file modifications in sensitive directories (etc/passwd equivalents, application config, web roots, cron/systemd jobs). Flag file overwrites with suspicious ownership/permissions changes or new executable writes to startup paths.

suggestion.title: WinRAR Exploit Archive Extraction and Suspicious Child Process
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'WinRAR Flaw Exploited' — no detection for the vulnerability weaponization itself. Should detect vulnerable WinRAR versions processing archives followed by unexpected child process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WinRAR/unrar.exe processing archives; alert when followed by child process creation (especially cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or unsigned executables) or direct writes to System32/Temp. Cross-check WinRAR version against known-vulnerable CVE (likely CVE-2023-38831 or similar pathtraversal variant).

suggestion.title: Stealer Malware Credential Access Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'deploy Stealers' — pipeline missed this payload class entirely. Stealers characteristically enumerate browser storage, LSASS, and credential manager.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process access to LSASS (excluding expected services), enumeration of HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings, or browser credential DB reads (chrome/edge/firefox data folders). Flag unsigned exe from temp directories performing these actions.

suggestion.title: Stealer Exfiltration to Russia-Aligned C2
suggestion.rationale: Stealer payloads require C2 contact; article specifies 'Russia-aligned' actors — no detection for victim-to-C2 exfiltration channels or geolocation-anomalous traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS POST requests from temp-spawned processes to newly-registered or Russia-hosted/bulletproof-hosting domains. Detect exfiltration-sized data transfer (>10MB) to non-CDN, non-corporate destinations. Correlate with stealer process identifiers and credential-like payload patterns.

suggestion.title: Ukraine-Targeting WinRAR Phishing Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies Ukraine as specific target and Russia-aligned actors — no delivery detection. Initial access likely phishing with weaponized archive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound email to Ukrainian domains/recipients with .rar/.zip attachments. Hash check archives against known exploit samples. Flag Ukrainian-language lures or spearphishing indicators (personnel names, entity references). Cross-reference sender IP geolocation and domain reputation.

suggestion.title: WinRAR CVE Post-Exploit Registry Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Stealer malware requires persistence post-exploitation — no detection for registry modification or scheduled-task injection commonly used by this threat class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registry writes to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run, HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, or HKCR\exefile\shell\open\command following WinRAR exploitation. Detect schtasks.exe or at.exe spawned by non-admin processes. Alert on base64-encoded or obfuscated payload in registry values.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-20262 Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' with template substitution for CVE-2026-20262. CISA KEV status means active exploitation observed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances. Cross-reference against patch inventory to identify systems running versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-20262. Prioritize external-facing instances.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt: Path Traversal Patterns in SD-WAN Manager HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'path traversal' and attackers can 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'. Monitor inbound HTTP/API for traversal exploitation signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP or REST API requests to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager containing path traversal sequences (../, .., %2e%2e, unicode encoding variants). Flag requests originating from authenticated sessions.

suggestion.title: Post-Authentication File System Anomalies: Unexpected Writes After SD-WAN Manager Login
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires 'authenticated, remote attacker' and yields ability to 'overwrite any file on the filesystem'. Monitor filesystem for suspicious writes post-successful authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or modification operations by Catalyst SD-WAN Manager processes outside expected application directories (system paths, binaries, configs). Correlate with successful authentication + path-traversal HTTP patterns.

suggestion.title: Credential Compromise Prerequisite: Brute Force / MFA Bypass Targeting SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires valid credentials. Article specifies 'authenticated, remote attacker', implying credential acquisition is the prerequisite attack step before path-traversal exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor failed login attempts to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager for brute-force patterns. Alert on successful logins from unusual geolocations, times, or IP ranges. Detect MFA bypass attempts or anomalous token usage.

suggestion.title: Log Tampering: Deletion/Overwrite of Audit Logs via Path Traversal
suggestion.rationale: File-overwrite capability enables deletion of audit evidence. Attackers often erase logs post-exploitation (T1070). Article's 'overwrite any file' phrasing suggests this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious deletion, truncation, or overwrite of SD-WAN Manager application logs, system audit logs, or authentication logs. Alert on gaps in audit trail during suspected exploitation windows.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Public Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability affects internet-facing instances; 'could allow an authenticated, remote attacker' establishes that public reachability is the prerequisite for exploitation. MITRE T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) was called out but no corresponding detection hunt was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful HTTP/HTTPS connections to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager web interfaces from untrusted/external networks. Cross-reference open ports and SSL certificates for instances that should be internal-only. Flag any publicly routable instances for immediate access review.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Payload Detection on SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'directory or path traversal vulnerability...create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem.' Pipeline left kill-chain reconstruction empty despite explicit file-system impact description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Cisco SD-WAN Manager endpoints for path-traversal patterns (../, ..\, unicode/encoding variants, etc.). Correlate with authentication events to detect exploit attempts, particularly if 'authenticated' attack path involves pre-auth bypass or stolen credentials.

suggestion.title: Unexpected File Write Operations on SD-WAN Manager Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies impact as 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem.' No use-case generated for post-exploitation detection despite clear file-system IOAs described.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager system for unexpected file creation/modification events, especially in web-server directories, config folders, and system paths. Baseline normal file operations and alert on anomalous write patterns following HTTP requests with path-traversal signatures.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerability Scan Matches
suggestion.rationale: Article is a CISA KEV entry; 'CISA KEV entry...only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild.' Pipeline generated zero IOCs; CVE-2026-20262 should be a primary vulnerability indicator for scanner correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match vulnerability scanner findings against CVE-2026-20262. Flag any systems running Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager with a scanned date after 2026-06-15 that have not been verified as patched. Federal agencies must remediate by 2026-06-29; similar urgency applies to private sector.

suggestion.title: Authentication Anomalies Against SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'authenticated, remote attacker.' Pipeline did not assess whether 'authenticated' means pre-auth bypass, credential reuse, or brute-force compromise. Omission of auth-layer detection despite this being the attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager authentication logs for: failed login attempts from external sources, successful logins followed by rapid anomalous API/file operations, concurrent logins from disparate IPs, or attempts using default/recycled credentials. Correlate with path-traversal detection to identify exploit sequences.

suggestion.title: Wallpaper Engine Spawning Suspicious Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article phrase: 'Application wallpapers are essentially standalone programs' and 'allows foreign code to be run directly on your computer.' Execution mechanism is core to the attack; pipeline generated zero execution detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Wallpaper Engine (wallpaper32.exe, wallpaper64.exe) spawning child processes: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe, or unsigned binaries from %TEMP% or %APPDATA%. High-risk if child process parent is scene/application wallpaper file, especially if wallpaper is recently downloaded.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Steam Account Access Post-Infection
suggestion.rationale: Article phrase: 'aiming to hijack their accounts' and 'lead to a stolen Steam account.' Lumma and Vidar are credential infostealers; pipeline missed credential exfiltration and account compromise detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Steam login from unusual geography/IP, login anomalies, or password changes within 1-48 hours of Wallpaper Engine malware execution. Infostealers typically stage login attempts or account abuse immediately after exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Wallpaper Engine Network Beaconing or C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names DarkKomet (known backdoor with C2), Lumma, and Vidar (staged downloaders). Malware must communicate; pipeline surfaced zero C2 or network-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Wallpaper Engine process (or child process spawned by it) initiating connections to non-Steam, non-CDN IP ranges, particularly to known DarkKomet, Lumma, or Vidar C2 infrastructure, or to cryptocurrency exchange/mining pools (for miner payloads).

suggestion.title: Persistence via Wallpaper Engine Scheduled Task or Registry Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'leave the victim's system infected with backdoors or crypto miners.' Long-term presence requires persistence mechanism; pipeline missed all persistence tactics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Registry modifications under HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Wallpaper Engine or creation of Scheduled Tasks executing from Wallpaper Engine data directories. Or: modification of Wallpaper Engine startup parameters to include malicious paths or command-line arguments.

suggestion.title: Local Credential Access via Infostealers (Post-Execution)
suggestion.rationale: Article names Lumma and Vidar infostealers. These tools perform local credential enumeration and theft; pipeline missed collection/discovery detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Child processes spawned by Wallpaper Engine reading lsass.exe, accessing C:\Windows\System32\config\SAM, querying registry for saved credentials (DPAPI), or accessing browser credential storage. Lumma/Vidar typically enumerate environment variables, command-line history, and clipboard.

suggestion.title: Wallpaper Engine Content Directory Containing Executable Files
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'malware hidden inside the wallpaper packages.' Legitimate wallpapers contain video/HTML/scenes; executables in Wallpaper Engine content paths are anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detection of .exe, .dll, .ps1, or other executable file types written to or extracted within Wallpaper Engine content directory (%APPDATA%\Wallpaper Engine\wallpapers). Correlate with recent Wallpaper Engine launch or Workshop download activity.

suggestion.title: Fake Microsoft Alert Phishing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'fake Microsoft alerts' as initial access vector. Article phrase: 'Fake Microsoft Alerts Used to Deploy...' — no email filter rule, sender validation, or alert-spoofing detection was generated despite this being the primary attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails impersonating Microsoft with urgency messaging or fake security warnings. Look for sender domain spoofing, missing DMARC/SPF alignment, shortened URLs pointing to credential harvesting sites, or unusual routing paths. Cross-reference legitimate vs. counterfeit Microsoft alert formats.

suggestion.title: NarwhalRAT Execution & C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'NarwhalRAT' as the payload malware family. Should detect RAT process execution, DLL injection, registry persistence, and C2 callbacks. No behavioral detection for RAT hallmarks (process enumeration, file staging, network beaconing to C2) was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect NarwhalRAT execution via file hash, process name patterns, or command-line signatures. Monitor for suspicious child processes, unsigned DLL loading, and network connections to known or suspected C2 infrastructure. Alert on suspicious registry modifications typical of RAT persistence mechanisms.

suggestion.title: RAT Command & Control Traffic
suggestion.rationale: As a Remote Access Trojan campaign, C2 communication is the backbone of post-compromise activity. Article title implies command and control phase, but no network-based or DNS detection rule for C2 beaconing was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections to uncommon or suspicious domains/IPs, especially with beaconing patterns (regular intervals, small payload sizes, anomalous User-Agent strings). Correlate with file execution timestamps and process names. Alert on encrypted DNS (DoH) queries that bypass corporate DNS inspection.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via RAT Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: RATs typically enable lateral movement through native tools (cmd.exe, PowerShell) or built-in Windows utilities. No detection for RAT-spawned discovery or lateral movement commands was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process trees spawning cmd.exe or PowerShell from suspicious parents (Internet Explorer, Office applications, rundll32, regsvcs). Watch for net.exe, tasklist, ipconfig, whoami, or nslookup commands executed by RAT processes. Detect outbound SMB (445) or RDP (3389) from newly-compromised machines to other internal hosts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Microsoft Office/PDF Document Execution
suggestion.rationale: Fake Microsoft alerts often arrive as malicious documents or executables disguised as system alerts. No detection for Office macro execution, suspicious document child processes, or PDF exploit chains was generated despite being common delivery vectors for RATs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) spawning cmd.exe, PowerShell, rundll32, or certutil processes. Monitor for suspicious PDF reader child processes. Detect macro execution in Office docs from non-standard locations (temp, downloads, appdata). Flag unsigned or suspicious scripts executed through Office automation.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Living-off-the-Land Binaries
suggestion.rationale: RATs frequently leverage LOLBins (certutil, regsvcs, mshta, rundll32) to evade EDR detection and execute payloads. No detection rule for suspicious LOLBin execution contexts or abuse patterns was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for certutil.exe with -decode, -urlcache, or -ping switches. Alert on rundll32 execution with suspicious DLL paths or ordinal numbers. Detect mshta.exe executing remote scripts or embedded HTML applications. Flag regsvcs.exe spawning cmd.exe or downloading files from the network.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt Against Cisco SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the flaw is 'actively exploited.' Pipeline must detect HTTP requests targeting the vulnerable endpoint with injection/traversal patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to /api/*, /admin/*, and known SD-WAN Manager paths for payloads indicating exploitation (command injection, path traversal, XXE). Flag requests from non-whitelisted IPs during off-hours.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation implies command execution risk. Pipeline should detect post-compromise process spawning and egress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SD-WAN Manager service spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash. Also monitor for outbound network connections from SD-WAN service to non-management IPs or high-port ranges.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized SD-WAN Configuration Modification
suggestion.rationale: Compromise of a network appliance typically leads to configuration tampering for persistence or lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect config-change API calls or file writes (policy, routes, VPN, admin accounts) originating from non-standard IPs or outside maintenance windows. Baseline: config changes from <5 known admin IPs during business hours only.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: SD-WAN Manager sits at network boundary with visibility into internal routing. 'Actively exploited' implies adversaries achieve post-compromise impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scans or connection sweeps from SD-WAN Manager host to internal subnets (DNS, DHCP, admin systems). Flag if connection profile expands beyond documented management relationships.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Authentication Events on SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Web-app exploits enable credential dumping or session hijacking. Monitor for login anomalies confirming persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed logins from anomalous IPs, successful logins outside maintenance windows, or creation of new admin accounts. Correlate with exploitation attempt timestamps.

suggestion.title: Exposed Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'public-facing' SD-WAN Manager vulnerability with active CISA KEV exploitation. Article explicitly references standard asset-exposure hunt templates but pipeline produced no use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances reachable from external networks on default management ports (8443, 9443). Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner results to isolate instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-20262 before federal remediation deadline 2026-06-29.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt Detection in SD-WAN Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article core mechanism: 'directory or path traversal vulnerability that could allow an authenticated, remote attacker to create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'. No detection for traversal payloads (.., %2e%2e%2f patterns) generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager HTTP request logs and WAF records for path traversal indicators (../, ..\, URL-encoded variants %2e%2e%2f) in request URIs and parameters. Alert on traversal patterns following successful authentication.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File System Modifications on SD-WAN Manager Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies impact: 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem of an affected system'. No detection for post-exploitation filesystem integrity violations generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager host filesystems for unexpected file creation, deletion, or modification in application and configuration directories. Alert on changes correlating with suspicious HTTP activity or authenticated sessions.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Configuration and Policy Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: File overwrite capability in a network management appliance implies post-exploitation persistence via configuration/policy/credential manipulation. Specific detection for config tampering missing from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish configuration baseline for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager (device policies, routing rules, VPN settings, admin accounts). Alert on modifications outside approved maintenance windows. Use file hashes or cryptographic signatures to detect unauthorized edits.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerable Software Inventory Flagging
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV underscores compliance urgency: 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date' (2026-06-29). No vulnerability-scanner or asset-inventory-based detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and CMDB for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances flagged with CVE-2026-20262 presence. Escalate by remediation deadline and network exposure level; enforce patch deployment by 2026-06-29.

suggestion.title: Malicious Go Module Package Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies `github.com/botdb-go/bolt` v1.3.1 as backdoored typo-squat. Pipeline failed to suggest detection for malicious package names in go.mod or go.sum, supply-chain repository poisoning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor go.mod / go.sum files for package names containing common typos or homoglyphs of popular modules (e.g., 'boltdb' vs 'botdb'). Alert on first-time or infrequent imports of similar-named packages. Cross-reference against known malicious package databases.

suggestion.title: Go Module Proxy Cache Abuse Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in...cached the backdored module.' Pipeline missed this caching mechanism exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to Go Module Proxy (proxy.golang.org) for packages that have mismatched versions between GitHub source and cached proxy. Flag when a version is deleted from source but continues to be served from proxy cache.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication from Go Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands.' Pipeline extracted no C2 or command-and-control detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections from Go runtime processes (go.exe, compiled Go binaries) to non-standard or newly-registered domains. Correlate with suspicious package installations from 3+ months prior.

suggestion.title: Long-Dormant Supply Chain Compromise Activation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'This version...allowed it to go unnoticed for several years...3 years' + 'developers to update the version that stayed in the system for 3 years.' Pipeline missed persistence detection window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when organizations bulk-update dependencies after a long quiet period (2+ years), especially for packages in proxy caches. Cross-check against supply chain vulnerability databases for recently-disclosed old versions.

suggestion.title: Package Name Homoglyph / Typo Squatting Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article defines and describes typo-squatting: 'Bad actors create and upload harmful software packages to online libraries using names very similar to popular ones.' No supply-chain typo detection UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement fuzzy-matching detection over package imports: flag packages whose names are edit-distance ≤2 from known popular modules (e.g., boltdb → botdb, lodash → loadash). Correlate with first-seen timestamps and lack of legitimate upstream maintainer.

suggestion.title: Repository Signature / Checksum Validation Failure
suggestion.rationale: Article states malicious package persisted despite removal; 'Go Module Mirror's vulnerable package has been removed from Github' but cached copies remained. Missing detection for integrity validation bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for go mod verify failures, checksum mismatches, or signature validation warnings. Alert when a package's hash in local cache differs from both upstream repo and public proxy. Flag if go.sum / go.lock shows version pinning to deprecated or revoked versions.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerability Present: Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'CVE-2026-20262 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' This is the baseline detection for any CISA KEV entry—identify vulnerable instances before they are exploited.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output and asset management systems for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager installations. Alert on any instance without patch released before federal remediation deadline (2026-06-29). Cross-reference CVE-2026-20262 status against deployed versions.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt Against SD-WAN Manager HTTP Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article core technical detail: 'directory or path traversal vulnerability.' Requires HTTP-level pattern detection for directory traversal payloads (../, ..\, encoded variants).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager for path traversal syntax: relative path sequences (../, ..\), URL-encoded variants (%2e%2e/), double-encoded sequences, or null-byte injection. suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Creation/Modification on SD-WAN Manager Host
