suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Nuance Powerscribe processes for unexpected child spawning or network communication patterns. Detect .NET deserialization payloads via network IDS. Alert on Powerscribe processing untrusted network files with immediate command interpreter spawning.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerability Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-20262 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and references asset-exposure hunt templates; pipeline generated zero use cases despite this direct guidance and federable relevance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results against asset inventory for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager installations. Flag any system with CVE-2026-20262 marked vulnerable, regardless of reported patch status—patch lag is endemic. Correlate with network segmentation policy to identify internet-exposed instances requiring emergency remediation.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Against Cisco SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability mechanic: 'directory or path traversal vulnerability'; this attack vector is unrepresented in detection logic despite being the exploitation method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager HTTP(S) request logs and WAF logs for path traversal indicators: `../`, `..\`, `%2e%2e/`, `%252e%252e/`, or encoding variants in URI paths, query parameters, or POST bodies. Focus on requests to file-operation or config-management endpoints. Baseline legitimate admin activity to establish FP threshold.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Creation/Modification on Cisco SD-WAN Manager Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes impact: 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'; no detection for the actual impact—file system abuse—despite it being the post-exploitation outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager host file-system logs (via auditd, Windows File Integrity Monitoring, or vendor audit logs) for unexpected file creation or modification in system directories, application paths, or config folders. Establish baseline of legitimate admin file operations; flag deviations especially in system-critical paths (bin/, lib/, web-accessible paths).

suggestion.title: Anomalous Admin Authentication Patterns to Cisco SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated, remote attacker'—exploitation requires valid credentials, but T1078 (Valid Accounts) is entirely absent from pipeline output despite being critical for this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate SD-WAN Manager admin authentication (source IPs, timing, frequency, MFA usage). Alert on: brute-force attempts (multiple failed logins), off-hours access, geographic anomalies, or credential-stuffing patterns. Cross-reference with corporate credential breach notifications and SIEM credential-compromise alerts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerability Scanner Coverage
suggestion.rationale: Article states CISA KEV entries are 'currently being exploited' and explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt'; pipeline generated zero use cases despite this directive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner result identifying CVE-2026-20262 or unpatched Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances. Establish remediation SLA aligned to federal due date 2026-06-29. Cross-reference with patch inventory to close patch-lag gaps.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Creation/Modification on SD-WAN Manager Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes exploitation outcome: 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'—a direct impact indicator the pipeline omitted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager system logs for unexpected file operations (creation, modification, deletion). Correlate file-write events with authenticated session logs to identify exploitation post-exploitation artifacts (e.g., files written to /tmp/, /var/www/, or config directories outside maintenance windows).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Authenticated Access to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly requires 'authenticated, remote attacker' but pipeline missed authentication anomaly detection despite this being the gateway to exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager followed by file-system operations or abnormal API/console activity within 5 minutes. Baseline legitimate administrative access; flag logins from non-expected geographies, off-hours, or credential sources.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal / Directory Traversal Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability type is 'directory or path traversal'; article body names this exploit vector but pipeline extracted no payload-pattern detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP requests to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager for directory traversal signatures: ../ sequences, ..\\, encoded variants (%2e%2e%2f, %252e%252e%252f), or absolute path prefixes in URI/POST parameters targeting sensitive directories (/etc/, /var/, Windows system paths).

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Patch Compliance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer' and sets Federal due date 2026-06-29; inventory-based compliance tracking is missing despite time-critical context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for all Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances. Compare version/build against vendor patch advisory. Report non-compliant systems with remediation timeline to due date; escalate any unpatched systems in internet-facing or DMZ segments.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Exploitation Detection — Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is actively exploited (CISA KEV status) and recommends applying standard asset-exposure hunt template with this CVE. Pipeline generated no use cases despite article's own template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager public-facing endpoints for exploitation attempts targeting CVE-2026-20262. Baseline normal administrative access patterns and alert on anomalous requests, path-traversal patterns (../, %2e%2e), or error-code spikes (403/401) in request URIs to manager API or web interface.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation File Manipulation — SD-WAN Manager Filesystem Integrity
suggestion.rationale: Article core impact: 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem.' Pipeline missed detection use case for this explicit attack outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected file creation or modification on Cisco SD-WAN Manager hosts following exploitation indicators. Monitor system directories and configuration paths for unauthorized writes. Correlate successful HTTP 200 responses to traversal probes with file-system events within 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: Authentication Baseline — SD-WAN Manager Admin Access Control
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploit requires authentication ('authenticated remote attacker'). Pipeline missed credential-access detection layer preceding exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate administrative logins to SD-WAN Manager. Alert on successful authentication followed by anomalous API activity, unusual request volumes, or file-manipulation attempts within 10 minutes—indicates post-auth exploitation.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Hunt — CVE-2026-20262 Exposed Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer' and recommends fleet-wide check despite scanner claims. Pipeline should trigger compliance inventory hunts, not just signature-based exploitation hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and CMDB for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances with patch status below patched version. Cross-reference with network exposure tools (DNS, shodan, port-scan data) to identify externally reachable unpatched instances. Flag for immediate remediation by federal due date (2026-06-29).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Write via Path Traversal (Cisco SD-WAN Manager)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows attacker to 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem of an affected system.' This is the direct impact of the exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected file creation or modification events on Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager systems, especially in system directories (/etc, /var, config paths, or Windows equivalents). Correlate with web access logs showing path traversal sequences or exploitation attempts. File writes from the SD-WAN Manager process or web service running under unexpected privileges are high-fidelity indicators.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Pattern Detection in SD-WAN Manager Web Logs
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability mechanism is 'directory or path traversal.' Web logs should contain malicious request patterns before file write succeeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for path traversal sequences in HTTP requests to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager endpoints: strings like '../', '..\\', URL-encoded variants ('%2e%2e', '%5c'), or doubled slashes in file paths. Filter on status codes indicating successful exploitation (200, 201, 204) rather than blocked attempts (400, 403). Correlate with subsequent file modification events.

suggestion.title: Configuration File Access via Path Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal typically targets configuration files; article's 'overwrite any file' capability implies attackers can access and modify sensitive configs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when SD-WAN Manager or web service processes open configuration files (e.g., passwords.conf, auth.conf, system.ini) via non-standard code paths or file handle paths that traverse parent directories. Detect unusual read-then-write patterns on sensitive configs within short time windows.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process or Service Writing to System Directories (SD-WAN)
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability outcome is ability to 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'—privileged file write is the impact.
log_sources: Windows Registry and File audit events
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On systems running Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, alert on file creation or modification in restricted directories (system32, /bin, /etc, /var, boot directories) initiated from the web service or SD-WAN process. Baseline file write activity for the affected application and trigger on deviations. Include file integrity monitoring (FIM) alerts for unexpected changes to critical system files.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow an authenticated, remote attacker' and is actively exploited; requires internet-facing Manager instance. Detection should identify exposed web interfaces before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for open/responsive ports associated with Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager (typically 8443, 8888) or HTTP GET/HEAD requests to known Manager paths (e.g., /apidocs, /admin). Cross-correlate with asset inventory to identify exposed instances not previously documented as internet-facing.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Payload Detection in HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'directory or path traversal vulnerability' as attack vector; specific payload patterns should be monitored. Attackers exploit this by sending crafted requests with ../, %2e%2e%, or encoded variants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request logs to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager endpoints for path traversal indicators: ../, %2e%2e%, ..%2f, %252e%252e%252f, or similar directory escape sequences. Correlate with User-Agent and authentication headers to identify exploitation attempts post-authentication.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Creation/Modification on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Host
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'could create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'; post-exploitation file operations are the immediate impact. Detection should monitor filesystem activity on Manager hosts for unexpected writes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Catalyst SD-WAN Manager hosts, flag file creation or modification events outside normal maintenance windows. Prioritize: (1) writes to system directories (/etc, /var, /opt outside expected paths), (2) new executable files, (3) config file modifications. Baseline normal file operations and alert on anomalies correlated with failed/successful authentications.

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication Followed by Successful Login to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 'authenticated' attackers; however, successful exploitation likely preceded by reconnaissance. Detection should flag patterns of failed attempts followed by successful auth and immediate file operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In Catalyst SD-WAN Manager audit logs, identify sequences: 10+ failed login attempts to single account → successful login from same source IP → immediate file operation event. Adjust thresholds per environment baseline; flag successful logins from IPs not previously authenticated.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerability Detection via Scanner/Configuration Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Even if your scanners say not vulnerable... it's worth one quick check.' Detection should cross-verify vulnerability scanner results with actual Catalyst SD-WAN Manager version inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner reports flagging CVE-2026-20262 against CMDB version records for Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances. Alert if scanner shows 'not vulnerable' but installed version is <= patched version threshold. Include all Manager instances (exposed and internal) — lateral movement risk exists.

suggestion.title: Typo-squatting Go Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack: 'The malicious Go Module Mirror's was named github.com/botdb-go/bolt, similar to the original one i.e. github.com/boltdb/bolt.' Detection should flag phonetically similar package names substituting legitimate ones.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go package manager operations (go get, go mod tidy) for installation of packages with names phonetically or visually similar to known-good packages. Flag 'botdb-go/bolt' or variants deviating from canonical 'boltdb/bolt'. Cross-reference against official Go package registry.

suggestion.title: Go Module Proxy Serving Malicious Cached Version
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Go Module Mirror service stored it permanently... Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in, and that cached the backdored module.' Detection should identify module proxy serving compromised versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go dependency resolution for checksum mismatches or version anomalies between requested and served modules. Alert on go.mod/go.sum validation failures. Correlate module downloads against Go Vulnerability Database and official package source hashes.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution from Backdoored Go Module
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands i.e. via a command and control server.' Detection should identify command execution orchestrated by C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process spawning from Go runtime or application processes. Correlate with outbound HTTP/DNS connections to non-whitelisted domains. Flag command execution lacking corresponding user input or code-path triggering.

suggestion.title: Bulk Dependency Auto-update to Malicious Version
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'we now wish to update our systems to the latest dependencies, which led developers to update the version that stayed in the system for 3 years.' Detection should flag automation-driven updates to compromised versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor dependency update operations (go get -u, go mod tidy) for targets matching recent vulnerability advisories. Flag updates to versions not yet widely adopted in legitimate builds. Require approval before applying updates to supply chain-critical dependencies.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Vendored Malicious Go Module
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'version...stayed in the system for 3 years,' indicating vendored persistence in git repos and build artifacts. Detection should identify malicious modules in vendor/ directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan vendor/ directories and go.sum in source control for known-malicious package names (botdb-go/bolt). Alert on presence of typosquatting packages in checked-in dependencies. Baseline legitimate packages across build pipeline.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 Beaconing from Compromised Application
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'backdoor allows...remote control...through a server.' Detection should identify beaconing behavior from applications using backdoored Go modules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from Go application processes for regular interval, low-volume C2 patterns. Flag connections to domains not in ASN whitelist or exhibiting high entropy. Correlate beacon timing with process parent relationships.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Internet Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article frames vulnerability as affecting 'exposed assets' (T1190 language) and explicitly recommends 'standard asset-exposure hunt.' No UC generated despite this direct guidance. This is the initial_access prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify internet-facing Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances on standard HTTPS ports (8443, 8080 variants). Correlate inbound traffic volume and source IP diversity against asset inventory to flag exposed management interfaces.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts on SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack is 'directory or path traversal'—exploit-phase reconnaissance. Pipeline skipped execution-layer detections despite vulnerability name being 'path traversal.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP request logs to SD-WAN Manager endpoints for path traversal patterns: ../ sequences, %2e%2e encodings, absolute path prefixes in file operation parameters, or suspicious directory enumeration requests.

suggestion.title: File Creation or Overwrite via SD-WAN Manager Post-Auth
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'could allow...to create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem.' This is the direct impact; no UC captured file I/O anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager system for unexpected file creation or modification in sensitive paths (config dirs, binary dirs, audit log locations) following remote authentication or concurrent with path-traversal-pattern HTTP traffic.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Authentication to Cisco SD-WAN Manager Pre-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated, remote attacker'—authentication is mandatory step before exploitation. No UC detects anomalous logins despite this gating requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track successful and failed authentication attempts to SD-WAN Manager from non-standard source IPs, bulk login patterns, or credential stuffing indicators. Correlate with subsequent file-system anomalies on same session.

suggestion.title: Code Execution via Overwritten SD-WAN Manager Binaries
suggestion.rationale: File-overwrite attacks often target executable startup scripts or plugins for RCE. Article does not exclude this escalation path; typical post-exploitation file manipulations enable command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected process spawning from SD-WAN Manager service context or child processes of manager daemons, especially within minutes of file modification events or from suspicious session origins.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager contains a directory or path traversal vulnerability' with active CISA KEV status. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite explicit mention of 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager with path traversal payloads (../, ..\ sequences) or CVE-2026-20262 exploit patterns. Alert on successful responses (200 HTTP) to admin or config paths from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Filesystem Writes Post-Catalyst SD-WAN Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated, remote attacker to create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem.' Pipeline missed the post-exploitation file modification impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful Catalyst SD-WAN Manager authentication events with abnormal file creation/modification on the same host, especially outside expected config/log directories. Flag rapid file overwrites or suspicious binary writes.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Directory Enumeration Against Catalyst SD-WAN
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal vulnerability ('directory or path traversal') implies directory discovery and enumeration. No use case generated for reconnaissance phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP GET/POST requests to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager endpoints containing sequential directory traversal attempts (patterns like /../../etc/passwd, /..%5c..%5cwindows) or unusual depth indicators in path parameters.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Detection – CVE-2026-20262 Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'it's worth one quick check across your fleet — patch lag is the silent killer.' Standard vulnerability-matching use case completely absent despite explicit CVE ID.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances in asset inventory against CVE-2026-20262. Flag unpatched versions and correlate with successful path traversal attempts in access logs. Use patch baseline against federal due-date 2026-06-29.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Internet-Facing Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability affects 'exposed assets' and is listed in CISA KEV (active wild exploitation). Identification of externally-reachable SD-WAN Manager endpoints is the foundational hunt—this CVE cannot be exploited remotely without network exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output (Nessus, Qualys, Tenable) for CVE-2026-20262 matches. Cross-reference discovered Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances against internal asset inventory for internet-facing exposure. Correlate with firewall rule inventory to identify instances with inbound rules from untrusted networks on management ports (443, 830 typical).

suggestion.title: HTTP Path Traversal Payload Detection Against SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies attack vector as 'directory or path traversal'—exploitation manifests as malformed HTTP requests. Attackers will attempt classic path-traversal sequences (../, %2e%2e/, url-encoded variants) against SD-WAN Manager web endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request logs for Cisco SD-WAN Manager endpoints (common URIs: /admin, /config, /api) containing path traversal indicators: sequences of '../', '..\', '%2e%2e', './', null bytes, or case-variation bypasses. Flag requests with 401/403 responses (auth required) followed by 200/201 (exploitation success) within short time window.

suggestion.title: Authenticated Session Followed by Filesystem Write on SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'authenticated, remote attacker' can 'create or overwrite any file'—post-exploitation impact is detectable via correlated authentication and file-modification logs. Successful exploitation will show login followed by suspicious filesystem activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate authentication logs (login event) on Cisco SD-WAN Manager with subsequent filesystem write events to sensitive directories (/etc, /opt, config paths, /var/www) from same source IP. Flag non-administrator accounts initiating file creation/overwrites, or writes outside business hours, or targeting system-critical files.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerability Scanner Match (Splunk Template)
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends standard asset-exposure hunt using vulnerability scanner results per CISA KEV template. CVE-2026-20262 is the canonical identifier for this vulnerability and federal patch due-date (2026-06-29) mandates rapid remediation for federal agencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management system (Nessus, Qualys, InsightVM) for CVE-2026-20262 detection results. Generate alert for any match on Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. Prioritize federal networks and internet-facing instances; flag any systems still unpatched past 2026-06-29 due-date.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Authentication to SD-WAN Manager from High-Risk Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated' exploitation—attacker must first gain valid credentials or exploit weak authentication. Detecting unusual authentication patterns (failed attempts followed by success, lateral credentials, new geographic sources) precedes path-traversal exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager authentication logs for: multiple failed login attempts followed by successful auth, logins from unusual geographic locations, authentication using service/default accounts, parallel sessions from different IPs, authentication outside maintenance windows. Correlate with subsequent HTTP path-traversal attempts.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanning: CVE-2026-20262 Patch Status Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CISA KEV entry' with 'observed exploited in the wild' and explicitly references 'Standard asset-exposure hunt'; all Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances must be scanned and remediated by federal deadline 2026-06-29.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager system running unpatched version for CVE-2026-20262. Cross-correlate scanner results with external IP access logs to prioritize internet-facing instances for emergency patching.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts in HTTP Access Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'directory or path traversal vulnerability'; HTTP request logs are the earliest detection point, preceding filesystem compromise. Article emphasizes attack surface via 'public-facing application.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager HTTP access logs for path traversal payloads: %2e%2e/, ../, null bytes, URL-encoded slashes, or directory escape sequences. Baseline legitimate admin activity; alert on high-velocity attempts from external sources.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Filesystem Write Events on SD-WAN Manager Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow...to create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'; filesystem integrity monitoring is definitive post-compromise detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected file creation or modification on Cisco SD-WAN Manager systems, especially in system-critical paths (/etc, /bin, Windows\System32). Correlate with prior path traversal HTTP requests or failed authentication sequences.

suggestion.title: Authenticated Admin Console Baseline: Unusual Access Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated, remote attacker'; establish baseline of legitimate administrative access to enable anomaly detection. Required to distinguish normal admin activity from exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager admin access (source IPs, timezones, request patterns, frequency). Alert on: new source IPs, access outside business hours, rapid failed-auth sequences, or auth followed immediately by path manipulation requests.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism Detection: Configuration File Tampering Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal capability to overwrite arbitrary files could be used for persistence via modified startup scripts, config files, or scheduled tasks. Pipeline completely missed persistence phase implications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modification of SD-WAN Manager startup configuration, task scheduler entries, or system service files. Cross-reference against change management tickets and admin approval logs. Any undocumented modification warrants incident investigation.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [`../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`].' Vulnerability is exploitable only if instances are reachable; asset discovery is prerequisite to remediation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances in environment via open-port scanning (443/HTTPS typical), TLS certificate CN matching, and vulnerability scanner results. Correlate against CMDB to locate exposed east-west SD-WAN management planes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerability Scanner Hits
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates: 'CVE-2026-20262 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Federal patch due date is 2026-06-29; any unpatched instances are actively exploitable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner result indicating CVE-2026-20262 detection against Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager assets. Flag for immediate remediation if current date exceeds federal patch deadline (2026-06-29). False-negatives from patched systems still in scanner databases should be suppressed against change-management records.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Creation/Overwrite on SD-WAN Manager Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article describes core impact: 'could allow an authenticated, remote attacker to create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem of an affected system.' File-system writes are the direct exploitation payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline file creation and modification events on Cisco SD-WAN Manager systems during normal administration windows. Alert on unexpected writes to system directories, config paths, or executable locations outside maintenance change windows. Establish whitelist of legitimate SD-WAN deployment operations to reduce noise.

suggestion.title: Remote Authentication Attempts to Cisco SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Exploit requires 'authenticated, remote attacker' — successful authentication is a prerequisite gate. Access logs showing unusual authentication patterns or lateral jump-points could precede file-write attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager authentication logs for successful remote authentications from non-administrative networks or out-of-band IP ranges. Alert on repeated failed-auth followed by success within short time window (credential-attack pattern). Correlate against change-request windows to suppress maintenance activity.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'directory or path traversal vulnerability' as the core attack mechanism. No detection use case was generated for this primary vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager for path-traversal sequences (../, ..\, %2e%2e, unicode variants) in URL paths or parameters. Correlate with successful authentication. High-confidence signals: ../ attempts to escape application root, requests to known SD-WAN endpoints with traversal syntax, or filesystem paths in request bodies attempting to access /etc, /var, system32.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Creation/Overwrite on SD-WAN Manager Host
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem.' Pipeline generated no file-system-impact detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager process for unexpected FileCreate/FileModify events outside normal application directories. Flag binary writes to system paths, script writes to startup folders, or modifications to application binaries. Baseline normal file operations per version and correlate anomalies with authentication events.

suggestion.title: Authenticated Remote Access to Cisco SD-WAN Manager Followed by File System Activity
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires 'authenticated, remote attacker.' Pipeline missed behavioral correlation between successful remote auth and subsequent file operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create baseline of normal post-auth file operations on SD-WAN Manager systems. Alert on: successful remote authentication + file creation in system paths within 5 minutes, successful auth + binary modification, successful auth + script execution in non-standard directories.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerable Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV indicates active exploitation. Article recommends 'quick check across your fleet.' Pipeline generated no asset-based detection for vulnerable versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results (Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7) for CVE-2026-20262 matches on Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. Generate list of unpatched instances, sort by network exposure (internet-facing priority). Cross-reference with authentication logs to identify exploitation attempts. Alert if any vulnerable instances remain exposed past federal patch due date 2026-06-29.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Persistence via File Write to Startup/Autorun
suggestion.rationale: File-overwrite capability enables persistence (startup scripts, scheduled tasks, registry). Article's 'overwrite any file' implies persistence-through-writes scenarios not covered by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file writes to persistence paths (/etc/cron*, /var/spool, Windows StartUp, HKLM\Software\Run) by or proxied through Cisco SD-WAN Manager service. Flag new scheduled tasks created within 5 minutes of suspicious SD-WAN file activity. Require manual verification of all writes to system startup locations by application services.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVE-2026-20262 is CISA KEV (actively exploited in wild). 'CVE:** `CVE-2026-20262`' is provided as a scannable artifact. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite vulnerability scanner match being the primary defensive control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner findings matching CVE-2026-20262 for any Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instance. Correlate with asset inventory to identify exposed instances. Federal patch due date is 2026-06-29; any unpatched instance post-deadline triggers escalation.

suggestion.title: Exposed Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Asset Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states T1190 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets' and references 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' as canonical detection. Pipeline did not generate this despite it being explicitly suggested in the article text.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for internet-routable instances of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager using asset metadata (SHODAN, Censys lookups, internal scanner results). Flag any instance accessible on expected ports (typically 8443 or 9000 depending on deployment) without VPN/corporate network gating.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager File System Write Activity Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'authenticated, remote attacker to create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem.' Pipeline missed impact-phase detection for the actual exploitation effect: file modification. This is the adversary's objective post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager system file-write events for unexpected file creation or overwrite in critical directories (config, webroot, library paths). Baseline benign writes; flag deviations. Correlate with authentication logs to identify if writes occur without corresponding legitimate admin activity.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Authenticated Access Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires 'authenticated, remote attacker.' Pipeline did not model authentication as a required gating step or flag anomalous auth patterns. Article implies stolen/compromised credentials or abuse of existing accounts as attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate administrative access patterns to SD-WAN Manager (IPs, times, frequency, operations performed). Alert on: new source IPs, off-hours access, rapid authentication failures followed by success, or successful logins from geographically impossible locations.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability mechanism is explicitly 'directory or path traversal.' Pipeline should detect exploitation attempts (e.g., directory escape sequences in HTTP requests) before files are overwritten. This is early-stage detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to SD-WAN Manager for path traversal payloads: sequences like `..`, `..%2F`, URL-encoded variants, or suspicious file paths in request parameters/headers. Match against common traversal patterns. IDS signatures for CVE-2026-20262 should exist post-disclosure.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Privilege Escalation via File Overwrite
suggestion.rationale: File overwrite capability combined with system-level access could enable privilege escalation (e.g., overwriting config files, system libraries, or scripts executed with higher privileges). Pipeline missed this derived impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file overwrites targeting privileged execution paths (startup scripts, library directories, service config files) followed by process elevation or unexpected service restarts. Correlate file modification logs with privilege escalation events on the same asset within minutes of the write.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Product explicitly named in scope; article states 'federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date.' Asset discovery is mandatory first step. Phrase: 'Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query CMDB, vulnerability scanners, and network telemetry for all instances of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. Cross-reference installed version against CVE-2026-20262 fix versions. Flag unpatched systems and report count/location for remediation tracking against 2026-06-29 federal due date.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts Against SD-WAN Manager Public Interface
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly described as 'directory or path traversal'; article notes it is 'public-facing.' This is direct T1190 exploitation activity. Phrase: 'directory or path traversal vulnerability'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP logs for SD-WAN Manager endpoints. Flag requests containing encoded or literal path-traversal sequences (../, %2e%2e%2f, ..\, unicode variants) in URL path, query string, or POST body. Correlate failed traversal attempts with IP reputation. FP baseline: legitimate admin tools may use normalized paths; whitelist known admin subnets.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Creation/Modification on SD-WAN Manager System
suggestion.rationale: Impact explicitly states 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem.' Post-exploitation, this is directly observable if host-level logs are collected. Phrase: 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Cisco SD-WAN Manager hosts, monitor filesystem activity for file creation/writes outside expected maintenance windows and admin accounts. Suspicious targets: /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /var/log, cron, sudoers, startup scripts. Correlate with web-application auth logs to establish attacker timeline. FP note: legitimate config changes and log rotations generate expected writes.

suggestion.title: Authentication Spike Against Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Public Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation means active exploitation in the wild. Exploit requires 'authenticated, remote attacker,' making failed/repeated auth attempts a leading indicator post-announcement. Phrase: 'authenticated, remote attacker'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for successful + failed authentication attempts to SD-WAN Manager by source IP. Post-announcement, alert on 5x+ increase in failed auth attempts from any IP in 1-hour window, or successful auth immediately followed by file-operation requests. Correlate with public PoC availability and patch-lag metrics.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Persistence via Configuration File Modification
suggestion.rationale: Path-traversal + file-write capability enables attacker to persist by modifying startup configs or placing backdoors. Article's impact description ('overwrite any file') implies configuration or code manipulation. Phrase: 'overwrite any file on the filesystem'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager for file writes to configuration directories, startup scripts (/etc/rc.d, /etc/systemd, cron.d), and web-server roots. Flag executable permission changes shortly after creation. Hash files against known vendor distributions. Alert on config changes outside change-management tickets.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager — Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CISA KEV' and 'observed exploited in the wild' — vulnerability scanner hits for CVE-2026-20262 are the canonical first-line detection. Article explicitly recommends: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — match against your vulnerability scanner'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any asset matching Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager product family running vulnerable versions prior to patch due date (2026-06-29). Cross-correlate scanner data with network exposure (reachable from external networks or trust boundaries).

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Attack Patterns — Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is 'directory or path traversal' — attackers will emit traversal sequences like `../`, `..\`, percent-encoded variants in HTTP requests. Article describes this as the exploitation primitive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS request paths to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager endpoints for directory traversal payloads (../, ..\, %2e%2e, Unicode variants). Catalyst SD-WAN typically runs on port 8443 or custom management ports. Flag any traversal attempt regardless of HTTP response code.

suggestion.title: File System Modification — Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem of an affected system' — file creation/modification events are post-exploitation observable. This is the impact phase and strongest IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation or modification under Catalyst SD-WAN Manager installation directory (typically /opt/cisco/catalyst/*, C:\Program Files\Cisco\*, or vendor-defined paths) performed by or in context of the Catalyst application service account. Flag unexpected write patterns, especially to binary/config directories.

suggestion.title: Authenticated Remote Access to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated, remote attacker' — exploit requires prior authentication or credential compromise. Monitor authentication logs for unusual access patterns to the management interface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag authentication attempts to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager from unexpected geographies, IP ranges, or during unusual hours. Correlate with failed login spikes (credential spray) or use of default/weak credentials. Monitor for lateral movement post-successful auth.

suggestion.title: Network Asset Inventory — Exposed Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'patch lag is the silent killer' and emphasizes auditor/regulator tracking. Maintain active inventory of all Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances and their patch levels, exposure status (external-facing vs. internal), and network position.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset database for all Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances. Verify patch version ≥ vendor-specified remediation version (released by federal due date 2026-06-29). Flag any instance not patched or without proof of compensating control (WAF, network segmentation, access restrictions).

suggestion.title: Exposed Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Admin Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'anything in CISA KEV is *currently* being exploited' and 'authenticated, remote attacker.' External accessibility to vulnerable interface is prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect external network connections to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager ports (8443, 8080 typical) from non-corporate ranges. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner confirming CVE-2026-20262 exposure on identified assets.

suggestion.title: Successful Remote Authentication to Vulnerable SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated, remote attacker'—direct prerequisite before traversal exploit. Successful logins to vulnerable manager instances are elevated-risk signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager authentication logs for successful remote logins. Enrich by CVE-2026-20262 vulnerability status; successful auth to vulnerable instances is high-risk. Baseline and flag anomalous patterns.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts Against SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'directory or path traversal vulnerability.' HTTP payloads with traversal sequences (../, %2e%2e, backslash variants) in manager endpoints are direct exploitation signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP logs for Cisco SD-WAN Manager endpoints containing ../, double-encoded, or backslash traversal patterns. Focus on authenticated sessions. Correlate with CVE-2026-20262 vulnerability status.

suggestion.title: Filesystem Modification via Path Traversal File Write
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem.' Unexpected file creation/modification outside expected app directories signals successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file-system logs on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager hosts for unauthorized creation or modification in system directories (/etc, /var), config paths, or web-root escapes. Correlate with remote SD-WAN Manager API calls in same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Sensitive File Access via Directory Traversal Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'overwrite any file on the filesystem' implies broad read access. Path-traversal exploits commonly precede credential theft from config, key, or password-store files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt unusual file-read patterns from SD-WAN Manager process/web context targeting credential-bearing paths (config files, .pem keys, .env, password databases). Traversal exploits often enumerate sensitive paths before exfil.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Persistence via Traversal-Based File Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'overwrite any file on the filesystem.' Attacker can inject persistence by modifying startup scripts, cron jobs, or application configs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modification of persistence-relevant paths (/etc/cron.d, init scripts, application configs) on SD-WAN Manager hosts during or shortly after remote authenticated sessions. Hash-baseline and alert on unauthorized changes to startup files.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Vulnerability Scanner Hit
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and 'standard asset-exposure hunt' for CVE-2026-20262. Pipeline generated zero asset-discovery detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner detections for CVE-2026-20262 against Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances. Cross-reference with network boundary data to identify externally-facing deployments. Flag any positive hit as priority remediation given KEV status and 2026-06-29 federal patch deadline.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Unauthorized File Write Post-Auth
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allow[s] an authenticated, remote attacker to create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'. Pipeline missed impact-phase detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file-write events on Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager servers for modifications outside documented application paths (e.g., system binaries, configs outside /opt/Cisco or equivalent). Correlate suspicious writes with preceding authentication events or path-traversal patterns in application logs. Alert on file overwrites in sensitive locations (boot loaders, cron, init.d).

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Path-Traversal Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly 'directory or path traversal' but no pattern-based detection in application/proxy logs was offered. This is the core exploitation signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse SD-WAN Manager HTTP/HTTPS request logs for traversal payloads: `../`, `..\`, URL-encoded variants (`%2e%2e`, `%252e`), absolute paths in request URIs, or null-byte injection. Inspect both GET/POST parameters and headers. Alert on any traversal attempt against management endpoints.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Auth Success Followed by File Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation chain requires prior authentication; pipeline did not suggest correlated auth-plus-impact hunting despite article's KEV-active-exploitation status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build a behavioral baseline of normal post-login file operations on SD-WAN Manager servers (e.g., legitimate config updates). Flag sessions where authentication is immediately followed (< 5 min) by file-write attempts to unexpected paths, especially if combined with path-traversal patterns in request logs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL' and provides template reference + CVE substitution guidance. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite clear instruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances across fleet (FQDN, IP, certificate scanning). Query vulnerability scanners for CVE-2026-20262 presence. Alert on any discovery; federal remediation deadline is 2026-06-29.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File System Modification on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability core behavior: 'authenticated, remote attacker to create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem.' Pipeline missed detection for this primary impact mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Catalyst SD-WAN Manager endpoints for unexpected file creation or overwrite in system, configuration, or boot directories. Correlate filesystem events with authentication logs to surface exploitation chains.

suggestion.title: Authentication Spike or Anomaly Against Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires valid authentication ('authenticated, remote attacker'). Pipeline ignored hunt for credential abuse, weak controls, or impossible-travel logins that enable exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed login spike, credential spray, out-of-band authentication, or geographically anomalous logins to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. Cross-correlate with file-system and process events to identify exploitation post-authentication.

suggestion.title: WebSocket payload contains HEEx template injection markers to storybook endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'user-controlled attribute values over WebSocket...interpolated them unsanitized into a HEEx template.' The attack surface is malicious payload content (HEEx tags, interpolation syntax). Detecting payloads with template markers (`{%`, `<%`, `#{}`, unquoted interpolations) in WebSocket frames targeting storybook routes is the actual exploitation event.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on WebSocket frames sent to phoenix_storybook routes containing HEEx/Elixir template syntax (e.g., curly-brace interpolation `#{}`, angle-bracket tags `<%` or `{%`). Correlate HTTP 101 WebSocket upgrade with suspicious payload submission within same session.

suggestion.title: HTTP 4xx/5xx error spike from storybook endpoint after WebSocket payload submission
suggestion.rationale: Article: unsanitized template code is 'compiled and evaluated.' Failed injections (syntax errors, type mismatches) would cause HEEx/Elixir compilation errors surfacing as HTTP 400/500 responses. This is a strong signal of failed exploit attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor storybook endpoint responses for sudden increase in 4xx/5xx status codes correlated with WebSocket activity or rapid payload submissions. Look for compilation error messages in application logs mentioning 'EEx', 'template syntax', or 'compile failed'.

suggestion.title: BEAM process resource spike (memory/threads) during/post-WebSocket activity to storybook
suggestion.rationale: Article describes injected code evaluated 'with full Elixir Kernel access.' Successful code execution requires compilation and runtime evaluation—computationally expensive operations. Memory, thread count, or CPU spikes immediately after WebSocket payload would indicate code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for BEAM process memory/thread count/CPU. Alert on 3x+ spike within 10 seconds of WebSocket message to /storybook endpoint. Include GC pause anomalies (garbage collection thrashing under injected workload).

suggestion.title: Phoenix storybook endpoint reachable without authentication in production environment
suggestion.rationale: Article: playground is 'unauthenticated' and 'any unauthenticated user' can exploit. Remediation requires disabling or auth-gating the endpoint. Detection should verify vulnerable version (UC_102_7) combined with unrestricted endpoint access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For hosts with vulnerable phoenix_storybook (UC_102_7), probe storybook routes (GET /storybook, /storybook/playground, /_storybook) from external/non-dev IPs. 200/101 response indicates exposed endpoint. Flag as critical if environment is production.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Elixir/Erlang inter-process communication (message queue activity) spike from storybook context
suggestion.rationale: Injected code executes within Erlang VM with 'full Kernel access,' likely using message passing or spawning new processes. Abnormal process spawning patterns or message queue depth spikes after WebSocket activity would indicate successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor BEAM process spawn events and message queue depth during storybook WebSocket sessions. Flag significant increases in child processes spawned by beam.smp/erl.exe within 30 seconds of unsanitized WebSocket payload.

suggestion.title: storybook_playground or similar debug/playground endpoint accessible in production with verbose error pages
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a 'playground' endpoint designed for development. Production exposure of such endpoints is a misconfiguration that enables reconnaissance and exploitation. Pipeline should detect configuration/environment mismatches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for presence of development/debug endpoints (storybook, playground, debug=true, mix.env=dev) in production environments. Cross-reference with asset inventory to find exposed development configurations in prod.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Internet-Facing
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires 'authenticated, remote attacker' — exploitation path requires exposed asset. Article explicitly recommends asset-exposure hunt as first detection step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances exposed to untrusted networks via external port scan or cloud asset inventory. Query vulnerability scanners for CVE-2026-20262 detection. Correlate IP exposure with patch baseline to identify unpatched instances against 2026-06-29 federal due date.

suggestion.title: HTTP Path Traversal Exploitation Against SD-WAN Manager Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'directory or path traversal' — attack requests will contain traversal sequences. Article body specifies this as the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Cisco SD-WAN Manager endpoints containing path traversal patterns: ../, ..\, encoded variants (%2e%2e%2f), or null-byte injection (%00). Flag anomalous request frequency or sequences suggesting automated exploitation. Correlate to source IP and authentication context.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Create/Overwrite on SD-WAN Manager System
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly allows attacker to 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem' — successful exploitation leaves evidence of filesystem mutations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager host for unexpected file creation or modification in critical directories (config, logs, application root). Alert on mtime changes to protected files during authenticated user sessions. Baseline legitimate patch and deployment processes to minimize false positives.

suggestion.title: Filesystem Directory Enumeration via Path Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal vulnerability enables adversary to 'create a file or overwrite any file' — implies prior directory discovery and enumeration of system paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential requests for directory listings or file-read operations on sensitive paths (system config, credential stores, log directories) via path traversal sequences. Correlate burst patterns to authenticated session IDs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mandates 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' for this CVE as foundational hunt ('live once in `../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`'). Pipeline produced zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify internet-exposed or remotely-accessible Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances using asset discovery scans, cloud metadata queries, or passive DNS. Correlate with patch status from vulnerability scanner to triage unpatched instances against federal patch deadline (2026-06-29).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Path Traversal File Write Attempts

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager endpoints for path traversal patterns (../, ..\, directory escape sequences) in URL parameters or POST bodies from authenticated sessions. Correlate with suspicious file creation/modification events on affected systems.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Authenticated File Manipulation Post-Access
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'authenticated, remote attacker' but pipeline missed detection for post-authentication file operations, which is the actual impact mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful authentication to SD-WAN Manager, detect unexpected file creation, modification, or deletion—particularly of system files, configuration files, or scripts in critical directories (/etc, /var, Windows/System32).

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scan: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-20262 Detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for unpatched Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-20262. CISA KEV indicates active exploitation; treat unpatched external-facing instances as critical priority against federal patch due date 2026-06-29.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation: SD-WAN Manager HTTP Logs
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows 'directory or path traversal'—exploitation requires crafted requests containing traversal sequences (./, ../, encoded variants). Web/proxy logs are primary signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP requests to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager for path traversal patterns: %2e%2e, ../, ..\ double-encoded variants, or anomalous URI path depth. Cross-reference successful responses (200/206) with subsequent file-write events.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Write: SD-WAN Manager Filesystem Events
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem of an affected system.' Filesystem write events are primary impact indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal file operations on SD-WAN Manager systems. Alert on unexpected file creation/modification outside known app directories, especially to system/config paths, executables, or startup folders. Correlate timing with web exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Authentication Anomaly: Remote Access to SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires 'authenticated, remote attacker'—implies successful credential compromise or abuse of valid account. Anomalous auth patterns signal attack precursor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful logins to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager from external/unexpected networks, off-hours, or with service account use. Escalate if followed by path-traversal requests or filesystem modifications.

suggestion.rationale: File-overwrite capability creates risk for persistence or log tampering. Overwriting audit logs, monitoring agents, or startup scripts enables follow-on attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any attempt to overwrite OS executables, syslog/audit logs, antivirus definitions, or autostart mechanisms on systems hosting Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. Flag as high-confidence post-exploitation activity.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'match against your vulnerability scanner' for CVE-2026-20262. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs despite this being the detection foundation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances with CVE-2026-20262 via scanner results. Cross-reference against patch inventory to identify systems where remediation is past due or not yet applied. Prioritize systems with public-facing network exposure.

suggestion.title: Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Authentication + Suspicious File Operations

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Catalyst SD-WAN Manager HTTP/REST API logs for directory traversal payloads (../, ..\, encoded variants) in request paths, query parameters, or POST bodies. Correlate with 400/403 response codes (failed attempts) and 200/201 (successful exploitation).
