suggestion.title: Unauthenticated POST to Joomla Editor Profile Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' Exploit primitive is profile creation from no-auth context—detect POST requests to profile endpoints with null auth session.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST requests to /index.php?option=com_contenteditor (or variant profile endpoints) from sources with no valid session token, JWT, or cookie. Track request frequency per source IP; baseline is near-zero for external IPs.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Web-Accessible Joomla Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'upload ... of PHP code.' Payload delivery mechanism—detect .php file creation in Joomla components, plugins, modules, or templates directories correlated with web requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .php file writes to /components/, /plugins/, /modules/, /templates/ within 5 seconds of an unauthenticated POST to profile endpoint. Flag suspicious PHP filenames (shell.php, upload.php, exec.php, test.php) or obfuscated names (base64-encoded, hash-like).

suggestion.title: PHP Process Child of Web Server (Code Execution)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'execution of PHP code'—after upload, PHP is invoked. Detect cmd.exe, bash, or powershell spawned by php-fpm, apache2, w3wp.exe indicating web shell activation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child process creation where parent is w3wp.exe, apache2, nginx, or php-fpm and child is cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or /bin/sh. Include command-line context; web shell payloads often surface GET/POST parameter references.

suggestion.title: Rapid Profile Creation from Single External Source
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'improper access control' suggests iteration or brute-force possible. Multiple profile-creation POST requests from one IP before successful exploitation indicates enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate POST requests to profile endpoint by source IP in 10-minute windows. Alert if single IP generates >5 requests, especially if mixed with HTTP 401/403 responses before eventual 200 OK. False-positive risk: admin bulk-upload workflows.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Vulnerable Joomla Content Editor Instances

Parse HTTP response headers and Joomla configuration.php for affected versions prior to 2026-06-19 patch deadline.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Editor Profile Creation Without Authentication

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor uploaded files in web-accessible directories for polyglot content: image file signatures (first bytes = GIF8, FFD8, 89504E47) combined with code patterns (`<?php`, `eval(`, `system(`, `passthru()`, backticks). This is the exact masquerading shape described.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Upload to Web-Accessible Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'upload and execution of PHP code' but execution phase is completely absent from kill chain. Must detect malicious file write.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .php/.phtml file writes to Joomla web-accessible directories (components, media, plugins) correlated with unauthenticated editor profile creation in preceding minutes. Flag suspicious PHP code in uploads (system(), exec(), passthru() calls).

suggestion.title: PHP Execution via Uploaded File
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'execution of PHP code'—no execution-phase detections provided. Must detect runtime command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for php/php-cgi child processes spawned by web server (apache2, nginx, httpd) with execution of recently-written PHP files in web-accessible paths. Alert on suspicious system commands invoked from PHP context.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence in Joomla Installation
suggestion.rationale: Uploaded and executed PHP code naturally persists as a web shell. Article describes execution capability but no persistence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for newly-created PHP files in Joomla directories with timestamps matching exploitation window. Scan content for web shell indicators (eval(), base64_decode(), $_REQUEST execution, one-liner command handlers).

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication Pattern Against Joomla Admin Panel
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires accessing editor functionality without credentials. Article emphasizes 'improper access control'—detect authentication-bypass attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track successful requests to Joomla editor endpoints without prior successful administrator login. Detect rapid, automated profile-creation requests from single IP/user-agent (behavior consistent with CVE exploitation tooling).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'improper access control vulnerability which could allow for upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' This is the attack entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/PUT requests to Joomla profile/editor creation endpoints (administrator/index.php, plugin manager) from unauthenticated sessions (guest user, no prior login event). Alert on successful 200/302 responses to profile creation followed by file writes in the same session.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Joomla Editor Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'upload and execution of PHP code via...editor profiles.' Uploaded .php files to web-accessible directories are the execution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .php file creation in /components/com_*/editor/*, /plugins/editors/*, /media/editors/*, or equivalent Joomla editor paths, within 5 minutes of unauthenticated profile creation POST. Correlate source IP across HTTP access logs and file change events.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Execution in Joomla Editor Context
suggestion.rationale: Article documents active wild exploitation (CISA KEV status), so uploaded PHP code must be executed. Process-level detection is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for php.exe or php-cgi process spawned by web server user (www-data, apache, iis apppool) with parent/CWD referencing plugins or editors. Monitor Joomla application logs for unexpected extension activation or task execution from editor components.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly prescribes: 'CVE-2026-48907 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline must generate scanner-driven detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor instances with versions in CVE-2026-48907 affected range. Prioritize internet-facing assets (public IP, no WAF). Cross-reference scanner match timestamp with netflow/Zeek for successful inbound remote connections.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Admin/Editor Feature Access Without Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability mechanism: 'improper access control' allows unauthenticated users to access admin/profile creation features. Authorization bypass detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla logs for admin task execution (task=save, action=create, component operations) from guest/anonymous users. HTTP proxy should show direct /administrator/ access with zero prior successful authentication from that IP in the session window.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Editor Profile Creation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability allows 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users' — this is the primary access control bypass vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla access logs for POST/PUT requests to editor profile endpoints (e.g., component=com_editors, task=profile operations) arriving without valid session tokens or authentication headers. Alert on profile creation attempts originating from external IP ranges or non-administrative user contexts.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Upload to Joomla Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Attack explicitly includes 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles' — file upload to web-accessible directories is the execution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web application logs for multipart file uploads to Joomla plugin/editor directories (e.g., /plugins, /components/com_editors/). Alert on .php, .phtml files written to web root with timestamps outside maintenance windows. Track file size anomalies in profile uploads (large binaries in profile data).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Widget Factory Component Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal due date 2026-06-19; vulnerability scanning is baseline detection for known-exploited vulnerabilities regardless of patch claims, due to industry patch lag.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor presence and version matching CVE-2026-48907 signature. Cross-reference asset inventory to flag public-facing Joomla instances. Generate high-priority alerts for unpatched instances with internet-routable IPs; escalate based on federal timeline.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Unauthenticated Requests to Joomla Administrator Functions
suggestion.rationale: Improper access control means attackers bypass authentication; monitor for abnormal request patterns to normally-restricted endpoints as described in 'unauthenticated' profile creation capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline HTTP request patterns to /administrator, editor profile endpoints, and component configuration pages — establish threshold for authenticated-only traffic. Alert on sustained requests from external/untrusted sources lacking authentication context. Correlate with failed login logs and IP reputation data.

suggestion.title: Recovery Partition XML File Access and Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Recovery Partition XML Files' as attack surface: 'Bypasses Windows BitLocker via Recovery Partition XML Files'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file-system access to Windows recovery/EFI partitions (\Recovery, \EFI, \BOOT, \BIOS) by non-system processes, or CREATE/MODIFY operations on .xml files within those paths. Alert on process elevation followed by XML file access in recovery contexts, or on attempts to mount recovery partitions via diskpart, SetupAPI, or direct partition access.

suggestion.title: BitLocker Metadata Enumeration and Key Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'Bypasses Windows BitLocker'. Recovery partition XML files store BitLocker metadata and key material. Article: 'GreatXML Exploit Bypasses Windows BitLocker'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process calls to manage-bde.exe, WMI BitLocker methods (win32_encryptablevolume), or direct reads of BitLocker configuration registry hives (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\BitLocker). Flag recovery key export or enumeration attempts, or access to recovery XML files by processes not signed by Microsoft.

suggestion.title: Privileged XML Processing in Pre-OS/Recovery Context
suggestion.rationale: Threat name 'GreatXML' and attack chain require XML parsing during recovery/pre-OS execution with elevated privilege. Article: 'GreatXML Exploit ... XML Files'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of XML parsers (powershell.exe, cscript.exe, mshta.exe, msxml3-6 library loads) with SYSTEM or TrustedInstaller privileges when processing files from recovery partitions or boot-time execution contexts. Flag unusual XML parser invocations from System32 that read recovery-related paths.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Recovery Partition Mount and Direct Access
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires access to recovery partition normally sealed from user-mode code. 'Recovery Partition XML Files' implies partition enumeration, mounting, or direct access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-OS processes invoking volume/partition APIs (SetupAPI, VDS/VSS, diskpart.exe, ioctl calls), attempting to enumerate or mount recovery partitions, or accessing raw partition tables. Flag processes acquiring SeSystemtimePrivilege or SeLoadDriverPrivilege that interact with recovery partition paths.

suggestion.title: XML External Entity (XXE) Attack on BitLocker Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Recovery partition XML files likely encode BitLocker configuration, key material, or encryption metadata. XXE or XML bomb exploitation is congruent with 'GreatXML' naming.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for XML parsing exceptions or resource exhaustion (billion laughs attacks, entity expansion loops) when XML parsers consume files from recovery/boot partitions. Alert on external entity (DOCTYPE/ENTITY) declarations in XML files recovered from recovery partitions, or on parser errors indicative of XXE attempts.

suggestion.title: Widget Factory Joomla Editor — Unauthenticated Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allow[s] upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' This is the exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to Joomla editor profile creation endpoints (e.g., /administrator/index.php?option=com_contenteditor) from unauthenticated sessions or sessions lacking admin privileges. Baseline: legitimate profile creation should be rare or nonexistent in typical environments.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Upload via Joomla Editor Profiles
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'upload and execution of PHP code.' This is the payload delivery and T1505.004 (Web Shell) execution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for multipart/form-data HTTP requests with .php, .phtml, or executable extensions being written to web-accessible directories via the editor profile creation endpoint. Flag unexpected executable file uploads to /media, /images, or web root followed by HTTP requests to execute the uploaded file.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires federal remediation by 2026-06-19 (same-day deadline). Scanner detection is primary IOC for asset prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any CVE-2026-48907 match in vulnerability scanner results for Joomla instances, especially those with internet-facing administrative interfaces. Prioritize for emergency patching ahead of 2026-06-19 deadline.

suggestion.title: Widget Factory Plugin Presence on Joomla Instances
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires the vulnerable plugin to be installed. Asset discovery of affected software is prerequisite for hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Joomla installations running Widget Factory Content Editor via plugin manifest enumeration (HTTP GET to plugin paths, plugin XML responses, HTTP headers). Flag unpatched versions in asset inventory for immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP Execution Post-Upload to Joomla
suggestion.rationale: After PHP file is uploaded via unauthenticated editor profile creation, attacker executes it. Correlation between upload and execution signals exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP POST requests to editor profile endpoints with subsequent HTTP requests to newly-created PHP files. Look for .php files in web root with recent creation timestamps matching upload requests, then accessed via HTTP GET/POST within seconds. This signals web shell execution.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability affects 'public-facing application' and CISA KEV only lists actively exploited flaws. Standard first-line hunt for exposed Joomla + Content Editor installations. Article: 'public-facing application'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Joomla installations with Content Editor plugin active. Use asset discovery scanners (e.g., Shodan, Censys) for 'Joomla' + 'Content Editor' headers, HTTP fingerprints, or plugin signatures. Correlate with internal vulnerability scanner CVE-2026-48907 findings. Prioritize publicly routable assets.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Unauthenticated Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users' — this is the attack entry point. Detection should flag profile creation from non-authenticated sessions before successful login.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to Joomla editor profile creation endpoints (typically /administrator/index.php or /component/contenteditor/profiles). Alert when requests originate from unauthenticated sessions (no valid session token, IP not in whitelist, user-agent anomalies). High FP risk from legitimate admin use — baseline typical profile creation patterns first.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload via Joomla Editor Profile
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles.' Detection must capture the actual payload delivery (PHP file upload) separate from profile creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file write events to Joomla Content Editor upload directories for .php extensions. Cross-correlate with process execution of PHP interpreter (php-cgi, php-fpm) immediately after upload. Baseline expected PHP uploads from admin users; flag all others. Watch for polyglot uploads (.php.jpg) as bypass.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Exploitation Pattern — Joomla Content Editor
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV catalog entry requires active threat hunting for this specific CVE. Article: 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date.' Standard practice is cross-fleet scanner correlation + intrusion attempt detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all hosts in vulnerability scanner output with CVE-2026-48907 present. Cross-correlate with patch management system to identify unpatched instances. Secondary: hunt logs for exploitation signatures (malformed profile creation requests, PHP error logs from editor component, unexpected PHP execution from web-accessible paths).

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via Joomla Editor — Post-Exploit Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article describes successful exploitation results in 'execution of PHP code' on server. Post-exploitation detection must cover attacker activity post-upload (webshell runtime, reverse shell, data exfil).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP process spawning unexpected child processes (bash, cmd.exe, powershell) immediately after Content Editor uploads. Alert on outbound network connections from php-cgi/php-fpm to non-whitelisted external IPs. Look for PHP sessions with abnormally long runtimes or memory allocation anomalies in application logs.

suggestion.title: Scanner/WAF Detection: CVE-2026-48907 Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation flow can be detected at ingress before profile creation succeeds. Article: 'improper access control' is the vulnerability class — WAF rules should detect unauthenticated attempts to access restricted endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: WAF signature-based detection for POST/GET requests to /component/contenteditor/profiles/* or /administrator/index.php?option=com_contenteditor&... from unauthenticated sources. Alert on 403->success state transitions (access control bypass). IDS rule: flag unusual HTTP methods or Content-Type headers targeting editor plugin paths.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Editor Profile Creation via Joomla Widget Factory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated users' can perform 'creation of new editor profiles'—this is the initial exploitation step and should be detectable via POST/create requests to editor endpoints without valid authentication tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor profile-creation endpoints (typical paths: /plugins/system/widget_factory/*, /components/com_widget_factory/*, /administrator/index.php?option=com_*) from sources without valid session/authentication cookies. Baseline legitimate profile creation and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Joomla Web-Accessible Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'upload... of PHP code'—profile creation likely accepts file uploads that are written to web-accessible paths. Detect uploads of .php files or suspicious content-type mismatches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .php file writes to Joomla web directories (typically /images/*, /media/*, /tmp/*, /components/*, /plugins/*) that correlate with preceding editor profile creation attempts. Correlate web server logs showing POST uploads with subsequent file-system writes.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Editor Profile Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'execution of PHP code' via newly created profiles—web server must execute PHP files uploaded to profile storage. Detect web process spawning child processes or executing code patterns indicative of PHP execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to uploaded profile paths (GET/POST to recently written .php files in editor directories) followed by unexpected child-process execution (typical for PHP shell: curl, wget, bash, powershell spawned by php or httpd processes).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scan Detection & Patch Gap
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry implies active exploitation in the wild—standard hunt is asset exposure. Article provides CVE identifier and federal patch due-date (2026-06-19) which should drive patch urgency hunts and scanner correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-48907 against live web services inventory. Identify hosts running Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor versions ≤ [vulnerable version] without patches. Correlate with web-server logs for any access attempts to known vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Improper Access Control: Unauthorized Access to Joomla Editor Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'improper access control' allowing unauthenticated access to editor features—detect requests to admin/protected editor endpoints from IPs/users lacking valid authorization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP 200/302 responses to Joomla editor configuration endpoints (/administrator/*, /backend/*, /editor/config*) from requests lacking valid session cookies, API keys, or authentication headers. Flag rapid iteration through editor endpoints as scanning behavior.

suggestion.title: Widget Factory Plugin Activation & Suspicious Component Access
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor' as the vulnerable product—detect deployment, activation, or suspicious interaction with this plugin/component as precursor to exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on web requests to Widget Factory component paths (/components/com_widget_factory/*, plugin_widget_factory* files) especially POST/PUT requests or high-volume GET requests from unusual sources. Correlate with file-system changes in plugin/component directories.

suggestion.title: Joomla Content Editor Unauthenticated Profile Creation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack: 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' This is the weaponization step and entry point; no use case generated for it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to Joomla Content Editor profile endpoints (/administrator/index.php?option=com_contenteditor or variant) originating from unauthenticated sessions (no valid admin token/session ID). Alert on HTTP 200/201 responses to profile creation requests from non-whitelisted source IPs or unusual User-Agents.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Web-Accessible Media Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'upload and execution of PHP code'—detection must capture the upload stage. No use case exists for file-write patterns after profile creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PHP-executable file extensions (.php, .phtml, .php3, .php4, .php5, .phtml) created in Joomla /media or Content Editor plugin directories within 5 minutes of an unauthenticated profile creation HTTP request. Cross-reference creator process context (should be web service account, not admin user).

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies execution occurs after upload: 'execution of PHP code via...creation of new editor profiles.' Detect process spawning (PHP interpreter invocation) or HTTP request execution of the uploaded payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Windows: detect w3wp.exe, httpd.exe, or nginx.exe spawning php.exe / php-cgi.exe with command-line referencing files in /media subdirectories. Linux: detect Apache/Nginx child processes spawning php-fpm with suspicious working directory or script arguments. Correlate process creation time with file creation timestamp.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' using template and CVE substitution. Pipeline failed to instantiate the template logic for this active-exploitation CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-48907 in Joomla Content Editor installations. Cross-reference against CMDB / patch-management records to identify systems with contradicting patch status (reported patched but still flagged). Prioritize internet-facing/DMZ instances. Validate federal due-date enforcement (2026-06-19 remediation deadline).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation PHP Web Shell Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'upload and execution' without limitation—adversary may establish long-lived web shell. No persistence-phase detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated HTTP requests to the same uploaded PHP file from multiple source IPs or scheduled/recurring request patterns. Alert on creation of additional files in the same directory by the web service account post-exploitation. Detect outbound traffic (C2 callbacks) from the web service account spawned after suspicious PHP execution.

suggestion.title: Joomla Editor Profile Creation by Unauthenticated Users
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users' — unauthorized profile creation is the earliest direct exploitation signal and distinguishes this from generic web scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for POST requests to Joomla editor profile endpoints (e.g., index.php?option=com_editorprofile&task=profile) originating without valid session cookies or Authorization headers, particularly if followed by 200-series responses. Cross-reference with failed authentication logs to isolate pre-auth attempts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP File Upload to Joomla Editor Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles' — detecting PHP writes to editor paths is post-auth-bypass, pre-execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful HTTP POST to editor plugin directories returning 200 status, correlated with new .php file creation in Joomla editor plugin paths (e.g., /components/com_editorprofile/, /plugins/editors/). Focus on timeline proximity (upload → file-write within <5 seconds).

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Joomla Widget Factory Editor Plugin Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor' as the vulnerable software; asset inventory is the preventive layer before exploitation window opens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for Joomla installations with Widget Factory editor plugin active (CVE-2026-48907 match). Cross-reference scanner version strings against patch-management DB to isolate unpatched or no-compliance instances. Enumerate via Joomla administrator panel or plugin-listing endpoints.

suggestion.title: PHP Command Execution in Joomla Editor Plugin Context
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'upload and execution' — post-upload execution detection captures actual code-run phase. Execution should occur in web-server process context with editor plugin in working directory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP interpreter (php.exe, php-cgi, php-fpm child processes) spawned by web server workers with working directory or process arguments containing Joomla editor plugin paths. Alert on unexpected shell metacharacters or system-command child processes (cmd, bash, powershell) spawned from PHP in these contexts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Asset Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in template, substitute CVE-2026-48907.' Pipeline generated zero use cases and ignored explicit template guidance. CISA KEV due-date is 2026-06-19 — detection is urgent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner signatures or HTTP fingerprints identifying Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor with CVE-2026-48907. Prioritize remediation by federal due-date. Use asset-exposure template with substitution of CVE-2026-48907 in both Splunk and Defender KQL.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability permits 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' This is the attack vector; profile creation without session should be detectable and alertable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla access logs for editor profile creation (POST/PUT to profile endpoints) originating from requests with no valid authentication token. Correlate request source, profile name, and timestamp for post-exploitation pivoting.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Upload to Editor Components
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability enables 'upload and execution of PHP code.' Pipeline missed detection for the upload phase and subsequent execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation/modification events (.php files) in Joomla editor component directories (typically /components/com_joomlaeditor/profiles/). Correlate with HTTP requests to the same paths from unauthenticated or suspicious sources.

suggestion.title: Joomla Web Shell Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: 'Execution of PHP code' is the stated impact. Detection of actual web shell execution (eval, system, exec, passthru calls) is a natural hunt for post-compromise analysis that pipeline omitted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt PHP execution logs for shell metacommands (system(), shell_exec(), exec(), passthru()) originating from Joomla editor component paths. Detect HTTP requests to newly-created .php files with abnormal query parameters or POST payloads.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance for Joomla Editor Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV active exploitation suggests scanning/reconnaissance phase. Pipeline missed detection for fuzzing or enumeration of Joomla editor management interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on patterns of HTTP 404/403 responses or parameter fuzzing against Joomla editor component paths. High volume of requests to non-existent profiles, permission-denied editor operations, or repeated failed authentication attempts to editor admin interfaces indicate scanning.

suggestion.title: Upload validation rule bypass: file extension mismatch on MIME-derived filename
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the vulnerability mechanism: 'ext_in upload validation rule checked the MIME-derived guessed extension instead of the client-provided filename extension.' Pipeline missed detection for the validation-bypass itself, not just post-exploitation. Could detect via form-data inspection or upload-handler logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multipart form submissions where Content-Type and filename extension are mismatched (e.g., Content-Type: image/gif but filename ends in .php/.phtml). If upload logs or proxy can capture multipart body metadata, flag discrepancies between declared MIME type and actual file extension.

suggestion.title: Recently-uploaded file retroactively executed by web server
suggestion.rationale: Article workflow: file uploaded, then web server spawns shell FROM that file. Detection should correlate file creation timestamp in upload directory with immediate subsequent process execution. Pipeline UC_102_1 and UC_102_3 are separate; this joins them.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Join file creation event (*.php in uploads dir) with process creation from same timestamp (webserver spawning shell) within a 5-10 second window. Alert on the temporal correlation, signaling that a just-uploaded script was immediately invoked.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated users' can trigger the flaw via 'creation of new editor profiles.' This is the attack vector — no authentication required, meaning any external actor can reach it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla application logs and HTTP access logs for POST requests to editor profile creation endpoints (e.g., /administrator/index.php?option=com_joomcontenteditor or equivalent paths) originating from non-authenticated sessions. Alert on HTTP 200/201 responses indicating profile creation success without prior authentication.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload via Joomla Editor Profile Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles.' This is the exploitation step — malicious code uploaded as part of profile creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST/PUT requests to Joomla editor profile endpoints with PHP file payloads or code patterns (.php files, PHP tags like <?php in multipart form data). Correlate with FIM alerts on .php file creation in Joomla plugin/module directories outside scheduled deployments.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution Post-Upload in Joomla Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'execution of PHP code' following upload. The malicious PHP is not just stored — it is invoked, creating web-accessible executable payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to newly created Joomla editor profile resources that trigger PHP execution (e.g., requests to /components/com_joomcontenteditor/profiles/* or similar). Correlate with unusual process spawning (php-cgi, php-fpm child processes) or outbound connections initiated by the web server user. High-fidelity signal if profile was created in the same session window.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence via Joomla Editor Profile
suggestion.rationale: Upload + execution of PHP creates a web shell. Article's emphasis on 'upload and execution' suggests the attacker maintains code execution post-compromise via the profile mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to Joomla editor profile paths that pass suspicious query parameters, encoded payloads, or shell commands (e.g., cmd=, exec=, system=, passthru=). Correlate with FIM alerts showing persistence of .php files in profiles or config directories, especially if file mod times predate profile creation by seconds.

suggestion.title: Joomla Plugin/Component Enumeration Pre-Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article names the vulnerable component explicitly ('Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor'). Active exploitation likely includes reconnaissance to identify vulnerable instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests probing for Joomla component signatures, plugin manifests, or administrator endpoints that reveal installed components (e.g., requests to /administrator/, /components/, /plugins/, XML manifest lookups). Spike in 404s or probing patterns against component URLs before successful exploit attempts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scanner / Exploit Kit Activity
suggestion.rationale: This is a CISA KEV with active exploitation. Threat actors and automated scanning tools will probe for vulnerable instances. Early detection of scanning activity can block before exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP User-Agent strings and request patterns consistent with vulnerability scanners (Shodan, Censys, Nessus, Metasploit modules targeting CVE-2026-48907). Flag requests to known-vulnerable paths with timing clusters (multiple attempts from same IP within seconds) or geographic anomalies inconsistent with user base.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Editor Profile Creation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'improper access control vulnerability which could allow...via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users'. Profile creation from unauthenticated sessions is the exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/PUT requests to Joomla editor profile endpoints lacking valid session tokens. Flag requests to /components/com_content/ or /plugins/editors/ containing profile-configuration parameters from unauthenticated origins.

suggestion.title: PHP File Creation in Joomla Editor Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles'. PHP files uploaded to editor paths are the malicious payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of .php, .phtml, or .pht files in Joomla editor storage paths (e.g., /media/editors/, /components/com_content/admin/). Alert when new PHP files are written within 5 minutes of unauthenticated profile-creation requests.

suggestion.title: Invocation of Newly Uploaded PHP in Joomla Editor Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'execution of PHP code'. After upload, the PHP is executed by the web server; detect this execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to .php files in Joomla editor directories within 60 seconds of their creation. Correlate with web-server process events; legitimate editor activity should not spawn shell interpreters (/bin/bash, /bin/sh) as child processes.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence in Joomla Editor Storage
suggestion.rationale: Article describes PHP upload capability enabling persistence. Uploaded PHP files survive and remain executable for future exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Use file integrity monitoring to baseline Joomla editor directories. Alert on new executable files (.php, .phtml, .pht, .phps) created outside change-control windows. Correlate suspicious PHP presence with unauthenticated web-access patterns.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated POST to Joomla Editor Profile Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users' — core exploitation vector requiring authentication context and session token analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to Joomla editor profile creation endpoints without valid session tokens or with missing authentication headers. Alert on multiple profile-creation attempts from single source within short time window.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Upload via Joomla Editor Profile
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability enables 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles' — requires file activity monitoring on upload directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .php file creation in Joomla editor profile or temporary directories. Flag multipart POST requests containing PHP payloads or double-extension files (.php.jpg) to component upload handlers.

suggestion.title: Widget Factory Joomla Editor Vulnerable Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV categorization means active exploitation; article identifies Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor as vulnerable product with federal patch due date 2026-06-19.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor installations. Cross-reference with public-facing asset inventory. Flag any instances with patched status lagging behind 2026-06-19 federal due date.

suggestion.title: Rapid POST Scanning to Joomla Component Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation pattern typically includes reconnaissance phase probing vulnerable component endpoints — article describes component-level attack surface suggesting pre-exploitation scanning behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume POST requests to /index.php?option=com_* endpoints from single IP address with mixed 401/403 and 200 responses, indicating permission-bypass testing followed by successful access.

suggestion.title: Joomla Content Editor Plugin Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor as the vulnerable product. Baseline asset discovery is prerequisite to all downstream hunts. Article states vulnerability requires product to be installed and accessible.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset inventories for Widget Factory Content Editor installations. Parse HTTP response headers and plugin directory enumeration for plugin version matching CVE-2026-48907 affected range. Establish asset registry baseline by 2026-06-19 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Profile Creation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users' — this is the sole attack vector and must be monitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla application logs and HTTP access logs for profile creation endpoint requests (typically components/com_joomcontent/profile or editor profile creation paths) from unauthenticated sessions. Flag POST/PUT requests to profile creation endpoints without valid auth tokens, session cookies, or CSRF tokens.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Joomla Editor Directories
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly enables 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles.' Pipeline must surface file creation events in Joomla component/plugin directories, the staging ground for web shell placement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .php file creation in Joomla plugin directories (components/com_*/*, plugins/editors/*). Correlate file creation timestamps with HTTP POST requests to editor profile endpoints from unauthenticated sources within 2-minute window. Priority if file is executable by web server.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Execution from Editor Component
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation manifests as PHP code execution in attacker-controlled files. Detection must identify command execution, outbound connections, or reconnaissance activity originating from Joomla web process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server process (apache, www-data, nginx user) for spawning child processes (sh, bash, cmd.exe) or unusual system calls. Flag outbound network connections initiated by web processes. Correlate to recent access logs showing requests to newly created PHP files in plugin directories.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Scanner-Based Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references templated asset-exposure hunt: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [`../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`]... Substitute this CVE wherever the template references `<CVE>`: CVE: `CVE-2026-48907`.' Pipeline should populate this template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Execute standard asset-exposure template substituting CVE-2026-48907. Query all vulnerability management platforms and patch compliance systems for Widget Factory Content Editor vulnerable versions. Cross-reference with web server inventories and access logs for exploitation correlation.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Unpatched Joomla Content Editor Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CISA KEV only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild' and Joomla Content Editor is a public-facing application. Standard asset-exposure hunt should detect instances running vulnerable versions before T1190 succeeds. Article phrase: 'patch lag is the silent killer.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results and network telemetry for Joomla installations with Widget Factory Content Editor on HTTP/HTTPS ports. Correlate against published Joomla version fingerprints and known-vulnerable Content Editor plugin versions < patched release date.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Unauthenticated Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could allow for upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' Anomalous or bulk profile creation, especially by unauthenticated/public sessions, signals exploitation attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla admin/editor API endpoints for POST requests creating profiles (profile/create, editor config endpoints) from unauthenticated sessions or high-entropy sources. Baseline normal admin profile creation frequency and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Upload to Joomla Editor Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'upload and execution of PHP code.' The attack requires uploading malicious PHP via the editor profile mechanism. Monitor for writes of .php, .phtml, or executable content to editor plugin/profile directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file writes of PHP extensions to Joomla editor directories (plugins/content/, components/com_*/upload/, cache/). Correlate with failed authentication attempts or requests from unusual IP ranges. Check file names for encoding tricks (double extensions, null bytes).

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Web Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes PHP code execution as the endpoint of the attack. T1059.004 execution from httpd/php-fpm processes indicates successful exploitation post-upload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by httpd/php-fpm (bash, sh, curl, wget, nc) especially with network connectivity or unusual arguments. Joomla out-of-the-box rarely shells from PHP; any shell spawn is high-fidelity. Cross-reference process timeline against editor profile creation and file upload events.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Exploit Pattern Recognition
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV article explicitly names CVE-2026-48907 as actively exploited. Standard practice is to alert on scanner detections, WAF signatures, or IDS/HTTP request patterns specific to this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on WAF/IDS signatures for CVE-2026-48907 payloads (likely HTTP POST to editor profile creation endpoints with PHP payloads or encoded executables). Correlate vulnerability scanner findings with actual exploit attempts from external sources.

suggestion.title: Web Application Error Spikes from Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Failed exploitation attempts often leave HTTP 403/500 errors or application logs before successful upload. Article does not specify whether the editor endpoints check authentication before processing; scanning for error patterns can catch both failed and successful attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline HTTP error rates (403 Forbidden, 500 Internal Server Error, 400 Bad Request) on editor profile creation endpoints. Alert on sudden spikes from external IPs or unusual user-agents. Look for patterns of repeated attempts to the same endpoint.

suggestion.title: Joomla Content Editor: Unauthenticated Profile Creation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' This is the direct attack vector and should be the first detection layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to Joomla Content Editor profile-creation endpoints (typically /administrator/index.php?option=com_jce or plugin-specific endpoints) originating from IPs with no prior valid session token or authentication cookie. Alert on successful 2xx responses to profile-creation requests without valid auth context.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Joomla Editor Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'upload and execution of PHP code' as the exploitation payload. Detect .php uploads to editor-controlled or plugin-accessible directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor multipart/form-data HTTP requests containing .php file extensions targeting editor plugin directories (e.g., /plugins/editors/jce/*, /components/com_jce/*). Correlate successful uploads (HTTP 200/201) with subsequent HTTP requests executing those .php files (e.g., GET /plugins/editors/jce/uploads/payload.php).

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution in Web Server Context (Content Editor Plugin)
suggestion.rationale: Article endpoint: 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles.' Detect PHP execution in editor-owned directories post-upload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests (GET/POST) to .php files in Joomla editor plugin directories, especially those preceded by recent file-creation or upload events in the same directory. Check web server error logs for PHP syntax errors or warnings during execution attempts.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Joomla with Vulnerable Content Editor Plugin
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'worth one quick check across your fleet — patch lag is the silent killer.' Identify all Joomla instances with Widget Factory Content Editor exposed to the internet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results and asset inventory for Joomla instances running Widget Factory Content Editor plugin. Flag instances without geographic or IP-range firewall restrictions, or those with default credentials. Cross-reference against Shodan/Censys for internet exposure.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Scanner Detection & Federal Patch Deadline Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article: CISA KEV status means 'currently being exploited.' CVE-2026-48907 is the direct match indicator, with federal due date 2026-06-19. Scan and track.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any Nessus/Qualys/Tenable detection of CVE-2026-48907 in network scans. Create a compliance-tracking record flagging patch due date 2026-06-19 for federal/regulated assets. Monitor CISA KEV feed for updates on active exploitation variations.

suggestion.title: Web Server Access Log Anomalies: Unknown Editor Plugin Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Joomla Content Editor plugin is the attack surface. Enumerate legitimate plugin endpoints and alert on unexpected access patterns outside normal admin workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal Joomla administrator and plugin endpoint access patterns. Alert on HTTP requests to /administrator or editor plugin paths originating from external/untrusted networks, or with User-Agent strings associated with scanners/bots. Correlate with lack of subsequent legitimate admin actions.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Content Editor Profile Creation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated users' to 'create new editor profiles'—the canonical entry point. Pipeline generated zero use cases for this attack step despite it being unambiguous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/GET requests to Widget Factory Joomla editor profile creation endpoints (typically /index.php?option=com_*&task=profile) from external sources without preceding authentication session. Flag HTTP 200/302 responses lacking associated login events or auth tokens.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'match against your vulnerability scanner' for CVE-2026-48907; this is the canonical detection baseline. Pipeline produced no IOC or scanner-based use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any scan result reporting CVE-2026-48907 on internet-facing Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor instances. Escalate severity if finding persists past 2026-06-19 (Federal patch due date cited in article).

suggestion.title: PHP Code Upload and Execution via Editor Upload Handler
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could allow for upload and execution of PHP code'—the terminal payload delivery and RCE mechanism. Zero execution-phase use cases generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to Joomla editor upload handlers with PHP file payloads or inline PHP code in request body. Correlate successful uploads with subsequent PHP execution (suspicious webshell HTTP patterns, runtime process spawning).

suggestion.title: External Access to Widget Factory Joomla Administrator Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'public-facing application' and recommends 'asset-exposure hunt.' Pipeline generated no reconnaissance or external-access baseline detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline external HTTP(S) access to Joomla Content Editor admin/profile creation paths (/administrator/*, /index.php?option=com_*). Alert on GeoIP anomalies, TOR/VPN origins, or non-corporate IP ranges attempting these endpoints.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation PHP Webshell Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: After successful upload, attacker gains PHP webshell capability for command execution. Article mentions 'execution of PHP code' but pipeline generated zero post-exploitation/C2 phase use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests with encoded/obfuscated parameters, system command patterns (whoami, id, ls, cat, curl, nc) hitting previously uploaded paths or standard webshell endpoints. Correlate with process creation by web server runtime (PHP process spawning shell).

suggestion.title: Host Header Mismatch with Spoofed auth-user Service Identity
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability requires BOTH 'req.get("host").startsWith(getHostName())' AND 'auth-user: service-brother' headers to bypass validation. Current UCs omit Host header analysis entirely, leaving half the attack pattern undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for HTTP requests containing 'auth-user: service-brother' header combined with a Host header that does NOT match the legitimate application FQDN or expected internal service endpoints. Track the source IP—if external, this strongly indicates exploitation of the bypass.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access Post-Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article describes authentication bypass leading to unauthorized access, but pipeline generates no detection for what happens AFTER the bypass—HTTP 200 responses to protected endpoints, access to admin resources, or token generation following a failed initial authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP requests with 'auth-user: service-brother' header against response codes (look for 200/201 on previously-protected endpoints) or against baseline access patterns. Flag transitions from 401/403 → 200 within same session or source IP.

suggestion.title: Cross-Process Service Identity Masquerading
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows unauthenticated clients to impersonate 'service-brother' service identity via header. Detection should flag cases where auth-user header source does not match legitimate service-brother process identity on the network (e.g., request claiming to be service-brother but origin is an attacker IP).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP requests bearing 'auth-user: service-brother' against the source IP's process ownership. If the source IP's processes do NOT include legitimate service-brother components, or if the request originates from an external/untrusted segment, flag as potential header spoofing.

suggestion.title: validateToken() Bypass via Service Account Reuse
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions service-to-service auth bypass where 'auth-user: service-brother' label acts as a hardcoded exempt path. Baseline service-brother's legitimate traffic patterns and alert on anomalous destinations, endpoints, or request methods deviating from normal service-to-service communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for legitimate 'auth-user: service-brother' traffic (expected destination IPs, ports, endpoints, request methods). Alert when service-brother identity is used to access unusual endpoints, execute mutations (POST/PUT/DELETE to non-expected paths), or communicate with unexpected destinations.

suggestion.title: NetLicensing Token Endpoint Unexpected Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the traversal redirects requests to the token endpoint, bypassing redaction. No baseline or deviation detection is present. Critical gap: 'silently redirecting the request to the NetLicensing token endpoint' (article body) requires monitoring for /token hits that originate from product_number traversals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate /token endpoint access. Flag hits to /token endpoint from sources/users who have no baseline history of token requests, or hits that correlate temporally with traversal-pattern activity on /product/ endpoints.

suggestion.title: MCP Tool Invocation with Path Traversal in product_number
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability is in direct interpolation of product_number into REST URL. Article identifies specific parameter: 'caller-controlled `product_number` argument'. This should be detected at the MCP server level if logging is available.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor netlicensing_get_product MCP tool invocations for product_number values containing ../, %2e%2e, %2f, %5c, or other path-traversal signatures. Flag any product_number that, when interpolated into a REST path, would resolve to a non-product endpoint (e.g., /token, /auth, /license).

suggestion.title: Encoded Path Traversal in Product Parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article body lists detection of encoded variants: %2e%2e, %2f, %5c. These bypass simple string matching. Requires specific hunt for URL-encoding of traversal characters in the product_number field.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for product_number parameter values containing URL-encoded path separators and dots (%2e, %2f, %5c) that decode to ../. Correlate with requests to go.netlicensing.io or netlicensing.labs64.com /product/ endpoints.

suggestion.title: Behavioral: Rapid Token Endpoint Probing Post-Product Requests
suggestion.rationale: An attacker would likely probe traversal success by attempting /token access after sending a crafted product_number. Article describes the bypass behavior but provides no detection for the behavioral sequence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences: product/ request with traversal characters → immediate /token endpoint request from the same source within 5 minutes, especially if /token is not in the source's normal baseline.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task Creation Monitoring USB Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The worm creates a scheduled task that monitors for newly connected USB storage devices.' Core persistence and propagation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for schtasks.exe or PowerShell creating scheduled tasks with triggers bound to USB/removable media insertion events or with descriptive names suggesting device monitoring. High signal: tasks created by non-admin processes or with unusual parent processes.

suggestion.title: Malicious LNK Execution from Removable Media
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The infection process starts with the victim opening the LNK file, triggering the malware on the USB drive.' Direct initial-access execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe or PowerShell spawning from explorer.exe with a removable-media-resident LNK file as the source. Look for process command lines containing .lnk paths from USB or external drives, or parent process being the LNK target itself.

suggestion.title: Original Files Hidden and Replaced by Malicious Shortcuts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the malware hides the originals and replaces them with malicious shortcuts bearing the same names. This causes the malware to execute when users attempt to open the documents.' Defense evasion + persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate attrib.exe +h calls (or direct file-hiding API) with subsequent .lnk creation in document directories (Users/*/Documents, Downloads, Desktop). Flag when .lnk file shares the name of a hidden non-shortcut file in the same directory.

suggestion.title: High-Frequency Clipboard Polling for Cryptocurrency Keys and Seed Phrases
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Every half a second, the malware checks the clipboard for... 12-word BIP39 seed phrases, 24-word BIP39 seed phrases, Ethereum private keys, Bitcoin WIF keys, Bitcoin legacy/P2SH/Bech32/Taproot addresses, Tron, Monero addresses.' Behavioral credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes calling GetClipboardData() or clipboard-hooking APIs at high frequency (polling every 500ms pattern). Detect regex/pattern-matching operations targeting wallet-address formats or BIP39 seed-phrase structure on clipboard contents.

suggestion.title: Rapid Screenshot Exfiltration via curl to Tor
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the malware also captures five screenshots of the victim's screen every ten seconds and sends them to the C2 using the curl tool.' Data exfiltration mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect curl.exe spawned as child of suspicious parents (not Windows Update, antivirus, or legitimate software), especially when preceded by screenshot API calls or screencap operations. Correlate with network connections to localhost:9050 or Tor exit-node subnets.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via Downloaded JavaScript in 'cfile'
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the malware downloads JavaScript content into a file named 'cfile,' and executes it on the infected machine.' C2-directed RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect wscript.exe or cscript.exe execution with command-line arguments referencing generic or suspicious filenames (especially 'cfile', temp-directory paths). Correlate with prior curl or wget downloads from .onion addresses.

suggestion.rationale: Article states 'application wallpapers are essentially standalone programs' and 'attackers are primarily targeting gamers in China and Russia.' suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child process creation with parent=wallpapersvc32.exe or spawning from WallpaperEngine installation/data directories. Alert on file creation in persistent wallpaper directories followed by process execution.

suggestion.title: Steam Account Credential Exfiltration via Infostealer
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'aiming to hijack their accounts' and 'we caught old, familiar threats such as DarkKomet, the Lumma and Vidar infostealers.' Need detection for credential access against Steam-related processes or registry hives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process access to HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Valve\Steam or SAM registry hives from non-system processes. Monitor for file access to Steam credential stores (e.g., loginusers.vdf, ssfn* files). Correlate with known infostealer process artifacts.

suggestion.title: Crypto Miner Persistence via Wallpaper Autostart
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'leave the victim's system infected with backdoors or crypto miners.' Need detection for miners establishing persistence through Wallpaper Engine or Steam-related autostart mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry modifications under HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run* or Active Setup hives that reference WallpaperEngine paths or create new executables. Correlate with high CPU/GPU usage and crypto-miner process signatures.

suggestion.title: Steam Workshop Malware Download and Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'malware has been spreading rapidly through the Steam Workshop...anyone can create a wallpaper and publish it.' Need detection for suspicious Steam Workshop content downloads and subsequent extraction/installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on downloads from steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails* or workshop staging servers followed by ZIP/archive extraction to WallpaperEngine directories. Flag wallpaper names matching known malicious uploads (requires IOC correlation).

suggestion.title: DarkKomet/Lumma/Vidar Command and Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific malware families: 'DarkKomet, the Lumma and Vidar infostealers.' Need C2 communication detection for these families across gameyer-heavy geographies (China, Russia).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network connections from child processes of Wallpaper Engine to known Lumma/Vidar/DarkKomet C2 domains and IPs. Include historical IOCs from Kaspersky threat feed and cross-reference with infostealer command infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Windows Script Host or PowerShell Invocation from Wallpaper Files
suggestion.rationale: Application wallpapers can embed arbitrary executables. Article notes wallpapers contain 'HTML pages powered by JavaScript' which may chain to script execution. Need detection for script interpreters spawned by or within wallpaper context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on powershell.exe, cscript.exe, or wscript.exe spawned directly or indirectly from Wallpaper Engine process or from files in wallpaper data directories. Include parent-child chain analysis.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk Service Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated user' can exploit via the endpoint. No UC generated to detect auth-less access to Splunk service ports or the PostgreSQL sidecar.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk service endpoints (default 8089 or custom) and PostgreSQL sidecar ports for access attempts with no authentication tokens or invalid/missing Authorization headers. suggestion.title: File Creation/Truncation via PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article core impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' No UC detects sidecar file operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL sidecar for file I/O operations outside expected data directories (e.g., writes to /etc, /var/log, application config dirs). Flag CREATE or TRUNCATE operations originating from unauthenticated sessions or unusual query patterns.

suggestion.title: Splunk Endpoint Asset Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt...live once in...templates' and urgency is high (CISA KEV, patch due 2026-06-21). Pipeline failed to surface recommended hunt.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Discovery and Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must first discover the sidecar endpoint. Article describes it as accessible via unauthenticated service endpoint; scanning/probing activity should precede exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for port/service scanning activity targeting typical PostgreSQL sidecar ports (5432, 9160, or custom) or repeated HTTP HEAD/OPTIONS requests to Splunk service endpoints from external sources, especially from scanning tool user-agents or rapid connection attempts.

suggestion.title: Evidence Destruction via File Truncate Operations

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on TRUNCATE operations in PostgreSQL targeting log tables or audit tables, or file truncation commands (e.g., > redirection) against Splunk logs, audit logs, or system logs from the sidecar process context.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access Attempt

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Arbitrary File Truncation via Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows attackers to 'truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'. File truncation via this service is the direct exploitation impact.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Arbitrary File Creation via Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker can 'create...arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'. File creation is the second exploitation primitive and potential foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected file creation in critical Splunk paths (bin/, etc/, var/lib/) that correlate temporally with unauthenticated sidecar endpoint access. Flag files with suspicious ownership, unusual extensions (.sh, .exe, .psm1 in config dirs), or created outside standard deployment windows.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL Sidecar External Network Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies this as CISA KEV ('currently being exploited') and recommends asset-exposure hunt. Sidecar endpoint must be identified as reachable from untrusted networks without authentication enforcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk Enterprise instances with exposed PostgreSQL sidecar service ports reachable from external networks. Verify instances respond to unauthenticated connection attempts; any successful unauthenticated session to sidecar indicates vulnerability. Cross-reference with patch status to find unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Two-Stage Exploitation: Sidecar Access + File Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Complete kill-chain detection: unauthenticated sidecar access followed by file creation/truncation. Sequential correlation reduces false positives and confirms exploitation intent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unauthenticated network request to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint (from external/untrusted IP, no valid auth) immediately followed (within 1–60 seconds) by file truncation or creation in Splunk-managed directories. This two-stage pattern directly indicates CVE-2026-20253 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated POST/GET to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Core attack vector; zero UCs generated despite explicit description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk instances for HTTP requests to sidecar endpoints (typically non-standard high-numbered ports) without valid authentication headers or session tokens. Alert on 200/201 responses to POST/GET operations from external or untrusted IPs.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation via Splunk Sidecar Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create...arbitrary files.' Exploitation indicator omitted from pipeline output despite being explicit attack capability.
