suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation on Splunk Servers
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'truncate arbitrary files.' Destructive action not represented in any UC; direct impact indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on truncate/delete operations on Splunk config, dashboard, or data files. Correlate with sidecar endpoint access to separate legitimate admin activity from exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-20253 and CISA KEV status indicates active wild exploitation. Pipeline generated zero vulnerability IOCs or scanner signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for Splunk Enterprise instances with unresolved CVE-2026-20253. Flag any instances unpatched after federal due date 2026-06-21. Correlate with network anomalies on sidecar ports.

suggestion.title: POST /crawl* with launcher-switch keywords in request body (body-aware variant)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Docker API server accepted a request-supplied browser_config.extra_args, which flowed into Chromium's launch arguments.' Payload is JSON in POST body, not query string. Original UC_3_2 searches wrong field entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to /crawl, /crawl/stream, /crawl/job where request body JSON contains 'extra_args' or 'browser_config' fields with values matching Chromium launcher-switch patterns (--utility-cmd-prefix, --renderer-cmd-prefix, --gpu-launcher, --browser-subprocess-path).

suggestion.title: Chromium process with --no-zygote AND subprocess-launcher flag co-occurrence
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'inject Chromium switches that replace a child-process launch command...together with --no-zygote, causing Chromium to fork/exec.' The --no-zygote flag is the attack enabler (disables zygote sandboxing); co-occurrence with launcher-override flags is telltale and extremely rare in legitimate Chromium usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single Chromium process event with simultaneous --no-zygote AND at least one of {--utility-cmd-prefix, --renderer-cmd-prefix, --gpu-launcher, --browser-subprocess-path}. This tuple is near-pathognomonic for this exploit.

suggestion.title: Docker/Kubernetes API access to Crawl4AI endpoint (container-aware context)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Docker API server' and vulnerability is specific to containerized deployment. Detection should correlate suspicious API calls with container infrastructure context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST to Crawl4AI /crawl* endpoints originating from within container infrastructure (Docker network, Kubernetes pod CIDR, or calls to container API gateways). Flag if source is unexpected container or external scanning.

suggestion.title: Malicious LNK File Creation Masquerading Original Documents
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'the malware hides the originals and replaces them with malicious shortcuts bearing the same names.' Detection opportunity for document masquerading and file type substitution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of .LNK files with names matching document extensions (.docx, .xlsx, .pdf, etc.) in user profile directories. Correlate with process execution spawning from shortcut files (cmd.exe, powershell.exe child processes from lnk execution). Baseline document-heavy directories for rapid .LNK file proliferation.

suggestion.title: Tor Executable Process Execution (ugate.exe)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'establishing communications with the command-and-control (C2) host using a Tor executable (ugate.exe).' Direct IOC and execution pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ugate.exe execution or any Tor executable spawned by unexpected parent processes (esp. from USB-mounted or temp directories). Correlate with localhost:9050 network connections (Tor proxy indicator). Monitor for process names matching common Tor launcher patterns.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task Creation Monitoring USB Device Insertion
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'The worm creates a scheduled task that monitors for newly connected USB storage devices.' Clear persistence and propagation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for scheduled task creation referencing removable drive detection or USB device monitoring. Look for tasks triggering on device arrival with payloads from temp/AppData/USB locations. Correlate with PowerShell/cmd.exe task creation commands executed outside administrative context.

suggestion.title: JavaScript Code Execution via C2 Download (cfile)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'the malware downloads JavaScript content into a file named 'cfile,' and executes it on the infected machine.' Remote code execution vector via dynamic JavaScript.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor wscript.exe/cscript.exe execution, particularly with file paths containing 'cfile' or temp directory references. Alert on JavaScript execution followed by curl, PowerShell, or cmd.exe child processes. Check for unexpected .js/.jse file creation from network-accessible locations.

suggestion.title: Clipboard Monitoring for Cryptocurrency Wallet Data
suggestion.rationale: Article details repeated clipboard reads 'Every half a second, the malware checks the clipboard for the following data: 12-word BIP39 seed phrases, 24-word BIP39 seed phrases, Ethereum private keys...' Behavioral collection pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes with elevated clipboard access frequencies (polling intervals <1 second). Baseline normal clipboard tools (Office, browsers). Alert on unusual processes reading clipboard in rapid succession. Correlate clipboard reads with network exfiltration or credential access patterns.

suggestion.title: Frequent Screenshot Capture with Curl-Based Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'the malware also captures five screenshots of the victim's screen every ten seconds and sends them to the C2 using the curl tool.' Distinct collection + exfiltration pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on curl.exe execution with Tor-related arguments or localhost:9050 proxy references. Monitor for screenshot-related tool usage (built-in Windows APIs) followed by curl network activity. Baseline curl usage and flag unexpected encryption/proxy parameters. Correlate timing of curl invocations with screenshot intervals.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Suspicious Kernel Driver Load
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'driver-based stealth' as the Windows expansion mechanism—this is the core persistence and evasion vector for kernel-mode backdoors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .sys file loads from non-standard paths, unsigned drivers, or drivers loaded via user-mode processes. Monitor HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services for new service entries with ImagePath pointing to suspicious locations or without publisher metadata.

suggestion.title: Kernel-Mode Process or File Hiding
suggestion.rationale: Driver-based stealth implementations hide processes, files, or connections at kernel level. The article's defining characteristic is 'driver-based stealth,' implying kernel-mode filter hooks or callbacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process or file discrepancies: events in EDR/ETW logs with no corresponding handle in process enumeration, files written but not appearing in filesystem APIs, or registry writes followed by invisible reads. Correlate with unsigned driver loads.

suggestion.title: Kernel-Mode Network Interception Driver
suggestion.rationale: Rootkit backdoors often install NDIS or WFP drivers to intercept traffic, enabling stealthy C2. Article describes 'driver-based stealth' for backdoor functionality.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services for NDIS or WFP entries. Detect kernel-mode driver installations that precede anomalous network flows or encrypted traffic without user-mode applications.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Signed/Vulnerable Driver
suggestion.rationale: Many Windows rootkits bootstrap kernel execution by exploiting publicly known vulnerable drivers (CVE-based). Pipeline should detect this stepping stone.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for user-mode processes invoking or writing to known exploitable drivers (e.g., Gigabyte APP Center, ASUS drivers listed in LOLDriver). Flag privilege-escalation events immediately preceding driver installation.

suggestion.title: System Service Installation for Driver Persistence
suggestion.rationale: SprySOCKS Windows expansion necessarily involves registry-based driver service setup. This is foundational to any kernel-mode persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services entries with Type=1 (kernel driver) and non-standard Start values. Correlate with DeviceFileEvents showing .sys file creation in %SystemRoot%\System32\drivers or alternative paths.

suggestion.title: Kernel Callback Registration and Hooking
suggestion.rationale: Driver-based stealth relies on kernel callbacks (PsSetLoadImageNotifyRoutine, CmRegisterCallback, etc.). Detection should look for callback registration patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for patterns indicative of kernel callback registration: rapid successive DeviceDriverLoad events, drivers with elevated runtime behavior (stalling process enumeration, intercepting file operations), or ETW events showing kernel-mode hooks.

suggestion.title: Asset exposure hunt — CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Enterprise
suggestion.rationale: Article directs: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [`../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`]' with CVE-2026-20253 substituted. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this explicit guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Splunk Enterprise instances for CVE-2026-20253 exposure status across fleet. Cross-reference vulnerability scanners, patch management systems, and network visibility tools. Alert on unpatched Splunk Enterprise versions facing the internet or reachable from untrusted networks given federal due date of 2026-06-21.

Flag successful responses (HTTP 200/201) indicating endpoint accessibility.

Alert on anomalous activity: files created/truncated outside normal directories, unusual sizes, or suspicious file names that suggest OS-level payload staging.

suggestion.title: Missing authentication control bypass to Splunk critical functions

Correlate with external source IPs and alert on successful responses.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 exploitation signature detection

Cross-reference IDS/IPS sensors for signature matches.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Exposed Instance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in `../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`' but template not instantiated. Critical for identifying at-risk Splunk instances on internet-facing segments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Splunk Enterprise instances accessible from internet or untrusted networks. Query Shodan/Censys for exposed Splunk instances, correlate with vulnerability scanner results, and alert on instances running versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthorized Access Attempt

suggestion.title: Splunk Arbitrary File Write/Truncate via Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — execution/impact behavior completely missing from use cases.

Flag rapid successive file deletions or creation of executables in sensitive locations correlated with unauthenticated access.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Sidecar Process
suggestion.rationale: Core exploitation impact missing detection. Phrase: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.'

Alert on writes to sensitive paths (etc, systemd, config directories) or unexpected file deletions originating from sidecar service.

Flag sidecar endpoint responses (HTTP 200/201) with zero authentication headers or absence of corresponding login events in preceding logs.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation via CVE-2026-20253

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Splunk Enterprise versions matching CVE-2026-20253 affected range. Alert if identified systems are internet-routable or on untrusted networks. Prioritize per federal due date 2026-06-21.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk HTTP access logs for successful requests to auth-required endpoints with missing, invalid, or mismatched credentials. Flag direct sidecar-port access. Correlate with known CVE-2026-20253 request signatures.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — this is the critical attack surface and initial-access mechanism that must be monitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar ports (typically 8191+) from external or untrusted networks arriving without valid authentication headers or session tokens. Alert on any successful connection followed by file operation requests.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation via PostgreSQL Sidecar Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'could allow an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files' — file creation is the direct exploitation outcome and must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected file creation events originating from Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar processes or related service accounts, especially in sensitive directories (conf/, plugins/, var/). Correlate creation timing with inbound sidecar endpoint requests.

suggestion.title: File Truncation Events from Splunk Services
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'truncate arbitrary files' as attack outcome — file truncation is destructive and indicates active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file truncation operations (truncate() syscalls, open with O_TRUNC flag) on Splunk hosts, especially in data indexes or configuration directories. Cross-correlate with inbound unauthenticated network activity to sidecar port.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerable Splunk Version Detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for Splunk Enterprise versions matching CVE-2026-20253 SLA (vendor advisory required for exact versions). For instances with version visibility, test sidecar endpoint for unauthenticated response as proof-of-concept confirmation.

suggestion.title: Splunk Service Account File I/O Anomalies Correlated to Network Events
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires both network access (inbound sidecar request) and file system impact (create/truncate). Correlation strengthens signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create tuples matching: (1) inbound HTTP/TCP to sidecar endpoint from untrusted source, (2) file I/O event from Splunk process within 5 seconds, (3) file modified in sensitive Splunk directories. Multi-hit correlation bypasses false-positive noise from legitimate operations.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user' can exploit 'through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—direct evidence of T1190 exploitation of public-facing authentication bypass.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation via Splunk Sidecar Exploitation

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation via Splunk Sidecar

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file delete/truncate operations sourced from Splunk sidecar or PostgreSQL process, correlate with failed authentication or abnormal sidecar API calls. High fidelity if targeting config or log files.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status indicates active in-the-wild exploitation. Need direct, scannable signature matching known payload patterns for this specific CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP requests containing CVE-2026-20253 exploitation signatures (e.g., sidecar endpoint probes, malformed PostgreSQL commands, authentication-bypass payloads). Correlate with Splunk versions 9.x per vendor advisory.

suggestion.title: Splunk Sidecar Service Anomaly - Unexpected Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes file creation capability via sidecar; unexpected child process spawning from sidecar indicates post-exploitation command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by Splunk sidecar/PostgreSQL process, particularly shells, cmd.exe, or file-operation utilities. Baseline expected sidecar processes and flag deviations.

Flag version pinning changes to newly discovered packages with similar names to established projects in the Go ecosystem.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network connections originating from web browser or content-parsing processes (user-agent strings visible in proxy logs) targeting 127.0.0.1, ::1, or localhost hostnames on non-standard or high-number ports. Filter for requests containing parameter values or payloads typical of MCP protocol exploitation.

suggestion.title: AutoGen Studio MCP Service Accepting Unauthenticated Commands
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies AutoGen Studio's MCP WebSocket as the vulnerable service endpoint exploited to achieve RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AutoGen Studio MCP service logs (if available) for WebSocket messages lacking required authentication tokens, originating from unexpected source IPs/ports, or containing serialized command payloads. Cross-reference with network logs showing the originating process is a browser context.

suggestion.title: Malicious Parameter Injection via Webpage into LocalHost Service
suggestion.rationale: Attack leverages 'unsafe parameter handling' in the MCP service — the malicious webpage crafts HTTP/WebSocket requests with injected parameters targeting localhost.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for HTTP or WebSocket requests from browser processes targeting localhost services (127.0.0.1, localhost) with URL-encoded or JSON parameters containing shell metacharacters (pipes, semicolons, backticks), process names, or command keywords. Alert on any successful 200/101 response followed by process creation.

suggestion.title: Vertex AI SDK Unexpected Bucket Upload Redirection
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack: SDK hijacked to upload models to attacker-controlled buckets via bucket squatting. Pipeline missed detection of SDK attempting to upload to GCS paths outside expected project hierarchy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GCP Audit Logs for Vertex AI SDK (via user-agent or source identity) initiating gsutil or storage.objects.create calls to bucket names not matching project naming conventions or not in approved bucket list. Flag if bucket name appears to be typosquatting legitimate infrastructure (e.g., similarity to 'vertex-ai-models-*' patterns).

suggestion.title: GCS Bucket Name Similarity to Google Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Bucket squatting attack requires attacker to register buckets with names resembling legitimate Google or project buckets. Article states attackers 'hijack model uploads' via squatting—detect attempts to create/own lookalike buckets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new GCS bucket creation where bucket name contains Levenshtein distance ≤2 from known Google Vertex AI or project bucket prefixes, or uses common typosquatting patterns (e.g., adding/removing underscores, swapping characters). Cross-reference with bucket ownership to detect external account ownership of look-alike buckets.

suggestion.title: SDK Version Downgrade or Dependency Confusion in Vertex AI
suggestion.rationale: Bucket squatting often works via dependency confusion—attacker publishes lower-versioned malicious SDK. Article mentions 'SDK flaw'—detect when teams are coerced to use unexpected SDK versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip/poetry/npm install logs for google-cloud-aiplatform or vertex-ai package installs from non-official registries (PyPI index confusion), version downgrades, or pinned-to-patch versions that deviate from team standard. Alert if package hash differs from expected Google-signed version.

suggestion.title: GCS Upload Credentials Exfiltration via Malicious SDK
suggestion.rationale: Hijacked SDK can capture upload credentials. Article attack involves 'model uploads via bucket squatting'—detection should flag credential leakage patterns when SDK interactions occur.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Vertex AI SDK processes initiating unusual outbound connections to non-Google IPs while GCS credentials are in memory or environment variables. Monitor for unexpected exfiltration of gs:// signed URLs or service account keys in HTTP request bodies to external hosts.

suggestion.title: Model Upload to Out-of-Band GCS Bucket
suggestion.rationale: Core attack step: attackers 'hijack model uploads'. Detection must catch when model training/deployment pipelines write to unexpected buckets instead of project-approved locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Vertex AI training jobs and model uploads for write operations to GCS buckets outside a whitelist of approved buckets per project/service account. Alert on upload_directory or model_artifact paths pointing to buckets with differing project IDs or cross-account ownership.

suggestion.title: Cross-Project GCS Access from Vertex AI Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Bucket squatting attack enables cross-project bucket access if service account permissions are overly broad. Article mentions 'hijack'—detect lateral movement into attacker-controlled GCS resources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Vertex AI service accounts (vertex-sa@*, compute-sa@*) attempt storage.objects operations on GCS buckets outside their home project. Combine with unusual caller_ip or caller_principal to identify compromised or hijacked credentials.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Asset Exposure — Splunk Enterprise Inventory by Version
suggestion.rationale: Article states CISA KEV entry requires immediate patching (due 2026-06-21). Pipeline must establish baseline of exposed Splunk Enterprise instances before hunting exploitation. Template explicitly references asset-exposure hunt as canonical first step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Splunk Enterprise instances in environment by asset inventory, extract product version, cross-reference against CVE-2026-20253 patched versions. Prioritize internet-facing instances. Flag all unpatched instances as critical by 2026-06-21 due date.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated user' can exploit via 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline should detect: (1) inbound HTTP/TCP connections to known Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar ports without valid session auth, (2) 401/403 responses followed by state-changing operations, (3) out-of-band PostgreSQL protocol traffic from unexpected sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound connections to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar (typically localhost:5432 or custom port) from non-Splunk-service sources. Baseline expected callers; alert on unauthenticated protocol attempts or missing API authentication headers. Correlate with file I/O spike.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk PostgreSQL Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'create or truncate arbitrary files through PostgreSQL sidecar.' This is direct impact post-exploitation. Pipeline must detect file operations (writes, deletes, truncates) where parent process is Splunk/PostgreSQL but target paths are outside expected Splunk directories (logs, indexes, metadata).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or truncation operations initiated from Splunk PostgreSQL service account (splunk, postgres, or custom service user) where target path is outside /opt/splunk/*, /var/log/splunk/*, /var/lib/splunk/*. Especially flag system-critical paths: /etc/passwd, /boot/*, /root/*, or executable directories.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Port Scanning or Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article implies PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint is exploitable if accessible. Attackers must first discover or probe the endpoint. Pipeline should detect: port scans targeting expected Splunk sidecar ranges, connection attempts from unusual source ASNs/geolocations, failed authentication attempts followed by successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple failed connection attempts to Splunk PostgreSQL port (5432 or custom) from single source within short window. Flag especially: external IPs, TOR exit nodes, IPs associated with vulnerability scanning frameworks, or sources with no legitimate Splunk dependency.

suggestion.title: Splunk Service Account Privilege Escalation or Lateral Movement Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Once attacker gains file write via PostgreSQL sidecar, next-stage tactics likely include writing cronjobs, modifying shell startup files, or injecting credentials. Article doesn't describe post-exploitation but pipeline should model likely follow-on attack vectors from persistent file write capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file modifications to Splunk service user's home directory startup files (.bashrc, .bash_profile, cron jobs, etc.) or system-wide persistence mechanisms (systemd timers, init scripts) where writer is the Splunk service account or PostgreSQL process. Alert on unexpected modifications, especially with embedded commands or exfiltration indicators.

suggestion.title: Title/Body CVE Mismatch Alert (Data Quality Issue)
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'CVE-2024-49035 Microsoft Partner Center' but body entirely describes 'CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Enterprise.' Pipeline should have flagged this discrepancy as a data integrity failure before processing. This suggests articles are being conflated or ingestion is corrupted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Meta-alert: do NOT trust any other IOCs or MITRE mappings from this article until title/body mismatch is resolved at source. Pipeline must validate CVE in title matches CVE in body before proceeding. Return to original CISA KEV feed to confirm correct CVE ID.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly defines attack surface as 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' exposed to unauthenticated users. Requires hunting for Splunk instances with accessible sidecar services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for inbound connections to Splunk sidecar ports (typically PostgreSQL-adjacent, port 5432 variants) from external sources with no prior authentication session. Correlate with vulnerability scanner output to identify CVE-2026-20253-affected Splunk builds.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly described as 'missing authentication for critical function.' Detection must capture failed and successful unauthenticated sidecar endpoint access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints lacking valid authentication credentials, session tokens, or Splunk user context. Baseline legitimate sidecar activity and flag anomalous access patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Creation and Truncation via Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This file manipulation must be detected across Splunk's critical directories and data stores.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation and truncation events in Splunk installation directories, index stores, and configuration paths without corresponding authorized process activity. Flag bulk file deletion patterns as data destruction attempts.

suggestion.title: Splunk Service Interruption Following File Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Truncating arbitrary Splunk files (indexes, binaries, state files) would trigger service failures. Article phrase 'truncate arbitrary files' indicates data destruction capability targeting operational continuity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unexpected Splunk service restarts, fatal errors in logs, or availability drops with prior suspicious file operations or unauthenticated sidecar access within a 5-minute window. Establish baseline index availability metrics.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk Enterprise Admin API
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — direct initial access without credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP POST/GET requests to Splunk admin endpoints (/_internal/, /services/) lacking valid session tokens or authentication headers, originating from non-whitelisted IP ranges. Focus on PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints exposed via HTTP.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via PostgreSQL Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the attack permits 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — direct file-system impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation and deletion in Splunk's data directories ($SPLUNK_HOME/var/lib/splunk/*) and PostgreSQL directories for unexpected writes or truncations. Correlate timing with unauthenticated HTTP access patterns. Flag rapid or bulk file modifications indicative of batch attacks.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Indicator Matching
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry denotes active exploitation in the wild; federal patch due 2026-06-21 requires urgent asset-exposure baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference scanner output and asset database for Splunk Enterprise versions matching vulnerable ranges. Prioritize internet-facing instances. Validate patch status and access controls. Flag instances without network segmentation or authentication proxies in front.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Asset Exposure — Splunk Enterprise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' is the recommended detection and references template substitution. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this clear guidance. The vulnerability affects public-facing Splunk instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Splunk Enterprise instances exposed on internet-facing endpoints without authentication controls. Query vulnerability scanners for CVE-2026-20253 matches; correlate against asset inventory to identify systems with patch lag or missing updates.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint — Unauthorized Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability exists 'through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the exploitation vector but pipeline generated no detection for endpoint access anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthenticated or unexpected connections to internal PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically non-standard ports). Flag any connection attempts from external IP ranges or without credential submission preceding database operations.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation — Splunk Host
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'could allow an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files.' This is the impact mechanism but no use case captures file operation abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected file creation or truncation operations initiated from unauthenticated network context or from PostgreSQL sidecar process running with unexpected privileges. Flag file operations on sensitive Splunk directories (configs, indexes, logs).

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass — Splunk Critical Function Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: CVE title explicitly mentions 'Missing Authentication for Critical Function.' Pipeline should detect authentication bypass attempts but generated no such use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk Enterprise endpoints for requests to critical functions (file operations, configuration changes, data access) arriving without valid session tokens or credentials in Authorization headers. Baseline normal credential submission patterns and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation — Indicator Match
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline IOCs are empty. Article recommends 'CVE match against your vulnerability scanner' — the CVE itself is the primary detection indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest vulnerability scanner results and flag any Splunk Enterprise instances with CVE-2026-20253 present (unpatched or unverified patch status). Correlate against federal due-date (2026-06-21) to identify remediation SLA breaches.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar — Data Truncation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states files can be 'truncated' — this is a specific destructive operation indicating either data exfiltration prep or denial-of-service. No use case for this impact vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on TRUNCATE or mass DELETE operations against PostgreSQL sidecar service initiated from unauthenticated context. Flag any table truncation within minutes of suspicious endpoint access or authentication bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Apache Spark ACL Bypass and Shell RCE (CVE-2022-33891)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'if an admin had enabled an ACL authentication filter, an attacker could bypass it and execute shell commands as the Spark service user' and notes 'ZeroBot botnet using this vulnerability to exploit and propagate malware through affected systems' in December 2022, with CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities confirmation. Zero UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for shell command execution spawned by Spark service account (java/spark processes) executing cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or /bin/sh with network-triggered invocation patterns. Detect ACL-bypass indicators such as unauthenticated inbound connections to Spark ports followed by child process execution.

suggestion.title: GitPython Command Injection via Malicious Repository URL (CVE-2022-24439)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'GitPython library did not properly sanitize git commands in versions below 3.1.30' and CTF challenge where 'with some clever syntax tricks, they could execute any arbitrary command.' Explicitly flagged as supply chain risk in CI/CD pipelines. Zero UC generated despite clear exploitation path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor git clone/pull operations that spawn unexpected child processes (shell interpreters, curl, wget). Detect shell metacharacters in git repository URL parameters (backticks, $(), pipe, semicolon). Flag Python processes executing non-git binaries after git method invocation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized API Endpoint Access Bypass (Insecure Access Control)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Protecting Camp' challenge where flag was 'tucked away at a hidden endpoint only accessible locally' but exploited via 'unsafe functionality of the app's API and how it retrieved metadata for items on sale.' Paralleled to 'Azure Power Apps misconfiguration exposing over 38 million records.' No detection UC generated for this OWASP Top 10 issue.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API calls accessing localhost/internal-only endpoints from non-localhost sources. Detect enumeration of metadata endpoints with sequential IDs or path traversal patterns. Flag privilege escalation in API access where a user accesses resources beyond their authorization scope via metadata retrieval tricks.

suggestion.title: ZeroBot Malware Exploitation Campaign (Spark CVE-2022-33891)
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'Microsoft observed the ZeroBot botnet using this vulnerability to exploit and propagate malware through affected systems' in December 2022. Named threat actor with documented active exploitation. No actor-based detection UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ZeroBot C2 communication patterns or malware signatures associated with Spark exploitation campaigns. Monitor for binary downloads and execution following Spark RCE success. Correlate network traffic to known ZeroBot infrastructure with Spark process creation events.

suggestion.title: GitPython Improper CVE Fix Bypass (CVE-2023-40267)
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'CVE-2023-40267 — an improper fix of this bug, which still allowed code execution via crafted repo URLs' indicating second-order vulnerability in GitPython mitigation. Represents supply chain persistence of a known vulnerability class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for exploitation using crafted Git repository URLs that bypass CVE-2022-24439 patches. Look for Git operation logs with URL-encoded shell metacharacters, double-encoded payloads, or alternative injection vectors. Detect shell execution following failed git command parsing.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk Sidecar Service Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user' can exploit 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Detection requires identifying external/untrusted connections to this endpoint without valid Splunk authentication tokens or session credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Splunk sidecar service endpoints from external/untrusted sources lacking valid Splunk authentication headers (X-Splunk-Authorization, Authorization tokens, or active session cookies). Baseline internal access patterns and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Creation or Truncation via Splunk Service Processes
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability permits 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Endpoint-initiated file operations require detection at file-system layer to catch post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation, modification, or truncation events initiated by Splunk service processes (splunkd, postgres, sidecar daemons) to unexpected paths outside documented baselines. Flag rapid bulk file operations or writes to system-critical directories.

suggestion.title: Port Enumeration Targeting Splunk Service Ports
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must first discover the exposed sidecar service before exploitation. Detection of external port scanning or service probing precedes successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify scanning patterns targeting documented Splunk service ports and sidecar-related ports from external sources. Look for connection attempts without completed handshakes or rapid sequential SYN packets indicating enumeration.

suggestion.title: API Requests to Critical Functions without Authentication Context
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause is 'missing authentication for critical function.' Detection requires identifying API calls to critical endpoints lacking valid authentication credentials or session state.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor requests to Splunk critical-function endpoints (particularly those handling file operations or system modifications) that lack Authorization headers, API tokens, or valid session cookies. Alert on unauthenticated POST/PUT/DELETE operations.

suggestion.title: Temporal Correlation: Unauthenticated Endpoint Access Followed by File Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation chain: external access to sidecar endpoint → file operations. Correlation of unauthenticated sidecar access with subsequent file creation/truncation events indicates active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate firewall/network logs showing external access to Splunk sidecar endpoint with subsequent file-system events (creation, truncation, deletion) within 60-second window from same source. Flag as exploitation indicator.

suggestion.title: Exposed Splunk Enterprise Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user' can exploit via 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — detection of internet-facing Splunk instances is the first line. Article references template '../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure' for this hunt. CVE-2026-20253 explicitly named as the matching CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Splunk Enterprise instances with open network access to default ports (8089, 8000, 9997) without authentication requirements. Cross-reference against patching status for CVE-2026-20253. Flag any instance responding to unauthenticated connection attempts to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically port 5432 or non-standard variants managed by Splunk).

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthorized File Operation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Core attack primitive: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Requires detection of suspicious file I/O from sidecar process without prior authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar process (typical executable names: postgres, splunkd child) for file creation or truncation operations outside normal working directories (e.g., in /opt/splunk/etc, /opt/splunk/var). Correlate with network events showing unauthenticated access to sidecar service port. Baseline expected file operations and alert on deviations or bulk file deletions.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scan Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-20253 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and warns patch lag is 'the silent killer' even post-patching. SOC should validate scanner results against known-vulnerable Splunk Enterprise versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner output with actual Splunk Enterprise version metadata from endpoints. Flag discrepancies where scanner reports 'not vulnerable' but product version falls within vulnerable ranges for CVE-2026-20253. Federal due date 2026-06-21 — escalate any non-patched instances past that date.

suggestion.title: Splunk Sidecar Service Port Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' as the attack surface. Unauthenticated reconnaissance or connection attempts to this endpoint should be detected before successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound connection attempts to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoints from external or untrusted networks. Look for incomplete handshakes, multiple failed connection attempts to the same port across multiple source IPs, or known scanner user-agents attempting connection. Baseline expected sidecar traffic and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Detect CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation (Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attack vector: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline should detect external requests to this endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk Enterprise instances for HTTP requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints from external/untrusted sources. Alert on requests lacking authentication credentials or arriving from non-allowlisted networks.

suggestion.title: Detect Arbitrary File Manipulation via CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' Direct post-exploitation behavioral indicator that must trigger detection when observed on Splunk hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation/truncation events on Splunk Enterprise systems in sensitive directories (config, data, logs), especially when correlated with unauthenticated API requests to PostgreSQL endpoints or anomalous process behavior.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Hunt: Internet-Facing Splunk Enterprise with CVE-2026-20253
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation + T1190 implies active exploitation against externally-exposed assets. Federal due date 2026-06-21 mandates rapid inventory and triage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Splunk Enterprise instances with PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints reachable from internet (port 5432 or exposed HTTP service). Prioritize instances without network segmentation or WAF protection for immediate patching.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthenticated Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — the direct attack vector requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unauthenticated connection attempts to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (port 5432 or custom). Baseline expected service-to-service traffic and alert on external or anomalous internal source IPs attempting to reach the endpoint without prior authentication handshake.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies impact as 'create or truncate arbitrary files' — requires detection of unauthorized file manipulation initiated through the compromised endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation and truncation events spawned by Splunk service processes (splunkd, postgres sidecar) outside normal operational directories. Correlate with unauthenticated endpoint access and establish baseline for file operation patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerable Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article references CISA KEV with explicit federal patch due date 2026-06-21 — immediate asset discovery required; 'patch lag is the silent killer' per article guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner output for Splunk Enterprise version matches to CVE-2026-20253 ranges. Flag instances with patch dates older than vendor advisory and identify deployment lag patterns to catch repeat offenders.

suggestion.title: Splunk Service Endpoint Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Pre-exploitation requires attackers to identify or probe the PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint location — necessary reconnaissance activity before exploitation attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scans or service enumeration targeting typical Splunk ports (8000, 8089, 9997, 5432) and REST API endpoints from external sources or unusual internal scanners. Establish baseline of expected infrastructure scanning.

suggestion.title: Splunk CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanning Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs 'CVE-2026-20253 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and recommends asset-exposure hunt. Pipeline generated zero IOCs or scanning detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Splunk Enterprise instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253 (critical severity, known-exploited per CISA KEV status). Prioritize unpatched systems past the federal remediation deadline of 2026-06-21. Cross-reference asset inventory against patch release dates.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability manifests specifically as 'unauthenticated user' access to 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline did not generate network or authentication-based detection for this attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically internal-only) from external or untrusted sources. Monitor for requests lacking valid authentication credentials. Alert on successful exploitation following failed authentication attempts.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Operations via PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Core attack capability: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline generated zero file-system detection for the actual exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation or truncation operations initiated from Splunk Enterprise service account or PostgreSQL processes targeting files outside normal Splunk directories (system paths, configs, boot files). Correlate with PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint access logs to establish exploitation causality.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV Exploitation Attempts in Splunk Logs
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status means 'currently being exploited in the wild.' Pipeline should hunt Splunk's own logs for exploitation attempts and reconnaissance activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Splunk access logs for anomalous endpoint paths, suspicious POST/PUT operations to sidecar functions, or path-traversal patterns. Monitor _internal logs for unusual service restarts, unexpected file access operations, or error conditions correlating with external requests.

suggestion.title: Fake Browser/System Update Prompt Click-Through
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'fake update lures' as primary delivery mechanism. Pipeline generated zero detections for this initial-access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect user clicks on fake update prompts followed by unscheduled download/execution of binaries from non-official update domains. Alert on browser or utility processes spawning unknown installers outside patch windows.

suggestion.title: Loader Binary Staging and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'new loaders' as expansion mechanism but pipeline captured no execution-phase detection despite loader being the core delivery component.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual parent-child process chains where browser/user-execution spawns secondary loader executable, especially with suspicious command-line arguments or unsigned binaries. Flag reflective DLL injection and unusual process memory operations.

suggestion.title: Command-and-Control Beaconing from Loader Processes
suggestion.rationale: Malware delivery campaigns require C2 callbacks; pipeline surfaced no network-based detection for post-execution command infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate auto-update domains and alert on outbound connections from newly-spawned loader processes to unknown external hosts, especially on non-standard ports or using uncommon protocols.

suggestion.title: Malware Defense-Evasion and Anti-Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Modern malware loaders employ evasion tactics (sandboxing checks, EDR disabling, obfuscation) but pipeline generated no defense-evasion phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes querying WMI for VM/sandbox indicators, disabling Windows Defender via registry, or executing encoded/obfuscated payloads. Monitor for process hollowing and parent-process spoofing.

suggestion.title: Persistence Registration Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Malware delivery inherently includes persistence establishment but pipeline captured no registry/task-scheduler persistence detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious modifications to HKCU/HKLM Run/RunOnce keys or unexpected scheduled task creation shortly after loader execution. Correlate timing with initial compromise window.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Go Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack: 'Typo squatting attacks happen when bad actors create and upload harmful software packages to online libraries using names very similar to popular ones.' Package github.com/botdb-go/bolt mirrors github.com/boltdb/bolt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go build/dependency resolution logs for package downloads with names matching known typosquatting patterns (character transposition, homograph variants of popular modules). Cross-reference go.mod and go.sum file changes against known-malicious package registry.

suggestion.title: Indefinite Module Cache Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in, and that cached the backdored module' and 'Malicious packages can still be searchable on Go Module Proxy.' Defense evasion via repository cache abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Go module proxy cache hits for packages that (a) were previously removed from the module registry, (b) have version timestamps inconsistent with package age, or (c) resolve to IP space associated with archive/mirror infrastructure after removal notice.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Package Version Resurrection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'we now wish to update our systems to the latest dependencies, which led developers to update the version that stayed in the system for 3 years.' Detects when dependency updates install previously-unknown or reverted-malicious versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor dependency management commands (go get, go mod tidy) that update to versions older than system baseline or that have suspicious gaps in publication history. Cross-correlate with vulnerability database (GO-2025-3451) for known-backdoored versions.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package C2 Egress
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states backdoor capability: 'This backdoor allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands.' Detects C2 traffic from systems with compromised dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate systems with github.com/botdb-go/bolt@v1.3.1 in dependency tree against outbound C2 traffic patterns (beaconing, unusual command server domains, anomalous port usage). Baseline expected network behavior for legitimate boltdb usage.

suggestion.title: Repository Health Degradation as Supply Chain Indicator
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'There have been over 80+ unresolved issues in the original repository since 2015.' Unmaintained repositories are vectors for compromise; paired with version staleness as leading indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Score Go packages on maintenance signals: commit recency, issue resolution rate, contributor continuity. Flag dependencies on packages with stale repositories + forced version updates as supply-chain risk indicator.

suggestion.title: Package Name Similarity Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes typosquatting mechanism: 'malicious Go Module Mirror's was named github.com/botdb-go/bolt, similar to the original one i.e. github.com/boltdb/bolt.' Detection via string distance and legitimate package baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Apply Levenshtein/Jaro-Winkler distance to package names at install time; flag those within edit distance 2 of known packages. Cross-check organization baseline for legitimacy. Alert on packages from untrusted publishers mimicking popular module names.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — this is the direct exploitation vector
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to Splunk internal service endpoints (sidecar, PostgreSQL gateway ports — typically 8089, backend listeners) originating from external IPs or untrusted subnets, with authentication headers absent or invalid. Alert on 200 responses to `/services/` paths lacking session validation.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — file-system impact must be detected
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation, deletion, or truncation events originating from Splunk daemons (splunkd, etc.) writing to paths outside /opt/splunk. Cross-correlate timing with successful unauthenticated sidecar endpoint access from network logs within preceding 1 hour.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Internet Exposure Asset Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires exposed service endpoint: 'unauthenticated user' implies public or internal-but-routable access; paired with 'missing authentication' this is asset-exposure risk
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query network baseline for inbound connections to Splunk service ports (8089, 8000, sidecar ports) from non-corporate CIDR ranges or verified untrusted networks. Cross-check against asset inventory to identify Splunk Enterprise instances marked as internal-only; flag any with observed external inbound activity.

suggestion.title: Splunk Sidecar Parameter Injection via POST Requests
suggestion.rationale: File manipulation via endpoint implies query/POST parameter abuse; 'missing authentication for critical function' suggests insufficient input validation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET parameters sent to Splunk sidecar endpoints for file path payloads, path traversal patterns (../, ..), or file operation keywords (truncate, create, write, rm) in request body. Alert on malformed or unusual sidecar function calls with parameters bearing resemblance to OS commands.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Attempt - Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite clear attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoints (typically port 5432 or service-specific API port) for HTTP/POST requests from external or unauthenticated sources. Alert on successful file creation/deletion operations returned by sidecar without prior authentication token validation. High confidence: any 4xx auth error followed by 2xx success on same endpoint.

suggestion.title: Anomalous File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Sidecar Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states the vulnerability allows 'create or truncate arbitrary files' — no detection suggested despite being the direct impact mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation and truncation events originating from PostgreSQL sidecar process (psql, postgres, or Splunk sidecar binary) in unexpected directories (system config, auth files, application binaries). Baseline normal file operations and alert on deviation. Correlate with suspicious service endpoint access in same time window.

suggestion.title: Exposed Splunk Instance with Unpatched CVE-2026-20253

High confidence for externally-routable instances with no compensating controls (WAF rules, IP restrict).

Filter out known legitimate service accounts. High confidence: unauthenticated external source + 200 response + file operation in response body.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Unexpected Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article vulnerability permits arbitrary file ops; attackers may spawn shell/command processes via sidecar to escalate impact. Pipeline did not map execution path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by PostgreSQL sidecar (psql, postgres, sidecar binary) — e.g., /bin/sh, /bin/bash, cmd.exe. Normal sidecar operation does not spawn shells. Alert on any such event. Medium confidence (some shell usage normal in scripts); escalate to high if preceded by failed auth attempts or unusual network connections.

Alert on HTTP GET/POST to service endpoints from IPs with no prior legitimate access history.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences where source IP receives 401 or 403 on /v1/* endpoint, followed by 200/201 response on any /v1/* endpoint, within 10-minute window. Indicates probe-and-exploit behavior against auth requirements.

suggestion.title: ASGI/HTTP trust-chain exploitation via Forwarded header injection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for requests where Forwarded, X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Host, or X-Forwarded-Path headers contradict the actual request origin or URI, sent to vLLM instances. Mismatches between proxy-supplied headers and true request path indicate header-injection exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Deprecated/Revoked Package Still in Production Dependency Tree

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan go.mod, go.sum, and active process listings for botdb-go/bolt any version, or boltdb/bolt v1.3.1. Cross-reference against Go vulnerability database (GO-2025-3451) and Snyk advisories; alert if found in prod deployments after Feb 7, 2025 removal date.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthenticated Access Attempts

suggestion.title: Detect Apache Spark Shell RCE (CVE-2022-33891) — ACL Bypass & Command Execution

suggestion.title: Typo-Squatting – Package Repository Enumeration by Name Similarity

suggestion.title: Implicit Dependency Update – Unvetted Version Promotion

suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—successful exploitation produces observable file system modifications.

suggestion.title: Splunk Sidecar PostgreSQL Anomalous Query Operations

suggestion.title: Joomla JCE Component Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly identifies 'actively exploited Joomla JCE Flaw'—pipeline extracted zero use cases. JCE is a specific, named Joomla component; requests to its endpoints should be baseline-divided into admin vs. attacker-controlled patterns.

Flag requests containing base64-encoded payloads, PHP serialized objects, or shell metacharacters in file upload or configuration parameters. Correlate with 200-series responses and rapid subsequent PHP execution.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution Detection from Web Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allowing PHP Code Execution'—core impact. Pipeline did not surface detection for PHP RCE spawning processes or files from web service account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP interpreter (php.exe, php-cgi) spawning child processes (cmd, powershell, bash) or creating files outside normal publish/cache directories immediately after HTTP request ingestion. Parent process should be httpd/apache/nginx; command line should lack typical development tool signatures.

suggestion.title: Joomla JCE File Upload to Webroot
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerability exploitation typically writes webshells or backdoors; article does not describe post-compromise behavior, but pipeline should have suggested detection for file writes to JCE-writable paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .php file creation in /components/com_jce/, /images/, /tmp/, or Joomla root within minutes of suspicious JCE HTTP requests. Baseline normal upload patterns by timestamp and source IP; flag writes outside maintenance windows or by the web service account without corresponding legitimate file-upload API calls.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Joomla JCE Version Inventory Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: CISA warning implies specific affected versions; pipeline did not extract or surface CVE number, affected version range, or asset-matching rules. This should be a standing vulnerability management use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference deployed Joomla instances and JCE component versions against CISA-published vulnerability advisory (extract CVE, fixed version). Alert on any Joomla server with JCE installed in vulnerable version range, especially if internet-facing.

suggestion.title: Repeated JCE Component Access from Attacker IP

Correlate with known exploit public details.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-20253 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and emphasizes patch lag as 'silent killer.' Asset inventory and scanner outputs are primary detection vector for KEV entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk Enterprise instances with software versions matching CVE-2026-20253 affected range via vulnerability scanner or asset management system. Prioritize externally-facing assets. Generate weekly reports against Splunk asset baseline.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor proxy/WAF logs and Splunk application logs for requests to sidecar endpoints (identified by port/path pattern) lacking valid authentication tokens or Authorization headers. Flag 403→200 sequences indicating auth bypass.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation via Splunk Enterprise Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' File-creation patterns initiated by Splunk process are the exploitation impact signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Splunk process (splunkd) creating files in system directories (/etc, /var, /root, /) or truncating existing files. Establish baseline of normal Splunk file operations first. Correlation with PostgreSQL sidecar request logs increases confidence.

suggestion.title: Internet-Routable Splunk Management Ports (8000, 8089)
suggestion.rationale: Article implies 'public-facing application' exploitation; T1190 requires exposed asset discovery. Network reconnaissance for Splunk default ports from untrusted segments is prerequisite for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk instances accessible from public internet or untrusted networks on ports 8000 (web UI) or 8089 (management port). Cross-reference against approved Splunk external access list. Flag instances without upstream authentication/proxy.

suggestion.title: Splunk Sidecar Database Exploitation Query Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies PostgreSQL sidecar as attack surface with file-path parameters implicit in 'create or truncate arbitrary files' capability. Query logs should reveal injection/path-traversal payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze sidecar query logs and HTTP request logs for path-traversal patterns (../, ../../) or suspicious file parameters (?file=/etc/passwd). Monitor for POST requests to file-management endpoints. Whitelist known legitimate administrative paths first.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—missing-authentication vulnerabilities require direct endpoint-access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk Enterprise for HTTP requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints that lack valid authentication tokens, session cookies, or Authorization headers. Establish baseline for legitimate sidecar traffic and alert on external or unauthenticated access patterns.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Write via Splunk PostgreSQL Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the vulnerability allows attackers to 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—this is the direct exploitation mechanism and must be detected at both the endpoint and filesystem layers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP requests to Splunk PostgreSQL endpoints (unauthenticated) with unexpected file creation/truncation operations on the same host within 5-minute windows. Flag writes to sensitive paths (/var/log, /etc, /opt/splunk/etc) and monitor for mass file truncations inconsistent with maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Splunk Log Truncation Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'truncate arbitrary files'—in post-exploitation context, attackers use file truncation to destroy audit and access logs; this is a critical defense-evasion indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected truncation or zero-length writes to Splunk audit logs, access.log, splunk.log, or PostgreSQL transaction logs. Cross-reference with failed authentication attempts or unauthenticated endpoint access in preceding hours to identify post-exploitation cover-up.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Asset Exposure and Patch Validation
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation indicates active exploitation. Article provides explicit CVE ID and federal remediation deadline (2026-06-21), requiring asset inventory and patch verification hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results and patch management systems for Splunk Enterprise instances missing CVE-2026-20253 patches. Cross-reference with network exposure scans (port 8089, 8000) to identify internet-facing instances. Flag any patch lag beyond 2026-06-21 deadline for compliance escalation.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' as the attack surface—probing or successful enumeration of this endpoint is a pre-exploitation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound traffic to Splunk hosts for HTTP/HTTPS requests to PostgreSQL-adjacent paths (containing 'postgres', 'sidecar', '_internal' in URI). Alert on repeated failed connection attempts or HTTP 401/403 responses followed by requests without auth headers, indicating reconnaissance or auth-bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Baseline detection for exploit attempts against this exposed endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically port 55432 or custom postgres ports) from external/unauthenticated sources. suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation via PostgreSQL Sidecar Process
suggestion.rationale: Attack explicitly targets file creation capability: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Detect abnormal file write operations initiated by sidecar.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or modification operations executed by postgres/sidecar processes targeting unexpected paths (config dirs, temp locations, sensitive application directories). Correlate with concurrent sidecar network activity from unauthenticated sources.

suggestion.title: File Truncation Operations via Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Threat explicitly includes file truncation capability: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Truncation is lower-signal than creation but distinct destructive pattern.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file size reduction or truncation events on critical Splunk config or data files correlated with PostgreSQL sidecar process activity. Alert on repeated truncation attempts targeting same paths.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with active wild exploitation. Article identifies specific CVE; standard practice is vulnerability-specific detection signature for early exploit attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on requests to known vulnerable Splunk Enterprise endpoints documented in public CVE-2026-20253 POC. Stack with absence of prior authentication or session cookie. Cross-reference against asset inventory for patched vs. unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Unauthenticated Sidecar Access
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector explicitly stated: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite T1190 being mapped; this is the baseline exploitation detection.

Correlate with Splunk Enterprise version to identify vulnerable instances. Baseline: any such request before patch-due-date 2026-06-21.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Operations via PostgreSQL Service
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation impact is file create/truncate; article: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline has no execution-phase detection for file operations initiated by or routed through the vulnerable service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation (File_Events.ActionType == 'FileCreated' or 'FileModified') or truncation operations initiated by Splunk service account without expected administrative context. Flag rapid file creation bursts in config/data/plugins directories. Cross-correlate with unauthenticated sidecar access events in the same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Version Exposure Audit

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanning logs for Splunk Enterprise version enumeration; cross-check asset inventory for instances running versions <patched_threshold. Flag any Splunk instance still vulnerable post-2026-06-21 as high-priority remediation debt. Include both on-prem and cloud deployments.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Lateral Access

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'; authentication-bypass detection for this vector was entirely omitted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk application logs and network IDS for HTTP/HTTPS requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically localhost/internal services) originating from external or unexpected sources. suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via CVE-2026-20253
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies capability to 'create or truncate arbitrary files'; file-operation detections on Splunk hosts during or after sidecar endpoint access were not proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk host systems for unexpected file creation or modification targeting config directories, plugin paths, or var/ locations. Correlate file events with access logs showing unauthenticated or anomalous requests to sidecar endpoints. Alert on file operations by Splunk service accounts to unusual or suspicious paths.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2026-20253 as the primary matching indicator and explicitly recommends scanning; no HTTP request pattern or endpoint-level exploitation signatures were defined.

Monitor all internet-facing Splunk instances regardless of reported patch status; patch lag frequently masks active exploitation.

suggestion.title: Splunk Service Anomalies Post-File Manipulation
