suggestion.title: JCE Vulnerable Version Identification
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'Joomla JCE Flaw' but pipeline extracted no version identifiers or file hashes. Vulnerable JCE plugin versions should be detectable via web scanning or file integrity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate /administrator/manifests/plugins/jce/* or /plugins/system/jce/* for version markers. Flag installation of JCE < [patched version] via manifest files or file timestamps post-deployment.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Patterns to Joomla Admin
suggestion.rationale: JCE exploits often bypass authentication or target unauthenticated endpoints. Article does not detail auth requirements but 'actively exploited' suggests low friction; pipeline should flag failed-auth followed by successful component access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed Joomla login attempts with subsequent successful requests to /components/com_jce/ from the same source IP/session. Flag requests to protected plugin endpoints without prior successful authentication.

suggestion.title: Outbound Command & Control from Web Process
suggestion.rationale: Once PHP RCE is achieved, attacker will establish persistence or C2. Pipeline should detect web processes (php, apache, nginx) initiating outbound network connections to non-whitelisted external IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for php.exe, apache2.exe, or nginx worker processes initiating outbound TCP/UDP connections to external IPs outside normal CDN/API whitelist. Flag DNS queries for suspicious domains initiated by web service parent processes.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—this is the primary exploitation path. Pipeline extracted no detection logic for this attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful HTTP requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (commonly port 8191 or service-internal endpoints) that lack authentication headers or valid session tokens. Baseline legitimate administrative access and alert on anomalous connection patterns from unauthenticated sources.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'create or truncate arbitrary files' capability—the impact mechanism enabling data destruction and system compromise. Pipeline produced no detection for this critical function.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation, deletion, or truncation operations initiated by Splunk service accounts or originating from PostgreSQL sidecar processes. Alert on modifications to Splunk index directories, configuration files, or system-critical paths not consistent with normal maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Patch Compliance — Splunk Enterprise
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal remediation deadline 2026-06-21. Article explicitly recommends asset-exposure hunt per template. Pipeline generated zero compliance-checking use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and patch inventory for Splunk Enterprise instances running versions prior to the patched release. Cross-reference against asset inventory to identify exposed instances. Flag all systems not patched by federal deadline for escalation.

suggestion.title: Exposure of Splunk Critical Function Endpoints Without Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'missing authentication for critical function'—indicates sensitive administrative endpoints are internet-accessible. Pipeline did not generate endpoint exposure detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Splunk instances on public internet (port 8000, 8089, or service-internal ports). Attempt unauthenticated access to /services/server/info and other critical endpoints. Alert on instances where sensitive functions respond without authentication requirements.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Operations from Splunk Service Process
suggestion.rationale: PostgreSQL sidecar compromise enables arbitrary file manipulation—detect when Splunk service account executes file operations outside its normal data directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate file operations by Splunk service accounts. Alert on file creation/deletion/truncation in system directories, /etc, /var/log, or Splunk index directories when preceded by connections from unauthenticated sources or unusual service calls.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the primary attack vector and should trigger detection for any non-credentialed access to this endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk Enterprise hosts for network connections to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically port 5432 or internal service port) originating from external/untrusted sources or lacking valid authentication tokens. Correlate with failed authentication or missing Authorization headers in HTTP/service logs.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Service Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the vulnerability allows attackers to 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' This represents data destruction/manipulation and should trigger on file operations initiated through the vulnerable endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk process or service for FileCreate, FileModify, and FileDelete events on critical configuration, data, or system files. Correlate file operations with preceding unauthenticated service endpoint access or with absence of valid user session context.

suggestion.title: Exploit Attempt: CVE-2026-20253 Service Endpoint Probing
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry means active exploitation in the wild. Article does not specify request patterns but mentions 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' as the attack surface—scan for reconnaissance or exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP or service-protocol requests to known Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (internal or exposed) with no or invalid authentication. Look for patterns consistent with CVE-2026-20253 exploit tools (e.g., direct endpoint requests, missing session tokens, unusual method/parameter combinations).

suggestion.title: CISA KEV Asset Exposure: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' via Splunk SPL and Defender KQL, substituting CVE-2026-20253. Pipeline generated no use case despite this clear instruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk Enterprise instances exposed to untrusted networks or without network-layer authentication controls. Cross-correlate with vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20253 patch status. Asset exposure is the enabling condition for T1190 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'allow an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'. This is the direct attack surface; pipeline missed it entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any unauthenticated TCP connections to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically port 5432 or custom) originating from external/untrusted networks. Baseline expected callers and deviation indicates exploitation attempt. Monitor process spawning from PostgreSQL service for anomalous file operations.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Database Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically describes impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files'. File truncation is destructive and detectable; pipeline missed the impact mapping to T1485.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation and truncation events originating from or proxied through PostgreSQL service processes, especially to system-critical or data directories. Truncation of large files to zero bytes is high-fidelity signal for T1485. Correlate with network access logs to identify if creation/truncation was preceded by unauthenticated external connection.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Critical Function Endpoint Calls
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability described as 'missing authentication for critical function'. Should detect unauthenticated HTTP/HTTPS requests to Splunk critical endpoints that normally require auth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Splunk access logs should show 401 (Unauthorized) or 403 (Forbidden) baseline for critical endpoints like `/admin`, `/search`, or PostgreSQL service proxies. Any 200 responses to these endpoints without valid authentication tokens or from unexpected source IPs indicates potential exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—direct exploitation vector must be hunted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP/network connections to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar service without authentication credentials. Monitor for requests to sidecar endpoints (typically PostgreSQL port 5432 or custom listeners, Splunk service ports 8000/9000) that return 200/201 without auth headers present. Baseline legitimate service-health checks to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation and Truncation via Splunk Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'could allow...create or truncate arbitrary files'—file system impact that indicates post-exploitation execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected file creation (in /opt/splunk, /etc, /var) and truncation events coinciding with PostgreSQL sidecar access. Detect zero-byte file creation or rapid file size reduction in sensitive config/data files. Parent process should be Splunk daemon or sidecar service, not interactive user shells.

suggestion.title: Splunk Service Exposure and Reconnaissance Scanning
suggestion.rationale: T1190 context implies 'public-facing' Splunk services—scanning/discovery activity must precede exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify network scanning for Splunk service ports (8000/tcp, 9000/tcp, PostgreSQL 5432). Look for multiple 404/403 responses followed by 200 on same service within short time window. Check for nmap/masscan fingerprinting signatures or rapid port-probe sequences in netflow data.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Missing Authentication Bypass Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry confirms active exploitation—need direct behavioral detection for authentication control bypass on critical functions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthenticated HTTP requests to Splunk critical-function endpoints (sidecar API, service configuration endpoints). Correlation: (1) request lacks Authorization header + (2) targets sensitive endpoint pattern + (3) returns 200/201 response. Cross-reference against patched Splunk versions to exclude patched assets.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Persistence via Splunk Config File Modification
suggestion.rationale: File-creation capability enables persistence through startup-script or config injection ('create arbitrary files')—extends impact beyond immediate data destruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized modifications to Splunk init.d scripts, systemd units, python package directories (/opt/splunk/etc, /opt/splunk/lib/python*), or application startup files. Alert on executable file creation in Splunk startup paths, particularly scripts or binaries created during or immediately after unauthenticated service access.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—missing authentication is the attack vector and primary detection point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthenticated HTTP/network requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints on vulnerable instances. Monitor for connections to sidecar service port without standard Splunk auth headers or from untrusted sources. Correlate with CVE-2026-20253 asset inventory.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation by Splunk Process
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies impact as 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—this is the observable post-exploitation behavior distinguishing this from generic auth bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file system events for unexpected file creation or truncation by Splunk services/processes, especially in configuration, log, or system directories. Baseline normal operations; alert on abnormal file size drops or suspicious new files in restricted paths.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerable Splunk Enterprise Inventory Check
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status confirms active wild exploitation; inventory of vulnerable instances against federal 2026-06-21 patch deadline is mandatory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset inventory for Splunk Enterprise instances against CVE-2026-20253. Verify patch status and exposed network surface. Flag instances missing patches against federal remediation deadline.

suggestion.title: Audit Log Destruction via File Truncation
suggestion.rationale: Article's file truncation capability enables deletion of audit logs for post-exploitation cover. This is implicit defense-evasion impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sudden truncation, deletion, or size drops in Splunk audit/transaction logs, especially if correlated with prior network anomalies or failed authentication attempts. Monitor for file wipe patterns.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user...through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — the direct attack surface. Pipeline missed the entry point entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/TCP traffic to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoints from unauthenticated or external sources. Alert when non-Splunk service accounts or out-of-band IPs connect to the sidecar port. Baseline expected internal traffic and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'create or truncate arbitrary files' — this impact phase requires file-operation auditing hunts to detect post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected file creation, deletion, or truncation operations correlated with PostgreSQL sidecar process execution or network activity. Alert on rapid batch file truncation patterns targeting Splunk config or data directories.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with active exploitation — article provides specific CVE identifier; WAF/IDS signatures should be deployed immediately. Pipeline failed to surface signature-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy vulnerability signatures for CVE-2026-20253. Monitor HTTP logs for requests to known vulnerable PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint paths with unauthenticated payloads or common PostgreSQL injection patterns.

suggestion.title: Splunk Service Crash or Abnormal Termination Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: File truncation via the sidecar can corrupt Splunk state or cause service instability — article implies operational impact from successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Splunk service process crashes, unexpected restarts, or exceptions coinciding with unauthenticated PostgreSQL sidecar access logs. Monitor Splunk _internal logs for file corruption or I/O errors on truncated paths.

suggestion.title: Non-Standard PostgreSQL Sidecar Connection Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies PostgreSQL sidecar as attack vector; should detect authentication anomalies on this service component.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL audit logs for connection attempts to the sidecar service without expected Splunk service credentials or from unexpected source IP ranges. Alert on successful unauthenticated connections or failed brute-force patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Patch Compliance and Remediation Urgency
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal due date 2026-06-21; article states 'patch lag is the silent killer' — asset-exposure hunt is required per article guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and patch compliance tools for Splunk Enterprise instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253. Rescan instances reporting old baseline dates (stale scans mask unpatched systems). Flag any systems with remediation date after 2026-06-21 due date for escalation.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar: Unauthenticated Critical Function Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'allows an unauthenticated user' to interact with PostgreSQL sidecar. This is the initial access path and should trigger detection of authentication-bypass attempts or direct endpoint access without credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint (typically port 5432 or service-specific) for connections without valid authentication tokens or API keys. Alert on successful unauthenticated requests to critical-function endpoints that would normally require authentication.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise: Unexpected File Creation/Truncation via PostgreSQL Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This file operation is the destructive payload and should be monitored at OS level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation, modification, or truncation operations initiated by Splunk PostgreSQL processes (e.g., postgres, splunkd) in critical directories (/opt/splunk/var, /var/lib/pgsql). Flag any file operations on system-sensitive paths (log directories, config files, database files) outside normal maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar: Service Endpoint Anomalous Request Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies a specific attack surface: 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Direct requests to this endpoint with file-operation parameters (create/truncate payloads) should be detectable at application or proxy layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/service requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints for suspicious payloads: file paths in query parameters, write/truncate directives, or requests originating from unexpected network segments. Baseline normal maintenance operations and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Splunk Instance: CVE-2026-20253 Patch Status and Remediation Timeline
suggestion.rationale: Federal patch due date is 2026-06-21 (3 days from publication). Pipeline should flag this as a compliance and risk-prioritization milestone, with UC to confirm patch deployment across fleet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all Splunk Enterprise instances for version/patch status against CVE-2026-20253. Cross-reference with external-facing asset inventory; prioritize exposure assessment for any instances accessible from untrusted networks. Trigger alert if unpatched instances are detected post-due-date.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Enterprise Vulnerable Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies CVE-2026-20253 and notes CISA KEV entries are actively exploited in wild. Standard asset-exposure hunt is the primary detection lever for a public-facing auth-bypass vulnerability. Article mentions 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' (T1190) and references asset-exposure template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Splunk Enterprise instances with versions matching CVE-2026-20253 scope. Cross-correlate with network exposure data (public IPs, cloud endpoints, externally routable interfaces). Prioritize instances accessible without authentication or with default credentials.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Endpoint Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is in 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' allowing unauthenticated file creation/truncation. Should detect abnormal access patterns or exploit attempts targeting this specific service component.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound traffic to Splunk instances targeting PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints from untrusted sources. Correlate with HTTP 200/201 responses (indicating successful endpoint access) or error patterns suggesting exploitation attempts. Flag any unauthenticated POST/PUT requests to file-manipulation endpoints.

suggestion.title: Anomalous File Creation/Truncation Through Service Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the vulnerability 'could allow an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Detection should flag unexpected file operations originating from the vulnerable service component.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or truncation events in Splunk application directories that correlate temporally with external HTTP requests to the PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint. Baseline normal file operations per Splunk version/deployment type; flag deviations in file paths, sizes, or ownership.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk Enterprise Critical Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires missing authentication; article emphasizes this is an 'unauthenticated' attack surface. Should detect bypassed or missing auth controls on Splunk endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Splunk endpoint access logs to establish normal authenticated session patterns. Flag HTTP 200/204 responses to sensitive endpoints (file operations, configuration endpoints, database sidecars) from source IPs with no corresponding successful authentication event in the preceding 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Inline remote config with command-execution backend options in HTTP path
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Inline remote configuration can set backend options that execute local commands during initialization.' No UC validates the payload itself. Attack requires specific option syntax (e.g., `exec=`, `cmd=` patterns) that triggers RCE during backend init. Purely port-based hunting misses non-standard ports or payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to rclone RC containing inline-remote config with backend options designed to trigger command execution. Pattern: `/[type://option=value]` where option is a known RCE vector. Correlate with child-process spawning and non-standard user-agents.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-41179 mitigation bypass via evasion-encoded inline-remote syntax
suggestion.rationale: Article: vuln 'bypasses CVE-2026-41179 fix.' Prior mitigation likely added guards that new attack circumvents. No detection for the novel evasion technique or requests that fail prior filtering but succeed in new variant.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track HTTP requests with unusual URL encoding (double-encoding, alternate bracket representations like `%5b:%5d`), nested syntax, or escape sequences that may evade CVE-2026-41179 regex guards. Look for init failures followed by success, indicating filter bypass.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP requests to rclone RC port lacking standard API headers
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated GET and HEAD requests.' UC_102_1 detects startup config but not runtime exploitation. Actual attack requires requests with no Authorization/X-API-Token headers and non-standard user-agents, distinguishing attacks from legitimate internal clients.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GET/HEAD requests to port 5572 that: (1) lack HTTP Authorization or X-API-Token headers, (2) originate from user-agents not matching rclone client regex (exclude curl with rclone version string), (3) target paths matching inline-remote pattern. Baseline legitimate internal clients to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—direct signal for the initial exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network connections to Splunk sidecar endpoints (PostgreSQL port patterns, internal socket communication) from clients lacking valid authentication tokens. Look for absence of auth headers, failed auth sequences immediately followed by successful file-manipulation requests, or direct file operations without prior credential validation.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Manipulation via Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes capability to 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—the measurable post-exploitation impact surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate sidecar endpoint access from unauthenticated sources with unusual file creation/truncation events on the Splunk host, especially targeting config dirs (/opt/splunk/etc), data dirs, or app directories. Flag truncate-to-zero and bulk file deletes; cross-check against change-control logs.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Public-Facing Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'observed exploited in the wild' + 'public-facing application'—requires asset inventory sweep for externally accessible Splunk instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Splunk Enterprise instances (ports 8089, 8000, 9997, sidecar ephemeral ranges) reachable from untrusted networks. Query IP geolocation, DNS reverse-resolution to public domains, certificate SAN lists, and Shodan/similar external-facing asset databases. Escalate any instances not explicitly documented as intentionally internet-facing.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Standard CVE-matching hunt for CISA KEV with federal remediation deadline 2026-06-21; article states Splunk Enterprise is the affected product.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Splunk Enterprise version via /services/server/info API or web UI banner grab across all hosts. Match against CVSS/vendor advisory for patched version; flag all instances below patched threshold. Given KEV active exploitation + federal deadline, treat all unpatched instances as critical.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Splunk Enterprise Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user' + 'CISA KEV implies active exploitation' — baseline internet-routable asset discovery is mandatory first step per template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk Enterprise instances on ports 8000, 8089, 9997 accessible from external networks. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner data for CVE-2026-20253 to surface unpatched instances. Port 8000 (web UI) is the primary unauthenticated-access attack surface for this vulnerability.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Suspicious File Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — direct attack mechanism not captured in any UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation/truncation operations on Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar paths initiated without corresponding authenticated Splunk service activity. Correlate unauthenticated HTTP requests to sidecar endpoints with subsequent filesystem changes.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated API Requests to Splunk Critical Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'missing authentication for critical function' — root cause is absent auth controls; direct hunting for missing session tokens is essential.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Splunk endpoints (file API, config endpoints, PostgreSQL sidecar routes) lacking valid authentication headers or session cookies. Baseline and alert on anomalies; high-volume scanning from single source IP may indicate active exploitation.

suggestion.title: Version Probing Against Splunk Enterprise Services
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV indicates active wild exploitation; reconnaissance attempts precede exploitation. Article notes 'patch lag is the silent killer.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated connection attempts or version-enumeration requests to Splunk ports from external networks. Detect error responses or headers that leak Splunk version information to untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — the sidecar is public-facing and authentication is missing, making any unauthenticated connection exploitation evidence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS access to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints that succeed without valid authentication headers or SSL client certificates. Baseline traffic patterns first, then flag any non-baseline origins accessing these endpoints.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Deletion from Splunk Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker can 'truncate arbitrary files' — file deletion/truncation from Splunk or PostgreSQL sidecar processes warrants immediate investigation as exploitation evidence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file deletion or truncation initiated by Splunk Enterprise or PostgreSQL sidecar processes, especially against system-critical or config directories. Correlate with unusual network access to the sidecar endpoint to confirm exploitation.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Detection for CVE-2026-20253
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries require active asset remediation tracking — article establishes federal patch-due date of 2026-06-21, making vulnerability scanner results the primary control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain continuous scanning for CVE-2026-20253 across Splunk Enterprise inventory. Flag any vulnerable instance, then correlate with network access logs to assess exploitation risk and blast radius.

suggestion.title: Network Reconnaissance of Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must discover the sidecar endpoint before exploiting; article identifies this as a PostgreSQL service on specific port, implying prior reconnaissance necessary.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scanning or service enumeration targeting Splunk service ports (5432 for PostgreSQL, 8000-8089 for Splunk web/API). Baseline expected scan sources; flag unauthorized external scans.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes this CVE is actively exploited in the wild (CISA KEV status) against exposed Splunk Enterprise instances. Article phrase: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' indicates the attack vector is network-accessible.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk Enterprise assets vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253 by scanning for exposed PostgreSQL sidecar service on standard Splunk ports (8089, 8000). Query vulnerability management feeds for patch deployment lag post 2026-06-21 federal due date.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Unauthorized Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user' can exploit the 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint,' indicating no auth required. This is a direct bypass detection: any network access to the sidecar endpoint is suspicious.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for connections to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically port ranges around Splunk's standard service ports) from unexpected external or internal subnets. Flag any traffic not originating from Splunk components or administrators.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation on Splunk Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the vulnerability 'could allow...to create or truncate arbitrary files.' This is direct impact; behavioral detection of file operations via the sidecar service should trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk system file creation and deletion events for anomalous patterns: sudden bulk file truncations, files created outside normal deployment windows, or modifications to Splunk config/data directories by unexpected processes or users.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Error Spike
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation attempts against CVE-2026-20253 will leave traces in Splunk's application logs. Article identifies the vulnerability in the 'PostgreSQL sidecar service,' which should log access attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Splunk's internal logs (_internal index) for unusual error rates or access attempts to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints. Look for 401/403/500 errors or 'unauthorized' messages from the sidecar service, especially from external IPs.

suggestion.title: Network Reconnaissance of Splunk Services
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must first discover exposed Splunk instances. Article's mention of 'public-facing application' vulnerability (T1190 category) implies reconnaissance precedes exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network scanning activity targeting Splunk's known port ranges (8089, 8000, 8088) followed by connection attempts to sidecar endpoints. Correlate source IPs across multiple scanning events to identify reconnaissance patterns.

suggestion.title: Single alarm DELETE across tenant boundaries (low-volume cross-realm IDOR test)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'An authenticated user in any realm can delete alarms belonging to other realms by supplying arbitrary alarm IDs.' UC_2_3 requires ≥10 deletes/10m and ≥2 realms (volume-based); attacker POC may delete 1–2 alarms spanning realms to confirm exploitation before bulk action. Low-volume variant needed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Single authenticated user issues DELETE on alarm endpoints mapping to ≥2 distinct realms (extracted from URI) within 5min, regardless of total delete count. Baseline per-user realm affinity; deviation signals scope/privilege violation.

suggestion.title: Langflow IDOR: Unauthorized flow execution via cross-user flow_id reference
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'authenticated attacker to execute any flow belonging to another user by specifying the victim's flow ID.' Pipeline missed the definitive detection: application-level logging of (requester_user_id ≠ flow_owner_id AND response=success).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on /api/v1/responses POST requests (status 200) where authenticated user executing a flow does not match the flow's owner. Requires Langflow to emit requester_user_id and flow_owner_id in audit logs. High-confidence exploitation signature.

suggestion.title: Langflow: Single-source enumeration of valid flow UUIDs
suggestion.rationale: Article describes IDOR but doesn't address reconnaissance phase. Attacker must discover valid flow_id values before exploit. Flag rapid sequential or near-sequential UUID attempts: 10+ distinct flow_id values in 5-minute window from one source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: POST requests to /api/v1/responses with flow_id parameters that are numerically sequential (or share common UUID prefixes) at high velocity from single IP+user combination, indicating UUID brute-force enumeration.

suggestion.title: Langflow CVE-2026-55255: Asset exposure via unpatched version detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability in versions <1.9.1. Pipeline missed version-range IOC. Correlate software inventory (Langflow instances) against known-affected version range with CVE-2026-55255 severity flag.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Langflow deployments via asset discovery; correlate against VulnerabilityDB for CVE-2026-55255 and version <1.9.1. Surface unpatched instances with timestamp of last patch availability. Treat as critical exposure.

suggestion.title: Langflow: Cross-org data exfiltration via IDOR flow execution
suggestion.rationale: Article says attacker can 'execute any flow belonging to another user'—flows may contain data processing logic, API integrations, or sensitive transformations. Detect execution of flows from users outside normal organizational boundaries or data-sharing policies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate /api/v1/responses executions against organizational user directory and data-classification metadata. Alert when authenticated user outside flow_owner's department/team successfully executes flow, especially if flow integrates external APIs or performs data serialization.

suggestion.title: Gravity SMTP REST Endpoint Probing — CVE-2026-4020 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly marks IoC: 'key indicator of compromise is requests to /wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data found in web server access logs, particularly those including the ?page=gravitysmtp-settings query parameter.' Pipeline completely missed this stated detection point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP GET requests to /wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data with ?page=gravitysmtp-settings query parameter from external source IPs. Baseline normal traffic and flag volume anomalies (>10 requests/hour from single IP or >100 unique sources/day).

suggestion.title: Credential Disclosure via System Report JSON — Gravity SMTP Info Leak
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exposed information: 'API keys, secrets, and OAuth tokens for configured email integrations... Credentials for third-party email services, including Amazon SES, Google, Mailjet, Resend, and Zoho.' Pipeline generated no use case for detecting this credential exfiltration pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP 200 responses from /wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data exceeding typical payload size (>5KB) or containing credential patterns (oauth_token, api_key, AWS secret, etc.). Correlate with external source IPs.

suggestion.title: Email Service Credential Abuse — Post-Compromise Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article warns: 'attacker could abuse the site's connected email services, while the detailed system report significantly lowers the effort required to plan further attacks.' Pipeline missed detection for abuse of exfiltrated Amazon SES, Google, Mailjet, Resend, Zoho credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor authenticated API calls to Amazon SES SendEmail, Google Workspace SMTP, and other configured services for anomalous patterns: large message batches to unusual recipients, API calls from new geographic regions, or authentication timing misaligned with normal site operations.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Plugin Version Enumeration — Gravity SMTP ≤2.1.4
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'affects all versions of the plugin from 2.1.4 and older and has been addressed in version 2.1.5.' Pipeline should include asset discovery use case for vulnerable versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query WordPress plugin directories and REST endpoints to fingerprint Gravity SMTP version. Flag any instances running v2.1.4 or below as vulnerable to CVE-2026-4020. Cross-correlate with previous REST endpoint access alerts.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Campaign Tracking — CVE-2026-4020 Source IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article provides telemetry: 'Wordfence blocked more than 17 million attempts...exploitation activity spiked on June 7, with 4 million requests being blocked that day.' Also states: 'listed the most prolific source IP addresses for exploit requests, which website administrators should add to their blocklists.' Pipeline extracted zero IP-based IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain blocklist of prolific source IPs identified by Wordfence and other security vendors as CVE-2026-4020 exploit sources. Alert on traffic from these IPs to any /wp-json/gravitysmtp endpoint. Update blocklists weekly as new attacker infrastructure surfaces.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline generated zero UCs. This is the core exploitation path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthenticated HTTP/network access to Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoints (typically internal ports). Flag any requests from non-Splunk service accounts or external IPs. Cross-reference with Splunk process logs to detect unexpected connection initiators.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Enterprise
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow...create or truncate arbitrary files.' No UC generated for post-exploitation file-system impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file create/delete/truncate operations initiated by Splunk Enterprise processes (splunkd.exe, postgresql.exe sidecar) targeting files outside expected Splunk directories. Establish baseline of legitimate Splunk-initiated file operations, then alert on deviations (e.g., /etc modifications, user home-directory writes, system binary overwrites).

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Patch Status Inventory (CVE-2026-20253)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch deadline 2026-06-21 and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Standard asset-exposure template mentioned but no UC instantiated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Splunk Enterprise deployments for versions prior to CVE-2026-20253 patch release. Cross-reference asset inventory with vulnerability scanner data. Flag any unpatched instances exposed to networks (particularly internet-facing or DMZ). Prioritize based on network exposure scoring.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Exposure Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires access to 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline did not generate network-discovery or service-enumeration UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for network scans or connection attempts targeting Splunk-internal PostgreSQL sidecar ports (commonly ephemeral or fixed range). Flag any non-Splunk-service processes attempting connections to these endpoints. Correlate with Splunk Enterprise asset inventory to detect lateral-movement or external reconnaissance patterns.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Splunk Service Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files' and describes missing authentication for critical function — direct indicator of auth-bypass exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Splunk service endpoints (port 8089, web UI, sidecar) originating from untrusted networks with no authentication header or invalid session tokens. Flag requests to `_internal` or service management endpoints from non-admin source IPs.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Suspicious File Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' as the attack vector for file creation/truncation — requires detection at the process/file system level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected file create/delete/modify events originating from Splunk or PostgreSQL sidecar processes, particularly in config directories, log paths, or authentication-critical files. Alert on bulk file deletion patterns inconsistent with normal maintenance.

suggestion.title: Splunk Instance Exposure to Internet
suggestion.rationale: Context states 'currently being exploited' and 'exposed assets' — asset exposure hunt is standard for CISA KEV; article references template hunt for CVE-2026-20253.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and network visibility tools to identify Splunk Enterprise instances with external-facing service ports (8000, 8089) accessible from untrusted networks or the internet. Cross-reference with patch status for CVE-2026-20253.

suggestion.title: Splunk Configuration or Authentication Bypass Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: File creation/truncation capability could enable persistence or further compromise — article does not detail post-exploitation artifacts but impact assessment requires monitoring for configuration drift.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk audit logs for unexpected file operations via the sidecar endpoint, unusual changes to authentication.conf or relevant configuration files, and service restart events that lack corresponding admin activity logs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scan Coverage
suggestion.rationale: Article states "CISA KEV only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild" and federal patch due is 2026-06-21. Pipeline must emit use case validating Splunk Enterprise instances are patched or mitigated. Cite: 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20253 in Splunk Enterprise deployments. Alert on any unpatched instances older than the federal due date. Confirm version against official Splunk security advisory.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk Critical Functions
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Requires detection of auth bypass or missing auth checks on these critical endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk audit logs for unauthenticated requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically internal but verify config). Alert on HTTP 200/201 responses to endpoints that require authentication. Inspect User field for null/empty values paired with file manipulation API calls.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is file system manipulation. Detection requires monitoring write/delete events correlated with sidecar process activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Splunk hosts, monitor file creation and truncation events (especially system/config files) that correlate with PostgreSQL sidecar process execution or API calls. Alert on unexpected file deletions in /etc, /opt/splunk, or application directories. Require process chain linking sidecar to file ops.

suggestion.title: External Network Exposure of Splunk Management/Sidecar Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article implies exploitation against 'exposed assets' and T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application). Splunk sidecar endpoint must be internet-accessible for remote exploitation. Hunt for exposed endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan external network perimeter for Splunk Enterprise instances with PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints reachable from WAN. Correlate with SSL certificate logs for new Splunk externally-facing hosts. Alert on any sidecar port (default varies, check Splunk docs) exposed to 0.0.0.0. Cross-reference with CISA KEV due date to prioritize.

suggestion.title: Splunk Service Restart / Sidecar Process Anomalies Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: File truncation attacks ('truncate arbitrary files') may corrupt Splunk config or logs. Post-exploitation, sidecar or main Splunk process may restart, crash, or enter error state. Pipeline should detect suspicious process lifecycle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk host for rapid restarts of PostgreSQL sidecar or main Splunk daemon in short windows. Alert on abnormal exit codes (e.g., segfault, permission denied) following file-write events. Cross-reference with syslog for 'file not found' / 'truncated' errors on Splunk system files.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies attack vector: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline generated zero detections for this endpoint access pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound HTTP/HTTPS to Splunk sidecar ports (commonly :8191, :9997) originating from untrusted subnets or lacking valid Splunk authentication headers (Bearer token, session cookie). Flag successful 200/201 responses to /api/*, /services/*, or sidecar-specific endpoints.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Manipulation via Splunk Service
suggestion.rationale: Direct impact mechanism: 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' No detection for file-system events tied to Splunk processes or service accounts exploiting this gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected file creates, deletes, or truncations by Splunk service accounts (splunk, _splunk_) or child processes of Splunk daemons, especially in sensitive directories (/etc, /var, Windows\System32, $SPLUNK_HOME/../..).

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Lateral Movement or Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability abuses PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint for unauthenticated access. Pipeline missed detection for abnormal sidecar process behavior, such as spawning shells or unexpected database operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL/postgres process spawning cmd.exe, /bin/bash, or other shell interpreters. Flag connections to non-Splunk databases or unexpected child processes with high privileges. Correlate with file-manipulation events.

suggestion.title: Splunk Authentication Bypass Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'missing authentication for critical function.' Pipeline did not generate rules for authentication bypass attempts or auth-less access to protected Splunk functions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Splunk /api/*, /services/*, /admin endpoints without Authorization header, valid Bearer token, or Splunk session cookie. Baseline against known admin IPs to reduce false positives. Flag any 200+ responses from unexpected sources.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Public Exposure (Asset Inventory)
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV emphasizes 'observed exploited in the wild' against 'public-facing' assets. Article recommends asset-exposure hunt; no specific detection for Splunk Enterprise listening on external IPs or cloud endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Splunk Enterprise ports (8000, 8089) on public-facing IPs or cloud instances without firewall restrictions. Cross-reference DNS A/AAAA records resolving to known Splunk instances. Compare against internal asset inventory; flag any undocumented external exposure.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' No detection built for HTTP requests to this endpoint without valid authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (internal service paths, typically API routes to postgres management endpoints) arriving without authentication headers, session tokens, or valid credentials. Flag requests from external IPs to these normally-internal service ports.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation via Splunk Sidecar Process
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'create or truncate arbitrary files' as direct impact. No file-system detection correlating unexpected file truncation/deletion with Splunk sidecar process activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file truncation (SetEndOfFile) and deletion events correlated with Splunk sidecar or PostgreSQL subprocess spawning. Baseline legitimate application file operations; alert on unexpected truncation of system or critical application files initiated through the sidecar.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Executing Unauthorized File Operations
suggestion.rationale: Attack flows through 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—process is execution vehicle. Article does not describe SQL syntax but implies file system commands executed via sidecar.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL query logs within sidecar for administrative/DDL commands (CREATE, DROP, TRUNCATE) on non-application schemas. Cross-reference with external HTTP requests to sidecar endpoint to confirm attacker-initiated execution chain.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Unauthenticated Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack vector: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the primary exploitation technique and highest-confidence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/TCP requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar service ports (typically 9997 or custom ranges) originating from external IPs without prior authentication session tokens. Flag any file write/delete system calls executed by the Splunk process immediately following unauthenticated sidecar requests.

suggestion.title: Splunk Critical Function Missing Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability type: 'missing authentication for critical function.' This describes direct bypass of auth controls on Splunk administrative functions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Splunk critical endpoints (e.g., /services/admin, /services/data) without Authorization headers or valid session cookies. Correlate with successful state changes (file creation, data modification) from the same source IP.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Write/Delete in Splunk Data Directories
suggestion.rationale: Attack outcome specified: 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—implies file system operations beyond normal Splunk runtime. The PostgreSQL sidecar is the vector but the impact is file manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or truncation events in Splunk PostgreSQL data directories (e.g., $SPLUNK_HOME/var/lib/splunk/pgsql/) or config directories that do not originate from the Splunk service account during normal maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Internet Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article references asset-exposure template as canonical approach; mentions 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets' and 'Anything in CISA KEV is *currently* being exploited.' Exposed Splunk instances are the prerequisite for this vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate and alert on Splunk Enterprise instances accessible from the internet on ports 8000 (UI), 8089 (management), or non-standard sidecar ports. Cross-reference against asset inventory to identify unpatched instances missing CVE-2026-20253 mitigations.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Port Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Specific attack surface: 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' The sidecar should never be exposed to untrusted networks. Port discovery/exposure is a prerequisite for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for open PostgreSQL ports associated with Splunk (9997 or custom sidecar service ports) responding to external probes. Flag any response that does not require authentication before accepting SQL commands or file operations.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Internet-Facing Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'exploit public-facing application'; CISA KEV context means active scanning. Canonical asset-exposure hunt required for any internet-exposed Splunk cluster.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search SIEM and cloud-asset logs for Splunk ports (8089, 8000, 9997) reachable from untrusted ASNs or /0. Correlate against authenticated patch inventory; flag hosts running Splunk Enterprise builds older than patched version for CVE-2026-20253.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthenticated Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'; article says unauthenticated users can exploit it. Monitor for HTTP requests to sidecar endpoints without valid Splunk session tokens or auth headers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests matching /services/postgres* or similar patterns (exact path inferred from Splunk architecture) with status 200–299 from sessions lacking valid authz headers. Flag from external IPs especially.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Create/Truncate by Splunk Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allow an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files.' Direct impact step; monitor file-system events originating from Splunk daemon.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file-create or file-truncate operations by splunkd, splunk-postgresql, or related process contexts targeting system paths (/etc, /boot, /var/log, /var/spool) or Splunk installation binaries, outside normal deployment/update windows.

suggestion.title: Audit Log Tampering Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Truncate capability naturally leads to log destruction; article establishes arbitrary file manipulation. Attackers will erase audit trails.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for zero-byte truncation or sudden size reduction of Splunk audit.log, access.log, or system syslog. Correlate truncation events with prior unauthenticated PostgreSQL sidecar requests on same host.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Splunk Configuration File Modification
suggestion.rationale: Arbitrary file creation/truncate could target Splunk configs (props.conf, inputs.conf, etc.) to persist access or disable logging. Article does not exclude config targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on writes to SPLUNK_HOME/etc/* or etc/apps/* with timing correlation to unauthenticated sidecar endpoint requests. Flag config modifications outside maintenance windows or by non-admin users.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline generated zero detections for unauthorized sidecar access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP/network requests to Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoints from external or unauthenticated sources. Look for requests lacking valid authentication tokens/session IDs targeting the sidecar API.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation
suggestion.rationale: Article core impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files' via sidecar. Pipeline missed impact-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk Enterprise hosts for unexpected file creation or truncation operations initiated from sidecar service process or unexpected file paths. Baseline normal sidecar file I/O; alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Exposed Splunk Enterprise Service Scanning
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV exploits require the target to be internet-facing. Pipeline provided no hunt for asset exposure despite article context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for external port scanning or connection attempts against known Splunk ports (8000, 8089, 9997) and non-standard sidecar service ports from untrusted CIDR blocks. Cross-reference with CISA KEV timeline.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' as attack surface. Pipeline missed reconnaissance phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for reconnaissance-pattern requests to Splunk infrastructure probing for sidecar endpoints, version detection, or error messages that disclose service presence. Look for repeated 404s or 403s against endpoint paths.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-20253. Pipeline emitted zero IOCs. Standard vulnerability detection hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners (Nessus, Qualys, Tenable, etc.) for Splunk Enterprise instances matching CVE-2026-20253. Cross-check against patch inventory to identify unpatched systems exposed to exploitation. Prioritize systems with external routing.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Authentication Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'missing authentication.' Pipeline missed detection of authentication failure/bypass patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk audit logs for failed authentication attempts followed by successful file operations, or direct unauthenticated API calls that bypass auth mechanisms. Flag sidecar access with null/empty auth headers.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Exposed on Public Internet
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'unauthenticated user' access to public-facing vulnerability—T1190 exposure hunt is foundational detection for this attack class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk Enterprise services listening on public IPs on default ports (8089, 8088, 9998). Correlate with CVE-2026-20253 patch status to identify exploitation-ready targets.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' as attack vector—direct exploitation channel requiring monitoring of this specific service interface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Splunk sidecar endpoints (e.g., `/postgres/*`, `/sidecar/*`) lacking valid authentication headers or session tokens. Flag POST/PUT requests attempting file operations.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—direct data destruction/manipulation impact requiring file-level integrity monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when splunkd or sidecar processes create/delete files in sensitive application directories (config, data, var) concurrent with or shortly after unauthenticated sidecar HTTP requests.

suggestion.title: Splunk Sidecar Spawning Unexpected Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: File manipulation via sidecar may involve subprocess execution—execution-layer detection gap for command invocation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes (sh, powershell, cmd.exe, touch, rm) spawned by Splunk sidecar or postgresql service processes—indicates command execution via file manipulation CVE.

suggestion.title: Splunk Configuration File Truncation for Audit Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Truncating authentication/audit configs disables logging—defense-evasion and persistence gap not addressed despite file truncation capability in CVE description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on deletion or truncation of Splunk authentication configs (splunk-auth.conf, props.conf, transforms.conf) concurrent with sidecar exploitation patterns. Detect configuration rollback attempts.

suggestion.title: JCE Plugin Remote Code Execution - HTTP Request Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Joomla JCE Flaw Allowing PHP Code Execution' — the attack vector is web-based exploitation of a known plugin endpoint, which should trigger web request inspection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to Joomla components, specifically /index.php?option=com_jce with suspicious task parameters or file upload attempts to jce plugin directories. Flag requests with encoded PHP or shell metacharacters in parameters.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution Post-JCE Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies 'PHP Code Execution' as the outcome — the execution phase requires detection of PHP interpreter activity spawning processes or writing suspicious files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP interpreter (php.exe, php-cgi) spawning shell commands (cmd.exe, powershell, /bin/bash) or unusual child processes immediately after JCE-related HTTP requests. Also monitor for php.ini writes or dynamic code execution via eval/system/exec.

suggestion.title: Joomla JCE Plugin File Upload to Webroot
suggestion.rationale: A file upload component flaw ('JCE' is JCE Media Manager, a file/image upload plugin) should be detected as suspicious file writes to web-accessible directories during the exploitation window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation/modification in web-accessible directories (e.g., /images/jce/, /media/) with PHP, PSM1, or EXE extensions immediately following HTTP requests to jce plugin endpoints. Correlate with parent process being PHP interpreter.

suggestion.title: Joomla Web Shell Creation and First Execution
suggestion.rationale: RCE exploitation typically results in web shell placement; 'Actively Exploited' signals live attacks with persistence mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new PHP files written to web-accessible directories (especially Joomla root and /images/) followed within seconds by HTTP requests to those same file paths. Cross-reference file creation and web request timestamps.

suggestion.title: Joomla JCE Component Access by Unauthenticated User
suggestion.rationale: A publicly-exploitable flaw implies attackers need no credentials; detecting unauthenticated access to restricted plugin components is a baseline control bypass indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP 200 responses to /index.php?option=com_jce endpoints from sources with no prior Joomla session cookie or authentication token. Flag as exploitation attempt regardless of subsequent response content.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthenticated Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Core attack vector requires detecting unauthenticated requests to this endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk logs and network proxy data for HTTP POST/GET requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically on non-standard ports or internal URIs like /_internal/postgres/) originating from external or untrusted sources without valid authentication headers. Baseline legitimate internal queries and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Splunk Unauthorized File Creation via Database Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Detection must capture the file system impact of this vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk $SPLUNK_HOME for unexpected file creation or truncation events, particularly in sensitive directories (etc/, var/, bin/). Correlate timing with unauthenticated sidecar requests. Alert on files created by Splunk processes through database endpoints that differ from normal maintenance operations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Detection - Splunk Enterprise
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies active in-the-wild exploitation. Article recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' with CVE substitution. Vulnerability scanner detection is the first line.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for Splunk Enterprise instances missing patches for CVE-2026-20253 (check version < fixed version). suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Anomalous Database Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article describes file operations 'through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—this implies manipulation of the database itself, not just file system.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL logs (if accessible) for unexpected CREATE/DROP/ALTER operations, or suspicious queries originating from the sidecar service layer. Look for batch file-write operations disguised as legitimate database transactions.

suggestion.title: Splunk Critical Function Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability title: 'Missing Authentication for Critical Function.' Detection must flag any access to protected functions without valid authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse Splunk authentication logs and API gateway logs for requests to critical functions (file operations, database modifications, credential management) that return success (HTTP 200/201) without a preceding successful authentication event (login, token validation). Alert on any function that should require auth responding successfully to anonymous requests.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthenticated Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—this is the primary attack surface and requires detection of unauthorized access.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Sidecar Process
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the vulnerability allows attackers to 'create or truncate arbitrary files' through the sidecar endpoint—this is the direct impact mechanism requiring file-system monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Splunk Enterprise hosts, monitor file creation and deletion events originating from or proxied through the PostgreSQL sidecar process (PID/parent chain analysis). Alert on unexpected writes to system directories, config files (/opt/splunk, /etc), or attempts to truncate audit/data logs.

suggestion.title: Internet-Facing Splunk Enterprise Vulnerability Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV classification means 'currently being exploited in the wild'—asset-exposure hunt mandatory to identify internet-facing vulnerable instances before federal due date (2026-06-21).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate vulnerability scanner data (CVE-2026-20253 detections) with network exposure intelligence (shodan, censys, internal port scans). Flag Splunk Enterprise instances with open sidecar service ports accessible from untrusted networks. Prioritize remediation by exposure level and patch status.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass to Critical Splunk Functions
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability title explicitly states 'Missing Authentication for Critical Function'—auth bypass is the core attack vector. Monitor for successful access to protected operations without valid credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Review Splunk audit logs for successful access to file-creation/file-truncation functions from users/IPs with no corresponding authenticated session. Flag attempts to invoke critical sidecar endpoints that bypass token/session validation. Cross-reference firewall logs to detect auth-bypass patterns.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user...through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — baseline detection for missing authentication bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk Enterprise instances for unauthenticated requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints lacking valid auth headers/sessions that return 2xx responses. Correlate with network-facing Splunk assets to identify exposure.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation via Splunk Sidecar Service
