suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for scanning or probing of common PostgreSQL ports (5432) and Splunk sidecar URIs. Correlate failed connection attempts and port-scanning patterns with subsequent successful exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Splunk CVE-2026-20253 Internet Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files' through exposed endpoint. T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) is primary attack vector — canonical asset-exposure hunt must run immediately before federal due date.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner detections for CVE-2026-20253 against Splunk Enterprise instances with egress routes to internet. Alert on any confirmed external accessibility to ports 8089 (mgmt) or 8000 (web).

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthenticated Access
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack surface: 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' exploited without authentication. Direct HTTP/HTTPS requests to this endpoint from untrusted sources indicate exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk instances for HTTP/HTTPS requests to sidecar endpoints (port 5432 or service-specific) from external IPs with missing or invalid auth headers. Baseline internal access patterns and flag external sources.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Write from Splunk Service
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' File-system write operations by splunkd to unexpected directories (outside /opt/splunk/var) indicate successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or modification initiated by splunkd or Splunk-owned processes to /etc, /root, /var/log, or web directories. Establish baseline of legitimate Splunk write paths and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Log Truncation / Evidence Destruction Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article capability: 'truncate arbitrary files' enables attacker to destroy audit logs. Unexplained log-flow discontinuities or sudden log-file size reductions correlate with post-exploitation cover-up.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for gaps in Splunk/application audit logs on CVE-2026-20253 affected instances. Alert when expected log entries stop flowing or log files shrink without corresponding deletion events. Correlate across syslog, Splunk audit logs, and OS audit trails.

suggestion.title: Splunk Service Suspicious Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation file-write capability enables attacker to write malicious scripts or binaries. Unexpected child process spawns from splunkd (bash, curl, wget, etc.) indicate secondary payload execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by splunkd or related Splunk processes with high entropy command lines or unexpected binaries (/bin/bash, /usr/bin/curl, /usr/bin/wget). Baseline legitimate Splunk process spawning behavior.

suggestion.title: Splunk Configuration File Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Arbitrary file-write capability enables persistence or lateral movement via modified configs (app.conf, inputs.conf, outputs.conf). Unauthorized config changes bypass normal change-control workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor integrity of /opt/splunk/etc/ configuration files. Alert on modifications outside maintenance windows with mismatched source process (not splunkd admin utilities) or unusual hash/timestamp deltas.

suggestion.title: Splunk Unauthenticated Endpoint File Operations (CVE-2026-20253)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' No detection UC generated despite explicit attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk audit/access logs for unauthenticated requests to service endpoints or PostgreSQL sidecar paths. Flag file-creation or file-deletion operations initiated without prior authentication session, especially in index/data directories.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation via PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'create or truncate arbitrary files' impact. No impact-phase detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file truncation/deletion operations in Splunk's index, data, or configuration directories when initiated from PostgreSQL sidecar context or unauthenticated source. Correlate with failed or unauthorized authentication attempts.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' as exploitation path. No sidecar-specific reconnaissance or access detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL sidecar service for: (1) connection attempts from non-localhost addresses, (2) unauthenticated session initiation, (3) file I/O operations outside normal Splunk process behavior.

suggestion.title: Splunk CVE-2026-20253 Exposure Hunt (CISA KEV)
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal due-date 2026-06-21 requires immediate fleet inventory and patch status verification. No vulnerability scanner or exposure-hunting UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Splunk Enterprise instances with CVE-2026-20253. Cross-reference with network exposure scans (internet-facing ports 8089, 8000, 9997). Flag all unpatched instances as P0 remediation due 2026-06-21.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthenticated Access to Splunk Critical Functions
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'missing authentication for critical function vulnerability which could allow an unauthenticated user.' Detection must distinguish legitimate sessions from exploitative unauthenticated endpoint hits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk audit logs for API calls to critical endpoints (/services/admin, /services/data) lacking valid session tokens or with null auth headers. Correlate spikes in 401/403 responses to subsequent file-modification events on the system.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Endpoint Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exact attack vector: 'through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This concrete service is the exploit channel and requires targeted monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on connections to Splunk's PostgreSQL sidecar (internal port 5432 or custom endpoint) originating from external networks or non-admin user contexts. Flag DDL/DML statements (CREATE, TRUNCATE, DROP) executed post-connection from unauthenticated sources.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation on Splunk Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Stated outcome: 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' This is the impact and directly observable via filesystem telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unexpected file creation, deletion, or truncation in Splunk directories ($SPLUNK_HOME, config, data, backup) by processes other than splunkd. Correlate with prior PostgreSQL endpoint access or failed authentication attempts within the same timeline.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanner Confirmation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends: 'CVE-2026-20253 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Confirms Splunk instances patched for this specific CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner output for Splunk Enterprise instances reporting CVE-2026-20253 status. Prioritize remediation on externally-facing instances; even patched systems warrant one sweep given patch-lag risk noted in article.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—this is the primary attack vector and requires detection on direct API/endpoint calls lacking authentication headers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk Enterprise instances for unauthenticated HTTP POST/PUT/DELETE requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically internal management ports). Track requests lacking valid session tokens or API keys that attempt file creation, truncation, or arbitrary I/O operations. Correlate with vulnerability scanner alerts for CVE-2026-20253.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Write/Truncation via Splunk Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article core impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—requires behavioral detection for file system activity originating from Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation, truncation, or deletion initiated by Splunk sidecar processes (e.g., postgres, postgresql, sidecar service user) with unusual paths (config directories, data stores). Baseline normal sidecar file operations and flag deviations; correlate with network telemetry showing unauthenticated inbound requests.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Presence
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV entry—'only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild'—basic scanning and patch verification required as SOC baseline detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match CVE-2026-20253 against vulnerability scanner output and asset inventory for all Splunk Enterprise deployments. Flag any systems reporting unpatched or patch-lag status as of federal deadline 2026-06-21. Cross-check patched assertions against running service versions.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Internet-Facing Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets'—requires discovery that Splunk instances are reachable externally, the prerequisite for T1190 exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Splunk Enterprise instances with ingress ACLs permitting unauthenticated external access to management/sidecar ports. Flag as high-risk if running vulnerable versions of CVE-2026-20253. Generate exception report for justification of public-facing Splunk.

suggestion.title: Host-header injection to management routes (CVE-2026-49468 exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'A crafted Host header could therefore make the auth gate evaluate a different route from the one FastAPI dispatches.' This is the exploit mechanism itself—core detection target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to LiteLLM management endpoints (/key/*, /user/*, /team/*, /model/*, /sso/key/generate, etc.) where the Host header contains injection markers (;, .., %20, @, 0x, \\, ?) or otherwise deviates from expected reverse-proxy or application hostnames. Hypothesis: attacker crafts Host to bypass route-matching in auth layer.

suggestion.title: Auth-gate evasion: 401/403 → 200 on protected route within 5m
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated access to protected management routes.' Direct sequence indicating successful bypass: rejection, then acceptance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP 401/403 then 2xx on same management route from same source within 5-minute window. If subsequent request uses different Host header or other attribute, boost confidence to high.

suggestion.title: Post-breach multi-category mgmt enumeration (CVE-2026-49468 discovery)
suggestion.rationale: After bypass succeeds, attacker discovers what resources are available. Article lists distinct management categories: keys, users, teams, models, spend, SSO, ACL—attacker would enumerate across categories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid successful access (2xx) to management endpoints spanning 3+ distinct categories (/key/*, /user/*, /team/*, /model/*, /spend/*, /sso/*) from same source within 10m. Post-exploitation reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated mgmt-route success: 2xx without auth headers
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated access to protected management routes.' Direct outcome: management endpoint replies 2xx to a request lacking any authentication credential.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP 2xx status for protected routes (/key/generate, /user/new, /model/new, /sso/key/generate, /add/allowed_ip) where request contains no Authorization header, no x-litellm-api-key header, and api_key not in query string. High-confidence exploitation success.

suggestion.title: Recon of exposed LiteLLM via /health, /version, /docs from external source
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must discover the service. Article lists these as recon targets. Phrase: 'External recon of exposed LiteLLM proxy.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor non-RFC1918 sources querying multiple LiteLLM recon endpoints (/health, /version, /docs, /openapi.json, /redoc, /routes) in rapid succession. Threshold: 3+ distinct paths or 25+ hits in 1h. Indicator of active service discovery.

suggestion.title: Credential harvesting via /key/list or /user/list post-bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article lists /key/list and /user/list as protected management routes. After bypass, attackers would enumerate and exfiltrate credential material. Logical post-exploitation step not explicitly detailed in hunts above.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 2xx responses to /key/list, /user/list, /team/list, /customer/list from unauthenticated requests, especially when correlated with prior Host-header anomalies or auth-bypass signatures. Indicates credential enumeration and exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Splunk Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated user' to access PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint. Pipeline generated no UC to detect such requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk web interface logs for HTTP requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typical paths: /api/pgsql, /services/pgsql, or similar) originating from unauthenticated sessions or missing Authorization headers. Alert on POST/PUT/DELETE operations that bypass standard auth checks.

suggestion.title: Splunk Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through PostgreSQL sidecar.' No use case addresses detection of file manipulation via the endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unexpected file-system modifications (create, truncate, delete) on Splunk hosts with HTTP request logs showing sidecar-endpoint access. Look for writes to sensitive config, data, or log directories originating from PostgreSQL worker processes triggered by unauthenticated API calls.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Patch Status & Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due 2026-06-21 and notes CISA KEV means active exploitation. Standard asset-exposure hunt is mentioned but pipeline generated no use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all Splunk Enterprise instances for version matching vulnerable range (if known); cross-check against patch date. Alert on any instances still unpatched post 2026-06-21. Combine with network exposure scans to identify internet-facing Splunk web consoles.

suggestion.title: Splunk sidecar Endpoint Discovery & Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Attackers will need to discover and probe the PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint path. No reconnaissance-phase detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web logs for patterns of repeated 404 or 403 responses to potential sidecar paths (/pgsql*, /postgres*, /sidecar, etc.) followed by successful 200/201 responses. Spike in non-standard endpoint requests to Splunk from external IPs.

suggestion.title: Gravity SMTP Plugin Vulnerability Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Gravity SMTP WordPress Plugin' as the attack surface and describes a bug being exploited. Title states 'Hackers Exploit Gravity SMTP WordPress Plugin Bug.' No use case generated despite being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Gravity SMTP plugin endpoints with known CVE parameters, POST requests to admin-ajax.php with Gravity SMTP action parameters, or 404/403 patterns indicating plugin enumeration prior to exploitation.

suggestion.title: API Key Extraction via Gravity SMTP Misconfiguration
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly identifies 'Expose API Keys' as the direct impact. No credential-access or exfiltration use case was generated despite this being the attacker's goal and objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect access to WordPress wp-config.php, plugin configuration files, or database tables containing SMTP credentials. Alert on bulk reads of wp-options or serialized credential objects from Gravity SMTP plugin directories.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized SMTP Service Abuse Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Exposed API keys enable attackers to abuse SMTP service. Article describes 'hackers exploit' (compromise achieved) leading to key exposure, implying follow-on SMTP abuse is the impact driver. No collection/exfiltration use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SMTP authentication with exposed plugin API keys, bulk email sends from WordPress server using exfiltrated credentials, or SMTP relay configuration changes tied to Gravity SMTP plugin compromise.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin Directory Write Access Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Gravity SMTP plugin vulnerability may allow unauthenticated file write or code execution in plugin directory. Title describes exploiting a 'bug' in a plugin. No execution-phase detection generated despite plugin code-injection being typical attack progression.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious file creation or modification under /wp-content/plugins/gravity-smtp/ from web server process (www-data, IUSR). Alert on PHP file uploads or .htaccess modifications within plugin directory tied to HTTP requests.

suggestion.title: Suspicious wp-admin Access via Compromised SMTP Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Exposed SMTP API keys may be associated with admin accounts or provide lateral movement to WordPress admin panel. No privilege escalation or lateral movement detection generated despite credential exposure typically enabling both.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate exposed API key usage in SMTP logs with concurrent wp-admin login attempts or access to /wp-admin/options.php (settings modification). Flag logins from IPs tied to SMTP abuse.

suggestion.title: Gravity SMTP Plugin Configuration Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: API keys exposed. Pipeline must detect when attacker reads plugin config. No data discovery or exfiltration use case generated despite 'expose' being the explicit attack outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for database queries selecting from wp_options where option_name contains 'gravity' or 'smtp', or bulk file reads of /wp-content/plugins/gravity-smtp/settings.json. Detect credential data in outbound DNS, HTTP POST, or email events.

suggestion.title: Single user DELETE spanning unauthorized realms (IDOR confirmation)
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'An authenticated user in ANY realm can delete alarms belonging to OTHER realms.' Pipeline detects realm-switching but should explicitly correlate: did user succeed in deleting from a realm they don't own? Missing the core IDOR signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify users who issue successful DELETE requests (200/204) to alarm endpoints in realms where they have no assigned role or access grant. Cross-reference DELETE request realm against user's authorized realm list from identity/RBAC logs. Rapid deletions across 3+ non-owned realms in <5min window suggest IDOR exploitation.

suggestion.title: Alarm endpoint 400/422 errors preceding successful cross-realm DELETE
suggestion.rationale: Attacker may probe alarm IDs (malformed queries, invalid IDs) before discovering valid ones to delete. Article mentions 'supplying arbitrary alarm IDs' but no UC covers malformed request pattern before success.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track sequences where a user issues 3+ requests to DELETE /api/*/alarm with HTTP 400/422 (bad request, validation error), then 1+ DELETE with 200/204 on different realm in same session. Pattern suggests ID enumeration across realm boundaries.

suggestion.title: OpenRemote DELETE request with user-controlled realm parameter tampering
suggestion.rationale: IDOR exploited by 'supplying arbitrary alarm IDs' — but also implicitly by tampering with realm in URL path. No UC explicitly covers detecting modified/anomalous realm values in DELETE requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DELETE requests where the realm in the URL path does not match the authenticated user's default/assigned realm and has no prior history with that user. Combine with 200/204 success response to indicate unauthorized cross-realm access.

suggestion.title: BaseFileComponent tar archive extraction with symlink path traversal
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'BaseFileComponent-based nodes arbitrary file read' and mentions 'tar extraction creates symlinks to sensitive paths'. UC_4_2 exists but is overly broad (any /etc/ file creation by Python). Should specifically detect symlink escape in archive unpacking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for symlink creation (not just file creation) during tar/archive extraction by Python-based Langflow processes. Symlinks should resolve outside their parent directory (e.g., /tmp/unpack/../../etc/passwd symlinks). Alert on symlink-to-sensitive-path creation within 5 seconds of tar invocation.

suggestion.title: Secret key material exfiltration post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: UC_4_3 discusses 'secret_key theft' enabling JWT forgery, but no UC captures the actual theft of the key material itself. Article states the exploit leads to 'arbitrary file read' which would include Django/Flask secret keys.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect read operations on Langflow secret key files (settings.py, .env files, config directories) by Python interpreter processes after BaseFileComponent exploitation attempts. Correlate with subsequent JWT signing operations within 1 hour.

suggestion.title: Docling/Unstructured/Video component initialization with malicious payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 'Docling (DoclingInlineComponent)', 'Docling Serve (DoclingRemoteComponent)', 'NVIDIA Retriever (NvidiaIngestComponent)', 'Video File (VideoFileComponent)', and 'Unstructured API (UnstructuredComponent)' as vulnerable, but pipeline produces no component-specific UCs. No detection for malicious DOCX/video/API payloads triggering BaseFileComponent vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Langflow component initialization (DoclingInlineComponent.run, UnstructuredComponent.run, VideoFileComponent.run) with file paths containing path traversal sequences (../, %2e%2e, etc). Correlate with subsequent Python subprocess spawning or file access to /etc, /.ssh, /.aws.

suggestion.title: T1081 credential harvesting from Langflow config/settings
suggestion.rationale: Article describes secret_key and JWT token theft but T1081 (Credentials in Files) is not mapped in MITRE techniques list despite being central to the attack—the exploit reads credentials from Langflow's settings/configuration files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file read operations on Django/Langflow configuration files (settings.py, .env, config.json, secrets.json) by non-administrative processes or from unexpected calling contexts (e.g., from web-accessible paths).

suggestion.title: Python eval/exec gadget chains in Langflow Python Interpreter node
suggestion.rationale: UC_4_4 captures subprocess spawning but misses inline code execution (eval/exec). Article mentions 'T1059.006 — Command and Scripting Interpreter: Python' as technique, implying Python eval chains. The 'Python Interpreter node RCE' likely chains through eval not just subprocess.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Langflow Python Interpreter node execution for eval(), exec(), compile() calls with unsanitized input from previous nodes. Look for base64-encoded payloads passed to eval or dynamic code generation patterns.

suggestion.title: Craft CMS actionResourceJs response with JavaScript payload injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Arbitrary JavaScript Injection' but no UC detects whether the response actually contains injected script payloads. 'Arbitrary JavaScript Injection via Host Header Poisoning' is the core attack, yet detection focus is only on the request side.
log_sources: Web proxy logs with response body inspection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Craft CMS `/actions/app/resource-js` responses contain injected JavaScript (script tags, dynamic var assignments with attacker domain, Guzzle client initialization to non-org domain). Look for HTTP response bodies from this endpoint containing script-injection patterns or base64-encoded payloads.

suggestion.title: SSRF exfiltration: outbound connection within 10s of resource-js request to same attacker domain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'forcing the application's... to fetched from attacker-hosted servers' but UC_6_2 only finds outbound connections generically. No detection correlates the poisoned request with the actual SSRF fetch. This closes the c2 visibility gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify requests to `/actions/app/resource-js` with suspicious Host headers, then correlate within 10 seconds with outbound HTTP/HTTPS from the web application to non-org destinations. Match source IP or web process. High fidelity if the attacker domain matches a known C2 sink.

suggestion.title: Admin privilege escalation via session-riding after resource-js exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Session-Riding RCE chain end' but no UC detects privilege escalation or session abuse. UC_6_3 finds plugin install but not the *privilege abuse* aspect. Need to detect admin actions (install, config change, user creation) from low-privilege contexts that correlate with prior resource-js requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Admin plugin-install or config-change POST requests from source IP that (a) previously accessed `/actions/app/resource-js` and (b) is not in the admin IP allowlist or does not match historical admin access patterns. Indicates session hijacking or privilege abuse.

suggestion.title: Craft CMS instance discovery and vulnerability enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article does not mention pre-exploitation reconnaissance, but attackers typically scan for Craft CMS instances before attempting exploitation. Should detect `/actions/app/resource-js` requests with HEAD/GET/OPTIONS probing from external IP ranges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inbound HTTP requests to `/actions/app/resource-js` with HEAD, OPTIONS, or GET from external IP ranges (non-org) without corresponding admin sessions. Bulk scanning patterns (multiple endpoints hit from same src IP in <1 min) raise confidence.

suggestion.title: Gravity SMTP REST API Reconnaissance Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly cites /wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data?page=gravitysmtp-settings as the indicator of compromise. 17M+ blocked attempts and June 7 spike prove active mass exploitation. This is the attack vector; pipeline extracted zero IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server access logs for GET requests to /wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data with query parameter page=gravitysmtp-settings. Alert on spikes (>100 requests/min or >3σ deviation from baseline). Endpoint returns System Report JSON containing API keys, OAuth tokens, DB config, and installed plugin inventory—sensitive even if endpoint access is denied.

suggestion.title: Email Service Credential Exfiltration via Gravity SMTP Leak
suggestion.rationale: Article states disclosed credentials 'for Amazon SES, Google, Mailjet, Resend, and Zoho' allow attackers to 'abuse the site's connected email services' and 'impersonate the victim to third parties.' Pipeline missed credential-usage detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate email service API logs (SES, Google Workspace, Mailjet, Resend, Zoho) for anomalous access using exposed credentials: unusual originating IPs, geographies, API call patterns, or bulk email-send operations. If Gravity SMTP API key leaked, flag any API calls 24–72 hours post-compromise.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin & Theme Enumeration via REST API
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies endpoint returns 'WordPress configuration details, including installed plugins, themes, and software versions.' This reconnaissance data 'significantly lowers the effort required to plan further attacks.' Pipeline missed enumeration detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated unauthenticated requests to /wp-json/gravitysmtp/* or /wp-json/wp/v2/plugins endpoints from same source. Correlate with requests to known-vulnerable plugin endpoints (e.g., /wp-json/breeze-cache/) if library versions in plugin list match historical CVE fingerprints.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Sensitive Data Exfiltration via Misconfigured REST Permission Callback
suggestion.rationale: Article root-causes the flaw to 'permission_callback' always returning 'true,' exposing 'API keys, secrets, and OAuth tokens' and 'Database configuration details, including server version and table names' without authentication. Pipeline missed permission-bypass detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP 200 responses from /wp-json/* endpoints that contain secret/token/password_reset fields to unauthenticated requests (no Authorization header or expired session). Inspect response bodies for patterns: 'secret', 'api_key', 'oauth_token', 'db_version', 'table_' to detect information disclosure.

suggestion.title: Volumetric Exploitation Spike Detection for CVE-2026-4020
suggestion.rationale: Article reports concrete timeline: exploitation spike June 7 (4M requests blocked in one day), sustained activity thereafter. Wordfence tracked daily metrics. Pipeline missed volumetric detection tied to this CVE's known exploitation window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create rolling 24-hour baseline for requests to /wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data. Alert if requests exceed baseline by >200% or spike >500 requests/hour. Correlate request sources across datacenter IP ranges and residential proxy services; June 7–30, 2026 exploitation window suggests automated mass scanning.

suggestion.title: Database Reconnaissance via Gravity SMTP System Report Disclosure
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically mentions 'Database configuration details, including server version and table names' returned by REST endpoint. This is OSINT-level reconnaissance enabling SQL injection or direct database attacks. Pipeline missed database-leakage detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for responses from /wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data containing database version strings (e.g., 'MariaDB 10.5.15', 'MySQL 5.7.32'), WordPress table names (wp_posts, wp_users, wp_options), or connection strings. Flag if endpoint access precedes failed database authentication attempts or SQL injection probes.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — requires detection of unauthorized endpoint access that should require authentication
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/HTTPS requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint paths (inspect Splunk config for exact URI patterns) when no authenticated session exists or from unexpected source IPs. Baseline internal-only traffic; flag any external origin hits.

suggestion.title: File Creation or Truncation via PostgreSQL Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article attack outcome: 'create or truncate arbitrary files' — requires detection of file operations directly attributed to sidecar process or triggered by sidecar-endpoint access
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate PostgreSQL sidecar process file-write operations with requests to vulnerable endpoint. Flag truncations of config, binary, or data files. Alert on file creation in unexpected paths (e.g., /etc, user homes, temp with persistence patterns).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Asset Exposure – Splunk Enterprise Patch Lag
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal due-date 2026-06-21 — article implies all Splunk Enterprise versions vulnerable until patched; standard asset-exposure hunt mandatory
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Splunk Enterprise instances. Cross-reference scan results for CVE-2026-20253. Flag instances with patch missing or applied after 2026-06-21. Verify all exposed instances (internet-facing, DMZ) for baseline connectivity to PostgreSQL sidecar ports from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Anomalous PostgreSQL Sidecar Port Access Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' exploitation — requires baseline-deviation detection on expected access behavior; unauthenticated access suggests endpoint should be access-restricted by default
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for legitimate Splunk-to-sidecar traffic (internal only, expected protocols). Alert on endpoint access from external IPs, non-Splunk processes, or over unusual ports/protocols. Correlate with unauthenticated session indicators.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Asset Exposure Hunt (CISA KEV)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mandates: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [`/_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`]' and cites federal patch due-date 2026-06-21. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this directive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Splunk Enterprise instances in the fleet. Cross-reference against vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20253. Flag any instance marked vulnerable and reachable from untrusted networks (internet-facing). Priority: any unpatched instance past the 2026-06-21 federal due-date is assumed compromised until proven otherwise.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Requests to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the exploitation path: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the precise attack surface and should be monitored.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query process logs for Splunk version strings (splunkd processes); cross-reference against known vulnerable version ranges for CVE-2026-20253. Correlate with network exposure data (ports 8000, 8089, 8191 visible to external scanners or WAF logs). Flag instances matching both criteria for immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: Anomalous PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Invocation Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies exploitation through 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'; unexpected activation or unusual request patterns to internal service ports indicate exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for requests to internal sidecar endpoints in Splunk audit/access logs (normally admin-only, low-volume, authenticated). Alert on anomalous spikes, requests from previously-unseen external IPs, or requests with HTTP 2xx responses when auth should have been required.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Direct evidence of auth-bypass exploitation path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar ports for HTTP POST/GET requests lacking authentication headers or valid session tokens. Alert on any non-error response (200, 201, 204) to sidecar endpoints from untrusted networks. Establish baseline of legitimate sidecar callers (internal Splunk processes) and flag external sources.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation via Splunk Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers can 'truncate arbitrary files' via the sidecar endpoint. Impact-layer detection for confirmed exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file truncate operations (ftruncate, truncate syscalls) initiated by Splunk service processes or from network context of sidecar listeners. Flag truncations of critical files (configs, logs, binaries). Correlate with preceding sidecar access logs.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation via Splunk Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article states capability to 'create...arbitrary files' through sidecar. Complements truncation detection; identifies both write and destruction paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected file creation from Splunk service processes in non-standard directories (e.g., /root, /etc, /var). Combine with network context: file creation correlating to recent sidecar endpoint access from unauthenticated sources. Establish whitelist of expected Splunk file-creation locations.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Exposed Port Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability in 'public-facing application' (KEV implies exposure). Asset-exposure hunt for sidecar listening on unexpected interfaces/networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run periodic port scans and compare against baseline. Splunk sidecar typically runs on non-standard high ports (5432-adjacent or 9000+ range depending on config). Alert if sidecar port becomes reachable from internet-routable addresses or untrusted subnets. Cross-reference with inventory: which Splunk instances have patches for CVE-2026-20253?

suggestion.title: Splunk Authentication Bypass Indicator: Sidecar Calls Without Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'missing authentication'—core of this CVE. Detect calls to sidecar endpoints in absence of auth tokens, session IDs, or API keys.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse Splunk and sidecar service logs for API/endpoint calls with empty or missing Authorization headers. Baseline legitimate service-to-service calls (which may intentionally omit creds in internal networks). Flag external-origin requests missing credentials. Compare request pattern to known-good traffic from patchlevels ≥ [vendor fix version].

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanner Match + Exploit Attempt Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article classifies as CISA KEV: 'currently being exploited.' Combine vulnerability scanner hits with behavioral signals to confirm active exploitation vs. false alarm.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert with elevated severity when vulnerability scanner confirms Splunk Enterprise vulnerability to CVE-2026-20253 AND concurrent access logs show sidecar endpoint queries from suspicious IPs. Use threat intel for known exploit PoC traffic patterns. Correlate scanner date with access log timestamps to identify lag between exposure discovery and exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious POST Requests to Joomla JCE Component
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'actively exploited Joomla JCE flaw'—exploit delivery almost always occurs via HTTP POST to /index.php?option=com_jce or similar. Pipeline missed web-based initial-access detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST requests containing 'com_jce' or 'jce' in URI, especially with suspicious parameters, base64-encoded payloads, or PHP function names (eval, system, exec, passthru) in request body. Flag requests from non-administrative IPs to known JCE exploitation endpoints.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution via Unexpected eval() or system() Calls
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names 'PHP Code Execution' as impact. Without detection for in-process execution of dangerous PHP functions post-exploitation, impact is invisible. Pipeline generated zero execution-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP processes spawning child processes (bash, cmd, powershell) or executing system commands. Monitor PHP error logs for eval() attempts. Flag php.exe/php-fpm with unusual arguments or working directories outside expected application paths.

suggestion.title: File Upload or Write to Web-Accessible Directory During JCE Request
suggestion.rationale: Successful JCE exploitation typically results in webshell or file placement; article says 'actively exploited,' implying post-exploitation file artifacts. No use case for file-system write detection during web activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP requests to JCE endpoints with subsequent file creation/modification in /components/com_jce/, /tmp/, /var/www/html, or other web-root subdirectories. Flag PHP file writes with timestamps within seconds of malicious POST requests.

suggestion.title: Joomla Vulnerable Component Access Pattern (JCE Version / Feature Abuse)
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'JCE flaw'—should trigger detection for abnormal access patterns to known vulnerable endpoints or parameters. Pipeline did not surface component-level indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for requests to Joomla administration or media management endpoints (/administrator/index.php, /media/, /images/) combined with JCE parameter manipulation (media=..., task=...). Detect requests with incomplete or malformed JCE parameters typical of CVE scanning/exploitation.

suggestion.title: High-Volume or Automated Exploitation Attempts Against Joomla
suggestion.rationale: CISA warning of 'actively exploited' flaw implies widespread scanning/attack activity. Pipeline should flag reconnaissance or mass-exploitation patterns even without specific CVE details.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate requests from single source IP targeting multiple /index.php?option=com_jce variants or common Joomla paths (/administrator, /components) in short timeframe (< 60s). Flag source IPs with > 5 JCE-related requests or error patterns (404→200→500 sequences).

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Enterprise Vulnerable Instances
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with active exploitation and federal due date 2026-06-21. Article identifies 'unauthenticated user' exploitation path. No asset-exposure hunt was generated despite being foundational for all downstream detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan enterprise for Splunk Enterprise instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253. Cross-reference with asset inventory and network boundary data to identify internet-exposed deployments. Flag any instance accessible from untrusted segments without authentication enforcement.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthenticated Access to Splunk Critical Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly specifies 'unauthenticated user' access to endpoints. No detection rule was generated for missing/bypassed authentication on Splunk admin functions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/HTTPS requests to Splunk admin endpoints (/admin, /etc, /services/configs) from untrusted sources that lack valid authentication tokens or return 200 without session validation. Monitor for unauthenticated POST/PUT attempts to critical paths.

suggestion.title: Detect PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Endpoint Access Without Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names attack surface: 'through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' No UC monitors for direct access to this boundary condition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound connections to Splunk's PostgreSQL sidecar (identify port/interface from asset inventory). Alert on connections lacking proper Splunk session forwarding or authenticated trust. Flag any successful unauthenticated access attempts.

suggestion.title: Detect Arbitrary File Creation and Truncation via Splunk Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes post-compromise activity: 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' This is the attacker's impact goal (data destruction) but no UC was generated to detect it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk audit logs and filesystem logs for file creation, deletion, or truncation originating from unauthenticated sources or sidecar endpoints. Alert on unexpected modifications to sensitive paths (/etc, /opt/splunk, /var). Correlate with preceding endpoint access anomalies.

suggestion.title: Detect Code Execution via Arbitrary File Write to Application Directories
suggestion.rationale: File-write primitives often enable RCE. Article's 'create arbitrary files' could precede execution if written to Splunk app directories or system hooks. No UC captures T1059 execution path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file writes to Splunk application directories (/opt/splunk/etc/apps, /opt/splunk/bin) via vulnerable endpoint. Inspect file content for script signatures (.sh, .py). Correlate with Splunk process spawning or abnormal command execution.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthenticated Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the direct attack vector and should trigger detection on any access to that service without valid authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar service (typically port 5432 or internal endpoint) for connection attempts lacking valid authentication credentials. Alert on any unauthenticated queries or connection strings from external/untrusted sources. Baseline known-good sidecar consumers and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Splunk Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via PostgreSQL
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the vulnerability enables attackers to 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Detection must monitor for file operations (CREATE, TRUNCATE, DROP) originating from the sidecar process or routed through it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on CREATE/TRUNCATE/DROP file operations in PostgreSQL logs that either (a) are not from expected maintenance jobs, (b) target sensitive Splunk configuration or data files, or (c) originate from connections established without authentication. Look for calls to pg_file_* functions or similar dangerous PostgreSQL file I/O.

suggestion.title: Splunk Missing Authentication Bypass on Critical Functions
suggestion.rationale: CVE title explicitly states 'Missing Authentication for Critical Function.' Any request to Splunk critical endpoints (likely including the sidecar) that bypasses authentication is the direct exploit pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any HTTP requests to Splunk critical function endpoints (enumerate from documentation) that lack valid session tokens, API keys, or authentication headers. Splunk should require authentication; requests bypassing this are the vulnerability exploit.

suggestion.title: Exposed Splunk Instance Asset Inventory with Patch Status Check
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry means active exploitation is occurring. Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and audit pressure. Enterprise must identify all Splunk instances exposed and cross-check patch dates against federal due-date 2026-06-21.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset hunt: enumerate all Splunk Enterprise instances across your fleet via CMDB, network scanning, or vulnerability scanner. For each, check (a) version against CVE-2026-20253 advisory, (b) last patch date, (c) network exposure (internal vs. internet-facing). Instances not patched by 2026-06-21 should be escalated as critical.

suggestion.title: Rclone process spawning shell or scripting engine (exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly defines this detection (exploit phase, HIGH confidence) to catch post-exploitation command execution when inline remote config triggers initialization code. Pipeline failed to extract despite structured Splunk and Defender KQL rules provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes (shell, scripting engines, curl, wget, LOLBins, mshta, wscript) spawned from rclone parent process. Filter for non-system accounts to reduce false positives from legitimate rclone automation.

suggestion.title: HTTP requests to rclone RC endpoint with inline-remote configuration pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article defines detection for delivery/initial access phase (HIGH confidence). Attack vector: unauthenticated GET/HEAD to /:remote:path patterns with inline config syntax. Pipeline failed to extract despite this being the direct exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GET/HEAD requests to port 5572 with URL patterns: brackets+colons like [local:...] OR parameters exec=/command=. High baseline risk given unauthenticated exposure. Pair Defender endpoint signals with WAF/web gateway logs since endpoint visibility is limited to connection-level.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable rclone version (1.46.0 - 1.74.2) deployed on managed endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly provides inventory detection (HIGH confidence) to identify at-risk assets. Version range clearly defined: 1.46.0–1.74.2 vulnerable; >=1.55.0 enables RCE, <1.55.0 file-read-only. Foundational for patch prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for rclone software with major=1, minor in [46..73], or (minor=74 AND patch<3). Bifurcate RCE-capable (>=1.55.0) from file-read-only versions for patch planning.

suggestion.title: Rclone RCD listener bound to non-localhost without HTTP authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article provides configuration-based detection (HIGH confidence) to flag vulnerable standing. Detects both explicit non-loopback binding via --rc-addr AND absence of authentication flags. Pipeline failed to extract despite structured rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rclone processes with --rc-serve but missing --rc-user, --rc-pass, or --rc-htpasswd. Flag if --rc-addr absent (vulnerable default) OR explicitly non-loopback. High-confidence misconfiguration indicator.

suggestion.title: HTTP authentication bypass attempt on rclone RC endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation via 'inline remote instantiation' that circumvents CVE-2026-41179 auth fix. Missing detection for HTTP request sequences where initial 401 response is followed by retry with modified parameters, indicating auth-layer bypass attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GET/HEAD to /:remote:path → 401/403 → GET with modified inline-remote parameters (different config) → 200 response. Sequence indicates attacker adapted payload to bypass authentication check.

suggestion.title: Network reconnaissance of rclone RC listener (port 5572 probing)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation beginning with unauthenticated requests, implying prior service discovery. Missing detection for attackers probing port 5572 to enumerate rclone RC service availability before exploitation attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network connections to TCP 5572 from unexpected external sources. Baseline legitimate RC client access, then alert on: rapid sequential probes (horizontal scanning), auth failures before successful exploitation, or connections from known scanning tool IPs.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—direct indicator of initial access vector. Pipeline missed endpoint-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk Enterprise hosts for unauthenticated HTTP/TCP access to PostgreSQL sidecar ports (typically 5432 or proxied variants). Flag successful connections from unexpected sources or without valid Splunk auth tokens. Baseline: who legitimately accesses this service.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Write/Truncation via Splunk Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies capability to 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—exploitation would manifest in filesystem operations. Pipeline generated no execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or truncation events originating from Splunk Enterprise sidecar service processes (splunk-postgresql or sidecar wrapper), especially to unexpected directories (/etc, system paths, application roots). Correlate with network connections to sidecar service from external sources.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'asset-exposure hunt' with template substitution for CVE detection. Pipeline failed to generate vulnerability-scanner-driven detection despite explicit instruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner assets for Splunk Enterprise instances flagged with CVE-2026-20253. Cross-correlate with network exposure (public-facing, internet-routable). Prioritize federal agency scan by patch due date 2026-06-21.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass to File Manipulation Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'missing authentication for critical function'—core weakness is auth-bypass enabling subsequent file ops. Pipeline skipped credential-access / defense-evasion framing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to Splunk sidecar endpoints that lack authentication headers or contain null/empty auth tokens, followed within seconds by file system modification events on the Splunk host. Alert on anomalous privilege escalation in service context.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin Vulnerability Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'Hackers Exploit Gravity SMTP WordPress Plugin Bug'—clear initial-access / exploitation event. Pipeline produced zero IOCs and zero kill-chain reconstruction, missing T1190 entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to /wp-content/plugins/gravity-smtp/ endpoints for signatures matching known CVEs in Gravity SMTP (version disclosure, unauthenticated config access, path traversal patterns). Alert if requests precede plugin update events on the same host.

suggestion.title: SMTP API Credential Exposure in Plugin Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Expose API Keys'—credential-access is the core threat. Pipeline failed to map T1552.001 or generate detections for credential disclosure via plugin settings/database.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized read access to Gravity SMTP configuration (gravity_smtp_settings, plugin options table rows). Alert on exfiltration of base64-encoded or plaintext SMTP API keys. Flag if API credentials are logged, cached, or transmitted over unencrypted channels.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Email Relay via Compromised API Keys
suggestion.rationale: Exposing SMTP API keys enables attackers to abuse email relay for C2, phishing, spam—post-exploitation impact the pipeline completely missed despite this being the direct consequence of the credential exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate SMTP API key compromise timestamp with anomalous mail relay patterns: sudden spike in email volume from WordPress instance, emails sent to attacker-controlled domains, SMTP authentication from unexpected IPs using recovered credentials.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Gravity SMTP Plugin Installation Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline did not extract plugin name, version ranges, or CVE identifier needed for asset inventory control. Article headline 'Gravity SMTP WordPress Plugin' should trigger version-specific detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate installed WordPress plugins via wp_options table, plugin directory scan, or WP-CLI enumeration. Extract gravity-smtp version. Alert on presence of versions ≤ [CVE-affected range]. Compare plugin versions against advisory baseline.

suggestion.title: First successful cross-realm alarm DELETE by authenticated user
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An authenticated user in any realm can delete alarms belonging to other realms'—the *first* successful cross-realm delete is the smoking gun of exploitation. Pipeline missed baseline detection for initial breach of realm boundary.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect a DELETE request to /api/{realm}/alarm that succeeds (200/204) where the authenticated user's home_realm does not match the target realm being queried. This requires joining Web logs with OpenRemote user-realm mappings to establish the user's authority boundary, then flagging cross-boundary DELETE operations.

suggestion.title: Alarm deletion from realm user has no membership in
suggestion.rationale: Core IDOR: 'the bulk removeAlarms() method only verifies that the caller's own realm is active and accessible, but never checks whether the targeted alarms belong to that realm.' Need correlation of deleted alarm IDs against realm ACLs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OpenRemote application logs for DELETE operations on alarm entities where the requesting user's realm authorization does not include the alarm's parent realm. Requires parsing alarm metadata (realm field) from logs and cross-referencing against user_realm membership tables.

suggestion.title: Repeated alarm ID enumeration within single HTTP session
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must enumerate or guess valid alarm IDs across other realms. Article describes 'supplying arbitrary alarm IDs'—detection should catch patterns of rapid, sequential ID probing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sessions that attempt DELETEs on 5+ distinct alarm IDs within a single realm within 2 minutes, where fewer than 2 actually exist (indicated by 404 or error response patterns in OpenRemote). This signals ID enumeration.

suggestion.title: IDOR privilege escalation: non-admin user deleting alarms outside base realm
suggestion.rationale: The IDOR grants delete capability beyond the user's authorized realm—this is privilege escalation via a broken authorization check. Pipeline assigned T1087 but missed T1548 (Abuse Elevation Control).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DELETE operations from users with base role != admin on alarms in realms where that user has no explicit membership or grant. Indicator of IDOR abuse escalating implicit privileges.

suggestion.title: Bulk alarm deletion after failed authorization attempts in other realm
suggestion.rationale: Attacker may probe /api/realm-X/alarm with failed auth, then if X's alarm DELETE endpoint is vulnerable, escalate to successful deletion. Combines UC_3_2 signal with successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In a 15-minute window, flag patterns where the same user generates 2+ 401/403 errors on DELETE /api/realm-X/alarm, followed by 3+ 200/204 responses to DELETE /api/realm-Y/alarm (where Y != user's home realm). Indicates probe-then-exploit against cross-realm IDOR.

suggestion.title: Explicit cosign verification failure followed by image pull success
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'could serve a correctly signed image for verification, then swap it with malicious content between verification and pull'—detection must catch explicit cosign API failures (wrong signature) that are ignored. Pipeline UC_7_3 is too vague.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Crossplane reconciliation logs for cosign verify commands that report verification failures or invalid signatures, immediately followed by successful image pulls of those same packages. TOCTOU assumes verification pass is recorded but pull pulls different content; catch where verification is attempted, fails or is bypassed, yet the package is still pulled and installed.

suggestion.title: ImageConfig verification disabled between package request and installation
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates attacker could modify ImageConfig to disable verification. Pipeline detects removal but misses the attack sequence: removal happens specifically when a mutable-tag package is pending installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate K8s API events: detect when an ImageConfig verification policy is deleted or modified to remove cosign checks, and within 120 seconds, a Provider/Configuration using a mutable tag is created/updated in the same namespace. This captures the defender-evasion phase of the attack.

suggestion.title: OCI registry credentials or permissions used from anomalous sources during tag overwrite
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on malicious registry serving different content per request. Pipeline UC_7_4 detects timing correlation but doesn't flag anomalous source identity. Detect when ECR PutImage/BatchPutImage originates from IP/principal not normally seen pushing to that repository.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build baseline of which IAM principals and source IPs push to Crossplane provider/configuration repositories. Alert when tag overwrites occur from anomalous principals or IPs, especially if they occur within seconds of Crossplane reconciliation events.

suggestion.title: Crossplane package reconciliation loop with repeated digest mismatches
suggestion.rationale: When TOCTOU exploit succeeds, Crossplane reconciler would pull mismatched content, fail validation, and retry. Pipeline doesn't detect the reconciliation failure pattern that indicates successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Crossplane Provider/Configuration reconciliation status for repeated failures due to digest mismatches (pull succeeds but content hash doesn't match expected). Cluster failures with mutable-tag packages getting pulled, failing validation, then re-pulled with different content indicates TOCTOU window exploitation.

suggestion.title: Rapid consecutive image pulls of same mutable tag with varying digests
suggestion.rationale: TOCTOU exploit involves pulling same tag twice in quick succession but getting different content. Pipeline UC_7_3 attempts this but with weak regex. Need explicit detection: same mutable tag, multiple pulls, multiple digests in kubelet/container logs within 30-60 second window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract image pull events from kubelet logs for mutable-tag references (no @sha256 digest). Group by tag, look for 2+ pulls of the same tag within 60 seconds from the same Crossplane pod. If different manifests/digests are pulled, flag as likely TOCTOU exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Gravity SMTP REST endpoint access attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Threat actors are exploiting an unauthenticated information disclosure vulnerability' with specific endpoint 'requests to '/wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data' found in web server access logs, particularly those including the '?page=gravitysmtp-settings' query parameter'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GET requests to /wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data with query parameter ?page=gravitysmtp-settings and HTTP 200 response, especially unauthenticated requests. Baseline: exploit spike was 4 million attempts on June 7 alone.

suggestion.title: Successful Gravity SMTP system report exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allowed unauthenticated GET requests to receive a comprehensive JSON "System Report"' containing 'API keys, secrets, and OAuth tokens for configured email integrations, credentials for third-party email services, WordPress configuration details, server and PHP environment information, database configuration details'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP responses from /wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data with large response body (200+ bytes) containing JSON fields referencing 'key', 'secret', 'token', 'password', or 'credential'. Response content should include AWS SES, Google, Mailjet, Resend, or Zoho service identifiers.

suggestion.title: Gravity SMTP vulnerable plugin version installed
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'affects all versions of the plugin from 2.1.4 and older' and 'has been addressed in version 2.1.5, released on March 17'. Active on 100,000 sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installation or continued presence of Gravity SMTP plugin versions ≤2.1.4 via WordPress REST API query /wp-json/plugins endpoint, or via web server logs showing activation, or via file system scanning. Flag if version < 2.1.5 and exploitation attempts are visible in access logs.

suggestion.title: Email service credential abuse via stolen Gravity SMTP credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exposure of live third-party API credentials means an attacker could abuse the site's connected email services, while...This allows an attacker to impersonate the victim to third parties'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AWS SES, Google Workspace, Mailjet, Resend, and Zoho API logs for access patterns anomalous to the WordPress site's known behavior: unusual IP addresses, unexpected geographic origin, API key first-use, bulk email sending, credential creation, or account modifications.

suggestion.title: WordPress reconnaissance via Gravity SMTP information disclosure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'detailed system report significantly lowers the effort required to plan further attacks' and exposes 'installed plugins, themes, and software versions, server and PHP environment information, database...server version and table names'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful Gravity SMTP endpoint responses (200 status with JSON system report) with subsequent exploit attempts against the enumerated plugins, themes, or server software within 24-72 hours. Flag if the same source IP exploits the SMTP endpoint then targets other known vulnerabilities matching the disclosed versions.

suggestion.title: Mass Gravity SMTP exploitation campaign detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Wordfence firewall has blocked more than 17 million attempts against protected customers' and 'Exploitation activity spiked on June 7, with 4 million requests being blocked that day'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sustained spike in requests to /wp-json/gravitysmtp endpoints from multiple source IPs (distributed scanning) or single IP with high request rate (4M+ per day). Baseline: June 7 2026 saw 4M blocked attempts globally. Tuning: filter to site's normal traffic volume + 200%.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthenticated Access Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — the core attack path. Pipeline generated no detection use case for this explicit exploitation technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/network requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint (port 5432 or service proxy) that successfully execute file operations (POST/PUT with truncate/create payloads) without preceding authentication challenge or valid auth token. Correlate timing with known CVE-2026-20253 exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation Impact on Splunk Backend
suggestion.rationale: Attack outcome stated as 'create or truncate arbitrary files' — represents destructive impact phase (T1485/T1561). Pipeline missed this impact detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk Enterprise backend processes (uid=splunk) for unexpected file truncation (size→0) or creation in critical directories ($SPLUNK_HOME/etc, /var/log, database paths). Flag files modified without corresponding administrative audit entries or configuration deployment events.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Asset Exposure and Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires fleet asset-exposure hunting. Article specifies federal patch due-date 2026-06-21 and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline output contains zero asset-inventory or scanning-based use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all vulnerability scans for Splunk Enterprise instances matching pre-2026-06-21 patch dates or affected versions. Cross-reference CMDB for network exposure (internet-facing vs. internal-only). Generate compliance report for federal agencies against 2026-06-21 remediation deadline.

suggestion.title: REST API Missing-Authentication Detection on Critical Functions
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause explicitly 'missing authentication for critical function.' Pipeline did not generate probing/enumeration detection for unauthenticated API access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Splunk REST API calls that should require authentication. Alert when critical endpoints (/services/admin/*, /services/data/*, /services/saved/searches) are accessed without X-Auth-Token or session cookie, or return successful responses (200/201) where 401 Unauthorized is expected. Correlate unauthenticated file-operation calls (POST with `truncate=1` or `create=true` parameters).

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Hunt – Splunk Enterprise Internet-Accessible Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'any sensible enterprise SOC' should conduct standard asset-exposure hunts, and explicitly recommends this approach as the primary detection method. Vulnerability affects Splunk Enterprise; federal patch due date is 2026-06-21.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory and scan all internet-accessible Splunk Enterprise instances. Cross-reference against known-vulnerable versions for CVE-2026-20253. Flag assets where patch is not yet deployed or where patch deployment date exceeds federal mandate (2026-06-21). Correlate with authentication logs to establish baseline of legitimate access patterns.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Endpoint Unauthorized Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' The unprotected endpoint is the direct attack surface; monitoring unexpected access to this internal service is a primary detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected network connections or inter-process communication targeting Splunk's PostgreSQL sidecar service. Flag requests to the sidecar endpoint that are not from expected Splunk internal processes or that bypass authentication mechanisms. Baseline normal sidecar traffic and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Creation/Truncation by Splunk Processes
