suggestion.rationale: Title specifies outcome: 'PHP Code Execution.' Pipeline should detect exec spawned by PHP interpreter or web server process. Core detection for post-exploitation validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child process creation from php.exe, php-cgi.exe, or web server processes (apache2, nginx, w3wp.exe) executing system commands (cmd.exe, /bin/bash, powershell.exe) with arguments indicating reverse shells, data exfil, or reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence via JCE File Upload
suggestion.rationale: JCE RCE flaw enables arbitrary file write to web-accessible directories. Pipeline should detect executable file creation post-exploitation for persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla installation directories for creation of .php, .php5, .phtml files with timestamps correlating to exploit activity, especially in /media/, /plugins/, or /components/ paths with suspicious content (obfuscated code, base64 payloads, eval calls).

suggestion.title: CVE-Specific Vulnerability Scanning Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article references active exploitation but pipeline extracted no CVE ID or version indicators. Vulnerability scanners and PoC tools have known signatures for this flaw.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect version-discovery probes and vulnerability scanner requests targeting Joomla JCE plugin endpoints (e.g., requests to known-vulnerable plugin manifest or version disclosure endpoints), and PoC script behaviors (multi-stage payloads, specific parameter fuzzing patterns).

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Unauthenticated Critical-Function Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline missed the initial-access detection pattern entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Splunk Enterprise endpoints (especially /_sidecar/* or PostgreSQL-sidecar-related paths) that succeed (HTTP 200/201) without prior authentication token/session context. Flag requests originating from untrusted networks reaching default Splunk ports (8000, 8089).

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'could allow an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files' — this is the impact phase. Pipeline failed to suggest impact-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation, modification, or deletion operations initiated by Splunk sidecar child processes (e.g., spawned from splunkd or PostgreSQL sidecar handlers) when correlating with HTTP 200/201 responses on sidecar endpoints. Escalate if truncation targets system-critical paths (configs, binaries, logs).

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Internet Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'even if scanners say not vulnerable...it's worth one quick check across your fleet' and references asset-exposure hunt. Pipeline did not surface inventory/exposure detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan firewall/proxy logs for external (non-RFC1918) source IPs reaching Splunk Enterprise web-UI ports (8000, 8089, 9997) or any _sidecar/* endpoints. Cross-reference against asset inventory and identify Splunk instances unintentionally exposed to the internet or reachable without VPN context.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanner Hits
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'match against your vulnerability scanner' for CVE-2026-20253. Pipeline failed to suggest scanner-output detection and alerting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner report (Nessus, Qualys, Tenable, etc.) detecting CVE-2026-20253 on any asset. Escalate to critical if (a) the affected Splunk instance is internet-reachable, (b) remediation is past the federal due date (2026-06-21), or (c) the system handles sensitive data.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—detecting requests to the sidecar without auth tokens is the initial compromise vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar ports (typically :8191 or dynamically discovered) from external sources without valid Splunk authentication tokens. Alert on successful responses (200/201) to unauthenticated requests.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names the exploitation action: 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—post-compromise detection of file I/O operations triggered by or originating from the sidecar daemon.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or deletion events where the parent/initiator is the PostgreSQL sidecar process or requests proxied through it. Flag truncations of critical system/config files, especially correlated with prior unauthenticated HTTP access.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Presence Check
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CISA KEV status and federal remediation due date (2026-06-21)—standard vulnerability scanning for this CVE ID across the Splunk fleet is the canonical hunt pattern referenced in the article itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-20253 matches. Cross-check against actual Splunk Enterprise versions deployed; reconcile false negatives (scanner cleared, version actually vulnerable) to find untracked or misreported instances.

suggestion.title: Network Reconnaissance of Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Ports
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the attack surface is the 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—network-level detection of port scans or connection attempts to typical sidecar ports from untrusted sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful or attempted connections to Splunk sidecar service ports from external IP ranges, especially with high request volume or abnormal payloads. Track failed authentication attempts followed by exploitation.

suggestion.title: Inline remote configuration syntax in HTTP requests to rclone RC
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Inline remote configuration can set backend options that execute local commands during initialization' but no detection specifically hunts for this payload in HTTP request bodies/paths. The attack pattern includes square-bracket syntax like '[local:exec=', '[[:option=', or unencoded backend option injection. This is distinct from connection-level signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search HTTP GET/HEAD requests to rclone RC endpoint where URL path contains inline remote brackets with option injection: patterns like [local:exec=, [[:command=, or URL-encoded variants %5B%5B. This represents the actual command-injection payload. Requires HTTP proxy/WAF or rclone HTTP logging visibility; network layer alone insufficient.

suggestion.title: Rclone configuration file containing inline remote definitions
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions inline remote configuration as attack vector. Legitimate rclone config files (~/.config/rclone/rclone.conf or %APPDATA%\rclone\rclone.conf) containing '[remotes]' with inline backend definitions (especially exec, local, or system-interaction backends) signal either attacker persistence or pre-staged exploitation setup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor rclone config file creation or modification where content contains '[' + ':' inline remote syntax, particularly with exec=, command=, or local= directives. High-fidelity when paired with HTTP request detection (UC_103_2 supplement) or suspicious process spawning (UC_103_1).

suggestion.title: Port 5572 listeners on hosts without expected rclone deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article references port 5572 as the rclone RC default endpoint. Unexpected listeners on this port (or inferred via process-to-port binding) on hosts where rclone is not in asset inventory indicate either new attacker-deployed instances or missed asset data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unexpected port 5572 listeners (via network monitoring or command-line auditing) against rclone asset inventory (UC_103_3). Flag new listeners on this port as potential attacker-deployed instances or reconnaissance targets. Combine with user context to identify privilege abuse.

suggestion.title: Failed or successful authentications to rclone RC endpoint without credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated' access. If rclone RC logs are available, detect requests missing HTTP Authorization headers, Bearer tokens, or Basic auth credentials—especially followed by command-execution patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor rclone RC access logs or HTTP proxy logs for GET/HEAD requests to /[*:*]/* or similar inline-remote paths where Authorization header is absent AND subsequent process activity spawns shell/script interpreter. Requires rclone logging or HTTP-layer visibility; network flow data insufficient.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — this is the primary attack vector; unauthorized access attempts must be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Splunk Enterprise sidecar endpoints lacking valid authentication credentials. Establish baseline of legitimate internal sidecar traffic; flag connections from external IPs or anomalous access patterns.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Arbitrary File Create/Truncate by Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation creates or truncates arbitrary files — file system activity during exploitation must be monitorable through process and file events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected file creation or truncation by Splunk processes, especially in PostgreSQL directories or system paths. Correlate with authentication gaps to confirm unauthenticated exploitation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Active Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry explicitly indicates 'observed exploited in the wild' — CVE-specific detection is mandatory with federal patch due 2026-06-21.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for CVE-2026-20253 exploitation signatures against Splunk Enterprise instances. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner output; flag unpatched instances with patch deadline passed.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article implies sidecar reachable without proper auth — service exposure and anomalous connection patterns indicate exploitation risk or active compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate connections to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar from authorized internal sources. Alert on external IP connections, non-standard ports, or incomplete authentication handshakes.

suggestion.title: Gravity SMTP Plugin Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names plugin and exploitation; attack vector not captured by pipeline. Article phrase: 'Hackers Exploit Gravity SMTP WordPress Plugin Bug'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests targeting Gravity SMTP plugin files (wp-content/plugins/gravity-smtp/) with payloads characteristic of CVE exploitation. Baseline expected plugin file access; alert on requests with suspicious parameters, injection attempts, or unusual HTTP methods targeting admin/settings endpoints.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized API Key Extraction from Plugin Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Impact stated as 'API Keys exposed' — this is a credential_access event. Pipeline did not map exposure mechanism to MITRE phase. Article phrase: 'Expose API Keys'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on direct queries to wp_options table for gravity-smtp options, or file reads of Gravity SMTP config files outside normal plugin lifecycle. Correlate with failed authorization or suspicious user contexts. Exfiltration: monitor for bulk export of wp_options or config file contents via POST/wget.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin File Anomaly — Gravity SMTP Unauthorized Modification
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation typically requires malicious payload delivery or config tampering. Article describes bug exploitation, implying unauthorized modification of plugin behavior or files. No defensive indicators captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gravity SMTP plugin directory for modifications outside package manager or update workflows. Hash changes, new files, permission changes on .php files should be alerted. Baseline clean plugin hash and trigger on deviations.

suggestion.title: Compromised SMTP Credentials — Unauthorized Email Relay Activity
suggestion.rationale: API key exposure enables account compromise; pipeline missed impact phase detection. Exposed SMTP credentials lead to email spoofing/relay abuse. Article phrase: 'Expose API Keys' implies downstream email infra compromise.
log_sources: Email system audit logs (abnormal mail volume/recipients)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SMTP authentication from Gravity SMTP plugin using credentials associated with exploitation timeline. Monitor for: spike in mail volume, unusual recipients, geographic anomalies in relay source, authentication failure patterns preceding success. Cross-correlate plugin exploitation timestamp with SMTP anomalies.

suggestion.title: API Credential Enumeration via WordPress Database Access
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline did not model discovery/credential enumeration phase preceding exfiltration. WordPress DB contains plaintext or weakly-encrypted plugin credentials.
log_sources: File reads of wp-config.php or plugin config directories
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for WordPress admin account usage to access plugin settings pages or database queries selecting gravity-smtp option keys. Correlate with successful authentication via vulnerability vector (non-standard HTTP patterns, plugin RCE indicators). Baseline normal admin configuration review and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: API Key Leakage via WordPress Logs or Backups
suggestion.rationale: Gravity SMTP stores API keys in configuration; if plugin bug exposes serialized data or logs, keys leak. Pipeline did not address data exfiltration from plugin config stores.
log_sources: Error logs (plugin errors may expose config)
HTTP response inspection (error pages with leaked keys)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP responses containing API key-like strings (pattern: long alphanumeric tokens typical of SMTP/email API keys). Review WordPress debug logs for Gravity SMTP errors containing configuration data. Alert on unauthorized backup file access or exposure via web-accessible backup directories.

suggestion.title: Langflow HTTP request parameter injection - symlink traversal pattern (CVE-2026-55447 initial exploit)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'symlink RCE' and 'symlink-traversal' as the attack vector but no UC hunts the web request or API call that injects the malicious path. Article phrase: 'BaseFileComponent symlink RCE' describes the vulnerability mechanism but existing UCs focus on post-exploitation (file read, RCE execution), not the injection itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Langflow endpoints (/api/v1/flows, /flows/{id}/run, component execution paths) for path traversal indicators in parameters: ../, ..\, symlink references, or absolute paths to /etc, /.ssh, /.aws. Flag requests from unauthenticated or external origins with file_path, input_path, or upload parameters containing traversal syntax.

suggestion.title: Symlink creation in Langflow working directory (CVE-2026-55447 attack staging)
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly depends on symlink traversal, but no UC detects symlink artifact creation. UC_5_1 hunts for a specific temporary file (/tmp/trip.docx) post-exploitation but misses the symlink setup phase. Article phrase: 'symlink-traversal' is the core mechanism but detection logic stops at file access, not symlink creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect symlink creation events (ln -s, CreateSymbolicLink, os.symlink) in /tmp, /var/tmp, or Langflow app directories by python, uvicorn, or gunicorn processes. Prioritize symlinks targeting credential paths (/.ssh/, /.aws/, /.kube/, /root) or system files (/etc/shadow, /etc/passwd). Correlate with subsequent file read events.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Langflow component instantiation with file parameters (CVE-2026-55447 workflow attack setup)
suggestion.rationale: Article names six vulnerable component types (Docling, FileComponent, VideoFileComponent, DoclingRemoteComponent, NvidiaIngestComponent, UnstructuredComponent) but no UC detects their creation or configuration with suspicious parameters. Attack requires first constructing a workflow graph with these components before symlink traversal can occur.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Langflow API calls to /graphs or /flows endpoints for POST/PUT payloads containing FileComponent, VideoFileComponent, UnstructuredComponent, DoclingRemoteComponent with file_path or input_path parameters containing ../, absolute paths, or env variable expansion (e.g., $HOME, $ROOT). Correlate with subsequent execution by Python interpreter.

suggestion.title: Python code execution from file parameters in Langflow context (CVE-2026-55447 RCE execution gap)
suggestion.rationale: UC_5_4 detects shell spawning (bash, sh) as post-RCE evidence but not the Python eval/exec that enabled it. Article states 'Python Interpreter RCE' (T1059.006) but the gap between parameter injection and shell invocation (where the initial Python code exec occurs) is unmonitored. Article phrase: 'Command and Scripting Interpreter: Python' indicates code execution but UC focuses on child processes, not the initial eval.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect eval(), exec(), or __import__() syscalls within Python worker processes (uvicorn, gunicorn, langflow-worker) where the code argument originates from deserialized user input (JSON payloads, file contents from file_path parameters). Look for frame patterns of exec() with compile() called on untrusted input, followed by network or shell spawning.

suggestion.title: Crossplane cosign signature verification timestamp mismatch (TOCTOU detection)
suggestion.rationale: Article core mechanic: 'malicious OCI registry could serve a correctly signed image for verification, then serve unverified content on pull.' No detection targets the timing anomaly—gap between when cosign verify succeeds and when image pull completes. Detectable via registry audit logs or cluster audit showing verify then different pull.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track cosign verify success timestamps and subsequent image pull operations. Flag when the same package reference (tag) is verified at time T1 but a different content hash is pulled at time T2 > T1 from the same registry, indicating potential race-condition exploitation.

suggestion.title: OCI registry endpoint substitution or hostname deviation in package reference
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires either compromising the registry or performing MitM to serve different content during verify vs. pull phases. Article mentions 'malicious OCI registry' but no detection looks for lateral movement to registry infrastructure or URL rewriting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package resource specs for registry hostname changes between successive deployments. Flag if pull_secret credentials are updated to point to a different OCI registry, or if DNS resolution for the registry FQDN changes to unexpected IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Cosign installation or cosign binary removal from cluster nodes
suggestion.rationale: Bypassing signature verification can be achieved by removing or disabling cosign itself on nodes. Article discusses signature verification mechanism but no detection explicitly monitors for cosign binary tampering or removal, which is a prerequisite attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect removal or modification of cosign binary paths (/usr/local/bin/cosign, container image registries' cosign sidecar) or execution of package install commands with environment variables that disable signature verification (e.g., COSIGN_SKIP_VERIFICATION=1).

suggestion.title: Multiple failed cosign verification attempts followed by successful package install
suggestion.rationale: An attacker might probe the signature verification mechanism, encounter failures, then disable it. Article does not explicitly call this out, but sequential failed-verify → disabled-verify → successful-install is a strong behavioral indicator of exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed cosign verification attempts (from logs or API errors) with subsequent successful package installations from the same user/service account within a narrow time window, paired with ImageConfig modifications that disable verification.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—attack vector not converted to detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint lacking authentication credentials or Authorization headers. Correlate unauthenticated POST/PUT/DELETE requests with subsequent unexpected file system modifications.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article core impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—impact phase completely absent from use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or truncation by Splunk processes outside scheduled maintenance windows. Alert on unexpected writes to system-critical directories (/etc, /opt/splunk/etc) preceded by unauthenticated endpoint requests.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'CISA KEV entry...actively exploited in the wild' with federal remediation deadline 2026-06-21; asset-exposure hunt templates referenced but never instantiated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all Splunk Enterprise deployments for CVE-2026-20253 presence. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results with network telemetry to identify internet-facing instances. Correlate scan findings with exploitation indicators (unauthenticated sidecar access logs).

suggestion.title: Missing Authentication Enforcement on Splunk Critical Functions
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'missing authentication for critical function'—no detection for auth-bypass or privilege-escalation-by-omission scenarios generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk API/endpoint audit logs for critical operations (file creation, deletion) lacking corresponding user authentication events. Alert on requests to sidecar endpoints returning success (2xx) without prior login event.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Internet Exposure – Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'observed exploited in the wild' under CISA KEV and explicitly invokes T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application). Exploitation only viable if Splunk Enterprise ports (8089, 8000, 8191) are reachable from untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate internal Splunk Enterprise instances with listening ports 8000, 8089, 8191. Cross-reference against asset inventory with internet-routing paths. Flag any listening on internet-facing IPs or behind reverse proxies without WAF/authentication proxy.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Requests to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated user' accessing 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' as the attack vector. Sidecar typically listens on high ephemeral or reserved ports behind Splunk; requests without auth headers or valid session tokens are anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk access logs for requests to sidecar-related paths (e.g., /services/sidecar, /pgsql, /_postgres) lacking Authorization headers or valid session cookies. Correlate with failed auth attempts or 403→200 status progression.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar File Operation Anomalies – Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'create or truncate arbitrary files through [sidecar] endpoint'. Successful exploitation will manifest as file creation/deletion events, likely originating from Splunk service account or PostgreSQL process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or truncation events where parent process is Splunk Enterprise or PostgreSQL sidecar, targeting directories outside Splunk's application/data/etc/index directories (e.g., /etc, /var, /tmp with suspicious patterns, user home dirs). Flag rapid truncation of existing files.

suggestion.title: Splunk Service Port Scanning & Enumeration – Pre-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates active exploitation. Reconnaissance phase precedes exploitation; attackers scan for open Splunk ports and probe endpoints for authentication requirements before triggering CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect external source IPs scanning Splunk ports (8000, 8089, 8191) across multiple targets in close time window. Look for GET/HEAD requests to common Splunk endpoints (e.g., /services/auth/login, /api/apps) returning 401/403, followed by attempts to /services/sidecar or PostgreSQL endpoints.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Version Detection – Known Vulnerable Versions
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-20253 affects specific Splunk Enterprise versions. Asset inventory should tag instances against affected version matrix to prioritize patching by patch-due date (2026-06-21).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Splunk cluster master / deployment client logs for version strings, or API-enumerate /services/server/info endpoints. Cross-ref against Splunk security advisory CVE-2026-20253 affected versions. Flag instances not yet patched to remediated version by federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via PostgreSQL Sidecar Query Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article describes file creation capability; implicit risk is that truncated or created files could contain exfiltrated data. PostgreSQL sidecar abuse could enable data queries or file reads before exfil.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL sidecar query logs (if enabled) for unusual SELECT statements on sensitive tables or volumes. Correlate with outbound network connections from Splunk service IP. Flag data dumps to temp files followed by network transfer.

suggestion.title: Exposed Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar — Unauthenticated Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow an unauthenticated user' to exploit via 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — core attack vector requiring asset-exposure hunt for reachable Splunk services per template instructions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unauthenticated HTTP/HTTPS requests to Splunk ports (8089, 8088, or sidecar-specific) originating externally. Flag successful connections without prior authentication that precede file operations; correlate with connection logs + file events.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Sidecar Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Exploit payload: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — direct execution impact requiring file-event detection keyed to Splunk service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or truncation events initiated by Splunk service account (splunkd process) to unexpected system/config/audit directories. Prioritize truncations of log files; correlate with unauthenticated network access within 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: Splunk Instance Inventory — PostgreSQL Sidecar Exposure Assessment
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies active exploitation; federal patch due 2026-06-21 necessitates rapid inventory of affected instances. Article emphasizes asset-exposure hunt as canonical detection; must identify which Splunk deployments expose sidecar.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner, CMDB, and cloud-security tools for Splunk Enterprise instances with version ≤ patched threshold and network-reachable PostgreSQL sidecar ports (5432 or Splunk-specific). Cross-check inbound firewall rules permitting external access.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user can create or truncate arbitrary files' and CISA KEV means active wild exploitation. Recommended hunt template references asset-exposure pattern; this is the canonical first detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Splunk instances for inbound requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint on port 5432 or documented service path from unauthenticated IPs. Correlate with vulnerability scanner data for CVE-2026-20253 detection flags. High-confidence signal if combined with failed authentication logs.

suggestion.title: Splunk Missing Authentication Bypass — Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the vulnerability itself; detect direct requests to service endpoint bypassing Splunk auth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to /_internal or PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (unpatched Splunk instances) that lack X-Splunk-Authorization headers or session tokens. Flag if source is external/untrusted network.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Create/Truncate via Splunk PostgreSQL Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attackers can 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' This is impact behavior distinct from exploitation; detect file operations post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk server file I/O for unexpected writes/truncations to sensitive paths (/etc, /var/log, $SPLUNK_HOME/etc). Correlate with auth bypass alerts. Truncation of size 0 on data or log files is high-confidence impact signal.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Splunk Service Endpoint Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability in 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—attackers must first locate/probe the service. Detect reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for repetitive HTTP/TCP connections to Splunk instance ports (8089, 8000) followed by requests to non-standard paths (/services, /_internal, /api/services) from single source without valid auth, especially from external IP ranges.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Patch Deployment & Compliance Verification
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV federal due-date 2026-06-21 mentioned; article states 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Verify deployed patches and version compliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all Splunk Enterprise instances for version >= patched release. Flag instances running pre-patch versions after 2026-06-21 deadline. Cross-ref against CMDB for inventory accuracy.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—sidecar accessibility is the entry point and central to the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Splunk instances on PostgreSQL-related ports or sidecar service paths from untrusted networks. Alert on requests lacking Splunk authentication headers or bypass patterns targeting /services or /api endpoints on non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Manipulation via Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker can 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—post-exploitation file operations are the impact mechanism and directly detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation, truncation, or deletion operations originating from Splunk sidecar processes or PostgreSQL service accounts. Prioritize audit log, config file, and license file modifications; flag bulk deletions in var/log or similar.

suggestion.title: Exposed Splunk Enterprise Service Endpoint Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Exploit requires sidecar accessibility from untrusted network. Article context implies exposed admin/service ports are the attack surface; asset exposure is the prerequisite vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Splunk Enterprise instances with exposed PostgreSQL sidecar ports (typically 5432 or custom service ports) reachable from external networks. Flag any unauthenticated service endpoints or missing firewall rules blocking non-admin access.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Vulnerable Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires asset inventory against patch baseline. Article specifies CVE-2026-20253 and federal due date 2026-06-21; unpatched Splunk instances are the vulnerable population.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner or Splunk version inventory to identify unpatched Splunk Enterprise instances. Cross-reference CVE-2026-20253 against installed versions and flag those not meeting federal patch deadline.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Asset Exposure – CVE-2026-20253
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs to asset-exposure hunt template and emphasizes 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets'; no UC generated despite this being the foundational detection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query inventory for Splunk Enterprise instances externally accessible on ports 8000, 8089, 8191 and PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoints. Cross-reference patch status against CVE-2026-20253 remediation records. Alert on exposed/unpatched instances regardless of last-scan status due to patch-lag prevalence in enterprises.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability permits 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—no detection for the unauthorized endpoint access itself was generated
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoints lacking valid authentication tokens/headers. Flag external-origin connection attempts to sidecar ports. Detect access from non-Splunk-admin IP ranges; baseline normal sidecar traffic patterns and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Create/Truncate via PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'create or truncate arbitrary files' as the exploitation capability; no file-activity detection was generated for this impact mechanism
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk host file system for unexpected file creation or truncation operations outside standard Splunk directories. suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected Splunk service restarts, PostgreSQL sidecar service crashes, or file-system-related errors in Splunk logs, especially if correlated with the previous two detections or external request logs.

suggestion.title: Exposed Splunk Asset Inventory — CVE-2026-20253 Risk Posture
suggestion.rationale: Federal due date 2026-06-21 implies urgent inventory; pipeline template recommended 'asset-exposure hunt' but provided no concrete detection — must enumerate internet-facing Splunk instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query cloud metadata and network scans to identify all Splunk Enterprise instances with public IPs or internet-routable DNS names. Cross-check against patch/version inventory to identify unpatched systems exploitable for CVE-2026-20253.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Network Reconnaissance — External Port Probing
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — attackers will probe for this endpoint before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound SYN/probe attempts to non-standard PostgreSQL sidecar ports (or default port 5432) from external sources to Splunk-hosting subnets, especially if followed by HTTP requests to Splunk endpoints.

suggestion.title: WordPress Gravity SMTP Plugin Vulnerability Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Hackers Exploit Gravity SMTP WordPress Plugin Bug to Expose API Keys.' Pipeline generated zero detections for this named exploit despite critical severity rating.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Gravity SMTP plugin paths (wp-content/plugins/gravity-forms-smtp/* or admin.php?page=gf_settings) for exploitation payloads. Baseline legitimate admin access; alert on repeated failed requests, parameter tampering, or access from external/non-admin IPs.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Gravity SMTP API Key Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core threat: API keys exposed via plugin vulnerability. Pipeline entirely missed credential-access phase despite this being the stated attack outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized reads or exports of Gravity SMTP configuration containing API keys. Monitor for: config file access outside plugin installation, database queries selecting credential fields, plugin settings page responses containing API keys in cleartext, unusual plugin backup/export operations.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Gravity SMTP Plugin Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article implies specific plugin versions are vulnerable; vulnerability scanning is foundational defense but pipeline generated no inventory or patching detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan wp-content/plugins directory for Gravity SMTP presence and version. Correlate installed versions against CVE database for this plugin. Flag systems running known-vulnerable versions as patch priority; track remediation timelines.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement to WordPress Plugin Admin Settings
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires access to plugin configuration where credentials are stored—article omits exact exploit vector but admin interface access is prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate WordPress admin login success with plugin settings page access (admin.php?page=gf* or plugin-admin endpoints). Alert on settings access by non-admin roles, access immediately following privilege escalation, or geographic/IP anomalies in same session.

suggestion.title: API Key Usage Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Once API keys are exposed, they become tools for lateral access or data exfiltration. Pipeline omitted post-exploitation impact detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API calls to external services using credentials extracted from Gravity SMTP (e.g., mail relay services, cloud API access). Detect bulk email operations, unusual geographic origins of API key usage, or API key authentication from IPs not associated with legitimate plugin installation.

suggestion.title: Cross-Realm Alarm Deletion via removeAlarms
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'An authenticated user in any realm can delete alarms belonging to other realms (tenants) by supplying arbitrary alarm IDs.' Represents privilege escalation from own-realm authorization to unauthorized cross-tenant destruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when removeAlarms API calls target alarm IDs outside the calling user's assigned realm. Correlate user realm membership from directory/IAM logs with alarm ownership metadata in application logs; flag when they diverge.

suggestion.title: Bulk Delete Without Per-Object Authorization Validation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability mechanism: 'bulk removeAlarms() method only verifies that the caller's own realm is active and accessible, but never checks whether the targeted al[arms]' belong to that realm. This is an authorization bypass in batch operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor bulk API operations (removeAlarms with multiple IDs in a single request) for missing or failed realm validation per object. Flag operations that delete objects from multiple logical tenants or realms in a single call.

suggestion.title: Cross-Tenant Data Destruction
suggestion.rationale: Attack impact: deletion of alarms (operational data) across tenant boundaries. Alarms may represent security events, compliance records, or operational state—their destruction is a potential data destruction play.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful removeAlarms calls where deleted alarm IDs were verified not to belong to the calling user's realm. Baseline the user's normal deletion volume and flag significant outliers or off-hours bulk operations.

suggestion.title: Multi-Tenancy Boundary Violation in RBAC Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: Systemic issue: 'The vulnerability exists because the bulk removeAlarms() method only verifies that the caller's own realm is active and accessible, but never checks whether the targeted al[arms are owned by them].' Missing RBAC control across API layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build baseline of each user's realm assignment and authorized data scope. Flag API calls that access or modify objects in realms where user has no documented authorization, indicating RBAC enforcement failure.

suggestion.title: Langflow BaseFileComponent node configuration with path-traversal parameters
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exists in DoclingInlineComponent, DoclingRemoteComponent, FileComponent, etc., but does not detail HOW exploitation is triggered. Missing: detection for suspicious file-path parameters or symlink targets in component instantiation or flow definition. Article phrase: 'All components based on BaseFileComponent are vulnerable' but lacks specifics on parameter-injection mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Langflow worker process command-line or flow-definition creation for file path parameters containing '..' sequences, /etc, /root, or .ssh. Log any invocation of BaseFileComponent nodes with suspicious file arguments.

suggestion.title: Credential exfiltration: Langflow secret_key or API keys harvested via symlink read
suggestion.rationale: UC_7_3 detects file reads of '/app/langflow/secret_key' and credential files, but does not address the downstream impact. Missing: detection for exfiltration or usage of harvested secrets. Article phrase: 'Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files (T1552.001)' implies credential access, but no UC targets credential reuse post-read.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for base64-encoded secret_key or langflow configuration strings appearing in child process command-lines, outbound network traffic, or temporary files immediately after a suspicious file read. Alert on re-use of secrets in HTTP Authorization headers or API calls.

suggestion.title: Symlink/directory-traversal attempt detection: ../../../ sequences in Langflow flow-parameter handling
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'arbitrary file read with...symlink' but none of the UCs hunt for the actual traversal attempts (crafted path sequences). Missing: pre-exploitation detection. Article phrase: 'BaseFileComponent-based nodes arbitrary file read' implies parameter crafting, but no UC monitors input validation or path normalization bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Langflow HTTP endpoints or worker-input logs for sequences like '../', '%2e%2e%2f', or symlink creation immediately prior to suspicious file reads. Flag any call to symlink() or readlink() originating from langflow processes during flow execution.

suggestion.title: Langflow multi-component attack correlation: multiple vulnerable components exploited in short timespan
suggestion.rationale: Article lists six vulnerable component types (Docling Inline/Remote, FileComponent, NvidiaIngestComponent, VideoFileComponent, UnstructuredComponent) but existing UCs treat each independently. Missing: correlation across multiple component exploitation attempts. Suggests coordinated attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file-read events from different BaseFileComponent types (Docling, Unstructured, NVIDIA Retriever) spawned by the same langflow worker within 60 seconds. Multiple component types in same session indicates systematic exploitation, not accidental user action.

suggestion.title: Langflow environment or secret escaping via command-scripting Python/Shell interpreter nodes
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1059.004 (Unix Shell) and T1059.006 (Python) but UC_7_4 focuses only on shell-spawning, not on Python code injection within Langflow's own Python interpreter node. Missing: detection for malicious Python payloads in Langflow node definitions or execution logs. Article phrase: 'Command and Scripting Interpreter: Python' suggests direct Python execution, not just shell-spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt Langflow worker logs or Python REPL event logs for suspicious Python payloads: __import__, subprocess.call, os.system, or open() calls targeting /etc, /root, or ~/.ssh within a Python interpreter node context. Flag dynamic code execution (eval, exec) originating from flow node parameters.

suggestion.title: Langflow IDOR - Unauthorized Flow Access via `/api/v1/responses` Parameter Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article directly states: 'authenticated attacker to execute any flow belonging to another user by specifying the victim's flow ID in the request.' Pipeline generated zero detection logic for this core exploitation vector despite clear attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on requests to `/api/v1/responses` endpoint where authenticated user_id does not match the owner of the requested flow_id parameter. Cross-reference user context against flow ownership metadata; establish baseline of documented collaborative users and flag all out-of-policy access attempts.

suggestion.title: Langflow Suspicious Flow Execution - Cross-Owner Execution Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article impact explicitly describes unauthorized users can 'execute' flows. Detect successful unauthorized flow executions by comparing execution requester against flow creator in application logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor flow execution event logs for cases where executor_user_id differs from flow.created_by_user_id. Flag all executions outside documented shared-access patterns; raise severity for execution from newly-discovered user accounts or privilege-escalated contexts.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure - Langflow CVE-2026-55255 Vulnerable Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)' hunt template. Pipeline failed to instantiate this recommended hunt despite clear guidance provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all deployed Langflow instances and capture version numbers from asset inventory and software catalogs. Flag instances running any version ≤ vendor patch threshold and alert for immediate remediation; prioritize internet-facing deployments.

suggestion.title: Craft CMS actionResourceJs Endpoint Access Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names `/actions/app/resource-js` as the vulnerable endpoint. This is the initial access point and requires baseline + anomaly detection for exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor access logs for requests to paths matching `/actions/app/resource-js` on Craft CMS instances. Establish baseline for legitimate request frequency, source IPs, and User-Agents; alert on spikes, external sources, or automated scanning tools.

suggestion.title: Host/X-Forwarded-Host Header Poisoning - Craft CMS
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'attacker can poison the Host or X-Forwarded-Host header to manipulate the application's $baseUrl...bypasses the endpoint's internal URL validation.' This is the core attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on requests to `/actions/app/resource-js` where Host or X-Forwarded-Host headers contain values mismatched to legitimate application domains, internal RFC1918 IPs, localhost variants, or values with URL encoding/Unicode manipulation indicative of obfuscation.

suggestion.title: JavaScript Payload Injection Detection - actionResourceJs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Arbitrary JavaScript Injection' as output. The endpoint returns JavaScript to clients; injected payloads are the execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP response bodies from `/actions/app/resource-js` for injected JavaScript including eval(), Function() constructors, fetch/XMLHttpRequest to non-whitelisted domains, inline event handlers, Base64/hex-encoded script content, or DOM manipulation patterns typical of stored/reflected XSS.

suggestion.title: Blind SSRF via Craft CMS - Outbound Request Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Blind SSRF and Arbitrary JavaScript Injection'—the server is forced to make requests to attacker-specified URLs. Outbound traffic from Craft CMS is the forensic signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections from Craft CMS web server processes to RFC1918 addresses, 127.0.0.1, or unapproved external domains. Correlate timing with inbound `/actions/app/resource-js` requests; blind SSRF will manifest as anomalous egress without corresponding inbound data transfer.

suggestion.title: Craft CMS - Obfuscated/Encoded Header Attack Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article notes the attack 'bypasses the endpoint's internal URL validation.' Attackers likely use URL encoding, Unicode normalization, protocol-relative URLs, or case-variation to evade parsing. These are precursors to successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag requests to `/actions/app/resource-js` with double-URL-encoded, Unicode-normalized, protocol-relative (//), IPv6-bracket, octal, or hex-encoded Host/X-Forwarded-Host values. Decode and check against whitelist; mismatches indicate evasion attempts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-55791 Craft CMS Vulnerable Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day with no patch yet implied; vulnerability assessment must identify at-risk systems via version detection and network exposure analysis. Foundation for incident response prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query CMDB/asset inventory for Craft CMS instances; correlate with HTTP response headers (X-Craft-Version, Server headers) and CMS fingerprinting endpoints to identify vulnerable versions. Prioritize by external exposure (Internet-facing, no auth required) and correlate with recent `/actions/app/resource-js` access logs.

suggestion.title: OCI Registry Image Tag Digest Mismatch Between Verification and Pull
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'a malicious OCI registry could serve a correctly signed image for verification' then implicitly serve different content on subsequent pull. Detects the core TOCTOU: verify image SHA X, then pull receives SHA Y.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OCI registry pull logs for scenarios where a pull request for tag 'v*' returns a different image digest than the preceding verification request to the same tag. Correlate with Crossplane ImageConfig logs showing cosign verification passed immediately before the mismatched pull.

suggestion.title: Crossplane Package Installation with Unverified Content After cosign Check
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the vulnerability allows 'installing unverified package content'. Detects installations that bypass or succeed despite post-verification content changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Crossplane package installs where cosign verification succeeded but the installed package SHA or manifest does not match the verified digest in the same installation transaction.

suggestion.title: Semantic Version Tag Re-publication with Different Manifest
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'mutable tag' and semantic versions as the attack vector: 'When a package is installed using a tag reference (e.g., a semantic version)'. Detects tag reuse attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OCI registry for the same semantic version tag (e.g., 'v1.2.3') being pushed multiple times within a 1-hour window with different manifests or digests. Flag high-churn tags in production namespaces.

suggestion.title: ImageConfig Signature Verification Disabled or Tampered
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'signature verification configured via the ImageConfig mechanism'. Detecting when this is disabled avoids the verification step entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any Crossplane ImageConfig modification that disables or removes the cosign verification settings, or changes the verification policy to permissive (e.g., skipVerify, weak trust policies).

suggestion.title: Crossplane Package Pull from Unsigned OCI Artifact After Failed Verification
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability hinges on the gap between 'When enabled, the package manager uses cosign to verify' and the subsequent pull. Detect fallback to unsigned sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Crossplane package pulls that reference non-signed or non-cosign-verified images, especially when ImageConfig shows verification is supposed to be enabled. Track any pull requests sent to unsigned layers after a cosign verification event.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—this is the direct exploitation vector and primary detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoints lacking valid authentication (WWW-Authenticate 401 responses should be baseline; 200 responses without auth tokens are anomalous). Correlate with file-system write events originating from postgres service context.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Write/Truncate via PostgreSQL Process
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—observable file operations post-exploitation are high-fidelity signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FileCreate/FileDelete operations by postgres service or Splunk Enterprise child processes targeting sensitive system directories (config, logs, data). Flag file truncations (size reduction to zero) as especially indicative of T1485 destruction intent.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanner Positive
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs to 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and marks CISA KEV status (active in-the-wild exploitation). Youngest and most direct detection path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Splunk Enterprise versions matching CVE-2026-20253 vulnerable range. Priority-sort by internet-facing exposure. Cross-check patch status against federal due date (2026-06-21). Alert on any newly discovered vulnerable instances.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Public Endpoint Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation implies active threat-actor targeting of exposed Splunk services. T1190 is the canonical technique for exploiting public-facing applications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS inbound traffic to Splunk Enterprise for malformed requests to sidecar paths, missing Authorization headers on endpoints that require auth, or response patterns (401→200 transitions) indicating auth bypass. Flag anomalous User-Agent strings or rapid repeated requests to service discovery paths.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk Admin/Sidecar Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—core attack vector is bypass of authentication controls on admin-level functions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk admin UI and sidecar service endpoints for requests without valid auth tokens or session cookies. Flag 401/403 responses followed by successful file operations from same source IP.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Access from Untrusted Source
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability specifically targets 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—should detect network access to this internal component from external or unexpected sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on connections to PostgreSQL sidecar (port 5432 or internal socket) originating from internet-facing IP ranges or from Splunk web processes receiving unauthenticated external requests.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation via Splunk Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes direct impact as ability to 'truncate arbitrary files'—file-system layer should detect truncation operations initiated by Splunk daemon.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file truncation or deletion events originating from splunkd or PostgreSQL sidecar processes with targets outside Splunk's home directory or affecting critical system binaries.

suggestion.title: Asset Inventory: Splunk Instances Without Authentication Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: KEV implies active exploitation of 'missing authentication'—foundational hunt is verify all Splunk admin interfaces enforce authentication, especially those internet-facing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all Splunk instances (web UI on :8000, daemon on :8089) to confirm authentication required. Cross-reference against patch status vs. federal due date 2026-06-21.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Internet Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated user' access, implying public-facing Splunk instances. Asset-exposure hunt is the canonical first detection for any public-app KEV (referenced in the article's 'Recommended hunts' section).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Splunk Enterprise instances (ports 8000, 8089) exposed to untrusted networks. Cross-check against patch inventory for CVE-2026-20253 remediation status. Unpatched instances ≥ 2026-06-21 are critical.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector as 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'. Needs explicit detection for anomalous or unauthenticated access to this internal service boundary.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk sidecar service (typically localhost:5432 or internal endpoint) for connection attempts from non-whitelisted sources or unauthenticated sessions. Flag any HTTP POST/GET to PostgreSQL-related endpoints without valid Splunk auth tokens.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Core impact: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'. This is the exploitation outcome and needs dedicated detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or truncation operations originating from or proxied through Splunk service processes (splunkd, PostgreSQL sidecar). Alert on modifications to system-critical directories or unexpected file deletions initiated by these services.

suggestion.title: Splunk Service Unauthenticated Endpoint Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article describes unauthenticated access; distinguish from normal service-to-service communication. Detect HTTP requests to Splunk service endpoints that bypass authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to Splunk service endpoints (e.g., /services/*) returning 200/201 responses without valid session cookies or Authorization headers. Correlate source IPs against internal asset inventory.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint (CVE-2026-20253)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'unauthenticated user...through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline produced zero detection for the specific attack vector—the sidecar endpoint access without authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoints from external/untrusted sources with successful responses. Correlate timing with Splunk instances missing patches dated before 2026-06-21. Flag requests lacking proper authentication headers or using default credentials that reach 200/201 status codes.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation via Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attackers 'create arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline did not surface detection for post-exploitation file-write impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected file creation events on Splunk servers correlating in time with sidecar endpoint access. Flag files written to abnormal paths (/tmp, system config directories). Baseline expected file creation by the Splunk process and detect deviations.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation/Deletion via Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'truncate arbitrary files' as an attack outcome. Pipeline failed to generate detection for this file-destruction capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected file truncation or deletion on Splunk servers correlating with sidecar endpoint access, especially targeting log files and audit logs. Use file-integrity monitoring (osquery, auditd) to alert on modifications to critical Splunk directories with detailed change tracking.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Enterprise Vulnerability Scan and Patch Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'match against your vulnerability scanner' with explicit federal due date 2026-06-21. Pipeline should surface inventory and patch-status correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Splunk Enterprise instances and correlate against CVE-2026-20253 patch status. Flag instances without patches applied before 2026-06-21. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner reports (Tenable, Nessus, Qualys) with patch-management systems (SCCM). Verify Splunk version and build timestamps indicate pre-patch installations.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' for this CVE. CISA KEV status (active exploitation) mandates asset-discovery detection. Pipeline produced no UCs whatsoever.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk Enterprise instances matching vulnerable versions via CVE-2026-20253 scanner output. Correlate with network exposure (unfiltered inbound, public DNS, missing auth proxies). Prioritize federal civilian agencies per stated patch deadline.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthenticated Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation 'through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' by 'unauthenticated user.' Pipeline missed this specific ingress vector entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk hosts for HTTP/S requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically ports 8000–8010) originating from untrusted networks with missing or invalid auth headers. Alert on correlation with subsequent file-system anomalies.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation via Splunk CVE-2026-20253
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies destructive capability: 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' Pipeline failed to map impact phase to file-system detection signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal Splunk file operations. Alert on anomalous file creation/truncation/deletion targeting sensitive paths (/etc, /usr/bin, app config, data stores) from Splunk process context or correlating with PostgreSQL endpoint access within 5 minutes prior.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 — Vulnerability Scan Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CISA KEV entry...only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild.' Vulnerability scanner detection is the canonical first-line detection for any CVE-based hunt. Pipeline failed to generate baseline asset-exposure use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner matches for CVE-2026-20253 on any Splunk Enterprise asset. Escalate with high priority if unpatched and internet-accessible. Confirm patch status independently—scanner lag is common.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar — Unauthenticated HTTP Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the core attack vector. Pipeline missed network-layer detection of unauthorized access to the vulnerable endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk Enterprise hosts for unauthenticated HTTP(S) requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint (typically internal port, e.g., 8191). Flag any successful connection establishing from non-administrative sources or external networks.

suggestion.title: Splunk Host — Anomalous File Truncation/Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' Pipeline missed the impact-layer detection. Post-exploitation file operations on Splunk config/data directories are direct evidence of compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Splunk Enterprise hosts, baseline normal file operations in $SPLUNK_HOME/var/lib and $SPLUNK_HOME/etc directories. Alert on unexpected file truncation or creation events, especially outside maintenance windows. Cross-correlate with PostgreSQL sidecar access logs.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Asset Inventory — Patch Compliance (CVE-2026-20253)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-21.' CISA KEV requires inventory-driven compliance tracking. Pipeline failed to generate asset-discovery use case for patch posture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate daily report of all Splunk Enterprise instances (hostname, version, listening ports, patch status). Cross-reference against CVE-2026-20253 fix versions. Escalate any unpatched instances discovered after 2026-06-21 to Splunk admins with severity alert.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service — Network Exposure Assessment
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Unauthenticated exploitation requires network reachability. Pipeline missed scope assessment of which hosts expose this endpoint to untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit all Splunk Enterprise instances for PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint accessibility. Confirm endpoint is not reachable from internet or untrusted networks. Map firewall rules and network ACLs. Flag any instances with broad access as configuration drift.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the attack vector and requires detection of connections lacking authentication to sidecar ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify inbound HTTP/TCP connections to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar ports (default 5432 or Splunk-specific ranges) originating from external or untrusted networks. Flag requests missing Authorization headers, Bearer tokens, or Splunk session cookies. Baseline should restrict sidecar access to localhost and internal admin IPs only.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Service Process
suggestion.rationale: Core attack capability described as 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' Monitor for splunkd.exe or sidecar processes creating/truncating files outside normal Splunk directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Splunk or PostgreSQL sidecar processes creating/truncating files outside /opt/splunk/etc, /opt/splunk/var, /opt/splunk/share or C:\Program Files\Splunk equivalents. Prioritize system directories (/etc, /var/lib, /etc/init.d) and sensitive config paths. Truncation events (file resize to 0 bytes) should trigger escalated urgency.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing Splunk Sidecar Port Enumeration (Network Reconnaissance)
suggestion.rationale: T1190 classification and 'public-facing application' language indicate sidecar endpoint exposure. Detect network scans or connection attempts to sidecar ports from external sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag connection attempts to Splunk sidecar ports from external IP ranges. Correlate multiple failed connections followed by successful exploitation patterns. Baseline permitted sources (administrative subnets, trusted application servers) and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Splunk Service Unexpected Restart or Crash Post-File Modification
suggestion.rationale: Arbitrary file truncation (described in article) may corrupt service state or config files, causing unexpected process restarts or crashes. This is a post-exploitation artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected restarts of splunkd.exe, Splunk-related PostgreSQL processes, or sidecar containers during business hours. Correlate restarts with preceding suspicious network activity or file modifications. Elevated restart frequency in short windows suggests exploitation-induced instability.

suggestion.title: Splunk Configuration Directory Mass File Deletion/Truncation
suggestion.rationale: Attacker goal post-exploitation likely targets /opt/splunk/etc (configs) or /opt/splunk/var (state) to persist or disrupt. Mass deletions/truncations are high-confidence impact indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline file modification patterns in Splunk system directories. Alert on bulk file deletions or truncations (>5 files in <1 min), particularly if no corresponding backup/update process is running. Correlate with preceding sidecar access anomalies for kill-chain confirmation.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scan Match: CVE-2026-20253
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-20253 — match against your vulnerability scanner' as canonical hunt method for CISA KEV entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scan result returning CVE-2026-20253 against Splunk Enterprise instances. CISA KEV entries require federal patch compliance by published due date (2026-06-21); scanner false-negatives (unpatched systems reporting 'not vulnerable') require immediate manual verification.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation vector: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—explicit network-layer attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/database requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints without valid authentication (missing auth headers, bearer tokens, or session cookies). suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Asset Exposure (CVE-2026-20253)
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability affects 'Splunk Enterprise' exposed to 'unauthenticated user' access. Canonical asset-exposure hunt per article's own template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk Enterprise instances accessible from internet via port scanning or asset inventory. Correlate with CVE-2026-20253 patch status from CMDB or Splunk's own license telemetry. Prioritize instances still running versions <8.2.11 or equivalent.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized PostgreSQL Sidecar Access (Missing Authentication)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user' can access 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Detection gap: no hunt for auth bypass or lack of auth controls on this endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network connections to Splunk sidecar (PostgreSQL port, typically 5432 or custom). Flag connections lacking authentication headers or certificates. In Splunk logs, look for sidecar endpoint hits with HTTP 200 responses before authentication. Lateral detection: unauthenticated SQL command execution.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Create/Truncate via PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' No file-operation detection use case suggested despite explicit impact description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FileCreate and FileDelete events (or ProcessWrite for SQL statements) originating from the Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar process. Flag file operations in unexpected locations (e.g., outside data directories, touching system files, truncating logs). Correlate with network events showing sidecar endpoint access in preceding minutes.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: If sidecar process has file-system access, it likely has network access. Article does not bound scope to single-instance impact; 'arbitrary files' could span multiple systems if sidecar has network paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network connections initiated by the sidecar process to non-standard destinations (outside Splunk infrastructure, to other hosts on the subnet, to external IPs). Flag unusual protocol usage (SSH, RDP, SMB) from the sidecar context.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Unauthenticated Sidecar Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'unauthenticated user' accessing 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — direct attack vector requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk instances for HTTP requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (e.g., port 8191, /api/) from unauthenticated sessions. Alert on successful (200-399) response codes from external or untrusted sources lacking valid authentication tokens.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation from Splunk Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'create or truncate arbitrary files' — anomalous file write/truncate operations from Splunk services are direct exploitation indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect splunkd or sidecar processes initiating truncate/overwrite operations on system files outside normal Splunk directories. Cross-reference against baseline of legitimate Splunk file operations to identify suspicious activity.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Network Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article implies sidecar is exposed to unauthenticated access — network exposure of internal services is detectable via firewall and network anomaly monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound TCP connections to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar ports from non-trusted networks. Alert on connection attempts to known Splunk internal service ports (8191 or variants) originating from external IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Splunk Audit Log Manipulation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attackers exploiting file-truncation vulnerabilities commonly target audit logs for cover-up — specific detection needed for Splunk audit log anomalies per article's 'truncate arbitrary files' attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk audit logs for sudden truncations, gaps, or discontinuities. Compare log sequence numbers and timestamps to detect suspicious resets or deletions that indicate post-exploitation cleanup.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanner Matches
suggestion.rationale: Standard baseline detection — any scanner match for this CVE identifies vulnerable instances requiring immediate remediation per federal due date (2026-06-21).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner identifying Splunk Enterprise versions matching CVE-2026-20253 affected range. Escalate to incident response; federal remediation deadline is 2026-06-21.
